cluster_name: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: States and MCOs build their own verification; payers buy slowly before the Jan 2027 deadline.
judges.note: Large prize with a hard deadline, and payer-as-buyer is right. But it is the consensus 2026 idea with weak defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: States build own verification portals; payer budgets and political timing uncertain.
judges.note: Huge, dated forcing function, payers lose capitation; but crowded with nonprofits and state-specific.

judges.fatal_flaw: Payers slow to contract; retained-member attribution is disputable and free nonprofit tools will appear.
judges.note: Same thesis as I1164 with less depth on plan constraints and privacy. Real deadline pain, but a weaker execution plan.

title: Test-once PFAS proof registry for packaging importers
one_liner: A SKU-level registry and group-buy of accredited PFAS lab reports, so importers of the same factory's food packaging share one test and can produce an authority-ready dossier fast.
cluster_name: PFAS exposure, testing and disposal

judges.fatal_flaw: Each importer keeps liability, so shared reports may not be accepted; labs can bundle.
judges.note: Timely ban and a real test-once network idea; niche market and thin defensibility beyond lab relationships.

judges.fatal_flaw: Authorities or lawyers may reject another importer's report for lot-specific liability.
judges.note: Ban already in force, compliance budget exists, reachable via trade groups, and pooled lab tests give quick margin revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Regulators or lab rules may demand lot-specific tests, limiting how much reports can be shared
judges.note: Real Aug-2026 ban, no grandfathering, and the proof attaches to the factory SKU, not the importer. Clear buyer, real network effect.

title: Heir-to-Own: Sibling Buyouts on Inherited Homes
one_liner: Help the sibling who wants to keep the family house buy out the others by assuming the parent's low-rate mortgage and financing the rest.
cluster_name: Houses caught in death, divorce or care transitions

judges.fatal_flaw: Mortgage licensing and lender dependence; thin volume per attorney channel.
judges.note: Locked-in low-rate mortgages make inherited homes cheap capital. Real insight and huge inheritance wave, but regulated and low fee per deal.

judges.fatal_flaw: Deal flow depends on probate referrals; mortgage licensing and lender assumption complexity slow closings
judges.note: Good per-deal fees and real family pain, but slow, licensed, referral-dependent sales make 10 closings in six months hard.

judges.fatal_flaw: Large buyout gap needs costly second-lien capital; MLO licensing and slow probate timelines.
judges.note: Parent's 3% mortgage as cheap capital to keep the house is non-obvious. Huge inheritance wave, real pain.

title: Konbini Pulse: Owner-Run Launch Verdict Panel
one_liner: A paid panel of convenience-store owners who report real shelf sell-through of new items in the first 48 hours after each Tuesday launch, sold to food makers who otherwise see only HQ's verdict.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Franchise contracts or HQ pressure may bar owners from sharing shelf data
judges.note: Sharp supplier-blindness insight, cheap panel economics, small pilot reachable; Japan-only, needs local founder and legal review.

judges.fatal_flaw: Franchise contracts and chains likely bar owners sharing sales data; retaliation risk
judges.note: Owners as only independent observers of supplier fate is fresh; legal exposure and Japan-only execution limit it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Chains' franchise confidentiality clauses could shut down owner participation and data sales.
judges.note: Suppliers are blind to their own sell-through; paid owner panel is a real moat, but Japan-only and modest prize.

title: Baseline: Bank-Feed Proof of Displacement Costs
one_liner: An app that reconstructs a displaced family's 'normal' spending from pre-loss bank statements and computes the exact increase that Additional Living Expense coverage owes, in carrier-ready format.
cluster_name: Flood and fire survivors: mapping, buyouts, claims and rebuilding

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers profit from under-claiming; public adjusters are a small buyer base.
judges.note: Clever insight that nobody records 'normal' spending, but it is narrow, event-driven and the buyer incentives are misaligned.

judges.fatal_flaw: Bank-data trust and carrier acceptance of the ledger format.
judges.note: Public adjusters pay per file, pain is concentrated in LA, insight is sharp. Small but reachable buyers; carrier upsell later.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers may reject bank-derived ledgers; consumers distrust sharing bank data.
judges.note: 'Nobody records normal' is sharp; reachable public-adjuster buyers in LA, live AB 1795 tailwind.

title: Section 8 Rent-Increase Deadline Capture Service
one_liner: A tracker that knows each voucher tenant's lease anniversary, sees the new FY2027 payment standard, and files the landlord's rent-increase request inside the tight 60-day window before a year of raise is forfeited.
cluster_name: Landlords in soft markets: vouchers, evictions, vacancies and retention

judges.fatal_flaw: One-shot annual value; landlords churn after learning calendar; PHA rules vary widely.
judges.note: Hard deadline, money on table, success fee, free BiggerPockets reach; ten paying landlords within weeks, tiny cost to test.

judges.fatal_flaw: Housing-authority rules vary and may auto-apply increases; niche caps market size.
judges.note: Real deadline money and fast first customers via BiggerPockets, but a thin wedge with low defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Narrow, low-ACV feature that PM software or housing authorities can bundle.
judges.note: Sharp deadline and fast to first revenue with success-fee pricing. It is small, and the moat is only authority data.

title: Employer-Backed Workforce Pell Program Packager
one_liner: Package 8-15 week, employer-guaranteed training programs that clear state approval and the 70% completion and 70% placement tests, paid per verified hire by the employers who need workers, with Pell covering tuition.
cluster_name: Colleges and training programs under new federal loan caps and earnings tests

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-hire revenue arrives after state approval plus 180-day placement, beyond six months
judges.note: Strong why-now and employer-pays insight; consulting fees can bridge, but slow college and state sales cycles.

judges.fatal_flaw: State approval is slow and Title IV incentive-compensation rules could constrain per-hire billing.
judges.note: Workforce Pell's 70/70 outcome test flips the payer to employers. Fresh 2026 shift, big federal subsidy, clear wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: State approvals and 180-day placement delay revenue past six months; incentive-compensation rules risk.
judges.note: Well-timed policy window with a smart insight that the employer is the payer. Slow, regulated sales, and rivals will pile in.

title: Fees-in-Kind: Harvest Becomes School Fee Credit
one_liner: A weigh-in and ledger service that lets parents pay school fees with maize, beans and potatoes at a transparent price, while schools get cheaper, steadier food supply.
cluster_name: Smallholders and rural households in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Physical grain logistics, spoilage and school tender rules squeeze a thin handling margin.
judges.note: Deeply non-obvious: barter is already the default, valuation and ledger are missing. Timed to the CBC senior-school cohorts, scrappy to pilot.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny early volume against a 4-8% margin; food logistics and tender politics.
judges.note: Genuine local pain and cheap pilot, but working capital, physical handling and thin margins make scaling hard.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin-margin food logistics; school procurement politics and working capital could swamp a small team.
judges.note: Non-obvious: school is the anchor institutional buyer, barter needs fair valuation. Cheap founder-level pilot, expands to receivables finance across Africa.

title: 24/7 named-filer retainer for CRA reporting
one_liner: A follow-the-sun 'fractional PSIRT' that pre-registers, drills and files CRA Article 14 vulnerability reports on the ENISA portal for small connected-device makers.
cluster_name: EU digital product laws for small connected-device makers

judges.fatal_flaw: Few small makers face actual exploited vulnerabilities; retainer looks like uninsured insurance
judges.note: Named awake human as the scarce resource is sharp and Sept 2026 deadline is live; crowded CRA consulting.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pain is latent until an exploited vulnerability; buyers may defer until enforcement bites.
judges.note: Binding deadline, fines, named-human scarcity, reachable hardware makers, recurring retainer; services-led so 10 customers is realistic.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rare incidents make a retainer hard to sell; small ticket, service-heavy margins.
judges.note: Perfect why-now (Sept 11 go-live) and a real named-human gap, but a small, consultant-replicable market.

title: Abandoned Property and Tenant-Death Response Crew
one_liner: A per-event service that handles the legally dangerous moments landlords dread most, such as a tenant who vanishes leaving belongings or a tenant who dies alone, with statutory clocks, next-of-kin outreach and documented disposal.
cluster_name: Landlords in soft markets: vouchers, evictions, vacancies and retention

judges.fatal_flaw: Sporadic events, state-by-state statutes, and field-ops margins limit scale and density.
judges.note: Real dreaded pain, per-event pricing, fragmentation moat; pilot with three PMs feasible, but slow to build density.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rare events per customer and local field ops make scaling beyond a regional service hard.
judges.note: Real, ignored pain with a 50-state playbook moat and easy first customers, but likely a good services business, not venture-scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low event frequency and field-ops economics make density hard to reach.
judges.note: Unglamorous, true insight: landlords fear abandonment and death more than eviction. Fragmented statutes act as the moat.

title: Warm-Backup Servicer for Orphaned Solar
one_liner: Be the standby operations-and-maintenance contractor for lenders and securitization trustees holding portfolios of systems whose installer died.
cluster_name: Residential solar leftovers: orphaned systems, leases and liens

judges.fatal_flaw: Securitization trustees buy slowly; truck-roll margins are thin and ops-heavy.
judges.note: Backup servicing sold to the party holding the balance sheet and pain; strong why-now from installer bankruptcies.

judges.fatal_flaw: Trustees rarely award servicing to unproven startups; truck-roll economics are thin.
judges.note: Credit-protection framing with balance-sheet buyer is sharp; real bankruptcy wave leaves orphaned portfolios. Field roll-up is heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Servicer and trustee sales are slow, and field service needs a technician network.
judges.note: Lenders' payment loss is real and budgeted; per-system retainer plus truck-roll margin works, but a pilot needs a distressed-portfolio owner.

title: O-1 Evidence Vault as a Startup Employee Benefit
one_liner: Continuously captures, verifies and time-stamps the evidence that O-1A, EB-1A and NIW petitions are actually won on, so a lawyer can file in weeks instead of scrambling for six months.
cluster_name: Immigrant households and workers: status deadlines and paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-employee pricing is hard when only a few employees need petitions; lawyers may own the workflow.
judges.note: Rich buyers, forced H-1B shift; continuous evidence capture is a sharp angle, but could be a feature.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded immigration-tech field; lawyers gatekeep distribution and per-employee pricing is unproven.
judges.note: H-1B fee pushes O-1 mainstream; continuous evidence capture is sensible, concierge wedge easy, insight only moderate.

judges.fatal_flaw: Immigration platforms and law firms can bundle evidence collection; employees churn out.
judges.note: H-1B fee makes pain urgent; $300 concierge audits give fast first revenue; the continuous-evidence insight is sharp.

title: Court-Ready Deepfake Authenticity Reports for Lawyers
one_liner: $500-1,500, 48-hour forensic reports on disputed audio, video, screenshots and voicemails, written to survive an authenticity challenge.
cluster_name: Defensible authenticity evidence for disputed digital media

judges.fatal_flaw: Services ceiling; the examiner's testimony liability and detector accuracy limit scale.
judges.note: Productized signature plus chain of custody for solo lawyers is sensible, fast to sell, but small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Detector accuracy and Daubert challenges expose examiners to credibility and liability risk.
judges.note: Lawyers pay $500-1,500 now. Sold through bar associations; productized human signature is the real product. Small but reachable market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small-firm willingness to pay is thin; examiner testimony invites Daubert attacks.
judges.note: Detectors are weak, so the sellable thing is a credentialed signature. Stalled federal rules leave a case-by-case gap.

title: Bulk Records-Request Refinery, Septic-First
one_liner: Build datasets that do not exist by filing thousands of automated public-records requests to county health departments, then reading the scans with vision models and selling address-level reports.
cluster_name: Land and property facts trapped in county records

judges.fatal_flaw: Records take weeks, missing inspection windows; low pay per address
judges.note: Friction-as-moat via bulk records requests plus VLMs is real and compounding; septic wedge is small and slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-address demand and county responsiveness may be too thin to sustain the business.
judges.note: Concierge-first, and each retrieval compounds into a proprietary dataset. Vision models make it newly economic. Generalizes to other missing municipal records.

judges.fatal_flaw: County response times exceed inspection windows; inspectors may balk at paying $39-99 per address.
judges.note: Concierge-first revenue on day one, compounding proprietary dataset, cheap to start. Small per-report ticket, data-license upside unproven.

title: Concession-Adjusted Comps for Appraisers
one_liner: A browser tool that reconstructs what homes really sold for after seller credits and buydowns, so appraisers, lenders and AVMs stop valuing collateral off gross headline prices.
cluster_name: Repricing softening property markets

judges.fatal_flaw: MLS license terms may bar the tool; appraisers are poor buyers and lenders slow.
judges.note: Real 2026 concession shift makes headline prices misleading. Appraisers generate the labeled net-price data. The lender and AVM prize is large.

judges.fatal_flaw: MLS license terms and unreliable remark data could block or undermine the tool
judges.note: Daily appraiser pain, $49/mo tool fits their spending, reachable via state groups, and data asset builds over time.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small appraiser seat market, and MLS license terms limit data reuse.
judges.note: Timely pain with a data flywheel, but $49 seats are tiny and Cotality-type incumbents can copy it.

title: Foreign-Ties Clearance Pack for SBIR Startups
one_liner: A fixed-price, agency-ready foreign-involvement and cyber-readiness dossier priced to fit inside the SBIR technical-assistance allowance, so the startup pays nothing out of pocket.
cluster_name: New defense and drone suppliers: compliance and financing hurdles

judges.fatal_flaw: Agencies may not yet accept vendors for T&BA money, delaying paid packs
judges.note: Earmarked statutory wallet, public lead list, fixed price, urgent new diligence; first 10 sales are straightforward.

judges.fatal_flaw: SBIR awardee population is small; agencies may not list vendors as T&BA-eligible.
judges.note: Earmarked wallet gives price-insensitive buyer, but a few thousand awardees means small ceiling and services-heavy work.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable pool and agencies may not yet accept vendors for the T&BA money.
judges.note: Statute created an earmarked wallet with a price-insensitive buyer. LP look-through is the real hard part. Fast to first sale, but the ceiling is low.

title: Lender-Required Benefit Records for F&I Add-Ons
one_liner: A 20-second, VIN-aware 'did this product actually benefit this buyer' check and signed record that indirect lenders demand as a funding stip, because California's CARS Act (SB 766) bans add-ons that provide no benefit and lenders inherit the exposure.
cluster_name: Consumer lenders' compliance and loss pressures

judges.fatal_flaw: Dealers won't pay unless lenders mandate it; credit union sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: Sharp Oct 1 deadline and clever lender-pays insight, but chicken-and-egg buyer and California-only initial wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders may not mandate it; F&I menu and DMS vendors can bundle rules.
judges.note: Buyer is the lender holding Holder Rule exposure, not the dealer. SB 766 starts Oct 1. Web form ships fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: California-only at first; lenders may not mandate it; DMS vendors could bundle.
judges.note: Perfect why-now (Oct 1 deadline) and clever lender-as-buyer insight, but prize is small unless states copy.

title: Warranty-Linked Installer Certification for African Solar Batteries
one_liner: Battery and inverter brands pay per certified installer and per registered installation, and every certification requires geotagged commissioning proof, which builds an installed-base registry that lenders and insurers cannot otherwise get.
cluster_name: Smallholders and rural households in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs a local presence in Africa; brands may already run installer programs and pay slowly
judges.note: Large, real market and clever registry-as-exhaust model. Founder-market fit and payer speed are the risks.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brands may not pay per install; on-the-ground execution across fragmented African markets.
judges.note: Certification as data exhaust builds a registry official statistics lack; large, fast-growing market; lenders and insurers are the eventual buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Big brands already run installer schemes; African distributor sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: Certification as data-collection exhaust, paid for by the brand's warranty bill, is clever. Registry value compounds to lenders.

title: Payment-Slip Doctor for Foreign Residents
one_liner: A LINE service that lets a foreign resident photograph a Japanese payment slip or government letter and get a plain explanation, deadline, consequences and payment help in their own language.
cluster_name: Immigrant households and workers: status deadlines and paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Japan-only, tiny per-student revenue; municipal payers slow to sign.
judges.note: Proven counter-level demand, visa-linked deadline, school buyer reachable now; ceiling modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Japan-only, thin per-student price, and unproven that schools will pay
judges.note: Founder sees the pain at the counter and the QR-sticker channel is clever. Revenue per pilot is tiny.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin per-student ARPU (¥300) and slow municipal buyers
judges.note: Insider-proven pain at a single document; 2027 visa-renewal rule forces demand; payer is school, not user; testable in 30 days.

title: Co-op Ledger Signals: Farm Distress Early Warning
one_liner: Benchmark co-ops on their own receivables, then sell the anonymized, county-level 'who is paying whom first' data to lenders, insurers and equipment financiers as a leading indicator of farm distress.
cluster_name: Farm and ranch risks: disease, cash, storage and machinery

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-sided data cold start; co-ops slow to share ERP ledger data.
judges.note: Co-op receivables as farm-distress leading indicator is genuinely novel alt-data; long sales cycle but timely.

judges.fatal_flaw: Data revenue needs many co-ops first; conservative managers slow to share ledgers.
judges.note: Clever back-office data insight, but two-sided cold start and multi-quarter path to licensed index revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Co-ops may refuse to share ledger data; slow trust-building delays data-buyer revenue.
judges.note: Boring co-op ERP ledger as leading farm-distress sensor is genuinely non-obvious; benchmark-first wedge builds a pooled data moat.

title: Fake-Citation Triage for Defendants Facing Pro Se Filings
one_liner: A same-day report showing which citations in an opposing pro se filing are fake, misquoted or overruled, formatted as a court-ready exhibit for a motion to strike or for sanctions.
cluster_name: Gatekeepers drowning in AI-generated submissions and bot responses

judges.fatal_flaw: Small filing volume per firm, and Westlaw/Lexis cite-checkers already exist.
judges.note: Counterparty-buyer insight is sharp and buildable in days. Recurring revenue looks thin and incumbents overlap.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small niche; Westlaw, Lexis and court tools can bundle citation checking.
judges.note: Counterparty-as-buyer flip is smart and quick to test, but limited prize and feature-like.

judges.fatal_flaw: Westlaw/Lexis brief analyzers already check opposing briefs; niche buyer pool.
judges.note: Flips buyer to the counterparty paying to verify junk filings. Fast to build, clear 2026 volume shift.

title: Water Towers as Virtual Power Plants
one_liner: Aggregate municipal pump stations and elevated tanks into a controllable flexible load that dodges peak-coincident charges and earns demand-response and capacity payments, with a hard guarantee on pressure and fire reserve and an operator veto.
cluster_name: Utilities avoiding costly network upgrades with distributed flexibility

judges.fatal_flaw: Municipal SCADA access and procurement push first revenue beyond six months.
judges.note: Real peak-charge dollars, shared-savings, sharp 'guarantee with a veto' insight; slow city sales cap early traction.

judges.fatal_flaw: Municipal SCADA and cybersecurity sales cycles; pump-optimization incumbents already exist.
judges.note: Guarantee-with-veto is a smart operator insight and demand charges are real, but sales are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Municipal SCADA access and operator trust make first paid pilots slow.
judges.note: Non-obvious link between capacity prices and pumping load. A veto-plus-guarantee product with shared savings and a clear why-now.

title: CRA Ten-Year Update Vault for Vendors
one_liner: An escrow-plus-hosting service that keeps a small vendor's signed security updates, vulnerability intake and orphaned open-source dependencies alive for the EU Cyber Resilience Act's ten-year obligation if the vendor folds or an upstream dies.
cluster_name: EU digital product laws for small connected-device makers

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers won't trust a startup with ten-year continuity; CRA deadline not yet urgent.
judges.note: Sharp regulatory why-now and a non-obvious escrow angle, but sells fear early, and the vault must itself survive.

judges.fatal_flaw: Demand premature: main duties bite Dec 2027, tiny vendors won't prepay.
judges.note: Software escrow revived by CRA's ten-year duty and MinIO's death; compliance crowd ignores continuity.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small vendors defer spend to 2027; incumbent software-escrow firms can bolt this on.
judges.note: Escrow-plus-continuity angle on CRA is fresh, but demand is unproven and timing to paid customers is slow.

title: Tariff Surcharge Credit-Memo Recovery for Mid-Size Manufacturers
one_liner: Mine a plant's accounts-payable history for 2025-26 tariff surcharges, then win credit memos from the distributors who are now receiving IEEPA refunds.
cluster_name: Recovering IEEPA tariff refunds and surcharges

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak legal claim against non-contractual vendors; crowded tariff-refund field
judges.note: Big pool and diplomatic credit-memo angle, but crowded 2026 refund trade and shaky downstream legal theory.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time windfall, and contract or unjust-enrichment claims against suppliers may be legally weak.
judges.note: Credit-memo negotiation fits how plant managers behave, and recovery is contingency-paid within months. Durability depends on future tariff regimes.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers' legal claim is weak; vendors can refuse; the windfall window closes.
judges.note: Found money, contingency fee, free-scan hook, specific wedge; first credit memos in 60-90 days.

title: Group Apprenticeship Employer for Data-Center Electricians
one_liner: An Australian-style group training organization that employs apprentices and rents them to small electrical and plumbing contractors, absorbing the paperwork, wage risk and poaching risk.
cluster_name: Skilled-trades labor gap

judges.fatal_flaw: Wage and working-capital risk; thin staffing-style margins; apprenticeship registration and compliance complexity.
judges.note: Huge proven overseas model with no US champion. Acute electrician shortage and entry-level collapse make the timing right. Staffing-scale outcome.

judges.fatal_flaw: Payroll float and thin staffing margins, while IEC/ABC chapters already sponsor group programs.
judges.note: Real labor shortage and workable GTO model, but working capital heavy and incumbents own the sponsor role.

judges.fatal_flaw: Wage float and workers' comp capital needed before margins; thin staffing-style 15-20% margin.
judges.note: Australian group-training import splits employer from host; big prize, real data-center demand, 6-month LOI path.

title: Ceremony-as-a-Service for Direct Cremation Providers
one_liner: White-label the memorial gathering that low-cost cremation providers can't deliver, so families buy a $1.5K box of ashes plus a $3.5K send-off.
cluster_name: Families choosing direct cremation with no ritual

judges.fatal_flaw: Price-sensitive direct-cremation buyers may not attach a $3.5K event; coordination is labor-heavy.
judges.note: Unbundling created an unowned high-margin ceremony purchase; white-label via providers is testable manually, and the market is growing.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hand-run event coordination has services margins and weak defensibility.
judges.note: Direct cremation unbundled the ceremony into an unowned purchase. First five events can be run by hand.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low attach rate at cremation providers; each event is manual coordination.
judges.note: Time-bound emotional purchase, 35-45% margin, one-metro test is cheap; scaling means coordination labor.

title: Solar Closing Desk for Listing Agents
one_liner: A per-listing service that clears solar leases, PPAs, loans and UCC-1 fixture filings before the house hits the MLS, so escrow does not blow up in week three.
cluster_name: Residential solar leftovers: orphaned systems, leases and liens

judges.fatal_flaw: Agents pay only once escrow breaks, and provider transfer queues are outside your control.
judges.note: Real, growing resale friction after solar bankruptcies. Manual service can start immediately, but the prize is modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-listing service in a small market; providers or title firms can absorb the workflow.
judges.note: Genuine escrow pain with a concrete process wedge. Prize is small and looks like a service business, not a platform.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-listing volume per agent is small; provider transfer queues are outside your control.
judges.note: Acute deal-killing pain, seller pays from proceeds, manual start, easy reach via agents and title firms.

title: Civil-Document Runners for Immigrant Families
one_liner: A vetted in-country network that retrieves, verifies and delivers birth, marriage, police and court records for consular and NVC cases, with chain-of-custody proof and no forged shortcuts.
cluster_name: Immigrant households and workers: status deadlines and paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Local-partner quality control and fraud risk across countries could cause bad documents and bar liability.
judges.note: Law firms already pay fixers for documents at $150-450 each. Real pain, 40-50% gross margin, and reachable through diaspora networks.

judges.fatal_flaw: Quality control of local runners abroad is hard, and existing apostille and document services compete.
judges.note: Genuine reframe of immigration as logistics. Reliability scorecard could be a moat, but why-now is generic.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin-margin, hard-to-scale manual logistics with fraud-bar liability and policy-dependent family-immigration volumes.
judges.note: Real bottleneck nobody funds; reliability scorecard by registry is a genuine data moat; quick first customers via law firms.

title: Pre-Inspected Wildfire Books From Moratorium Zip Codes
one_liner: Turn California's public nonrenewal-moratorium ZIP lists into a supply of mitigation-verified risks, sold to carriers and MGAs who want good business and to commercial-residential owners who need it.
cluster_name: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: Carrier demand for verified files is unproven; inspections are low-margin labor.
judges.note: Time-boxed public target list and commercial-residential entry are clever; big insurance-crisis prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carrier willingness to pay for pre-inspected files is unproven; inspections are physical labor
judges.note: Time-boxed urgency and a reachable commercial-residential owner list; the carrier-side data sale is hypothetical.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carrier demand for pre-inspected files is unconfirmed; the moratorium may be extended.
judges.note: Public geocoded list with a hard expiry date and reachable commercial-residential buyers. Fast to test, though defensibility is thin.

title: Defensibility Desk for GenAI Document Review
one_liner: An independent validation service that samples, blind-reviews and documents the accuracy of AI-assisted document review so litigators can defend it to opposing counsel and judges.
cluster_name: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Services-heavy, and courts may never require independent validation of LLM review.
judges.note: Auditor-for-AI-work wedge; validation becomes the billable act as review cost collapses; sellable in weeks.

judges.fatal_flaw: Courts accept self-validation under TAR precedent; buyers won't pay for independent audit yet
judges.note: Independent validation becomes the billable act as review cost collapses; good insight but demand unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow law-firm sales and vendors already bundle validation reports.
judges.note: Validation is an established billable act, and $3-5k pilots on closed matters are sellable. No accepted protocol yet.

title: Independent audit desk for city surveillance vendors
one_liner: A fixed-price monthly service that checks whether a city's license-plate-reader and drone vendor is actually following the city's own sharing rules, and hands the council a report it can cite.
cluster_name: City and county governments: thin staff, grants and vendor oversight

judges.fatal_flaw: Small city budgets and slow procurement cap the market; vendor export cooperation uncertain.
judges.note: Sharp ordinance-created demand and evidence, easy first customers, but ceiling is low.

judges.fatal_flaw: Total market is small and depends on vendor log-export cooperation
judges.note: Ordinance-created mandate, priced under the procurement threshold. It is niche but reachable, with urgent councils and named buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny city budgets and vendor log-export cooperation cap deal size and speed.
judges.note: Ordinances create the market, not the vendors; config drift is a simple, verifiable problem; sub-threshold pricing lets pilots close fast.

title: Two-Way Kasuhara Desk for Tiny Japanese Businesses
one_liner: A QR-and-LINE 'complaint lane' plus staff backup button that gives micro-businesses the customer-harassment policy, consultation channel and evidence log Japan now requires.
cluster_name: Workforce compliance for remote, tipped and platform workers

judges.fatal_flaw: Enforcement is soft guidance; free government templates cap willingness to pay at low ARPU.
judges.note: Huge mandated market with reseller channel via sharoushi, but requires Japan-native team and thin ~$20 monthly pricing.

judges.fatal_flaw: Soft enforcement, tiny ARPU; HR SaaS incumbents and free government templates commoditize it.
judges.note: Perfect why-now (law starts Oct 1), sharoushi channel, fast revenue; ceiling limited to Japan SME compliance.

judges.fatal_flaw: Enforcement is soft, so a free template and poster may satisfy owners.
judges.note: Hard 1 Oct 2026 deadline and a sharoushi resale channel. The insight that customers are chilled from complaining is novel. Needs Japan-native execution.

title: Inherited-Rental Stabilization Service for Estate Attorneys
one_liner: A flat-fee 30-day service that stabilizes rental properties the moment an owner dies, sold through probate attorneys and trust officers who fear personal liability.
cluster_name: Houses caught in death, divorce or care transitions

judges.fatal_flaw: Field-services model scales linearly with headcount, local by metro, small ceiling.
judges.note: Attorney-liability wedge is sharp and easy to sell. Essentially a local services business, not a venture-scale one.

judges.fatal_flaw: Local, hands-on service that scales poorly and depends on attorney referral trust.
judges.note: Attorney liability, not price, buys the service; ghost-landlord period is real and sellable; scrappy team can start now.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin per-metro estate volume; attorneys slow to trust an unproven field operator.
judges.note: Attorney-channel flat fee $2.5-6k, urgent liability pain, recurring PM conversion, ten customers reachable via one bar section.

title: Pre-Loss Home Reconstruction Dossiers for Insurance Claims
one_liner: Rebuild, in the exact quality and condition language insurers can't wave away, what a destroyed home actually had, using old appraisals, listing photos, permits and imagery.
cluster_name: Flood and fire survivors: mapping, buyouts, claims and rebuilding

judges.fatal_flaw: Episodic demand and appraiser-labor bottleneck; LA claims mostly resolved soon.
judges.note: Sharp evidence insight and easy pilots, but small, disaster-dependent services business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers may discount appraiser dossiers; demand is concentrated in a few disaster zones.
judges.note: Pre-loss evidence already exists in lender files and MLS. Neutral appraiser vocabulary wins finish-level disputes. Fast paying customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Demand is disaster-event driven, and appraiser-independence and insurer pushback could cap volume.
judges.note: Adjusters have a contingency-fee motive to pay $1-2.5k per dossier now. Concentrated buyers, flat fee, quick to first 10 sales.

title: Error-Rate Cliff Insurance for SNAP Agencies
one_liner: A managed QC service that re-reads a sample of newly approved and recertified SNAP cases against federal review rules and builds federal-dispute packets, sold to county and state agencies facing cost-share penalties.
cluster_name: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: Government sales cycles and PII/security requirements delay first paying counties past six months.
judges.note: Concrete penalty cliff, hard dates, small county purchases. Insurance-style second-look pricing is a sharp wedge with a huge cost-shift budget.

judges.fatal_flaw: Government procurement and PII constraints make first paid pilots slow
judges.note: Cliff-function penalty logic is sharp, with real dated exposure. County-by-county small-purchase entry is clever. Sales cycle is the drag.

judges.fatal_flaw: Government procurement plus PII access needed before any paid revenue.
judges.note: Big penalty-cliff prize, but county sales cycles and PII security review make ten paying customers in six months unlikely.

title: Battery passport starter that feeds on repair-shop events
one_liner: A cheap battery-passport package for e-bike and small pack makers, plus a repair-shop scanning app that supplies the lifecycle events the passport is legally supposed to track.
cluster_name: Recycling quality, distressed capacity and battery/EPR compliance

judges.fatal_flaw: EU deadlines may slip; small e-bike brands pay little; DPP vendors crowd.
judges.note: Repair-shop event stream is the real wedge for the passport lifecycle; hard deadline, but small buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded passport vendors, shifting standards; small brands may wait for pack suppliers.
judges.note: Feb 2027 deadline and underserved small e-bike brands make a paid EUR 2k readiness sprint sellable now.

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak willingness to pay; standards and access rules still slipping; repair shops won't adopt.
judges.note: Repair-shop lifecycle events are the real passport burden, an overlooked angle, but small budgets and compliance-vendor crowding.

title: Large-Load Water Tariff Desk for Utilities
one_liner: An advisory-plus-software desk that gives small water and wastewater utilities the tariffs, effluent valuation and contract terms to negotiate with data centers.
cluster_name: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: Municipal procurement cycles and incumbent rate consultants slow first paid engagements.
judges.note: Urgent deal clock, weak side of the table, big tickets, and a public-data lead magnet. Prize and originality both strong.

judges.fatal_flaw: Municipal procurement is slow and small utilities have thin budgets for $30k+ engagements.
judges.note: Effluent becoming an asset gives the weaker party leverage; fresh angle beyond power; public-data one-pagers are a smart wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cash-poor municipal utilities buy slowly; bespoke consulting with few clients per region.
judges.note: Advising the weaker side on effluent value is non-obvious, but niche, project-based and overlaps the data-center advisory theme.

title: Cash Caregiver Rails: Deductible, Reimbursable, Legal
one_liner: Payroll plus clinician plan-of-care paperwork that turns cash-paid family and neighbor caregivers into tax-deductible, insurance-reimbursable, workers'-comp-covered employment.
cluster_name: Home and residential care: labor supply, family caregivers and small-scale models

judges.fatal_flaw: Employer taxes often outweigh deductions; families avoid formalizing cash care.
judges.note: 'Get reimbursed, not stay legal' is a smart reframe, but household payroll incumbents exist and benefit value is uncertain.

judges.fatal_flaw: Informal aides resist payroll; deduction and LTC-insurer reimbursement value may be far smaller than claimed.
judges.note: Big prize and sharp 'get reimbursed' framing; reachable via elder-law attorneys, but benefits thesis unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tax and insurer acceptance of NP-certified plans is untested; household-employer CAC stays high.
judges.note: Biggest prize here. Reimbursement wedge unlocks money families already lose, and white-label payroll gets first customers fast.

title: Persistent Methane Plumes as Equipment Sales Leads
one_liner: Sell satellite-detected methane emitters to the vendors who profit from fixing them: a lead-gen engine, not a compliance tool.
cluster_name: Novel environmental and infrastructure data from satellites and crowd-sensing

judges.fatal_flaw: Built on open plume data, so easy to copy; emitters may lack capex to act
judges.note: Genuine inversion: sell plumes as sales leads, not violations. Cheap to start, no regulation needed. Weak moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Public plume data is free; buyers need proof leads close; small TAM.
judges.note: Nice inversion (plume as sales lead) but a thin data layer, replicable, and a small vendor universe.

judges.fatal_flaw: Leads may convert poorly because emitters resist fixing and equipment sales cycles are long.
judges.note: Open data, near-zero COGS, lead-gen has measurable ROI, buyers are small vendors with sales pain, and no regulation is needed.

title: Courthouse-Handwriting Graph to Clear Heirs' Property
one_liner: Use AI that can read old handwritten deeds and probate files to map who really owns family land that never went through probate, and sell clean title to the buyers who need it.
cluster_name: Land and property facts trapped in county records

judges.fatal_flaw: Heir outreach and quiet-title are slow, legal-heavy, and risk looking predatory.
judges.note: Handwriting-reading LLMs unlock a compounding county title graph; developers with solar and data-center land needs pay now.

judges.fatal_flaw: Clearing title takes attorneys and months per parcel; revenue only on cleared parcels.
judges.note: Big blocked-asset prize and paying developers, but slow cash conversion and landman incumbents.

judges.fatal_flaw: Multi-heir consent, slow quiet-title, and predatory-acquisition optics
judges.note: Handwriting AI unlocks blocked inventory that energy developers pay to clear; landmen incumbents exist.

title: Pay Farmers to Under-Irrigate, Not Fallow
one_liner: A broker and satellite-verification layer that pays growers of alfalfa, hay and cotton for mid-season deficit irrigation and hands corporate and municipal buyers audited acre-feet.
cluster_name: Water scarcity: irrigation allocation and new supply

judges.fatal_flaw: Water-rights law, district approvals and a few concentrated buyers make first revenue slow.
judges.note: Big prize and good why-now, but a winter contracting cycle and existing Reclamation programs mean no revenue in six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Reclamation and state programs already pay for conservation; ET verification contested.
judges.note: Big water prize, strong timing, audit-trail standard-setting potential, but government programs are entrenched.

judges.fatal_flaw: Water-rights law and slow district contracting push first revenue past six months.
judges.note: Big prize, fresh Colorado River ROD, real insight that consumptive use is what counts. Whoever owns the audit sets the standard.

title: Sole-source price-reasonableness memos from council agenda data
one_liner: A buy-side benchmark built from public council packets showing what other governments pay Tyler, Axon, OpenGov and Flock, sold as the missing price-reasonableness memo for every sole-source renewal.
cluster_name: City and county governments: thin staff, grants and vendor oversight

judges.fatal_flaw: Low purchase frequency; small governments may see no urgency to benchmark.
judges.note: $495 briefs sit under purchasing thresholds, data is public, and sole-source justification is a documented requirement.

judges.fatal_flaw: Governments pay little per brief and buy slowly; GovSpend and co-op contracts already benchmark.
judges.note: Clever data arbitrage from public packets, scrappy start, plausible price-data asset; buyer economics are weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small-government purchasers rarely pay for benchmarks; procurement sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: Price-reasonableness memo is a real gap filled by public data; free leaderboard earns inbound; small buyers limit revenue.

title: Roof Rebuttal Kits for Aerial-Photo Insurance Drops
one_liner: A 48-hour, flat-fee evidence packet and cheap-fix dispatch that lets homeowners beat insurer non-renewals based on aerial imagery instead of paying $20k for an unneeded roof.
cluster_name: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers may ignore rebuttals; low-ticket local service has costly customer acquisition.
judges.note: Evidence-format wedge on real aerial-imagery non-renewals; fast to first revenue, but a modest ticket and a crowded cluster.

judges.fatal_flaw: Local field services with low ceiling; insurers may change imagery practices or share images.
judges.note: Acute consumer pain with a flat-fee, fast first-customer path; agents as second buyer. Scaling is manual.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers may ignore packets; thin per-packet margin depends on local inspector supply.
judges.note: Deadline-driven consumer pain, high-intent search, $299 impulse-level price versus $20k roof, first customers within weeks.

title: Ship-Anywhere Prices for Pickup-Only Auction Lots
one_liner: Embed binding, lot-level delivered prices and a booked load-out window into online auction listings, so pickup-only machinery, estate and surplus lots attract national bidders, with the broker taking a cut of freight and the auctioneer sharing the hammer-price uplift.
cluster_name: Resellers and liquidators of surplus and fandom goods

judges.fatal_flaw: Freight brokerage margins are thin and auction platforms could build or bundle it.
judges.note: Real insight that bidder radius drives hammer price, and the single-forklift load-out constraint is unmodeled. Concierge-testable in 30 days.

judges.fatal_flaw: Existing estimators and thin freight margins; auctioneers may not integrate or trust binding quotes.
judges.note: Bidder radius, not freight cost, is the insight. Very feasible concierge start, unsexy, weak why-now, moderate defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Binding quotes on unseen heavy lots risk margin loss; little defensibility beyond operations.
judges.note: Concierge test is measurable, freight margin pays from day one, bidder-radius insight is real; needs only auctioneer buy-in.

title: Fish Settlement Audit Becoming the Fleet's Payment Rail
one_liner: Start by auditing settlement sheets against fish tickets to recover missed money, then become the split-pay rail that routes each settlement to crew, lessors, lenders and the IRS.
cluster_name: Fisheries and ecosystem-service operators

judges.fatal_flaw: Fishing settlement flow is small, so the rail ceiling is low.
judges.note: Great wedge: audit recovers money, feeds underwriting data. Fast to first customers, but niche market caps the outcome.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable fleet, and the payment-rail vision needs money-transmitter licensing.
judges.note: Highly non-obvious customer. Audit wedge earns money now during settlement season; settlement history becomes underwriting data. Small prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Audit recoveries are small per skipper; the payment rail needs licensing.
judges.note: Free-audit hook fits fishermen's Facebook groups and the settlement season is live. The audit fee pool is tiny and the rail is heavy.

title: Payroll and Tax-Prep Rails for Scholarship Credit
one_liner: Embeddable 'route my credit' flows in payroll, CPA and banking tools that turn the federal scholarship tax credit into a mass-market donation default.
cluster_name: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Treasury rules unresolved; payroll giants may build the routing default themselves.
judges.note: Legislated $25-50B annual flow with a dated Q4 2026 default-setting window; take rate on giving is venture-scale and non-consensus.

judges.fatal_flaw: Treasury rules are unresolved, so payroll partners will not integrate before 2027.
judges.note: Big potential flow and good timing, but a middleware take rate depends on partners and rules outside your control.

judges.fatal_flaw: Depends on unfinished Treasury rules, politicized program, and slow payroll-partner integration.
judges.note: Largest prize and sharpest why-now: a $25-50B credit starting Jan 2027 that most people haven't noticed, won by owning the default.

title: Notary-Witnessed Hiring Against Deepfake Candidates
one_liner: On-demand licensed notaries sit beside a remote candidate for the final interview or day-one onboarding and sign an attestation.
cluster_name: Verifying real human skill, identity and authorship in hiring and education

judges.fatal_flaw: Candidate and employer friction; notaries cannot clearly attest outside notarial acts.
judges.note: Clever physical defence to deepfake hiring, but low frequency and unproven willingness to pay per session.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin volume; employers can just require in-person interviews or use existing proctoring services.
judges.note: Physics beats deepfakes is contrarian and timely; huge latent notary supply; but small, easily copied niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employers can simply mandate in-person onboarding; Snapdocs-style networks could copy it.
judges.note: Contrarian 'physics beats software' answer to deepfakes. Could grow into a human-presence attestation layer; fast to pilot.

title: Broker Spread Reveal: Two-Sided Freight Ledger
one_liner: Match what shippers paid brokers against what carriers were actually paid, so every broker's true margin by lane becomes visible for the first time.
cluster_name: Freight brokers, carriers and shippers: fraud, liability and disputes

judges.fatal_flaw: Pairing loads to ratecons needs two-sided data the crowd cannot supply early.
judges.note: Drivers hold the hidden half of the ledger; a clever two-sided data insight. Cold start and DAT/Greenscreens benchmarks weaken it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowd ratecons rarely overlap a given shipper's loads; cold-start data liquidity, slow shipper sales.
judges.note: Big prize and real insight on hidden broker spread, but two-sided data cold start weakens first-10-customer path.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cold-start matching of driver ratecons to shipper invoices; broker NDAs and retaliation.
judges.note: Two-sided ledger nobody holds; shippers pay, drivers supply free data. Real data moat in a giant market.

title: One-Filing Shield for At-Risk Public Servants
one_liner: A single intake that files every county office's address-confidentiality forms, fixes what gets recorded next, and monitors leaks for judges, election officials and clinicians.
cluster_name: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Public risk pools buy slowly; attorney network raises unauthorized-practice and fulfilment complexity.
judges.note: Urgent, emotional pain with clerk-association access and per-person pricing. Concierge start is feasible; scaling is fragmented.

judges.fatal_flaw: State-by-state concierge ops plus slow public-sector pool procurement stretch the first 6 months.
judges.note: Redaction is a display mask; fix what gets recorded. Post-2025 doxxing shift, insurers as payers, county-first-mile nobody works.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low ARPU, concierge-heavy delivery, and a small buyer universe outside insurance pools.
judges.note: The insight that redaction is a display mask is sharp, and pools and associations give a real B2B channel. The prize is limited.

title: Incretin-in-a-Drop Assay for Life Underwriting
one_liner: A dried-blood-spot or oral-fluid lab test that tells insurers whether an applicant is actually on semaglutide, tirzepatide, orforglipron or retatrutide.
cluster_name: Access, affordability and supply integrity for GLP-1 and compounded drugs

judges.fatal_flaw: Incumbent underwriting labs can copy the assay; insurer adoption and unfair-discrimination rules slow the first sale.
judges.note: Cash-pay GLP-1s bypass Rx plumbing; direct measurement beats questionnaires. Non-obvious, real 2026 shift, cheap add-on, pilot-able.

judges.fatal_flaw: Incumbent paramedical labs can add this assay; it is a feature, not a company.
judges.note: Sharp GLP-1 blind spot in underwriting data and clear buyer pain. Fast pilot, but defensibility and adoption by insurers are thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurer procurement takes 12+ months; ExamOne-type lab networks can copy the assay.
judges.note: Original wedge and clear underwriting value at $35 per test. Assay validation and slow carriers delay first revenue.

title: One Annual Fee for Every Mandatory EU Representative
one_liner: A roll-up of small EU authorised-representative shops that bundles every legally required local presence (GDPR Art. 27, AI Act, Data Act, product safety, CRA) into one liability-bearing annual contract for non-EU companies.
cluster_name: Exporters meeting foreign sustainability and representation rules

judges.fatal_flaw: Demand rests on weakly enforced EU rules; acquisitions need capital and carry liability.
judges.note: Boring, sticky, liability-bearing recurring revenue with many EU regimes converging; pricing power and regulator-address moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Roll-up needs acquisition capital; liability is hard to insure and margins on reps are thin
judges.note: Liability-bearing local presence is the scarce good; real 2026 regimes; capital-heavy execution.

judges.fatal_flaw: Roll-up needs acquisition capital and liability insurance before meaningful revenue.
judges.note: Real mandatory demand, sticky renewals; the reseller-bundle version is feasible, the acquisition plan is not bootstrappable.

title: Funeral Committee Escrow and Fixed-Price Vendor Network
one_liner: A per-funeral M-Pesa vault where contributions can only be released to pre-priced vendors with two-of-three committee approvals, ending the 'where did the burial money go' fights.
cluster_name: Informal finance and payment frictions in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: One-off event per customer; M-Changa incumbency; payment-provider licensing dependence.
judges.note: Real cultural pain and spend-side control is novel, but per-funeral revenue is small and repeat use is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: M-Changa-style incumbents and payment licensing; ops-heavy per-funeral service with thin fees.
judges.note: Original insight: locked money protects treasurers, so it sells social protection. Scrappy first customers via churches; extends to funeral cover.

judges.fatal_flaw: Payments licensing and trust; M-Changa incumbency; vendor network liquidity in rural Kenya.
judges.note: Locked money as protection from the 'sharing tax' is a sharp insight. Huge informal market, hard execution.

title: Church-Basement Microschools for Retired Teachers
one_liner: A turnkey venue, insurance, fire-code and ESA-billing kit that lets a retired teacher open an 8-15 student paid school in a congregation's empty weekday classrooms.
cluster_name: Microschools, homeschoolers and shrinking districts

judges.fatal_flaw: Prenda-style microschool platforms and ESA vendors could add occupancy and insurance kits.
judges.note: ESA money now flowing; occupancy and insurance, not curriculum, is the real bottleneck; church-space wedge is sharp.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-school revenue is small, and many microschool-support outfits already exist.
judges.note: Asset-light, specific customer (retired teachers), ESA money is live; sharper and cheaper to start than the master-lease version.

judges.fatal_flaw: Permits, zoning and ESA vendor approval vary by state, and microschool players already use churches.
judges.note: Large ESA-funded prize. Retired-teacher pension angle and church space is a clever moat, but defensibility is weak and it is state-by-state grind.

title: Amnesty Desk: Legalizing Unpermitted Backyard Units
one_liner: Fixed-fee 'legalize your existing unit' service that is paid at closing, turning unpermitted ADUs and garage conversions into appraisable, financeable, insurable square footage.
cluster_name: Small builders' crew coordination, permits and speed

judges.fatal_flaw: Each city processes amnesty differently, so delivery depends on licensed local partners.
judges.note: Homeowners see $80-150K unlock; reachable via listing agents; fixed-fee cash in weeks; city-by-city know-how compounds.

judges.fatal_flaw: City-by-city permit delays make it a services business with unpredictable cycle times.
judges.note: Real value unlock and a city-behavior database as a moat, but California-centric and operationally heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Owners fear reassessment and enforcement; existing ADU consultancies compete
judges.note: AB 2533 opens a real backlog; city-by-city procedural knowledge and paid-at-escrow model are practical and fundable.

title: Dock Tax: Pricing Every Shipper Facility's Hidden Premium
one_liner: Use pooled broker quote and cover data to compute the exact per-load premium carriers add to any lane touching each bad dock, then sell shippers a ranked 'fix these five docks' report with dollar savings attached.
cluster_name: Freight brokers, carriers and shippers: fraud, liability and disputes

judges.fatal_flaw: Brokers reluctant to pool quote data; facility effects hard to isolate; shippers already own dwell data.
judges.note: Prices a hidden cost the payer never sees; neutral third party, ROI-led sales, credible consulting-to-data flywheel.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brokers profit from opacity and may refuse to pool the quote data.
judges.note: Hidden facility premium is invisible to the payer and priced by nobody. Clear ROI, timely driver-supply tightening.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pooled broker data is hard to get, since brokers profit from the hidden premium.
judges.note: Sharp non-obvious insight and shippers can pay $7.5-40K, but data cold-start and attribution noise undermine the report.

title: Executive Physicals for Union Trades Members
one_liner: Mobile 'Physical Days' at union halls and apprenticeship centers that give tradespeople the CEO-style cardiometabolic checkup, sold to the multiemployer health funds that pay their claims.
cluster_name: Preventive and longevity care outside conventional insurance

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow trustee sales cycles; clinical liability and operational complexity of mobile circuits.
judges.note: Multiemployer funds are the rare long-horizon payer for prevention; unusual customer and strong relationship moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow trustee sales cycles, thin evidence executive physicals reduce claims, heavy clinical operations.
judges.note: Union funds are the payer with a long time horizon; real distribution insight but ops-heavy services.

judges.fatal_flaw: Biometric screening is commoditized; thin margin at $150-250 per head and slow trustee decisions.
judges.note: Pooled long-horizon payer is genuinely well-matched; concrete pilot, but incumbents and ROI proof drag closing.

title: Dialysis Chair-Fill Rides Paid Per Completed Treatment
one_liner: A dedicated, route-based ride service for dialysis patients (same driver, same van loop, three times a week) priced per treatment completed instead of per trip, sold to the clinics and risk-bearing kidney-care companies that lose money on every missed session.
cluster_name: Rural and underserved patients who cannot reach care

judges.fatal_flaw: Ride operations are thin-margin and insurance heavy; clinic anti-kickback concerns.
judges.note: Sharp insight (chair as perishable inventory), outcome-based pricing, cheap subcontracted pilot; margins and ops are the risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: Ops-heavy, low-margin paratransit with Anti-Kickback constraints; large chains may resist outsourcing.
judges.note: Priced on completed treatment against a $280 chair-day; risk-bearing buyers exist and ModivCare's collapse opens contracts.

judges.fatal_flaw: Anti-Kickback constraints and thin-margin fleet operations before payers pay for outcomes.
judges.note: Chair-as-perishable-inventory framing is sharp; ModivCare exit helps; but capital-heavy operations and regulatory friction.

title: Closing-Time Recovery for Shutting Small Businesses
one_liner: A contingency-fee agent that finds and collects the money owners forget when they close: tariff refunds, overpaid taxes, insurance returns, deposits and vendor credits.
cluster_name: Unclaimed money: settlements, refunds, penalties and unpaid invoices

judges.fatal_flaw: Only importer-of-record closings hold refunds; slow cash conversion and refund-claim competition.
judges.note: Urgent, rolling deadlines, no-risk contingency for exhausted owners, high ticket per client; letters to bankruptcy filings reach 10 clients fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: In Chapter 7 the claims belong to the trustee, not the owner.
judges.note: Forgotten claims at closing is a fresh funnel, but legal ownership, lead sourcing and broad scope blur it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tariff-refund window is time-limited and already swarmed by brokers and law firms.
judges.note: Fast contingency revenue and real windfall now; wind-down funnel broadens, but venture-scale ceiling and one-time nature limit it.

title: Genki Tap: Konbini Clerks as Paid Elder Watchers
one_liner: Pay convenience-store staff to log a three-second 'seen and how they seemed' note on enrolled elderly regulars, and alert family and local support centers when someone goes quiet or drifts.
cluster_name: Adult children managing aging parents from afar

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs franchise HQ consent and privacy trust; low-ARPU consumer subscription
judges.note: Founder owns stores, unusual paid-attention insight, quick 50-family pilot; thin unit economics and scaling through franchisors.

judges.fatal_flaw: Convenience-chain HQ and privacy norms may block clerk participation; low ARPU.
judges.note: Genuinely unusual insight: pay trusted humans for attention. Founder owns stores, so first customers are quick. Japan-only ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Franchisor rules, clerk turnover and privacy consent could block store-level rollout.
judges.note: Senior-care category, but paying konbini clerks turns unpaid goodwill into data. Founder owns stores, so the pilot is fast.

title: Pay-Per-Decibel Neighbor Trust for Data Centers
one_liner: An independent trust that owns a sensor mesh around a data center and automatically pays nearby households every time the hum exceeds agreed limits, turning 'trust us' into a self-executing contract.
cluster_name: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: Developers unlikely to accept open-ended self-executing payouts; long, political sales cycle.
judges.note: Timely and inventive trust structure; hyperscalers have budget, but the buyer's incentive to self-penalize is doubtful.

judges.fatal_flaw: Developers unlikely to fund self-executing payouts; hyperscaler sales cycles long.
judges.note: Clever and paid baseline entry point, but buyer's willingness to bind itself to payouts is doubtful.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hyperscalers may balk at automatic payout liability, and enterprise sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: Turns unpriced harm into a self-executing contract. Fits the failed lump-sum offers. Novel, large ticket, but a heavy sale.

title: File-Cabinet-to-Pipeline Digitization Crew
one_liner: A mobile scan-and-extract crew that turns a newly acquired trades company's filing cabinets and paper job files into a clean customer and equipment-age database plus a ready-to-run replacement and membership campaign.
cluster_name: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: Project-based services with a tiny buyer pool; revenue-share attribution is messy.
judges.note: Sharp insight that archives are a lead list; fast paying customers but low scalability and weak moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Narrow buyer pool (search funders); services model with limited scale
judges.note: Unusual wedge: paper archive as a proprietary equipment-age lead list. Evidence-backed and fast to first revenue. Modest ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few acquirers per year, one-off engagements, and scanning is commoditized.
judges.note: Services revenue from day one, with the archive-as-lead-list insight. Buyer pool is small and shares depend on campaigns.

title: Special-Tool Exchange for Retiring Regional Fleets
one_liner: Buy or take on consignment the OEM special tooling stranded when regionals retire 50-seat jets and older turboprops, calibrate it, and rent or sell it to operators who cannot get it from the OEM for months.
cluster_name: Aircraft and drone operators: maintenance, parts, permits and navigation

judges.fatal_flaw: Small niche; brokers and OEM channels may already move tooling informally.
judges.note: Near-free inventory, urgent demand, no cash outlay to start. Unusual and feasible, but ceiling is limited unless it widens to all aviation GSE.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small niche needing aviation insiders; OEM tooling IP and airworthiness liability unclear.
judges.note: Near-free inventory, urgent grounded-aircraft demand, rental margin; first rentals could close fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: Niche is small, and calibration liability and OEM control of tooling could block resale.
judges.note: Near-free inventory with urgent demand from regional-fleet retirements; genuinely unusual, but a modest prize.

title: Certified Raw Milk: Testing, Herdshares, Insurance
one_liner: The neutral assurance layer for the gray-legal raw milk market: weekly pathogen and H5N1 testing, herdshare paperwork, and the first insurable 'tested farm' program.
cluster_name: Food and beverage producers facing new rules and safety risks

judges.fatal_flaw: Farms are cash-poor and lab costs eat margin; legally gray customers.
judges.note: Reachable via farmer associations, clear trust and insurability gap. Small farms will pay little; insurance layer is distant.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny farm base and political or regulatory hostility cap the market.
judges.note: Certifier-plus-insurance-data moat is original and testable in 30 days, but the ceiling is low.

judges.fatal_flaw: Farms avoid publishing failures; a positive H5N1 test triggers regulatory shutdown.
judges.note: Contrarian certifier-as-UL bet on a gray market with real MAHA-era momentum, but the customer is hostile to disclosure.

title: Canary Humans: Leak-Testing ID Verification Vendors
one_liner: Put consenting, instrumented real people through a platform's ID and age checks, then prove whether the vendor kept, leaked or resold their documents.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Leaks are rare and hard to detect, so clean attestations prove little; vendors may block testing.
judges.note: Honeytokens applied to ID verifiers is genuinely new and well-timed, but enterprise sale and unprovable negatives are hard.

judges.fatal_flaw: Long enterprise security sales cycles and legal risk of enrolling real IDs with vendors
judges.note: Novel honeytoken insight, urgent after breaches. Hard to close 10 payers in six months, though.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small buyer pool, and vendors or their legal teams may block consented canary testing.
judges.note: Honeytokens applied to ID vendors is genuinely novel. The breach-driven why-now is sharp, and outcome-based attestation beats paper compliance.

title: Supplier-Funded Books for Trade-Credit Customers
one_liner: Regional distributors pay to give each micro-customer done-for-you books, and get a permissioned live view of that customer's credit risk.
cluster_name: Restaurants' idle hours, used oil and credit risk

judges.fatal_flaw: Micro-customers may not connect bank feeds; books may add little over the distributor's own payment history.
judges.note: Smart buyer inversion: the receivable holder pays for the customer's books. Large trade-credit pool and a testable pilot.

judges.fatal_flaw: Done-for-you books at $10-25 per account may not hold margin; distributor sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: Payer-of-the-receivable insight is real; backtest on 100 accounts is a cheap proof.

judges.fatal_flaw: Micro-owners may not connect bank feeds or engage, so risk signals stay weak.
judges.note: Party carrying the receivable pays for bookkeeping; inverted buyer is clever, and backtest on invoice history is cheap.

title: Duty Refund Claims Desk for Small Importers
one_liner: Over $100B in tariff refunds are flowing, but small importers can't afford the paperwork. Run the filing, deadline tracking and refund advance as a service.
cluster_name: Recovering IEEPA tariff refunds and surcharges

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded gold rush with brokers and law firms; advance financing needs capital
judges.note: Contingency fee on real owed cash, urgent, deadline-driven. Easy first 10 closes; window is time-limited.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded with brokers, law firms and claim buyers; window is transient.
judges.note: Huge near-term dollars and advance-financing upside, but obvious from headlines and finite in duration.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded with law firms, brokers and claim buyers; the window closes as refunds flow.
judges.note: Big, dated, fast cash and easy first customers. But it is the obvious news-driven play with weak defensibility.

title: Diaspora-Financed Home Batteries for Family Back Home
one_liner: Sell home battery and solar systems to migrants in the US, UK, Canada and EU as a monthly subscription that keeps the lights on for their relatives, underwritten on the sender's credit rather than the recipient's.
cluster_name: Smallholders and rural households in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Cross-border install, service and default recourse can wreck unit economics.
judges.note: Underwrites the diaspora sender, not the recipient. Huge TAM, sharp credit insight, testable with deposits fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cross-border collections and hardware repossession make this capital-heavy lending with high default risk.
judges.note: Underwriting the sender rather than the recipient is a real inversion. Huge remittance market, but heavy working-capital needs.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hardware and financing working capital across borders, plus default and warranty logistics, need heavy capital.
judges.note: Credit-on-the-sender is a clever wedge and deposits prove demand. Capital-hungry, with installation and service risk abroad.

title: Biotech Graveyard Data Exchange
one_liner: Rescue, clean and license the wet-lab data of shutting-down biotechs, especially the failed and negative results that AI drug-discovery models are starved of, and split the proceeds with the estate.
cluster_name: Biotech capital: diligence and salvage

judges.fatal_flaw: Encumbered rights and unproven buyer willingness to pay for negative-result data.
judges.note: Counterintuitive: dead companies' failed data is the scarce asset. Wind-down wave is real, and the trust moat is human.

judges.fatal_flaw: Each dataset is a bespoke rights-clearing project with uncertain buyer willingness to pay.
judges.note: Sharp negative-data insight and motivated sellers, but slow, lumpy revenue and few buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Heterogeneous, rights-encumbered legacy assay data may be unsellable at meaningful prices.
judges.note: Contrarian scarce-data thesis with trust-at-death-moment moat; but buyer willingness to pay and IP clearance are unproven.

title: Contingency Water-Bill Recovery for Small Commercial Sites
one_liner: A no-win-no-fee service that rebuilds small commercial sites' water, sewer and stormwater bills from the local tariff and claws back irrigation-sewer overcharges, leak credits and stormwater-fee errors.
cluster_name: Unclaimed money: settlements, refunds, penalties and unpaid invoices

judges.fatal_flaw: Small tickets, unproven overcharge prevalence, thin defensibility versus utility-audit firms.
judges.note: Contingency model fits an underserved segment and gets fast first revenue, but the prize is modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-site contingency fees are small against heavy analyst labor and slow cash.
judges.note: Zero-risk contingency offer closes easily and the audit category is proven. Economics hinge on LLM cutting analyst time.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-site recoveries are tiny and tariff variance across utilities wrecks analyst unit economics.
judges.note: Contingency audit for too-small-for-auditors accounts is quick to test; LLM tariff reading is real, moat is modest.

title: SNAP-Ready Kits for Corner Stores
one_liner: A UPC-level 'variety counter' plus a pre-built wholesale fill kit that tells a convenience store exactly what to stock to keep SNAP authorization under USDA's new staple-food rule.
cluster_name: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: Marginal store owners may drop SNAP rather than pay $79 for compliance.
judges.note: Hard USDA Nov 4 deadline and wholesaler channel are sharp; wallet is thin and enforcement is rolling.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time regulatory wave, tiny ARPU; many stores will simply drop SNAP.
judges.note: Hard deadline five weeks out gives instant customers via wholesalers, but small prize and fading demand.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low ACV; owners may simply drop SNAP, and enforcement only bites at reauthorization.
judges.note: Hard rule deadline in five weeks and wholesaler case-sales channel; small ticket but reachable and concrete.

title: Recurring-Gift Migration Concierge for Churches
one_liner: A fixed-fee service that moves a church's recurring donors off an expensive or hostile giving platform without losing them.
cluster_name: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: Small ticket per church; incumbents must release card data and can stall transfers.
judges.note: Donor-migration fear is the real lock-in; concierge wedge is plausible and cheap, but niche and low ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rival giving platforms offer free migration to win churches, undercutting the fee
judges.note: Concrete pain, easy reach via church-admin groups, Q4 timing; but small one-time fees and thin defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time small-ticket migration fees; incumbents can slow-walk card-data release.
judges.note: Real lock-in pain and denominational word of mouth; only big if it becomes the cheaper processor.

title: Spray-Drone Service Depots for Grounded Fleets
one_liner: Independent repair, parts and loaner service for the roughly 80% of US spray drones that are DJI Agras.
cluster_name: Aircraft and drone operators: maintenance, parts, permits and navigation

judges.fatal_flaw: DJI parts and firmware support may be cut off or restricted
judges.note: FCC Covered List freezes new models while the installed base keeps flying. Fast first revenue, but modest ceiling and low defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: DJI parts and firmware supply can be cut off under the Covered List.
judges.note: Real installed base and demand, but a regional repair-shop business with supplier dependency and no software leverage.

judges.fatal_flaw: Parts supply depends on DJI or gray channels amid customs and FCC uncertainty.
judges.note: Installed fleet must fly; off-season is when maintenance contracts sell; recurring revenue; existing dealers thin.

title: Coolant Assay Lab for Liquid-Cooled GPU Racks
one_liner: Oil analysis for GPU clusters: mail-in and inline coolant testing that catches corrosion and biofilm before they kill racks, and produces the neutral evidence for warranty fights.
cluster_name: Data center build quality, commissioning and waste-heat reuse

judges.fatal_flaw: Coolant and CDU vendors can bundle free testing; lab margins and market size are modest.
judges.note: Oil-analysis analogy is sharp and first customers are easy. Longitudinal data is a moat only if you get there first.

judges.fatal_flaw: Coolant and CDU vendors bundle fluid testing; few early buyers.
judges.note: Oil-analysis analogy for liquid-cooled racks is sharp and physical. Neutral evidence for warranty fights, but the buyer pool is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: OEMs and water-treatment incumbents like Ecolab will bundle coolant testing.
judges.note: Real failure risk and low-capex partner-lab model. Small per-loop tickets and OEM-mandated test channels limit wins.

title: Boundary Truth: Ledger of Special-District Lines
one_liner: Turn recorded annexation, inclusion and exclusion instruments into a single authoritative boundary ledger that catches wrong tax bills, wrong ballots and wrong 911 routing.
cluster_name: Land and property facts trapped in county records

judges.fatal_flaw: Government sales cycles and per-county bespoke work; hard to reach 10 counties in six months
judges.note: Clever recorder-fund budget angle and real boundary errors, but custom audits per county and slow buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow, fragmented county govtech sales and low ACV unless the boundary layer becomes a standard
judges.note: Sharp insight that the recorded instrument is the truth; the recorder's tech-fund budget path is smart and LLMs are newly capable.

judges.fatal_flaw: County sales cycles, and LLM-drawn polygons still need human surveyor-grade review.
judges.note: The recorded instrument is the legal boundary, not the GIS layer. LLMs now parse legal descriptions. The clerk tech-fund route sidesteps the usual govtech sales trap.

title: Defense Magnet and Tungsten Provenance Dossiers
one_liner: A shared investigator that produces audit-ready provenance files on magnets and tungsten parts for the sub-tier suppliers who cannot get answers from their distributors.
cluster_name: Critical minerals and rare-earth supply chain recovery and provenance

judges.fatal_flaw: Services-heavy and deadline-driven; primes or distributors may absorb the demand.
judges.note: Hard DFARS January 2027 deadline forces sub-tier buyers; pooled fingerprint library is plausible but the business is consultancy-shaped.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consulting-style service; small suppliers may switch sources instead of paying for provenance.
judges.note: Hard January 2027 deadline gives near-term buyers. Shared fingerprint library helps, but it is a service business with limited scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Distributors can't disclose provenance, so dossiers may only document non-compliance.
judges.note: January 2027 DFARS deadline is urgent and budgeted; reachable sub-tier suppliers; deliverable is fuzzy and lab fingerprinting unproven.

title: Predict Walk-In Cooler Failures Via Refrigeration Techs
one_liner: White-label predictive monitoring that local commercial-refrigeration companies sell as a maintenance plan, so a failing compressor becomes a Tuesday service visit rather than a Saturday-night emergency.
cluster_name: Condition monitoring for asset owners and their service contractors

judges.fatal_flaw: Hardware logistics, low ARPU per compressor, and monitoring incumbents already sold through contractors
judges.note: Selling through the local refrigeration tech is a smart channel and amp draw is an early signal, but it is small and crowded.

judges.fatal_flaw: Failures are rare, so proving predictive value takes long; hardware fulfillment burdens tiny team.
judges.note: Sell-to-the-refrigeration-tech channel is sharp; recurring per-compressor revenue; operator has test sites and immediate design partners.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hardware pilots slow; Emerson/Copeland-type monitoring incumbents and cheap temp sensors
judges.note: Sell to the refrigeration tech, not the owner; amp-draw beats temperature probes. Founder has real test sites.

title: Verified Colony-Strength Ledger for Commercial Beekeepers
one_liner: Third-party hive-strength verification and escrowed pollination contracts, turning bees into a gradeable, financeable commodity after record die-offs.
cluster_name: Farm and ranch risks: disease, cash, storage and machinery

judges.fatal_flaw: Niche market; beekeepers and brokers may resist third-party grading transparency.
judges.note: Record die-offs, trust-based grading, Feb 2027 almond bloom forces a real pilot window; verifier-becomes-exchange thesis.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market; growers and beekeepers may not pay for verification.
judges.note: Good verifier-becomes-exchange insight, but the pollination market is a few hundred million dollars. Seasonal timing helps the pilot.

judges.fatal_flaw: Beekeepers resist verification that exposes weak hives; inspectors and brokers already exist.
judges.note: Hard almond-bloom deadline forces buying this winter; $4-8/hive is simple to price; seasonal window is tight.
