title: Court-Safe Esper Machine From Bystander Video
one_liner: Blade Runner's Esper machine, made honest: a scaled, non-generative 3D reconstruction of an accident scene from mixed dashcam, doorbell, CCTV and phone clips, with error bars built to survive an admissibility challenge.
cluster_name: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: One Daubert exclusion in an early case could destroy credibility.
judges.note: Admissibility over photorealism is the right insight. PI firms buy fast, ~$1-2K per case, and error-barred metric scale is defensible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Metric multi-clip reconstruction is hard; unproven admissibility; dependent on a signing expert.
judges.note: Right insight that admissibility is the product, but heavy R&D and Daubert risk before reliable revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Novel method may fail Daubert scrutiny; rests on one reconstructionist's credibility.
judges.note: Admissibility over photorealism is the right inversion of splat hype; PI firms have budgets and cases; fast paid pilots.

title: Tamper-Proof Photo Evidence for Produce Rejections
one_liner: A capture-only app that produces AI-proof receiving-dock photo and video evidence so shippers can contest bogus load rejections and reroute rejected produce to salvage buyers within hours.
cluster_name: Defensible authenticity evidence for disputed digital media

judges.fatal_flaw: Receivers control the dock, and USDA inspection already settles disputes; small load-fee TAM.
judges.note: Sharp wedge on shipper and factor; trusted photo equals money, but the market is narrow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Receivers control the rejection and may refuse to use the shipper's capture app.
judges.note: Fabricable photos are a price-negotiation weapon in produce. Factors and shippers are a plausible wedge, but the market is niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs receiver-side capture at the dock, and receivers have no incentive to comply.
judges.note: Real price-dispute weapon and a sharp shipper/factor wedge; cheap to build and pilot, but adoption needs both parties.

title: AV-TEST for Deepfake and Liveness Detectors
one_liner: A buyer-funded independent lab that red-teams deepfake and liveness detectors every month against fresh in-the-wild fakes and publishes procurement-grade scorecards.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow bank procurement and the credibility burden of a new lab.
judges.note: Sells the referee, not another detector. Accuracy decay makes continuous scorecards recurring, and the fresh attack corpus is a real moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Independent-lab trust takes years to build; buyer pool and revenue ceiling are small.
judges.note: Buyers have no independent evidence and accuracy decays, so monthly retesting is recurring. Testing labs rarely become venture-scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow bank buying, vendor cooperation, credibility of independence; existing liveness test labs.
judges.note: Model-risk teams have real validation budgets, but a new lab needs reputation before anyone pays $10K.

title: Vendor-neutral body-cam redaction bureau with fee pass-through
one_liner: A CJIS-cleared remote team that returns double-reviewed redacted police video priced per minute below the fee small cities already charge requesters, so the bureau funds itself.
cluster_name: Rural sheriffs, jails and small police agencies

judges.fatal_flaw: Small agency budgets and Axon bundling squeeze a labor-heavy, low-margin service bureau.
judges.note: Concrete pain and pass-through pricing, fast to first jobs, but human-review services cap scale and defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: At $0.45/min, double human review likely loses money.
judges.note: Urgent, budgeted pain with fee pass-through and a CJIS moat. Slow procurement, but a services-first start works.

judges.fatal_flaw: Double human review at $0.45/min barely pencils; Axon bundling; slow government procurement.
judges.note: Fee pass-through model funds itself and second review is the real bottleneck. Grounded in council-adopted fee schedules.

title: Crash-Test Ratings for Collusive Pricing Agents
one_liner: A simulation lab and clean-room negotiation venue that certifies your pricing or negotiating agent does not tacitly collude with counterpart agents, like Euro NCAP for antitrust.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers; credibility needs economists and antitrust lawyers before any sale.
judges.note: Legal urgency is real, but AI-audit pattern, small buyer pool and long trust-building sales cycle.

judges.fatal_flaw: Counsel may avoid creating discoverable audit records that could later be used against clients.
judges.note: Counterfactual-behavior tests as antitrust unit tests. Enforcement is live and the first buyers are vendors already sued.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers may fear creating discoverable evidence of collusion; privilege structure is untested.
judges.note: Live antitrust shift (AB 325, DOJ). Counterfactual-behavior testing is a sharp insight. Pre-litigation vendors are reachable, urgent buyers.

title: Pay-Per-Win Appeals Desk for Nursing Homes
one_liner: A 24/7 appeal desk that turns every Medicare Advantage post-acute denial and coverage-termination notice into a filed appeal, paid only when the plan reverses.
cluster_name: Provider revenue leaks and payer denials

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded denial-appeal automation; plans may counter-automate and cut overturn rates.
judges.note: Contingency pricing on a 95% overturn, under-worked receivable gives fast proof and a big prize. Category is crowded.

judges.fatal_flaw: Contingency cash arrives slowly; PointClickCare integration and 24/7 desk strain a small team
judges.note: Huge unworked receivable, 95% overturn, no-risk pricing; reachable via state associations; crowded RCM adjacency.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded denial-appeals automation; plans respond with counter-AI
judges.note: Strong data and contingency pricing win fast, but pattern is on the cliche list; SNF wedge modest.

title: Tariff Refund Kit for Informal-Entry Sellers
one_liner: Turn a small seller's DHL/FedEx/UPS duty invoices into a filed IEEPA refund claim, for the importers who never had a CBP account.
cluster_name: Recovering IEEPA tariff refunds and surcharges

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded refund-recovery field; CBP fixes gaps and the refund wave expires
judges.note: Fastest path to paying customers and real shift, but a herd idea with an ephemeral window.

judges.fatal_flaw: Refund window is transient; carriers and brokers may absorb small claims cheaply.
judges.note: Urgent money-owed pain, flat $99 fee, free-checker lead gen in seller communities; first 10 customers within weeks.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time refund wave with $99 tickets; the window closes and CBP may fix the gap.
judges.note: Perfect timing and immediate revenue, but a temporary, low-ticket services pool with no compounding moat.

title: Burn-Lot Exit Desk for Fire Survivors
one_liner: Package burned lots and stranded insurance claims into sellable assets, and auction them to vetted builders at fair prices.
cluster_name: Flood and fire survivors: mapping, buyouts, claims and rebuilding

judges.fatal_flaw: One-off, geographically bounded event; brokerage licensing and competing cash buyers.
judges.note: Liquidity-not-rebuild insight is sharp and deal sizes are big; disaster-cycle repeatability is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs licensed brokerage; finite lot pool, many already sold to investors.
judges.note: High-ticket success fees ($20-60k per lot) and claim-plus-lot packaging are unusual; scrappy start works, market limited.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny geography, brokerage licensing, and the survivor sale window may already be closing.
judges.note: Liquidity over rebuilding is a good reframe, but the market is one disaster and time-bound.

title: Blue Tarp Index: Adjuster Ground Truth for ILS
one_liner: A subscription that sells cat-bond and reinsurance investors what veteran field adjusters can see in the first 10 days after a disaster, before any model or carrier report exists.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Adjuster confidentiality or legal exposure, and thesis unproven until a live catastrophe event.
judges.note: Contractor capacity as unmeasured severity driver is truly non-obvious; buyers are rich, back-testable, pilot-able within months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers, no live event to prove product; adjuster confidentiality liability
judges.note: Novel data with a rich insight, but hedge-fund buyers need proof that a quiet season withholds.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers and event-driven demand cap the prize; needs a live disaster to prove value.
judges.note: Very non-obvious alt-data insight (contractor capacity sets severity). Strong margins, but a narrow buyer universe.

title: Inherited Low-Rate Mortgage Concierge for Heirs
one_liner: A flat-fee service that helps heirs keep, assume or transfer a parent's low-rate mortgage instead of paying it off at closing, and values that rate as an estate asset so siblings can buy each other out fairly.
cluster_name: Houses caught in death, divorce or care transitions

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven willingness to pay; heirs often keep loans via servicers without help.
judges.note: Genuinely non-obvious rate-as-asset insight with attorney referral channel; demand sizing and conversion uncertain.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few estates pair a low-rate mortgage with heirs who can qualify or keep the house.
judges.note: The lock-in rate as an estate asset is non-obvious and true; $499 report is a cheap wedge via attorneys.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-volume, one-time estate events; estate attorneys can absorb the advice for free.
judges.note: Nice insight that the parent's rate is the asset, but this is a narrow service, not a scalable company.

title: Help-Desk Reset Firewall for MSPs
one_liner: A plug-in for ConnectWise, Autotask and HaloPSA that makes it impossible for a technician to reset a password or MFA without out-of-band verification and manager approval.
cluster_name: Small firms and property managers defending against fraud and impersonation

judges.fatal_flaw: PSA and identity vendors (Huntress, Okta, Nametag) can bundle help-desk verification as a feature.
judges.note: Process-lock design is smart and the MSP channel is leveraged, but the ticket size is small and it is feature-shaped.

judges.fatal_flaw: PSA, RMM and identity vendors could bundle a reset gate
judges.note: MSPs buy per-tech tools, insurance renewals force the purchase, and a webhook plus Teams bot is buildable in weeks.

judges.fatal_flaw: PSA vendors or identity vendors can bundle a reset gate; low defensibility.
judges.note: MSPs are a leveraged, underserved channel and the process lock survives deepfake progress; insurers push adoption; simple to build.

title: Deferred-Payment Shield for Grain Sellers
one_liner: A counterparty-risk monitor plus surety/letter-of-credit wrap that turns the unsecured December 'deferred payment' loans farmers unknowingly make to their elevators into protected receivables.
cluster_name: Farm and ranch risks: disease, cash, storage and machinery

judges.fatal_flaw: Elevator failures are rare; farmers won't pay and sureties may refuse to wrap.
judges.note: Genuine hidden counterparty risk and hard December deadline, but urgency is latent and the wrap product needs licensed partners.

judges.fatal_flaw: Securing the payment may trigger constructive receipt, destroying the tax deferral.
judges.note: Genuine hidden counterparty risk and hard seasonal deadline; the wrap product likely breaks the tax logic.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sureties may refuse elevator risk; short deferral season limits conversion.
judges.note: Farmers unknowingly act as unsecured lenders to elevators; hard December deadline, free calculator wedge, CPAs and lenders as channels.

title: Last Day Co: Small Business Wind-Down
one_liner: A flat-fee retirement service for owners who do not want to sell, just stop: legal wind-down, lease exit, records custody, customer-list handoff and a proper last day.
cluster_name: Owner wind-down, sudden death and tacit-knowledge handoff

judges.fatal_flaw: Owners buy closure only at the end, so acquisition is hard and lumpy, and custody rules vary by state
judges.note: Brokers skip tiny firms, and records custody is a sticky annuity, but low-tech services with hard lead generation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Services-heavy and one-off; records-custodian liability could outrun the flat fee.
judges.note: Retiring regulated practitioners have legal closing duties and cash; $299 entry offer via associations gets early customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Owners avoid planning closure, so demand is low-urgency and state-by-state legal work is heavy
judges.note: 'Nobody closes' is a sharp reframe. Records custody for regulated practices is recurring revenue. The why-now is weak.

title: Substitute-Plan Binders for Retiring Business Owners
one_liner: Retired teachers interview 60+ owner-operators and write a 'sub plan' any stranger could use to run the shop for a week, sold through business brokers.
cluster_name: Owner wind-down, sudden death and tacit-knowledge handoff

judges.fatal_flaw: Human-services business that doesn't scale like software; owners may resist paying for documentation.
judges.note: Clever teacher-elicitation insight and broker channel, quick to sell, but consulting economics cap the venture outcome.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brokers may not push a $2,400 add-on; buyers rarely pay for documentation.
judges.note: Teacher sub-plan framing is a fresh wedge with cheap fast pilots, but small ticket and easy to copy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Owners and brokers may not pay $2,400 for a document; urgency is weak.
judges.note: Cheap to start, broker channel, sharp elicitation insight; labor-light; buyer urgency only moderate.

title: GLP-1 Palate Panel for Food R&D
one_liner: A managed panel of GLP-1 users and their households that food and restaurant companies rent to test products, portions and health claims.
cluster_name: Businesses adapting to GLP-1 users' changed consumption

judges.fatal_flaw: Circana, Ipsos and NielsenIQ can bolt on GLP-1 panel segments quickly.
judges.note: GLP-1 consumers are several dose-dependent sensory segments. Real reformulation wave, clear buyer, fast pilot, though panel moat is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Panel research is lumpy, slow to sell, and low-margin for a venture outcome.
judges.note: Segmenting GLP-1 consumers by dose and week is a real insight, and a first $25k pilot is feasible. It is a services business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Panel incumbents like Kantar or Circana can launch GLP-1 panels; project revenue is lumpy.
judges.note: Cheap panel recruiting, real CPG research budgets, $25K pilot reachable in weeks, and a non-obvious segmentation insight.

title: Orphan-Element Audits for Copper Concentrate and Tailings
one_liner: A 90-day survey that measures the tellurium, selenium, bismuth, cobalt, germanium, rhenium, indium and scandium copper mines already ship for free, then brokers by-product credit rights with refiners.
cluster_name: Critical minerals and rare-earth supply chain recovery and provenance

judges.fatal_flaw: Miners act slowly and recovery needs smelter cooperation and capex; volumes may be tiny.
judges.note: Non-consensus measurement wedge into export-control-driven critical-mineral demand; cheap to prove; royalty upside; unusual insight.

judges.fatal_flaw: Smelters hold leverage; slow mining sales cycles; small absolute by-product value per mine
judges.note: Genuinely contrarian: nobody measured, so nobody owns value. Export controls plus zero treatment charges make timing real.

judges.fatal_flaw: Mining sales cycles run 6-18 months; recovery needs refiner capital.
judges.note: Real measurement gap and strong ACV, but 10 paying miners in six months is unrealistic for a scrappy team.

title: Presence Ledger: Reconstruct Every Trip You Took
one_liner: Ingests flight emails, CBP I-94 history, location exports and passport stamps to produce an evidence-backed, officer-proof travel table for naturalization, green-card retention and tax residency.
cluster_name: Immigrant households and workers: status deadlines and paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Sensitive-data trust, fragile CBP I-94 scraping, low price points and unauthorized-practice-of-law exposure.
judges.note: Real pain, sharply timed, and a tax-residency expansion path. Tracker competitors exist and immigrant users may distrust the data access.

judges.fatal_flaw: Fragile I-94 and Gmail access, privacy trust hurdles, low per-case price
judges.note: Real pain with 2026 naturalization scrutiny; reconcile-with-government-record is smart but small ticket.

judges.fatal_flaw: I-94 retrieval and email access friction may stall automation and spook immigration clients.
judges.note: Concrete billable paralegal pain, $49/case, easy reach via immigration attorneys, high-intent self-serve search, cheap to build.

title: Settlement Back Office for Farm Water Conservation
one_liner: Program administration as a service that enrolls small farms in paid fallowing and conservation programs, verifies acre-feet with satellite evapotranspiration plus meter data, pays within 14 days, and hands the farm's CPA a clean tax packet.
cluster_name: Water scarcity: irrigation allocation and new supply

judges.fatal_flaw: Government-like buyers and the state water-agency shield letter delay first revenue.
judges.note: Funders lack a back office and the money is flowing; a paid pilot with one program is plausible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Public-program procurement is slow, and 3-5% admin fees on early pilots are tiny.
judges.note: Right insight: water markets fail at settlement, not price. Colorado River deal and corporate money create a real gap. Slow buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow government payers and small program budgets limit admin-fee revenue.
judges.note: Settlement-not-marketplace insight is right and timely post-ROD; 4% of modest disbursements is thin.

title: Scam Recovery Desk for Community Banks
one_liner: Banks buy scam detection, but the untapped money is recovery: stablecoin issuers, receiving banks and exchanges can freeze funds if someone asks fast and correctly.
cluster_name: Banks and platforms disrupting scam networks and recovering victims' funds

judges.fatal_flaw: Recovery depends on counterparty cooperation; community-bank sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: Big loss pool, aligned contingency pricing, ops and contact-directory moat; recovery is the neglected half of scam tooling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Recovery depends on receiving institutions' cooperation; low recovery rates cripple contingency economics
judges.note: Speed-and-relationships operations moat; stablecoins as most freezable rail is contrarian; community banks slow buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: US banks often bear no scam-reimbursement duty, and vendor onboarding and 314(b) limits slow deals.
judges.note: Contingency pilots are an easy risk-free ask. Speed and relationships are a real moat, but recovery rates are low.

title: Federated Settlement-Benchmark Co-op for Small Firms
one_liner: Small plaintiff firms pool de-identified settlement outcomes from their practice-management systems to get case-value benchmarks that only insurers and big firms have today.
cluster_name: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Settlement confidentiality and Rule 1.6 make lawyers unwilling to share data.
judges.note: Give-to-get flywheel is smart but cold-start, ethics risk, slow monetization; small firms pay little.

judges.fatal_flaw: Settlement confidentiality clauses, Rule 1.6 and lawyer reluctance to share block the cold-start data flywheel.
judges.note: Right insight that settlement data sits in small-firm ledgers; give-to-get co-op is defensible if it bootstraps.

judges.fatal_flaw: Settlement confidentiality and Rule 1.6 block sharing; give-to-get cold start.
judges.note: Genuinely proprietary dataset with a registry-style flywheel; can start manually; legal-ethics risk is the crux.

title: Quality-of-Earnings Audits for Robot Fleets
one_liner: A finance-native auditor that verifies deployed units, productive hours, teleoperation share and revenue per robot for the lenders, lessors and investors underwriting robot, AV and drone fleets.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool; vendors control telemetry access; needs Big-4 credibility to close.
judges.note: Insightful metric (intervention hours) but boutique diligence yields 1-2 engagements, not ten, in six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers; vendors may refuse telemetry access; needs assurance credibility before first engagement.
judges.note: Hidden intervention hours decide software vs labor-arbitrage robotics; capital-side payer is right, but market thin today.

judges.fatal_flaw: Boutique assurance services with few buyers; hard to reach venture scale.
judges.note: Buyer-paid verification of hidden teleop hours is sharp and timely; could become the covenant standard for robot leasing.

title: Escaped-Burn Liability Cover Verified From Orbit
one_liner: Go/no-go data and liability cover for prescribed burn associations, priced from fuel dryness and settled by satellite proof that the fire never left the unit.
cluster_name: Cover and data for emerging or neglected risks

judges.fatal_flaw: Small burn-association wallets; certificate value unproven without insurer acceptance.
judges.note: Uninsurable because unprovable; FireSat and free perimeter data make proof cheap. Genuinely non-obvious, timely, small but growing.

judges.fatal_flaw: Certificates have little value until an insurer accepts them; no early revenue.
judges.note: Strong insight and a tight-knit reachable market, but burn associations are poor and WTP precedes insurance.

judges.fatal_flaw: Burn associations have little money and insurers lack escape-loss actuarial base.
judges.note: Uninsurable because unprovable is a clean insight; satellite proof timely; no licence needed to start; small prize initially.

title: Status-Cliff Benefit Sold Through PEOs
one_liner: A confidential, employer-paid benefit that screens temporary-status workers for alternate immigration relief, tracks work-authorization cliffs, and pre-arranges counsel and family plans before a raid, TPS termination or EAD lapse hits.
cluster_name: Immigrant households and workers: status deadlines and paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Political and professional-conduct risk of employer-paid immigration counsel; slow PEO procurement.
judges.note: Non-consensus buyer (PEO benefits desk), huge affected workforce, acute why-now, churn-based ROI; pilot sellable fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employer knowledge of workers' status creates liability; ethics rules limit employer-paid counsel; PEO sales are slow.
judges.note: Urgent labor-churn pain and a workable pilot with home-health agencies, but legal and political exposure is heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employer-paid screening creates knowledge liability and worker distrust; long PEO sales cycles.
judges.note: Sells to the PEO benefits desk with the employee as attorney's client; strong 2025-26 status-cliff shift, but legal minefield.

title: EUDR reference-number desk for downstream buyers
one_liner: An inbox-and-validator service that collects, checks and vaults EUDR reference numbers and plot GeoJSON from suppliers, sold to downstream operators and via customs brokers.
cluster_name: Exporters meeting foreign sustainability and representation rules

judges.fatal_flaw: Another EUDR delay or a crowded compliance-software field erodes urgency.
judges.note: Downstream chase-and-validate is the neglected job with a hard December gate. Free validator lead magnet and fastest path to paying customers here.

judges.fatal_flaw: EUDR could slip or be diluted again, and funded compliance vendors already cover this.
judges.note: Concrete near-term pain and a fast first sale, but a crowded, deadline-driven compliance wave.

judges.fatal_flaw: Another EUDR delay or simplification would kill urgency; low ARPU.
judges.note: Fixed deadline, clear downstream buyer, free validator as lead magnet, EUR 500 audits close fast.

title: Night-Shift Bench Techs for Time-Critical Experiments
one_liner: An agency of vetted, laid-off bench technicians who show up at 2 a.m. or on Christmas morning to harvest time points, feed cells and load overnight runs from the lab's own protocol cards, with photo proof and a break-glass line to the postdoc.
cluster_name: Autonomous and AI-directed labs: infrastructure, safety and access

judges.fatal_flaw: One ruined cell line destroys trust, and the niche stays small.
judges.note: Original, sellable in weeks. Trust wrapper plus shared-lab operator channel is a real insight; layoffs supply labor.

judges.fatal_flaw: Labs won't hand irreplaceable cells to strangers; staffing margins cap the prize.
judges.note: Nice trust-wrapper insight and shared-lab operators as a channel, but a niche staffing agency is not venture scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lumpy tiny demand; labs may not trust strangers with irreplaceable cells.
judges.note: Real pain, roughly 50% gross margin, shared-lab operators unlock many labs; a scrappy agency is feasible.

title: Shelf Zero: Unclaimed Cremains Clearance Service
one_liner: A done-for-you compliance service that legally and respectfully empties the closet of unclaimed ashes that nearly every funeral home and crematory is afraid to touch.
cluster_name: Independent funeral homes facing key-person, overnight and consolidation pressure

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Per-box pricing, no capital, reachable via state associations, guilt plus diligence pain; five paid pilots plausible in 30 days.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small per-home revenue and state-by-state legal drafting; disposition partners could be squeezed.
judges.note: Unglamorous, real compounding liability with a clear payer and easy first sales. Sellers' diligence adds a timely wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time cleanup revenue and small TAM; hard to become a very large company.
judges.note: Charming, real, underserved pain with a solid insight, but the market is a finite backlog, not recurring.

title: PTO Bureau: Cash Advances Priced on Utility Delay
one_liner: A data co-op plus bridge lender that advances the 10-20% held back until utility Permission-to-Operate, and prices each advance from real per-utility delay history.
cluster_name: Cash-flow gaps from slow-paying institutions

judges.fatal_flaw: Residential solar is shrinking post-25D; lending needs capital and carries credit risk.
judges.note: Pooled PTO delay data is a real insight and the 2027 deadline creates urgency. Shrinking market caps the outcome.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lender or TPO assignment consent for holdbacks; lending to distressed installers.
judges.note: Post-25D and 48E deadline makes PTO delay predictable and priceable; pooled utility clock is a real data moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lending to distressed solar installers needs capital and licences; adverse selection.
judges.note: PTO clock data and SWAT service are scrappy, but the lending core is capital-hungry and credit-risky.

title: Made-in-USA Proof Files for Relabeling Brands
one_liner: Audit-ready substantiation files and monitoring for brands rushing to claim 'Made in USA' after tariffs.
cluster_name: Brands substantiating origin, recycled-content and green claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Project-based audits with small total market; lawyers and consultancies can copy.
judges.note: Sellable compliance wedge with legal-budget buyer; modest ceiling and services-heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Enforcement is sporadic and law firms could offer the same audit.
judges.note: Public-listing scorecard gives cold-outreach hook, $3k audits, legal-fear budget, tariff-driven timing.

judges.fatal_flaw: Service-heavy audits that need lawyers; brands may just soften claims.
judges.note: The label is the first casualty of reshoring, and legal is a buyer outside the tariff-software budget. Cold scorecards are cheap.

title: Plaintiff-Evidence Pipeline for Kids-Tech Litigation
one_liner: Software and services that automate platform data requests, device-usage exports and chat-log preservation into court-ready per-plaintiff timelines for firms litigating social media and AI-chatbot harms to minors.
cluster_name: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Tied to specific dockets; e-discovery incumbents can copy the export parsers.
judges.note: Unglamorous real bottleneck at mass-tort firms that buy fast; could generalize to all plaintiff data collection.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers, existing litigation-support vendors, and a settlement could end the wave.
judges.note: Timely picks-and-shovels for kids-tech mass torts. Real bottleneck but narrow customer set. Requires careful ethics and chain-of-custody work.

judges.fatal_flaw: Big firms may already have vendors; minors' sensitive data creates liability and slow trust.
judges.note: Cash-rich firms, per-plaintiff pricing, clear ROI, pilot of 40 plaintiffs is a fast, concrete first sale.

title: Surge Beds: Pre-Contracted Lodging for Catastrophe Responders
one_liner: Sell adjuster firms and storm contractors reserved-bed options on inland RV pads, seasonal parks and closed motels, contracted before landfall at prices that stay legal after an emergency declaration.
cluster_name: Heat, fire and evacuation protection for vulnerable people

judges.fatal_flaw: Reservation fees are hard to sell without a storm; demand is lumpy and seasonal.
judges.note: Gouging-law price freeze turns lodging into an options market; genuinely non-obvious structure, modest prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Adjuster firms have incumbent lodging vendors and won't prepay without a fresh storm.
judges.note: Clever gouging-law option angle and idle RV supply, but lumpy seasonal demand and quiet hurricane years cool urgency.

judges.fatal_flaw: Demand is lumpy and storm-dependent; buyers with existing hotel relationships may not pay reservation fees.
judges.note: Anti-gouging laws make pre-season options the only lawful certainty; clever, but seasonal, relationship-heavy and hard to scale.

title: Shared-Docket Lawsuits Against Scam Infrastructure
one_liner: Turn Google's and Microsoft's civil-seizure playbook into a membership where 20-50 mid-size banks and brands co-file one John Doe action against the kit or ring impersonating all of them.
cluster_name: Banks and platforms disrupting scam networks and recovering victims' funds

judges.fatal_flaw: Domain seizures are whack-a-mole; members' ROI unclear; litigation outcomes uncertain.
judges.note: Reverse class-action cost sharing is a fresh product form; big scam losses, but proof of value is weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Litigation outcomes uncertain; members balk at pass-through legal costs and standing issues.
judges.note: Original cost-sharing model with real fraud budgets; pre-selling $2k/month before any filing is hard.

judges.fatal_flaw: Civil seizures may not durably reduce losses; offshore defendants and law-firm structuring complicate delivery.
judges.note: Cost scales with defendant networks, not victims: a reverse class action. Google/Microsoft precedents make it credible; recurring retainers.

title: Design-for-Duty: Engineer Below the 15% Metal Line
one_liner: A CAD/BOM tool that redesigns imported products to fall under Section 232's metal-weight cliffs or qualify for the 10% US-melt rate.
cluster_name: Tariff cost, classification and customs for small importers

judges.fatal_flaw: Tariff rules change too fast; product redesign cycles are slower than policy shifts.
judges.note: Right insight that duty is a bill-of-materials problem, but the value depends on volatile policy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tariff regime and the 15% cliff can change or be litigated overnight.
judges.note: Sharp BOM-level reframe that nobody in the chain is paid to touch; urgent, spreadsheet-first; policy volatility is the risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: Section 232 rules keep shifting, and redesign requires retooling that buyers resist.
judges.note: Original BOM-mass insight with urgent duty pain. Spreadsheet audits at $1.5k can sell fast but the rules are volatile.

title: Insider-Trading Watchdog for Entertainment Announcements
one_liner: Sportradar-style integrity monitoring for game publishers, studios and awards bodies whose announcements and results now trade as prediction-market contracts.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: IP owners earn nothing from these markets and may not budget; exchanges already surveil in-house.
judges.note: Timely and non-consensus for prediction-market integrity, but the buyer with the budget is unclear.

judges.fatal_flaw: Publishers don't feel the pain yet; only exchanges have incentive to pay.
judges.note: Fresh angle on prediction-market leakage, but compliance buyers lack an urgent budgeted problem today.

judges.fatal_flaw: Studio compliance teams may lack urgency or budget; exchanges may keep surveillance in-house.
judges.note: Non-obvious: embargoed announcements now have a price. Sports-integrity analogy is sound and Kalshi growth is a real 2026 shift.

title: Pay the Grandmother: Relative-Care Subsidy Enrollment
one_liner: A multilingual concierge plus verified-attendance software that turns unpaid grandparents and relatives into subsidy-paid, health-and-safety-cleared caregivers, billed per enrollment to states and referral agencies.
cluster_name: Childcare shortage: providers, buildings and employer funding

judges.fatal_flaw: State and county agencies buy slowly and fraud scrutiny slows relative-care enrollment.
judges.note: Real unpaid-supply insight and a cheap concierge pilot. Government procurement makes paying customers in six months unlikely.

judges.fatal_flaw: Selling to state agencies is slow, and subsidy fraud scrutiny is a risk.
judges.note: Real insight that unpaid relative supply already exists and is blocked by paperwork. Verified attendance answers fraud fears.

judges.fatal_flaw: State procurement is slow and subsidy-fraud scrutiny may freeze license-exempt relative payments.
judges.note: Unlocks existing unpaid supply with verified attendance; large government-funded pool; per-enrollment pricing; concierge pilot is cheap.

title: Search-Fund Accelerator for Buying Scrap Yards
one_liner: A cohort program that turns laid-off mid-career managers into owner-operators of small scrap yards, e-scrap shops and transfer stations. It brings deal sourcing, environmental diligence and SBA-lender access.
cluster_name: Trade-shop succession and buyouts

judges.fatal_flaw: Environmental liability and slow deal closings; services model with limited scalability.
judges.note: Weird, contrarian: buy permitted cash-flow, use laid-off managers; tuition revenue quick, but it is a search-fund-style services play.

judges.fatal_flaw: Scrap-yard environmental liability and low close rates mean success fees rarely arrive.
judges.note: Tuition can be sold fast to laid-off managers, but the model depends on hard deals closing and looks like coaching.

judges.fatal_flaw: First closings take over six months; environmental liability and deal execution risk.
judges.note: Contrarian insight that permits are the moat and displaced managers supply operators; tuition gives early cash but the model is stretched.

title: Supervised-Hours Bench for Counselors and Social Workers
one_liner: A managed group-supervision network and hour-logging platform that lets clinics fund the thousands of post-degree supervised hours gating counseling, MFT and social-work licenses.
cluster_name: Behavioral health and addiction care capacity

judges.fatal_flaw: State board rules vary and many clinics already supervise in-house.
judges.note: Employer-paid bottleneck with billable associates; cheap to start with spreadsheets and recruited supervisors.

judges.fatal_flaw: State board supervision rules and malpractice liability vary and existing supervision networks compete.
judges.note: Real bottleneck sharpened by loan caps, and clinics can pay because associates bill; hour-logging alone is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: State board rules, supervisor liability and existing group-practice supervision programs limit differentiation.
judges.note: Real supply bottleneck with employer as payer; easy first customers, but marketplace-like services with modest defensibility.

title: Weather Forecasts for GPS Jamming
one_liner: A crowd-sensed, forecastable map of GNSS jamming and spoofing for the civil operators nobody warns: survey and RTK fleets, drone operators and marine underwriters.
cluster_name: Aircraft and drone operators: maintenance, parts, permits and navigation

judges.fatal_flaw: Jamming is largely military and may not be forecastable; civil buyers can't act on alerts.
judges.note: Novel, timely, sensor network built with hosts. Insurer and drone buyers are real; forecastability unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Building a sensor network is capital-heavy, and persistent jammers make forecasting less valuable than mapping.
judges.note: Novel civil buyers for GNSS jamming, real 2026 surge, but hardware cold start and speculative forecastability.

judges.fatal_flaw: About 30 receivers can't deliver forecast-grade resolution, and hobby-scale operators may not pay.
judges.note: Original angle, real jamming pain. Forecastability is unproven and the insurer sales cycle is long.

title: Independent Battery Safety Review for Counties
one_liner: Sell counties and fire marshals a developer-funded third-party plan review, hazard analysis and first-responder plan for every battery project.
cluster_name: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Established fire-safety consultancies compete; county procurement and escrow adoption are slow.
judges.note: Developers already lose 6-12 months to hostile hearings; developer-pays pre-application dossiers are a fast first sale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consulting-style revenue with independence-conflict optics; engineering firms already sell this.
judges.note: Timely developer-funded escrow model for county trust. Quick revenue but low defensibility and a services business, not software.

judges.fatal_flaw: DNV, Jensen Hughes and Exponent already sell this; county procurement is slow.
judges.note: Developer-funded county-chosen reviewer is sensible and timely, but it is a consultancy with established rivals.

title: Proctored Truth Audits for School Edtech
one_liner: Short, paper-based, device-free probes that tell districts whether the practice software they license teaches anything, now that AI can do the practice for the child.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow district procurement; incumbent efficacy evaluators and paper-proctoring logistics.
judges.note: Right contrarian insight: AI contaminates practice metrics, so unassisted paper measurement becomes the scarce layer. Sales cycle drags.

judges.fatal_flaw: K-12 procurement is slow and teachers resist audits; free pilots burn cash.
judges.note: Strong, timely insight that AI contaminates usage metrics. Pre-renewal pilots are clever, but the buyer is slow and politically wary.

judges.fatal_flaw: District sales cycles are slow, budgets tight, and paper proctoring is operationally heavy.
judges.note: Sharp insight that measurement, not content, becomes the moat; unclear buyer urgency and manual scaling.

title: Roll Up the Layer Under Funeral Homes
one_liner: Instead of buying funeral homes, buy the removal services and wholesale crematories that independent homes depend on, and run them with AI dispatch, chain-of-custody and paperwork agents.
cluster_name: Independent funeral homes facing key-person, overnight and consolidation pressure

judges.fatal_flaw: Roll-up needs acquisition capital that a scrappy team lacks.
judges.note: Buying the invisible removal and cremation layer is a clever roll-up angle, and the paperwork-chaser wedge gets revenue first.

judges.fatal_flaw: Roll-up capital needs and services-margin reality; seed money cannot fund acquisitions.
judges.note: Non-consensus layer under funeral homes, large market, workable paperwork wedge; risk is roll-up capital.

judges.fatal_flaw: Roll-up needs acquisition capital before the AI ops layer matters.
judges.note: Paperwork-chaser wedge at $60 per case is real and scrappy, but the roll-up thesis is capital-heavy and a template.

title: Verbal-Promise Ledger for Mine Community Relations
one_liner: A voice-first, offline-capable phone tool that turns every promise a mine makes at community assemblies (Spanish, Quechua, Aymara) into a tracked commitment register the community can verify by WhatsApp.
cluster_name: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer universe of mid-tier miners; long trust-building and multilingual data hurdles.
judges.note: Sharp insider insight on commitment debt; small prize, hard to expand beyond mining.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small buyer universe and founder must already know mining community-relations heads.
judges.note: Sharp insight, named buyer with risk-line budget, $5-10k audit needs no integration, converts to SaaS.

judges.fatal_flaw: Mines may refuse a discoverable register of their own promises.
judges.note: Conflict risk as commitment debt, with community receipts as the moat. A $5-10k audit of old actas needs no integration.

title: Dumpster-Drop Leads for the Next Trade
one_liner: A white-label booking flow for independent roll-off dumpster companies that sells the homeowner's renovation start as an exclusive, unshared lead to the next trade in sequence.
cluster_name: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: Haulers see limited volume and pros may not pay; lead marketplaces are hard to scale.
judges.note: Dumpster as first hard commitment in a remodel is a clever exclusive-lead wedge. Local, fragmented, modest ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low lead value per hauler, thin repeat volume, and haulers may not push a sequence of trades.
judges.note: Dumpster as earliest hard commitment is a neat wedge, but it is still home-services lead gen.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin lead volume per hauler; two-sided marketplace across trades needs liquidity.
judges.note: Dumpster is the earliest hard commitment, so leads are high-intent and exclusive. Pros pay per lead, cheap to test.

title: Remote Load Calcs That Avoid Panel Upgrades
one_liner: A photo-and-utility-bill service that proves an existing electrical panel can take a heat pump or EV charger, with load-management devices when it cannot.
cluster_name: Households upgrading homes: electrification, roofs and solar loans

judges.fatal_flaw: Remote engineer stamp liability and AHJ acceptance vary; heat-pump incentives fading.
judges.note: Panel capacity is a real electrification bottleneck; simple paid desk job, fast start; moderate prize, copyable by panel makers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Jurisdictions or utilities may reject remote stamped calcs; existing load-calc services compete
judges.note: Concrete $99 desk product that unblocks contractor jobs; PE partner suffices; easy to reach HVAC installers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Local code officials may reject remote calcs, and stamp liability squeezes thin margins.
judges.note: Panel capacity is the true electrification bottleneck; useful $99 service, but existing calc vendors and weak demand.

title: EU Liable-Party-of-Record for AI Products
one_liner: The registered agent of the AI era: an insured EU entity that stands as authorised representative under the new Product Liability Directive and keeps clients' evidence court-ready.
cluster_name: EU digital product laws for small connected-device makers

judges.fatal_flaw: Assuming EU product liability for $3k a month is underpriced; insurers may refuse cover.
judges.note: Hard December 2026 deadline and GPSR-rep precedent; distribution-chain demand plausible; liability tail is scary.

judges.fatal_flaw: Taking on strict liability for clients' products without underwriter appetite or capital.
judges.note: Hard 9 Dec 2026 deadline, proven GPSR-rep buying pattern, distribution via marketplaces; regulated entity plus insurance is defensible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unlimited product-liability tail priced at $1-3k/month; carriers unlikely to front it.
judges.note: Dated deadline and GPSR-rep precedent, but bearing liability needs insurance capital and legal entity before revenue.

title: Family Bank: Bank of Mom and Dad, Papered
one_liner: A family office's real job is governance and records, not investing; for $20/mo, give ordinary parents and adult children a promissory-note, autopay and sibling-fairness ledger for the money that already flows between them.
cluster_name: Making family estate plans fair and contest-proof

judges.fatal_flaw: Need is episodic; retention drops after the note is signed.
judges.note: Huge, unserved handshake-lending market; sibling ledger is genuine insight; SEO funnel and document packs sell fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consumer $20/mo with weak urgency and high CAC; lending apps already exist
judges.note: Sibling-ledger insight is nice; doc packs might sell, but subscription retention looks doubtful.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consumers rarely pay recurring fees for one-off family loans; attorneys and loan servicers exist.
judges.note: Sibling advancement ledger is the sharp insight; big latent market, but low defensibility and weak retention.

title: Insurability Passport Attached to California Home Listings
one_liner: A pre-listing report that verifies wildfire mitigation and attaches bindable insurance options (FAIR Plan plus wraparound, admitted where available) to the listing, so buyers see the real insured cost before they make an offer.
cluster_name: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: Quoting can't be automated; sellers and agents reluctant to pay per listing.
judges.note: Real, large pain and timely, but the insight (insurance discovered in escrow) is obvious to anyone in California.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs licensed agency partner; agents may balk at paying per listing.
judges.note: Urgent, budgeted escrow pain, big California market, manual 10-listing start, commission upside. Best prize-to-feasibility mix.

judges.fatal_flaw: Quotes are hard to automate; thin product, crowded insurtech and mitigation-verification players, licensing constraints.
judges.note: Real escrow-time insurability pain in California; distribution via listing agents plausible but value mostly commissions.

title: Workup Cover: Insurance for Scan Findings
one_liner: A prepaid guarantee sold at checkout for $800-$1,000 whole-body MRIs and $949 cancer blood tests that covers the second read, the guideline triage and pre-priced follow-up when a scan finds something.
cluster_name: Follow-up gaps and anxiety after consumer scans and mega-panels

judges.fatal_flaw: Scan sellers can bundle their own second read; state licensure and corporate-practice hurdles.
judges.note: Prices the unpriced tail of cheap screening. Attach-fee wedge is immediate, but distribution depends on scan sellers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Radiologist state licensure and malpractice exposure; second-read phase has weak moat.
judges.note: Urgent fear-driven consumer pain, quick $149 test; underwriting phase needs capital and data.

judges.fatal_flaw: Radiologist licensing and liability; consumers reluctant to pay extra after a scary scan.
judges.note: Pricing the unpriced follow-up tail like a warranty is sharp; $149 second-read wedge sells immediately, timing tied to Galleri.

title: Human Callback Line Sold Through Credit Unions
one_liner: A staffed 'is this really my grandson?' phone line and call-screening kit for members over 70, paid for per enrolled member by community credit unions whose deposits walk out the door in voice-clone scams.
cluster_name: Seniors targeted by impersonation scams and the institutions that bear the losses

judges.fatal_flaw: Labor-heavy service with services margins; unproven loss reduction; elder-fraud vendors already sell to credit unions.
judges.note: Credit union as payer is smart, easy pilot, but staffed phone line does not scale like software.

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit unions bear little fraud liability, so budget and sales cycles may stall pilots.
judges.note: Clear institutional buyer, $2k pilot, no engineering needed; cheap to test but pilot volume is slow to reach ten.

judges.fatal_flaw: Banks are mostly not liable, so credit union ROI is soft and sales cycles long.
judges.note: Right buyer (institution losing deposits), human out-of-band ritual beats detectors; staffing is cheap to pilot.

title: Tariff Refund Liquidation-Cliff Radar
one_liner: A deadline tracker and filing generator for small importers and small customs brokers that tells them, entry by entry, which refund route is still open and when it closes.
cluster_name: Recovering IEEPA tariff refunds and surcharges

judges.fatal_flaw: Time-boxed refund window; brokers or Flexport-type incumbents may bundle the same tracker.
judges.note: Urgent money on the table, hard deadlines, reachable broker channel, per-entry pricing, and a spreadsheet-service start.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time refund window; brokers, law firms and platforms already chase the same importers.
judges.note: Extremely timely and easy to sell, but consensus 2026 opportunity with weak defensibility and a shelf life.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time refund wave; brokers and CBP tooling commoditize the calendar.
judges.note: Acute deadline-driven pain and clear buyer, but transient, crowded cluster, and an obvious tool.

title: Chaos Testing for Buildings as Code-Required Commissioning
one_liner: An agent that safely actuates a building's HVAC at night, forcing dampers, valves and pumps through scripted step tests, to produce the functional-test evidence that codes require and passive analytics cannot.
cluster_name: Condition monitoring for asset owners and their service contractors

judges.fatal_flaw: Owners and integrators resist write access to building systems; liability if equipment damaged.
judges.note: Mandated-test angle and safety-envelope insight are good; trust and access barriers delay first customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: BAS write-access liability and OT security approvals stall pilots for months.
judges.note: Active probing yields labels passive analytics lack; mandated tests make it a cost cut, not a discretionary sale.

judges.fatal_flaw: BAS vendors and owners resist third-party write access; liability blocks adoption.
judges.note: Active-probing insight is smart and tied to mandated tests; sales through commissioning firms is small.

title: Percentage-Rent Rails for Small Retail Strips
one_liner: Sales-linked leases with rent automatically swept from the tenant's POS, so independent landlords can fill dark restaurant and shop spaces and tenants stop dying under fixed rent.
cluster_name: Landlords in soft markets: vouchers, evictions, vacancies and retention

judges.fatal_flaw: Landlords and tenants must both adopt; take rate on rent flow is tiny.
judges.note: POS data does fix percentage-rent trust, but two-sided adoption and low revenue per lease hurt.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small landlords and tenants resist sales-linked leases; Toast or Square could copy it.
judges.note: Huge rent-flow prize. Reframes percentage rent as an information problem solved by POS APIs. Real why-now and payments take-rate.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tenants can under-report cash or off-POS sales, and lenders underwrite only base rent.
judges.note: POS data solves percentage rent's trust problem; a plausible wedge, but small tickets and lease-law friction limit it.

title: Human Viva Examiners for AI-Wary Universities
one_liner: A per-student oral-defense service where trained examiners in Nairobi, Manila and Chennai run 12-minute recorded vivas on submitted essays and code, giving US professors human-verified authorship evidence for about $10 a student.
cluster_name: Verifying real human skill, identity and authorship in hiring and education

judges.fatal_flaw: Adjuncts and departments unlikely to pay $10 per student; institutional sales slow.
judges.note: Human attention as the bottleneck is a real insight, but payer is weak and false-accusation liability is heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Adjuncts lack budget; FERPA and student-scheduling friction slow institutional sales
judges.note: Proctoring budgets give a price anchor; human-verified authorship is timely; per-section pilots are easy to sell and run.

judges.fatal_flaw: Adjuncts lack budgets; institutional procurement slow; AI-run vivas will undercut on price.
judges.note: Human oral exams via emerging-market labor is contrarian, but buyer budget and slow university sales hurt.

title: TurkBridge: MTurk-Compatible Verified-Human Marketplace
one_liner: An MTurk requester-API-compatible endpoint backed by an identity-verified, proof-of-human worker pool, launched as Amazon Mechanical Turk closes on 30 Sept 2026.
cluster_name: Gatekeepers drowning in AI-generated submissions and bot responses

judges.fatal_flaw: Prolific and CloudResearch absorb displaced demand; two-sided marketplace with tiny early supply.
judges.note: Sharp timing and a cheap API shim, but the shutdown is tomorrow and obvious. Small prize, thin defensibility beyond a migration window.

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-sided marketplace cold start; Prolific and CloudResearch absorb displaced requesters; the shim is easily copied.
judges.note: Extreme timing on the MTurk shutdown, but the moat is thin and the window is short.

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-sided marketplace cold start; Prolific and CloudResearch absorb displaced academic requesters first.
judges.note: Maximum why-now, real API-compat switching wedge, cheap to ship; weak moat and small take-rate pool.

title: Proof-of-Review Receipts for AI-Using Professionals
one_liner: A tamper-evident record that a named, licensed human actually reviewed AI output, backed by planted-error vigilance tests, sold to firms and their malpractice carriers.
cluster_name: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Professionals resist planted-error testing; carriers haven't proven they will grant premium credits.
judges.note: Real sanction and underwriting pressure, but slow carrier partnerships and skeptical firms delay first customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers unlikely to grant premium credits without loss data; add-in adoption friction.
judges.note: Planted-error vigilance testing is a fresh insight and insurers are the paying channel, but space is crowded.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers slow to grant premium credits; planted errors in real client work are risky.
judges.note: Vigilance canaries to measure automation complacency are original, but the AI-assurance cluster is crowded and buyer conversion is slow.

title: Cure Desk: Medical-Bill Triage for Delinquent Tenants
one_liner: A landlord-paid service that turns a late-rent notice into a medical-bill rescue, using hospital charity care, bill negotiation and coverage re-enrollment to free up the cash that pays the rent.
cluster_name: Landlords in soft markets: vouchers, evictions, vacancies and retention

judges.fatal_flaw: Causal chain from medical bills to rent is narrow and charity-care work is labor-heavy.
judges.note: Success-fee only is easy for landlords to accept, but cure rate is doubtful and unit cost high.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a small share of late rent is medical-bill driven; cure attribution is murky.
judges.note: Non-obvious payer flip: landlords fund tenant medical-bill rescue. Success-fee pilot is cheap to run manually.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unknown share of delinquency is medical-driven; tenants may not opt in.
judges.note: Landlord as payer for health-side bill rescue is surprising; success-fee pilot is cheap, but cure rates unproven.

title: Blinded Diligence Bureau for AI-Biotech Financiers
one_liner: A buyer-paid, blinded prospective testing service that tells pharma BD teams, royalty funds and lenders whether an AI drug-discovery platform's claims hold up in a neutral wet lab.
cluster_name: Biotech capital: diligence and salvage

judges.fatal_flaw: Lumpy consulting revenue; AI vendors may refuse blinded testing.
judges.note: Buyer-paid independence and open-model baseline is smart; high ticket but few buyers and limited scalability.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small buyer set, long sales cycles, credibility gap, and vendors may refuse blinded tests.
judges.note: Buyer-paid independence is a smart insight and tickets are large. Lab rental and BD trust make the first pilots slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: AI vendors may refuse to submit designs; long pharma sales cycles.
judges.note: Buyer-paid blinded test against a free open-model baseline is unpriced. High ticket, and neutral labs can be rented.

title: License-in-a-Box for Insourcing Property Owners
one_liner: A licensed managing-broker entity, trust-account oversight and compliance layer that lets owners run AI-native property management in-house without building licensing state by state.
cluster_name: Landlords in soft markets: vouchers, evictions, vacancies and retention

judges.fatal_flaw: Broker-of-record supervision liability and state rules against nominal oversight.
judges.note: Employer-of-record analogue for licensing; incumbents won't sell it; few but large buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Regulators treat rented broker-of-record without real supervision as unlawful; narrow customer base
judges.note: Licensed human of record is the true bottleneck, but renting licenses invites regulatory attack. Narrow insourcing niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Supervising-broker liability and state rules against rented licenses; hard to insure.
judges.note: Real regulatory bottleneck and per-unit pricing, but broker-of-record liability far exceeds the fee.

title: DKIM for Bank Accounts: Signed Payee Records
one_liner: A free, domain-verified payment record that suppliers publish, plus an AP plug-in that blocks any bank-detail change the supplier's own domain has not signed.
cluster_name: Small firms and property managers defending against fraud and impersonation

judges.fatal_flaw: Cold-start supplier adoption; bank payee-verification and vendor-validation incumbents may absorb it.
judges.note: DKIM-for-payees framing is sharp; accountant channel avoids two-sided cold start; protocol upside if adopted.

judges.fatal_flaw: Suppliers won't publish records, so the check has no value at launch.
judges.note: Sharp DKIM-for-payees insight and accountant channel, but cold start plus low willingness to pay at $5-9 per client.

judges.fatal_flaw: Suppliers must publish records; cold-start adoption and bank-side account validation rules undercut it.
judges.note: Clever provenance reframing of BEC as one string of digits, but network adoption is the hard part.

title: Verifier-Ready Emissions Data Rooms for CBAM Exporters
one_liner: A metering-to-evidence pipeline that gives small non-EU steel, aluminum and fertilizer producers a clean, pre-audited data room for accredited verifiers, so their EU and UK buyers stop defaulting to punitive default values.
cluster_name: Exporters meeting foreign sustainability and representation rules

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded CBAM tooling and consultants; small producers reluctant to pay for data collection.
judges.note: Hard 2026-27 deadlines and importer-funded upstream readiness is a smart angle; services-heavy start but real willingness to pay.

judges.fatal_flaw: Selling to small foreign factories is slow; verifier capacity bottlenecks delivery.
judges.note: Supplier-side CBAM readiness is a smart angle, but hard for a scrappy team to reach. Near the carbon-accounting crowd.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small emerging-market plants resist paying EUR 6-25k; importer sponsorship needed.
judges.note: Real CBAM and UK deadline; upstream-supplier wedge is non-obvious; importer-funded pilots close plausibly within six months.

title: Government Property Control Kit for New Defense Makers
one_liner: A fixed-price property-system-in-a-box (tags, procedures, mock audit, reconciliation) that keeps first-time defense manufacturers from failing their government property audit and having payments withheld.
cluster_name: New defense and drone suppliers: compliance and financing hurdles

judges.fatal_flaw: none
judges.note: Urgent, budgeted (withheld payments), named list of buyers via SBIR awards, fixed-price service closes fast; software optional.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consulting-like service with modest market and weak moat
judges.note: Unsexy picks-and-shovels for defense boom; fixed-price mock audit sells fast; prime sponsorship channel.

judges.fatal_flaw: Fixed-price consulting for a tiny customer set; hard to productize into software.
judges.note: Practical and quick to sell, and the prime as sponsor is smart. It is a compliance services shop.

title: Pre-Permitted School Suites for Micro-Schools
one_liner: Master-lease vacant office and retail suites, pre-solve the change-of-use to educational occupancy, and rent furnished seats by the student to micro-school operators funded by education savings accounts.
cluster_name: Microschools, homeschoolers and shrinking districts

judges.fatal_flaw: Master-lease liability against thin-capital operators whose funding depends on state ESA politics.
judges.note: Permit, not demand, gates micro-school supply; Texas ESA timing strong; capital-heavy but sizeable and non-obvious.

judges.fatal_flaw: Change-of-use permitting and master-lease liability outrun six-month timeline and seed capital.
judges.note: Correctly finds the true gate (certificate of occupancy) behind ESA-funded demand. Capital-heavy but genuinely non-obvious.

judges.fatal_flaw: Long master leases versus month-to-month seat rents, plus build-out capital and permit delays.
judges.note: Insight on occupancy permits is good, but a capital-heavy lease-arbitrage model punishes a scrappy team.

title: Texted Pond-Algae and Forage-Poison Alerts for Ranchers
one_liner: Satellite imagery plus weather models watch every stock pond and frost-stressed sorghum field for the handful of killers that wipe out cattle in hours, then text the rancher and route the case to the vet.
cluster_name: Farm and ranch risks: disease, cash, storage and machinery

judges.fatal_flaw: Small-pond satellite accuracy and false alerts; $149 price makes rancher CAC hard.
judges.note: Vivid unmet pain; free data; vet and extension channels; cheap to pilot this frost season, though tiny ticket.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small-pond satellite accuracy unproven; ranchers rarely pay; ceiling well under venture scale.
judges.note: Non-obvious, feasible via vets, loss-avoidance framing; niche and feature-like.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small ARPU; 10 m imagery may not detect blooms in one-acre ponds.
judges.note: Sells 'don't lose cows' via vets, open CyFi model, in-season now; vet-confirmed cases compound. Small prize.

title: The Recorder's Rulebook: Avalara for the Recording Counter
one_liner: A verified, machine-readable rulebook and fee oracle for every recording jurisdiction, with a preflight checker that tells you a document will be rejected before you send it.
cluster_name: Home closings, condo boards and HOAs tangled in title and records rules

judges.fatal_flaw: Building 3,600-county dataset is a grind; e-recording vendors already embed checks
judges.note: Genuine rejection pain but $1-3 per check and occasional users; slow data moat before meaningful revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Occasional submitters pay little; big title firms use runners.
judges.note: Boring verified county rulebook is a real dataset moat; small prize and weak why-now.

judges.fatal_flaw: Total market may cap at tens of millions; county-by-county data build is slow.
judges.note: Boring verified dataset with clerk cooperation, occasional-submitter pain and embed path into closing platforms; defensible but modest prize.

title: Pre-Cut Electrical Kits Per House Plan
one_liner: A regional kitting shop ships each production home's wiring as pre-cut, labeled, bundled kits so a helper pulls and a journeyman only terminates and inspects.
cluster_name: Small builders' crew coordination, permits and speed

judges.fatal_flaw: Electrical subs resist workflow change; supply houses already offer kitting on thin margins
judges.note: Real labor-arbitrage pain and cheap start, but few subs per metro and per-plan engineering limits scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Electrical distributors like Graybar or Rexel can copy kitting; thin moat.
judges.note: Clear ROI, fast first customers, labor-gap tailwind; prefab for residential wiring is under-served.

judges.fatal_flaw: Electrical distributors already kit; low defensibility and licensing rules limit unlicensed pulling
judges.note: Journeyman-minutes insight is sound and concrete; residential prefab is real but easily copied.

title: Audit-Proof Records for CDL Training Schools
one_liner: A compliance layer that captures entry-level driver training records as training happens, so legitimate CDL school owners survive FMCSA registry purges and audits.
cluster_name: Colleges and training programs under new federal loan caps and earnings tests

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable market; some customers are the fraudsters the crackdown targets.
judges.note: Frightened, scrapeable, named buyers and fast first sales. Modest prize; the carrier graduate-verification network is speculative.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny universe of schools, and the crackdown is temporary while FMCSA may build tooling.
judges.note: Reachable buyers and acute fear give fast first sales, but the SaaS ceiling is low and pain is transient.

judges.fatal_flaw: Modest TAM; owners are cheap, marginal operators; FMCSA rules may shift.
judges.note: Frightened owners on a scrapeable public list, existential pain, $1,500 audit packages sellable in weeks.

title: The 40 Days: Postpartum Confinement Caregiver Guild
one_liner: A trained, insured, tradition-certified caregiver guild delivering the 26 to 42 day postpartum confinement (yuesao, sanhujori, cuarentena) to diaspora families whose grandmothers are far away.
cluster_name: Diaspora families managing death, care and property across borders

judges.fatal_flaw: Labor-intensive services with thin margin; limited venture-scale expansion path.
judges.note: Real cash demand and $5-12k tickets in an unprofessionalized market; feasible quickly, but service-business ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Labor-heavy 30-35% margin and W-2 caregiver liability limit scaling.
judges.note: Proven cash market, $5.5-12k tickets, reachable via WeChat groups. Professionalized caregivers are the wedge. First families come fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin service margin, caregiver supply and worker-liability risk
judges.note: Real diaspora demand and a guild angle, but labor-heavy, informal-market service with hard scaling and trust economics.

title: White-Label Camera Forensics for Cities and Schools
one_liner: Scan municipal and school camera, recorder and IoT fleets to unmask white-labeled hardware with covered Hikvision or Dahua internals and produce grant-ready compliance attestations and phased replacement plans.
cluster_name: City and county governments: thin staff, grants and vendor oversight

judges.fatal_flaw: Government and school buyers move slowly; urgency only appears at grant audit
judges.note: Concrete compliance trigger, free scanner as lead-gen, grant-funded $5k audits sold via integrators and grant writers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small one-off audit market; security scanners can add Section 889 lineage checks.
judges.note: Real grant-driven compliance need and a fingerprint moat, but a narrow buyer set.

judges.fatal_flaw: Audits are discretionary, so budgets stay small and integrators resist exposing their own past sales.
judges.note: Compliance is set by the chip, not the label. Real NDAA and grant enforcement, and a fingerprint-database moat.

title: Insurability Index and Tax-Base Hedge for Towns
one_liner: Measure insurance withdrawal town by town, then hedge municipal property-tax bases against it.
cluster_name: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: Hedge needs insurance license and ILS capital; index buyers unproven at $10-50K
judges.note: Good insight and public data, but muni buyers are slow and the year-two hedge is a capital miracle.

judges.fatal_flaw: Muni buyers are unproven, and the parametric tax-base hedge is unrealistic in year two.
judges.note: Insurability as tax-base risk is a real shift, but muni finance is slow. The public-data index is a feasible start.

judges.fatal_flaw: Muni analysts have small budgets; parametric hedge needs ILS capital and regulatory approval.
judges.note: Insurance withdrawal is the real transmission channel into tax bases. Public-data index is cheap to build, with a hedge upside.

title: Peptide Assurance Mark for Clinics and Processors
one_liner: Independent lot testing and supplier audit with a QR-verifiable mark that lets peptide sellers pass payment-processor and insurer underwriting.
cluster_name: Recovery-studio and peptide businesses needing safety evidence and insurability

judges.fatal_flaw: Certifying a gray-market category invites regulatory reversal; processors may still refuse.
judges.note: Trust-and-testing picks-and-shovels for a booming category. Revenue starts fast; the payments-bottleneck insight is real but unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Legal status unsettled; processors unlikely to accept a third-party mark quickly.
judges.note: Blind-purchase report is a smart hook and clinics may pay for testing; the processor thesis is slow and uncertain.

judges.fatal_flaw: Processors may not accept a third-party mark; certifier liability and shifting FDA status
judges.note: Processors as hidden buyer is non-obvious; blind-purchase audit is a cheap, PR-friendly wedge in a hot 2026 category.

title: Pay-on-Pass: Inspections Trigger Sub Payments
one_liner: Same-day payment to framers and foundation crews the moment the city inspection clears, financed against the builder's draw.
cluster_name: Small builders' crew coordination, permits and speed

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit risk and fragmented municipal portals; construction-payments fintechs already exist.
judges.note: Inspection pass as payment trigger is clever and one metro is enough to start. Needs a credit line; crowded adjacent fintech.

judges.fatal_flaw: Construction payments are crowded and the real delay is the builder's cash, not the inspection.
judges.note: Inspection pass as verified payment trigger is clever, but it collapses into subcontractor factoring with credit risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs lending capital and credit risk; builders benefit from float and resist paying faster.
judges.note: Clever verified-milestone trigger and a sub-paid instant-pay option, but this is fintech with capital needs. Pilot possible in one metro.

title: The Neutral Verdict on Dad's Driving
one_liner: An independent on-road evaluation of an aging parent's driving that gives adult children a credentialed Green, Yellow or Red verdict, plus a graduated plan so nobody has to be the villain about the keys.
cluster_name: Adult children managing aging parents from afar

judges.fatal_flaw: Scarce credentialed evaluators, liability exposure, and parents refusing evaluation
judges.note: Third party absorbing blame is real insight; robotaxi off-ramp is new; supply and liability cap scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs credentialed OTs and liability coverage; existing driver-rehab programs already offer similar evaluations
judges.note: Emotional pain families will pay $349 for, reachable through elder-law and care-manager referrals. Ten paid evaluations are easy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Evaluator supply is scarce, liability is high, and the B2B payer path is speculative.
judges.note: Original consumer insight (a third party absorbs the blame) with real willingness to pay. Hard to scale and low defensibility.

title: Pull-the-Plug Testing for Hospitals and Water Plants
one_liner: Bring data center-grade full-facility blackout testing to hospitals, water utilities and other critical facilities that never actually pull the plug, and help them source scarce backup gear the AI build-out has hoarded.
cluster_name: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Hospitals fear a failed test more than a failed storm; long sales cycles.
judges.note: Data center commissioning discipline applied to under-tested critical facilities is smart. Services-heavy, insurer channel unproven, gear resale is a distraction.

judges.fatal_flaw: Inducing an outage at a hospital creates liability; NFPA 110 testing already required.
judges.note: Data-center IST discipline applied to critical facilities is a sharp transfer; stranded-gear sourcing claim is shaky.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hospitals fear a failed test and the liability, so the sales cycle is long.
judges.note: Large ticket with existing NFPA testing budgets. Load-bank capital and gear-sourcing side quest distract, and reaching directors is slow.

title: Polling-Agent Payroll With Proof-of-Presence Release
one_liner: Pay each party or observer polling-unit agent directly, releasing money only after a geo-fenced arrival selfie and a result-sheet photo, so nothing gets skimmed on the way down.
cluster_name: Informal finance and payment frictions in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Partisan-payment legal and reputational risk; revenue lumpy around four-year election cycles.
judges.note: Sharp deadline and leakage insight, but political-finance toxicity and small recurring base.

judges.fatal_flaw: Vote-buying perception, political-legal exposure and coordinator resistance; one-off election-cycle revenue.
judges.note: Hard deadline, existing allowance budgets, clear fraud-reduction pain, pilotable in weeks; fee revenue modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Skim layers are political patronage; vote-buying accusations and legal risk for a payments platform.
judges.note: Original, deadline-forced fraud-reduction wedge. Buyers may not want transparency, and demand is one-off electoral.

title: Certification-Ready OS for Sober Living Operators
one_liner: Software and audit-readiness for independent recovery residences, so the good operators become visible, certified and eligible for opioid-settlement and referral funding.
cluster_name: Behavioral health and addiction care capacity

judges.fatal_flaw: Small, low-budget operators cap ARPU and the total market at tens of millions
judges.note: State mandates force certification. Selling software to operators and dashboards to funders is a clean model, and the trust data compounds.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small operators have thin budgets and few competitors' switching costs.
judges.note: Mandatory certification in Ohio and Virginia creates budget, reachable via state associations. Clean EKRA-aware model; modest ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small sober-living operators are cash-poor and spreadsheet-loyal; slow willingness to pay.
judges.note: Certification mandates give a real wedge and the no-referral-fee rule is smart, but vertical SaaS is incremental.

title: Independent Conformance Bench for CMS-0057-F APIs
one_liner: A testing-and-attestation service that runs the open-source Inferno and Da Vinci test kits against a health plan's real FHIR APIs and produces the evidence pack its compliance officer needs before January 2027.
cluster_name: Health-tech and device makers needing regulatory-grade validation evidence

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time compliance event; enforcement lax and consultancies or vendors can offer same testing.
judges.note: Sharp deadline timing and independence framing, but it is a services play on a fading window.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time compliance spike; becomes a consultancy that FHIR firms replicate.
judges.note: Very fast to paying customers with a hard deadline, but services-shaped, niche and short-lived demand.

judges.fatal_flaw: Plans may accept vendor attestation, since CMS does not mandate independent third-party testing.
judges.note: Hard Jan 2027 deadline, compliance budget, open-source tooling; independence sells; 3 pilots by year-end realistic.

title: AI-Use Attestation to Keep SMB Liability Cover
one_liner: As liability policies exclude generative AI, small firms need underwriter-ready proof of AI controls to win affirmative cover, and independent agencies need a renewal ritual that keeps them relevant.
cluster_name: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers haven't defined accepted evidence; agencies are slow adopters at low ARPU.
judges.note: Insurer-driven compliance pull like Coalition's scans; agency channel is unusual; must win a standard-setting race.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers may never accept a third-party attestation; chicken-and-egg with underwriters.
judges.note: ISO gen-AI exclusion is a live shift; standardizing the evidence artifact via independent agencies is a clever, unusual channel.

judges.fatal_flaw: No carrier has committed to accept the attestation, so it has no proven value
judges.note: Timely exclusion trend and agency channel, but chicken-and-egg evidence standard and crowded AI-compliance space.

title: Verified Gig Work History via Data-Access Rights
one_liner: Use statutory data-access requests as an API to pull couriers' and drivers' records from platforms, and issue a verified work-history credential they can carry to landlords, lenders and rival platforms.
cluster_name: Gig, tipped and cash workers unable to prove income

judges.fatal_flaw: Platforms slow-walk data requests; lenders' willingness to pay per pack unproven.
judges.note: 'The statute is the API' is a clever, non-obvious wedge with a Platform Work Directive tailwind, but EU/UK-only and slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Payers (landlords, lenders) have weak urgency; slow DSAR turnaround; income-verification incumbents exist
judges.note: Neat statute-as-API insight, but the buyer is fragmented and users are free.

judges.fatal_flaw: Platforms may stall or degrade DSAR responses, and bank-data income verification substitutes.
judges.note: Statute as API is a sharp insight. Platform Work Directive deadline is a real catalyst; Plaid-for-gig-work ceiling.

title: Contingency-Fee 45F Childcare Tax Credit Shop
one_liner: An R&D-credit-style boutique that finds, structures and files the newly expanded employer childcare credit (40%, or 50% for small businesses, capped at $500k/$600k) for firms already spending on childcare.
cluster_name: Childcare shortage: providers, buildings and employer funding

judges.fatal_flaw: Few mid-market employers have qualifying childcare spend; big CPA firms will crowd in.
judges.note: Fresh 2026 credit expansion and know-how gap are real, but contingency credit shops are a familiar template.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs credible tax counsel and a long diagnostic cycle; R&D-credit boutiques could add 45F.
judges.note: Found-money contingency fee, $40-50k per deal, hard Q4 budget timing, CPA channel, no upfront cost to buyer.

judges.fatal_flaw: Boutique tax-credit services capped by few eligible employers; low scalability and no moat.
