judges.note: Timely credit expansion and contingency fees give quick revenue, but it is a consulting shop, not a venture-scale business.

title: Neutral Legacy Animal-Data Vault for NAM Validation
one_liner: A neutral data trust that turns pharma's shelved animal-study results into blinded concordance benchmarks organoid and organ-chip makers use to prove their methods are 'adequately validated.'
cluster_name: Health-tech and device makers needing regulatory-grade validation evidence

judges.fatal_flaw: Pharma won't pool proprietary data; NAM startups can't fund $20-100K reports.
judges.note: Clever archive-as-yardstick insight, but slow, credibility-gated, cash-poor buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pharma may not pool proprietary data; public-only benchmarks are replicable by NAM startups.
judges.note: Contrarian: animal data becomes scarce ground truth as testing declines. Timed to FDA shift; moat only if contributors join.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pharma may not contribute data; FDA may not recognize a private benchmark.
judges.note: Legacy animal data as fixed scarce ground truth is sharp; FDA rule lands this week; sellable from public data.

title: Driver-Sourced Dock Queue Index for Funds
one_liner: Pay verified truckers to report what they see at plants, ports and distribution centers, and sell the resulting real-economy index to funds, credit analysts and site-selection teams.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Funds need backtested history and clean compliance, so paying subscribers take far beyond six months.
judges.note: Novel data category with good driver-side economics. MNPI questions and long alt-data sales cycles hurt.

judges.fatal_flaw: MNPI or carrier-contract legal risk, and driver panel too thin for statistically credible indices
judges.note: New alt-data category from a unique human panel; buyers already pay, backtestable, cheap to seed, and defensible as the panel grows.

judges.fatal_flaw: Signal quality, coverage and MNPI legal risk stall funds that need long backtests.
judges.note: Human-observed dock data is a novel category, but funds won't pay without history and compliance comfort.

title: Vacant Inherited-Home Insurance and Caretaking
one_liner: A bundled insurance-plus-sensors-plus-caretaker program for the house that sits empty during probate.
cluster_name: Houses caught in death, divorce or care transitions

judges.fatal_flaw: Surplus-lines vacancy cover and MGA licensing slow launch; cover already exists in some form
judges.note: Huge inheritance wave with an acute uninsured gap and reachable attorney and funeral-home channels; insurance execution is the hurdle.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs vacant-dwelling carrier capacity plus local caretaker field ops per market.
judges.note: Genuine coverage gap at death, probate-attorney channel, clear fees; local ops and insurance licensing slow scaling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Surplus-lines vacant-dwelling cover already exists; executor advances need scarce capital.
judges.note: Real coverage gap at death with probate-attorney distribution, but insight is modest and differentiation from existing vacant policies thin.

title: Smell Graders for Recycled Plastic
one_liner: A network of trained human noses that gives every batch of post-consumer recycled plastic an odor grade from 1 to 5, creating the price tier and spec that brands need to hit recycled-content mandates.
cluster_name: Recycling quality, distressed capacity and battery/EPR compliance

judges.fatal_flaw: Incumbent testing labs and slow standard adoption; per-batch fees are tiny.
judges.note: Clever standard-setting angle riding EU recycled-content rules, but a low-ticket, slow-to-adopt sensory service.

judges.fatal_flaw: Batch-grade revenue is tiny; buyers may keep in-house or existing odor standards.
judges.note: Non-obvious: whoever standardizes odor sets PCR price tiers, timed to EU PPWR. Quirky, cheap to start, standard-setting upside.

judges.fatal_flaw: Recyclers have thin margins and no brand-backed standard yet; free pilots delay revenue.
judges.note: Odor is a real PCR barrier and EU mandates help, but standard-setting is a slow game.

title: Critical-Error Benchmark for Legal Transcription AI
one_liner: An independent, reporter-built test suite that scores transcription AI on the errors that lose cases, such as dropped negatives, swapped numbers, wrong speaker and uh-huh versus huh-uh. Court and law-firm buyers pay for procurement reports, and vendors pay for certification.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow court procurement, and vendors pay only if buyers demand the certification.
judges.note: Sharp insight and cheap start, but small buyer pool and independence conflict from vendor-paid certification.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny customer set; vendor-paid certification creates credibility conflicts.
judges.note: Reporter-built critical-error benchmark is insightful and quick to start, but it is a niche evaluation shop, not a large company.

judges.fatal_flaw: Niche prize; vendors may game the benchmark or fund rival audits.
judges.note: WER hides dropped negatives; reporters are natural auditors. Cheap to start, procurement-timed, generalizes to other high-stakes transcription.

title: Scam-Spell Breakers: Human Callbacks for Seniors
one_liner: A human 'callback' service in which ex-call-center agents are trained to talk older customers out of scams, sold to credit unions and community banks as a per-member protection benefit.
cluster_name: Seniors targeted by impersonation scams and the institutions that bear the losses

judges.fatal_flaw: Banks resist paying per-call human costs; privacy and liability slow the sale to community banks.
judges.note: Rapport-not-detection is a known framing; real pain but the services model scales poorly and sales cycles are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Bank vendor-risk reviews and hold liability push first revenue past six months.
judges.note: Huge senior-fraud losses, crisp dollars-saved ROI, human rapport wedge. Credit-union sales cycle is the drag.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-intervention pricing may not cover human labor; credit union sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: Human rapport is the missing layer. ROI is crisp for a CFO, though it is a labor-scaled service.

title: Reliance Ratings for SOC 2 Reports and Auditors
one_liner: A buyer-paid forensic desk that tells vendor-risk teams how far to trust a given SOC 2 or ISO report, and the audit firm that signed it.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Defamation exposure rating audit firms; unclear willingness to pay per report
judges.note: Timely Delve fallout, buyer-paid reversal of vendor-paid audits; TPRM budgets exist but a free-data-for-verification model yields little cash.

judges.fatal_flaw: TPRM teams pay little per report; Delve news-cycle urgency fades; defamation risk from audit firms.
judges.note: Rating agency for auditors is a real conflict-of-interest fix, but the buyer's willingness to pay is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: SOC 2 reports are NDA-bound, so the corpus is hard to build; auditors may sue over ratings.
judges.note: Bond-rating analogy for buyer-paid audit quality; Delve fallout gives a real trigger and a cheap start.

title: L-Band Radar Watchdog for Small Levee Districts
one_liner: Turn free NISAR L-band radar into monthly, engineer-stamped settlement and seepage alerts for the small local districts that own most of America's levees.
cluster_name: Novel environmental and infrastructure data from satellites and crowd-sensing

judges.fatal_flaw: 10 m NISAR pixels may not resolve narrow levee slumps; slow district buyers
judges.note: Original timing on free L-band data and stamped-trigger insight, but technical validity and slow public sales.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small, slow-buying districts and a roughly 10 m pixel barely resolve narrow levees.
judges.note: Fresh NISAR L-band timing and an engineer-stamped trigger are clever, but the customer is poor and the market small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny district budgets, slow boards, and false-alert liability limit early revenue.
judges.note: NISAR L-band went free July 2026; the engineer-stamped trigger, not the data, is the product. Sharp why-now.

title: Beneficiary-Funded Dynamic Line Ratings
one_liner: Skip the utility's missing incentive: let the data center or generator that needs capacity pay for dynamic line ratings and take a slice of the capacity released.
cluster_name: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility must accept ratings, and interconnection cycles run years.
judges.note: Clever customer-funded structure and real pain, but a utility gatekeeper and DLR vendors slow the first ten customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility acceptance of ratings plus incumbent DLR vendors can cut out the middleman.
judges.note: Customer-funded reframe is genuinely clever and the prize is large, but reliability gatekeepers slow first revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility must accept the ratings and has no incentive; DLR vendors can sell to beneficiaries directly.
judges.note: Beneficiary-pays structure is smart and the prize is large, but utility acceptance and capital needs slow a 6-month start.

title: Dementia Desk: Ex-Aide Call Center for Banks
one_liner: A remote call-center pod staffed by former dementia aides, taking the confused, repeat and possibly scammed callers that credit unions and utilities cannot handle.
cluster_name: Seniors targeted by impersonation scams and the institutions that bear the losses

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit union vendor due diligence and member-data sharing slow any pilot.
judges.note: Original labor-supply insight and real fraud-loss budget; compliance onboarding makes early sales slower than pitched.

judges.fatal_flaw: Banks reluctant to hand vulnerable callers and PII to third party; low warm-transfer volume.
judges.note: Unusual ex-aide labor supply and de-escalation skill; easy pilot, but BPO ticket size and adoption are modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low call volume per credit union and PII/privacy limits on warm transfers to third parties.
judges.note: Turns lost home-aide labor into a premium BPO skill; cheap pilot, Senior Safe Act hook, credit unions reachable via leagues.

title: Mod-Approved Human Panels for Rare Audiences
one_liner: A research-recruitment service that turns Reddit's hardest-to-reach niche communities into bot-proof, mod-approved survey panels, with participants paid directly and the community getting the results back.
cluster_name: Gatekeepers drowning in AI-generated submissions and bot responses

judges.fatal_flaw: Depends on Reddit's terms and mods, and User Interviews and Prolific compete.
judges.note: Bot-proof rare panels is real pain, but two-sided marketplace with platform dependency and slow supply build.

judges.fatal_flaw: Reddit API and mod dependence; researchers already buy rare respondents from User Interviews and Respondent
judges.note: Mod approval plus tenure as an anti-bot screen is contrarian and matches PNAS agent findings. Reddit platform risk is real.

judges.fatal_flaw: Dependent on Reddit mod goodwill and API terms; services-heavy margins.
judges.note: Provable-human respondents is a real buyer fear. Mod-approved tenure screen is clever, but the supply channel is fragile.

title: Lot Vault: Reagent Warranty Claims and Lot Registry
one_liner: A photo-the-label app that files unclaimed reagent-guarantee refunds for labs, quietly builds the only lot-level reagent performance database, and then group-buys locked good lots for small labs.
cluster_name: Warranty claims left unfiled

judges.fatal_flaw: Small lab budgets; vendor guarantees yield replacements, not much cash.
judges.note: True bench-scientist insight and a warranty-claim Trojan horse to a lot registry; tiny prize but scrappy-feasible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Refunds and lab subscriptions are tiny; academic budgets are slow
judges.note: Clever claim-filing Trojan horse with quick ROI, but low ACV, small market, and a logistics-heavy group-buy phase.

judges.fatal_flaw: Academic labs have tiny budgets; vendors may resist a claims and lot-data layer.
judges.note: Warranty refunds as Trojan horse for a lot-level performance dataset is clever; niche scale limits the prize.

title: Lead-Refund Recovery for Home-Service Pros
one_liner: Auto-dispute junk paid leads from Google Local Services, Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp, and take a share of the credits recovered.
cluster_name: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: Lead platforms can restrict or change dispute rules, and the tool is thin and weakly defensible.
judges.note: Contingency-fee arbitrage that owners will say yes to fast. Real dollars, but it is more product than empire.

judges.fatal_flaw: Platform dispute access is partly manual and ToS-fragile; acceptance rates unproven.
judges.note: Contingency fee on money owners already lost, reachable via trade groups, ROI is instant, first 10 customers easy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Platforms can restrict or block dispute automation; per-lead credits are small.
judges.note: Easy to start and pays on contingency. Small tickets, platform dependence and near-zero defensibility.

title: Modern Lodges for Fraternal Insurers
one_liner: A Lodge-as-a-Service company that builds young-adult chapters for existing fraternal benefit societies, pairing initiation ritual and mutual aid with their insurance licence.
cluster_name: Loneliness and purpose: belonging programs for isolated adults and elders

judges.fatal_flaw: Fraternal insurers sell slowly, and Thrivent/Woodmen-style incumbents already run chapter programs.
judges.note: Most contrarian insight: cringe ritual is a legal moat; licence-for-community swap is genuinely non-obvious, large prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Building young-adult community is notoriously hard, and societies move slowly and may distrust outsiders.
judges.note: Unusual licence-for-community trade: fraternal law requires lodges. High variance and original, but CAC and cold start are unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow, conservative insurer buyers and unproven ability to recruit young members.
judges.note: Genuinely original licence-plus-community insight, but the enterprise sales cycle is long and the member CAC economics are unproven.

title: Assisted Short Sales for Underwater Auto Loans
one_liner: Record auto originations lead to record delinquencies and a repossession glut. Give lenders a mortgage-style short sale for cars that recovers more than auction does.
cluster_name: Consumer lenders' compliance and loss pressures

judges.fatal_flaw: Underwater borrowers can't cover the shortfall, so voluntary sales rarely beat repossession.
judges.note: Large real distress and a sensible port from mortgages. But the economics are unproven and credit-union sales cycles are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Underwater borrowers rarely cover shortfalls; credit-union onboarding and 50-state title work drag.
judges.note: Real repo-loss pain and plausible per-unit economics, but few borrowers can complete a sale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders' slow procurement and borrower cooperation limit volume despite performance-only pricing.
judges.note: Huge lending market, record delinquencies, mortgage short-sale playbook unported to autos; clear payer and measurable ROI.

title: Landlord Loan Radar for Office Tenants
one_liner: Monitoring and lease-audit software that warns small office tenants when their landlord's loan is heading for trouble and recovers overbilled operating expenses.
cluster_name: Small commercial tenants and renters facing landlord leverage

judges.fatal_flaw: Small tenants sign leases every 5-10 years, so churn is high and only CMBS-financed buildings are covered.
judges.note: Public CMBS deadline as leverage is a fresh angle, but it works as an add-on to contingency lease-audit firms.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small-lease overbilling recoveries are modest and audits are labor-heavy; radar is gimmicky.
judges.note: Success-fee opex audits sell without upfront risk; broker white-label channel; CMBS radar adds genuine leverage insight.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small tenants are hard to reach; only CMBS-financed buildings are visible.
judges.note: Non-obvious leverage: landlord's public refinance deadline makes a lease extension valuable; tenant-rep brokers offer a channel.

title: Fractional Licensed Qualifier for Trade-Business Buyers
one_liner: Rent a vetted master-licensed professional as the bona fide qualifying officer, so first-time buyers of HVAC, plumbing, electrical and engineering firms can get financed and keep the license alive after the seller leaves.
cluster_name: Trade-shop succession and buyouts

judges.fatal_flaw: License-lending laws in many states could invalidate the core structure.
judges.note: Acute lender-driven pain, strong $2-4K/month economics, but tiny buyer pool and legal gray zone.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rented-qualifier arrangements are illegal or unenforceable in many states; lenders may reject them.
judges.note: Credential, not capital, is the real acquisition bottleneck. Non-obvious and monetizable, but legal structure is the whole risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: License-lending rules in many states; small market and severe legal exposure.
judges.note: Credential as binding constraint in trade acquisitions is genuine insight, but tiny niche and regulatory landmines.

title: Hidden Satellite Tags Against Fictitious Pickups
one_liner: A cargo custody kit that pairs a verified-carrier check at pickup with several disposable Bluetooth-to-satellite tags hidden in each load, giving brokers and insurers evidence of where freight went when it was stolen.
cluster_name: Freight brokers, carriers and shippers: fraud, liability and disputes

judges.fatal_flaw: Hours-long sat-BLE revisit and unproven insurer premium credits
judges.note: Abundance beats stealth for tracking; fictitious pickups are a real, growing theft mode. Fresh Hubble funding, but weak defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Satellite BLE revisit takes hours; per-load cost versus proven theft prevention is doubtful.
judges.note: Real fictitious-pickup pain and insurer angle, but immature tag network and hardware dependence delay proof.

judges.fatal_flaw: Depends on Hubble's network, which has multi-hour revisit times; freight tracking is already crowded.
judges.note: Cargo theft is a large, growing problem and an insurer-evidence angle helps, but it is hardware on someone else's satellites.

title: Reefer Claim Vault for Small Carriers
one_liner: An always-on evidence recorder that captures the proof that decides cargo claims, giving small carriers and their cargo insurers a one-click defense packet.
cluster_name: Freight brokers, carriers and shippers: fraud, liability and disputes

judges.fatal_flaw: Small-carrier drivers won't sustain the ritual, and per-truck ARPU is low.
judges.note: Insurers and MGAs as distribution and payer is smart. Evidence-at-the-dock is concrete, with a measurable loss-ratio pilot.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small-carrier drivers won't consistently use the app; $30 per truck per month needs volume
judges.note: Concrete claim pain with insurers who can subsidize. The pilot has a control group, but driver adoption is uncertain.

judges.fatal_flaw: Drivers won't perform the ritual; low ARPU; insurers slow to fund.
judges.note: Real claim-evidence gap, but small ticket, behavior-change dependent, and logistics niche with modest prize.

title: Certified SDE for Sub-$1M Business Sales
one_liner: A CPA-signed, AI-prepared earnings certificate that lets brokers, buyers and SBA lenders trust a small business's seller's discretionary earnings.
cluster_name: Trade-shop succession and buyouts

judges.fatal_flaw: CPA liability and lenders refusing to rely on a third-party certificate.
judges.note: Concrete seller pain, reachable brokers, cheap per-report price, fast first revenue. Lender acceptance is the growth gate.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brokers profit from inflated SDE and CPA liability squeezes thin per-report margin.
judges.note: Real trust gap in main-street deals, easy pilot, but adoption by lenders and brokers is uncertain.

judges.fatal_flaw: CPA attest liability and lenders' refusal to rely on third-party earnings certificates.
judges.note: Trust gap in sub-$1M deals is real, but lenders decide acceptance, and QoE-lite competitors exist.

title: Collateral Condition Reports for Farm Equipment
one_liner: Use newly opened Deere diagnostics to certify used-equipment condition for lenders and auctioneers handling a farm-distress wave.
cluster_name: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Auction houses and OEM data already give lenders condition views; small per-report revenue
judges.note: Right-to-repair repurposed as collateral valuation during farm distress is clever, cheap to pilot, but prize is modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Inspection reports may not move auction prices; incumbent appraisers; niche market
judges.note: Clever use of right-to-repair for lenders, but a small inspection business on a cyclical distress wave.

judges.fatal_flaw: Independent diagnostic access to Deere data may be clunky; field-inspector labor eats thin per-report margin.
judges.note: Budgeted lender/auction buyers, distress timing, fast paid pilots, report price tiny versus collateral value at stake.

title: Orphan Bin Network: Leased Farm Storage Capacity
one_liner: Lease the thousands of idle grain bins left on consolidated and inherited farmsteads, retrofit them with cheap sensors, and run them as licensed satellite storage for co-ops.
cluster_name: Farm and ranch risks: disease, cash, storage and machinery

judges.fatal_flaw: Scattered bins need hauling; ground piles may stay cheaper than leased steel
judges.note: Storage shortfall is real and contrarian; licensed monitored steel via co-op license is clever; seasonal timing tight.

judges.fatal_flaw: Seasonal, cyclical storage shortage; per-bin economics are small and harvest timing is already tight.
judges.note: Licensed, monitored steel as the scarce asset is a nice insight, but co-op adoption is slow and the prize is modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small ARPU, single-state warehouse-law dependence, grain-spoilage liability, and harvest window already half gone.
judges.note: Real storage shortage and unusual customer; co-op sales cycles and per-bin economics modest.

title: Workforce Pell Approval-as-a-Service
one_liner: A fixed-fee desk that turns a college's short-program idea into an approved Workforce Pell application with employer-demand evidence, outcomes math and state sign-off.
cluster_name: Colleges and training programs under new federal loan caps and earnings tests

judges.fatal_flaw: Consulting-only, unscalable, and higher-ed consultancies will crowd it once approvals normalize.
judges.note: Real new gatekeeping regime with early demand, but obvious from headlines and a services business with weak defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Project consulting fades once states standardize approvals; not venture-scale.
judges.note: Acute new-policy timing and fast first customers, but a consultancy whose demand evaporates as process matures.

judges.fatal_flaw: Window may close as states standardize; approval outcomes outside your control.
judges.note: Brand-new program, only 5 approvals, colleges want the enrollment money; fixed-fee consulting closes fast with proprietary schools.

title: Bonded Claims: Bug Bounties for Product Labels
one_liner: Brands post a forfeitable bond behind a testable label claim, and anyone can buy the product, get it lab-tested and collect the bond if the claim is false.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-sided cold start; brands unlikely to post bonds; challenge gaming and lab variance.
judges.note: Original trust primitive (bug bounty for labels), potentially large, but hardest to bootstrap and legally murky.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brands that need it won't post forfeitable bonds; challengers can game it
judges.note: Interesting bug-bounty analogy, but lab variance, gaming, and the adverse-selection cold start block early brand signups.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lab variance and competitor gaming make bond-forfeiture disputes endless; brands may refuse to post bonds.
judges.note: Bug-bounty inversion: brand funds its own scepticism, so the bond signals honesty. Original, big prize, Finnrick shows crowds fund tests.

title: Capacity-Attested Wishes Recordings for Estate Attorneys
one_liner: Elder-law attorneys add a clinician-scored capacity note and a hash-sealed, attorney-controlled recording of the client's stated wishes to every will or trust signing, so heirs cannot wave the evidence away as a deepfake or as undue influence.
cluster_name: Making family estate plans fair and contest-proof

judges.fatal_flaw: Attorneys avoid recordings, and a capacity note by an NP may not persuade courts
judges.note: Clear litigation-insurance framing with per-client pricing, but slow attorney adoption and clinician-credential questions blunt the wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: Attorneys fear recordings backfiring; cross-state telehealth clinician licensing complicates delivery.
judges.note: Lucid-window capacity finding plus provenance is clever, sold as litigation insurance. Narrow channel and unproven that courts value it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Attorneys avoid recordings that could backfire; small, conservative buyer base.
judges.note: Capacity finding sold as malpractice insurance is clever, and attorney channel is reachable, but the ceiling is modest.

title: Recertified Used Transformer Exchange
one_liner: A test-and-warranty marketplace that turns utility-retired transformers into energizable supply for data centers, solar and storage projects, instead of scrap.
cluster_name: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Incumbent used-transformer dealers already arbitrage this; warranty liability and inventory capital.
judges.note: Urgent, budgeted, high-ticket buyers with schedule pain; margin per unit is real but sourcing and trust are hard.

judges.fatal_flaw: Utilities and data-center developers may reject used units; warranty and efficiency-rule liability.
judges.note: Weight-versus-lead-time arbitrage is real, but used-transformer dealers exist and this rides the consensus power-scarcity story.

judges.fatal_flaw: Utilities rarely sell serviceable units, and refurbishers like Sunbelt Solomon already exist.
judges.note: Real scarcity and clear arbitrage between scrap weight and lead time. Warranty and test layer is a credible wedge.

title: Transition Sponsor Radar for Strategic Breakthrough Awards
one_liner: A subscription and dossier service that maps each SBIR Phase II technology to the specific budget line, program office and person who could commit to a Program Objective Memorandum (POM), which the new $30M Strategic Breakthrough awards require.
cluster_name: New defense and drone suppliers: compliance and financing hurdles

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool, and value depends on personal relationships, not data.
judges.note: Clever public-data join tied to a new law, but a consulting-like info product with a small market and unproven demand.

judges.fatal_flaw: Strategic Breakthrough awards may be slow to launch and few firms can meet the 100% match.
judges.note: Budgeted via the T&BA allowance, a reachable public awardee list, a consulting-first product, and a sharp gate (POM commitment) to sell against.

judges.fatal_flaw: SBIR consultants already sell relationships; public data cannot deliver a POM commitment.
judges.note: Specific new statute makes the POM sponsor the bottleneck; buildable data join, but few awards and modest defensibility.

title: Ex-Botter Red Team for Limited Drops
one_liner: Pay former sneaker-bot users to attack your product drop before launch, then rent you the checkout filter that stops what they found.
cluster_name: Resellers and liquidators of surplus and fandom goods

judges.fatal_flaw: Indie drop brands are a tiny, sporadic market with low willingness to pay.
judges.note: Authentic wedge from botter credibility; could grow into promo-abuse and identity-multiplication defense, but starts small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small brands may not pay for anti-bot; niche is thin and Shopify apps exist.
judges.note: Service-first pentest at $750 is sellable this month via DMs; founder-market fit. Ceiling limited by small market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small ticket; Shopify order-limit apps and bot vendors exist; resellers adapt
judges.note: Authentic founder edge and real insight that bots win on identity multiplication; fast to start but small.

title: IEP-Ready Adaptive Hardware, Printed to Order
one_liner: A micro-manufacturer that acts as the approved vendor for special-education adaptive hardware, starting with custom AAC keyguards for tablets and expanding to OT-prescribed grips, switch mounts and positioning aids.
cluster_name: K-12 districts' legal service duties: IEPs, attendance, nutrition and Title I

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny per-item revenue; district sales cycles and modest ceiling.
judges.note: Procurement wrapper, not printing, is the true scarcity. Non-obvious, feasible, defensible via vendor status; small prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small niche; district vendor onboarding slow; AT incumbents and Etsy sellers
judges.note: Legally mandated spend, PO-friendly procurement wrapper, $4 cost vs $80+ price, 15 orders testable fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market; free open-source designs cap pricing power.
judges.note: Procurement-wrapper insight is sound and scrappy-feasible, but lifestyle-business ceiling.

title: Grid-Paid Spiffs for Water Heater Installers
one_liner: Make the plumber on the emergency water-heater call the distribution channel for heat pump water heaters and grid demand-response programs, with a same-day rebate stack, an electrician handoff and a per-device bounty paid to the tech.
cluster_name: Households upgrading homes: electrification, roofs and solar loans

judges.fatal_flaw: Fragmented utility programs and slow aggregator bounty payments; plumbers resist electrical handoff
judges.note: Plumber-as-channel insight is sound, but insight is known in industry and programs are patchwork.

judges.fatal_flaw: Depends on utilities or aggregators paying; slow procurement, plumbers not the payer.
judges.note: Best insight (plumber decides) but revenue hinges on slow utility and aggregator bounties and messy multi-party workflow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Aggregator and utility bounties are policy-dependent and may shrink or vary by territory.
judges.note: Plumber, not homeowner, decides at tank failure. Sharp channel insight with a grid-funded CAC. Crowded electrification space, but unusual wedge.

title: Compliance Co-op for Group-Buy Hobby Hardware
one_liner: A pooled EU compliance desk (CRA incident reporting, EU responsible person, battery/e-waste registrations, SBOM monitoring) that lets one-person keyboard, FPV, synth and LoRa hardware makers keep selling to Europe.
cluster_name: EU digital product laws for small connected-device makers

judges.fatal_flaw: Small dues pool; liability for acting as EU responsible person and CRA contact.
judges.note: Scene-level pooled compliance for micro-makers under the live CRA is genuinely non-obvious. Trust in Discords is the channel; small prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hobby makers rarely pay for compliance without visible enforcement; insured liability for unknown firmware.
judges.note: Sharp niche, Discord distribution, break-even near 40 members. Pain is deadline-driven but not yet acute or budgeted.

judges.fatal_flaw: Micro-ARPU customers; legal liability as EU responsible person exceeds dues collected.
judges.note: Perfect timing on CRA, but lifestyle-scale niche; break-even at 40 members signals tiny ceiling.

title: Certified Scrap Kill for Aircraft Parts
one_liner: A mobile crew and app that destroys, photographs and certifies scrapped aircraft parts so they can never resurface as fake 'serviceable' parts, and sells the segregated metal.
cluster_name: Aircraft and drone operators: maintenance, parts, permits and navigation

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market; airlines already have scrap procedures and won't pay for a van crew.
judges.note: Highly original niche where metal value funds the service. Retirement-wave premise is doubtful and the prize is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Airlines don't budget for it; existing aerospace scrap and destruction dealers compete.
judges.note: Near-zero out-of-pocket for buyer, metal value funds the service, physical crew is scrappy. Ops-heavy and niche, but real.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market, so hard to reach venture scale, and the mobile crew work is labor-intensive.
judges.note: Odd, non-consensus, tangible, and metal value funds the service. Certified destruction records are a real wedge but a niche.

title: PFAS Land-Application History Reports for Farmland
one_liner: A 'Phase I environmental site assessment' for PFAS on farmland, built from biosolids land-application records and upstream discharger data, sold to lenders, farmland funds and appraisers before the sensors exist.
cluster_name: PFAS exposure, testing and disposal

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders may not require it without liability rules; state biosolids records patchy
judges.note: Records-linkage beats sensors; Phase I analogy, CERCLA/EPA 2026 guidance hook, scrappy desk product, unusual customer.

judges.fatal_flaw: State biosolids records may be spotty, and lenders may not yet demand PFAS diligence.
judges.note: Phase I ESA analog for PFAS is non-obvious and timely. Slow lender adoption and uncertain records access.

judges.fatal_flaw: No lender mandate; state records access unverified; conservative slow-moving buyers.
judges.note: Record-linkage over sensors is smart, but no forcing function yet and $400 reports need volume.

title: Cash-Flow Lifeline for K-12 Service Vendors
one_liner: Same-week invoice funding for small vendors who serve schools (after-school, tutoring, therapy, van companies), priced using each district's known payment calendar, with a service-continuity guarantee for principals.
cluster_name: Cash-flow gaps from slow-paying institutions

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-intensive lending with thin spreads; district assignment friction.
judges.note: Timing-not-default insight is sound and first customers are easy, but factoring is capital-bound and weakly defensible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs $150-300k lending capital; districts often refuse notices of assignment
judges.note: Real late-pay pain and public-payer safety, but a capital-hungry factoring business with government-friction.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-hungry lending with fraud and offset risk; scale limited by balance sheet.
judges.note: Contrarian: timing risk not credit risk on tax-backed receivables. Principal confirmation owns the data. Real 2025 funding shock.

title: Night Ledger: Sleep Evidence for Live-In Aides
one_liner: A camera-free $35 bedroom-door sensor kit that logs every night-time awakening of a dementia patient, giving live-in agencies court-grade proof of sleep or interruption, and a case for the second aide.
cluster_name: Home and residential care: labor supply, family caregivers and small-scale models

judges.fatal_flaw: Sensor logs create discoverable evidence of violations against the very agency paying for them.
judges.note: Sharp buyer, live class-action urgency, $1.5-3K audit entry product; hardware and buyer-conflict slow the sale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Logging interrupted nights creates discoverable wage-liability evidence, so agencies may refuse to buy.
judges.note: Sharp legal-driven wedge in an otherwise cliche eldercare space. Sued agencies are hungry buyers, and pilots are cheap.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agencies buying sensors would create discoverable proof of back-pay liability, which they avoid.
judges.note: Timely NY wage-claim shift, but the buyer's incentives are perverse and the market is NYC-specific.

title: Notary Network for Human-Verified Hiring
one_liner: Bonded local human witnesses (mostly mobile notaries and loan-signing agents) sit with a job candidate for a phone-free live work sample and sign an attestation the employer can rely on.
cluster_name: Verifying real human skill, identity and authorship in hiring and education

judges.fatal_flaw: Few sessions per employer; small startups may not pay $200 per finalist
judges.note: Contrarian physical-witness fix to deepfake candidates; marketplace logistics heavy and per-customer volume tiny.

judges.fatal_flaw: Candidate and employer friction; post-hire laptop-farm substitution stays unsolved.
judges.note: Notaries as physical trust anchors is non-obvious and fast to test. Fraud budget helps, but low defensibility and remote-I-9 overlap.

judges.fatal_flaw: Candidate travel friction; employers may not pay $200 per session for marginal risk.
judges.note: Contrarian physical-witness answer to deepfake hiring fraud; idle notary supply; could extend to proctoring and credentialing.

title: Battery Passport Onboarding for E-Bike and Storage Makers
one_liner: Done-for-you EU battery passport, QR labelling and supplier data collection for makers of e-bikes, scooters and industrial or stationary batteries facing the 18 Feb 2027 date.
cluster_name: Recycling quality, distressed capacity and battery/EPR compliance

judges.fatal_flaw: Delegated acts may slip so buyers wait; many passport vendors already exist.
judges.note: Hard 2027 deadline, real compliance budgets, services-led EUR 8-30k tickets; supplier-chasing insight is practical.

judges.fatal_flaw: Delegated acts may slip; specialist passport vendors already exist; heavy services load.
judges.note: Real EU deadline and underserved small assemblers; buyers exist now, but it is a service-heavy compliance play.

judges.fatal_flaw: Delegated acts may slip; Circulor and other passport vendors could serve small makers.
judges.note: Real Feb 2027 deadline, and a buying club against cell makers is a neat move. Compliance services get commoditized.

title: Open-Banking Rails for EU Connected Products
one_liner: A consent-and-access hub that lets manufacturers meet the EU Data Act's access-by-design duty and lets owners route product data to repairers, insurers and energy optimizers through one integration.
cluster_name: EU digital product laws for small connected-device makers

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak enforcement means SMEs do the minimum, and the receiving-side network may never form
judges.note: Deadline passed 17 days ago and forced buyers are unprepared. Compliance kit gets first revenue, and the network is a large option.

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak enforcement lets SME makers ignore it; network side has no demand.
judges.note: Forced buyers with a live deadline; compliance kit sells first. The Plaid-for-products network is speculative.

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak Data Act enforcement; makers ship minimal endpoints; two-sided network cold start
judges.note: 'Plaid for machines' meta-pitch; compliance kit is a real deadline wedge but crowded and enforcement is weak.

title: Local-Law Radar for Data Center and Battery Developers
one_liner: A system that continuously reads city and county codes, planning agendas and minutes nationwide and warns developers which jurisdictions are drafting moratoria or new setback, noise and fire-safety rules before they pass.
cluster_name: Localities, utilities and landowners facing speculative data-center demand

judges.fatal_flaw: Scraping and LLM parsing of public agendas is easily copied; coverage moat is thin.
judges.note: Buyers can afford it and results arrive fast, but this is the predictable AI-reads-public-documents play with only curation for defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Scraping thousands of messy jurisdictions is costly and civic-data rivals may cover it.
judges.note: Developers with real budgets lose stranded land options; leading-indicator alerts and a free tracker give a fast path to ten subscribers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded LLM-on-agendas pattern; low defensibility once scraping is commoditized.
judges.note: Leading-indicator value is real and developers pay, but it is the first idea for siting fights.

title: Contingency Collection for Small-Claims Winners
one_liner: Post-judgment enforcement for the $500-$10k creditor who won in court but cannot collect: skip-trace, levy and garnishment paperwork done for a percentage.
cluster_name: Unclaimed money: settlements, refunds, penalties and unpaid invoices

judges.fatal_flaw: Collection-licensing burden and judgment-proof debtors squeeze contingency margins.
judges.note: Large real gap, fast to first revenue, but old industry with weak why-now and modest insight.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small judgments, slow uncertain recoveries and per-state licensing make contingency economics and cash flow thin
judges.note: Easy to find customers with judgments, but you fund the work and wait months for maybe 30% recoveries.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low recovery rates against judgment-proof debtors wreck contingency unit economics; licensing hurdles.
judges.note: Huge uncollected-judgment pool and automatable middle segment, but collections are grinding and state-by-state regulated.

title: Listing Bodyguard: Scam-Listing Takedown for Property Managers
one_liner: Continuously scans the web for scam copies of a property manager's listings and takes them down, and gives real prospects a fast way to verify that a listing is legitimate.
cluster_name: Small firms and property managers defending against fraud and impersonation

judges.fatal_flaw: Low ARPU, and platforms or syndication vendors can absorb it as a feature
judges.note: Real top-of-funnel leak with a manual-audit sales pitch. Buyer is clear and the first sale is fast. Ceiling is modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Facebook Marketplace unsearchable and platform takedowns unreliable, so results may underwhelm.
judges.note: Audit-led pitch shows live scams; B2B subscription with reachable marketing buyers; cheap reverse-image build.

judges.fatal_flaw: Takedowns depend on platform cooperation; property managers may value it lightly.
judges.note: Frames scam listings as a lead leak. Scrappy audit-as-pitch, but modest prize and easy to copy.

title: Dealer-Fee Decoder for Solar and Home Loans
one_liner: Use the auto F&I trick of hiding the buy-down in the price to expose the hidden 'dealer fee' inside 0% and low-rate solar, HVAC and roofing loans, then sell the evidence to consumer lawyers and the refinance to credit unions.
cluster_name: Households upgrading homes: electrification, roofs and solar loans

judges.fatal_flaw: Implied cash-price estimates may not survive court scrutiny; case volume unproven.
judges.note: Plaintiff firms with live solar-loan intake pay per screen today; credit-union takeout bounty adds a second revenue leg.

judges.fatal_flaw: Counterfactual cash price is noisy, and lawyers need expert testimony, not $99 screens.
judges.note: Dealer-fee mechanics are known to advocates. Law-firm screening is a real niche, but the solar loan market is shrinking.

judges.fatal_flaw: Dealer fees are often disclosed; law firms may not pay per screen.
judges.note: F&I insight yields a cash-price counterfactual; plaintiff intake plus credit-union takeout bounty is a workable wedge.

title: Fill the Empty EU Wallet: Payroll Attestations
one_liner: Issue consented, selectively disclosed employment-and-income attestations from payroll systems into EU Digital Identity Wallets, sold per verification to rental platforms, lenders and landlords fighting AI-forged payslips.
cluster_name: Gig, tipped and cash workers unable to prove income

judges.fatal_flaw: Revenue depends on wallet adoption and payroll-vendor integration; open-banking income checks already exist.
judges.note: Timely regulatory gap, but two-sided cold start, long enterprise cycles, and incumbents in income verification.

judges.fatal_flaw: EU wallet adoption may lag, leaving relying parties with no reason to require it.
judges.note: Income verification is a huge category, the deadline is hard, and the issuer supply side is a real gap. Pre-wallet QR revenue de-risks it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Wallet adoption uncertain; open-banking income verification and payroll vendors already compete.
judges.note: Issuer-supply gap for EU wallets is a real insight, but long enterprise cycles and crowding from identity vendors slow it.

title: Advance Hotels Their Stuck OTA Payouts
one_liner: A neutral lender advances 90-95% of completed-stay OTA payouts on checkout day for a flat 1.5-2% fee, so independent hotels stop financing the OTAs.
cluster_name: Cash-flow gaps from slow-paying institutions

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs cheap capital and OTA data access; Booking or Expedia can offer advances themselves.
judges.note: Clever unpriced-collateral insight and quick manual test, but capital-intensive lending where the OTAs hold the data.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs warehouse-line capital; OTA payout assignment and post-checkout chargeback or fraud risk
judges.note: Merchant model made hotels unpriced OTA lenders. Near-risk-free receivables nobody packages. Manual pilot is feasible with small capital.

judges.fatal_flaw: OTAs control payout accounts, so repayment is hard to secure; needs lending licences.
judges.note: Fee economics work on short paper and EUR 400K is modest, but repayment control and licensing drag.

title: Evacuation Lift Registry Ending Double-Booked Buses
one_liner: A neutral county-level registry that guarantees each ambulance, wheelchair van and bus seat is promised to only one nursing home per storm, paid for by facilities and by carriers who finally get standby retainers.
cluster_name: Heat, fire and evacuation protection for vulnerable people

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers are cash-poor nursing homes and grant-funded counties with slow sales; the registry needs density.
judges.note: Genuinely original insight that unique promises are the shortage, not vehicles; strong pilot wedge, weak willingness to pay.

judges.fatal_flaw: Multi-sided marketplace with slow county buyers and seasonal urgency
judges.note: Sharp insight about double-promised lift, but needs facilities, carriers and counties before value appears.

judges.fatal_flaw: Facilities and counties pay slowly; value only shows during a storm, grant-dependent
judges.note: Real non-obvious insight: unique promises, not vehicles, are scarce. Hand-built overlap heat map is a sharp wedge; FEMA shift anchors it.

title: Fake-Support Scam Takedown for Fintechs
one_liner: A monitoring and takedown service that finds scammers posing as your customer support in public help threads, clusters them by phone, WhatsApp and Telegram identifiers, and kills them fast with regulator-ready evidence files.
cluster_name: Small firms and property managers defending against fraud and impersonation

judges.fatal_flaw: Brand-protection incumbents can add this; social platform data access is fragile.
judges.note: Identifier-graph insight plus EU liability shift gives real dollar value; sharp wedge with free exposure audits.

judges.fatal_flaw: Depends on Reddit data access; entrenched brand-protection vendors compete.
judges.note: Free exposure audit is a sharp outbound wedge; EU liability gives fintech fraud heads a budget.

judges.fatal_flaw: Doppel, ZeroFox, Netcraft already sell takedowns; Reddit data access is fragile.
judges.note: Identifier-graph insight is decent, but brand-protection space is crowded and PSR liability tailwind is slow.

title: Death Certificate Sign-Off Copilot for Hospices
one_liner: Get physicians to complete valid cause-of-death certifications in hours instead of days, sold to the hospices and care groups that get blamed for the delay, with funeral homes as the free wedge.
cluster_name: Hospice, dying and the first weeks of bereavement

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-certificate revenue pool is small, and EDRS integration and hospice sales cycles are slow
judges.note: Clever free funeral-home wedge and a real unowned workflow, but it is a narrow feature with a small ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small per-certificate revenue pool, and state EDRS systems limit integration.
judges.note: Sell-backwards GTM from a free funeral-home chase tool is clever. Post-death workflow orphan is real but modest in size.

judges.fatal_flaw: Free funeral-home wedge does not pay; hospice buyers need BAAs and slow procurement.
judges.note: Real daily pain, clever sell-backwards wedge via funeral homes. Monetization arrives late and the buyer is slow.

title: Tariff Forward Curve for Section 232 Lists
one_liner: A probability feed for which HTS codes join the next Section 232 lists, with parametric hedges to follow.
cluster_name: Tariff cost, classification and customs for small importers

judges.fatal_flaw: Section 232 outcomes are politically driven, so forecast accuracy is unprovable and trade counsel compete.
judges.note: Non-crowded forecasting angle with parametric or event-contract upside; small buyer pool at first.

judges.fatal_flaw: Too few past inclusion rounds and political discretion make the model weak.
judges.note: Forecasting docketed 232 inclusions is a contrarian claim on a live 2026 channel, but the sample is tiny.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few historical inclusion rounds and political decisions make forecast accuracy unprovable.
judges.note: Forecasting inclusion is a fresh angle with CFO budgets; cheap to pilot, but accuracy claims are hard to prove.

title: Scam-Baiting AI Fleet Selling Mule Intel
one_liner: Thousands of realistic AI victims answer scammers' calls and chats around the clock, extract the accounts and wallets they are told to pay, and hand them to the holding institutions before real victims do.
cluster_name: Banks and platforms disrupting scam networks and recovering victims' funds

judges.fatal_flaw: Banks may not act on unverified third-party mule indicators; recording-consent legal risk.
judges.note: Non-obvious proprietary data asset, pre-loss intel, speech models enable it now. Compounding honeypot data is defensible and large.

judges.fatal_flaw: Recording-consent and entrapment legal risk; bank procurement is slow and intel quality unproven.
judges.note: Novel and asymmetric, but a $10K pilot needs a proof cycle banks may never give.

judges.fatal_flaw: Mule accounts churn fast; recording-consent law and Apate-style incumbents
judges.note: Clever inversion: AI victims burn scammer labor and yield pre-loss intel; banks' willingness to pay unproven.

title: Belonging Pods to Cut Home-Care Aide Turnover
one_liner: Weekly peer pods and buddy mentors for isolated home-care aides, sold to agencies as a turnover-reduction service priced per retained aide.
cluster_name: Home and residential care: labor supply, family caregivers and small-scale models

judges.fatal_flaw: Retention lift is unproven; facilitator cost outweighs $8-15 per aide pricing.
judges.note: Turnover is the top budgeted pain for agencies and reachable via associations; pilot proves ROI but unit economics are thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Retention lift unproven and human facilitation eats thin $8-15 per aide margins.
judges.note: Retention-ROI framing unlocks real agency budget; acute shortage; measurable pilot with control; weak defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Belonging-to-retention causality is unproven and agencies have thin budgets
judges.note: Framing belonging as a retention ROI is sensible. Immigration-driven aide shortage adds urgency. Low price point and easy to imitate.

title: 72-Hour Diligence Engine for Vet Clinic Acquirers
one_liner: Upload a PIMS export and P&L and get retention cohorts, price-versus-volume decomposition and doctor-dependence risk in three days, then keep the same schema as the post-close KPI dashboard.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Small buyer pool; PIMS export mapping is messy per system and acquirers are few.
judges.note: Concrete diligence pain and $3-6k tickets, reachable buyers; but niche size and messy data integration limit scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small pool of acquirers; QoE firms or PIMS vendors could absorb this as a feature.
judges.note: Price-masking-attrition insight is real and diligence is sellable fast, but the buyer universe is narrow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny universe of buyers; QoE firms or brokers can replicate as services.
judges.note: Sharp price-versus-volume insight and dashboard upsell, but a narrow vertical tool business.

title: Retiring Masters' Exit Interviews, Funded by Employers and AI Labs
one_liner: Capture the last generation of unrecorded tradespeople as expert playbooks for their employer and consented, royalty-bearing training data for robotics and industrial-AI labs.
cluster_name: Real-world skill and object data for robot and industrial-AI builders

judges.fatal_flaw: Robotics buyers want scale and diversity; 20 hours per expert is thin and dual-sided.
judges.note: Employer-subsidized expert capture makes robot data a by-product, a clever wedge. Dataset demand is speculative and retiree supply is slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Robotics buyers of expert footage are unproven; per-expert capture is labor-intensive.
judges.note: Dual-payer structure subsidizes scarce expert data, but data-licensing demand is speculative and the knowledge-capture market is crowded with consultants.

judges.fatal_flaw: Robotics data buyers' willingness to pay is unproven; municipal budgets move slowly.
judges.note: Employer-funded knowledge capture is real, and the dataset resale is a speculative bonus; services-heavy, lumpy.

title: Fixed-Price MDR Clinical Evaluation Reports via ASReview
one_liner: A tech-enabled service that uses the open-source ASReview active-learning screener plus medical writers to deliver audit-ready literature-based Clinical Evaluation Reports at a fraction of consultant prices.
cluster_name: Health-tech and device makers needing regulatory-grade validation evidence

judges.fatal_flaw: Service margins depend on scarce regulatory medical writers; weak moat versus consultancies.
judges.note: Existing EUR 10-40k budget, 2027-28 MDR deadlines, short services sales cycle; sell reproducibility to small device makers directly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded CER consultancies; notified-body acceptance uncertain; professional liability.
judges.note: Sell reproducibility not speed is a nice angle, but it is tech-enabled consulting with thin defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded consultants plus LLM tools compress price; low-margin service, not venture-scale.
judges.note: Reproducibility-as-compliance is a good insight and deadlines are real, but EUR 4-9k tickets cap the prize.

title: Second-Look Verification for Imagery-Based Nonrenewals
one_liner: A $50-80, 48-hour human check between an aerial-imagery flag and a nonrenewal, sold to carriers' compliance teams.
cluster_name: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers may just quit imagery flags or use existing inspection networks rather than buy.
judges.note: Regulation makes a compliant second look required, but the idea is thin and per-case revenue small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers may resist added cost or build cheaper in-house remediation workflows.
judges.note: Regulation forces a human step; sits in a huge insurance market; cheap-verification wedge is sharp.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers move slowly, and imagery vendors could bundle human review themselves.
judges.note: Statute (CA AB 75) creates compliance budget; cheap 200-policy pilot proves clearance rate.

title: Lifetime Income Leases for Retiring Farmers' Water
one_liner: A 'water pension' that turns a retiring farm couple's senior Colorado River water right into guaranteed, inheritable lifetime income via a long-term forbearance lease, satellite-verified and sold as verified acre-feet to cities and corporates.
cluster_name: Water scarcity: irrigation allocation and new supply

judges.fatal_flaw: Water transfer and forbearance approvals by districts and states delay revenue; buyer demand unproven.
judges.note: Big, non-consensus reframing of water as retirement income; timely Colorado River framework and corporate money; strong supply-side insight.

judges.fatal_flaw: Water-right transfers need multi-year regulatory approval; no revenue within six months.
judges.note: Big prize and good pension framing, but slow, legally heavy, and needs buyer capital.

judges.fatal_flaw: Water-right leasing needs slow state approvals; first paid deal unlikely within six months
judges.note: Retirement-income framing unlocks supply owners won't sell; timed to Aug 2026 river framework; big prize.

title: Point-in-Time Certification for Alternative Data Vendors
one_liner: A vendor-paid, buyer-trusted forensic test that a dataset's history is genuinely point-in-time, extended to certify that an LLM-driven signal isn't leaking hindsight, plus a cheap timestamp 'witness' service.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Issuer-pays model risks a credibility collapse, and the vendor universe is small.
judges.note: Non-obvious, precise pain quants share; shifts diligence cost to vendors. Open-sourced tests build trust quickly, but the market is niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a few hundred addressable vendors; issuer-pays ratings invite credibility collapse.
judges.note: Smart arbitrage and useful witness timestamps, but a tiny market and a pay-for-grade conflict.

judges.fatal_flaw: Issuer-pays certification has credibility conflict, and few vendors will pay to be graded.
judges.note: Sharp quant pain and clever witness service, but small buyer pool and trust chicken-and-egg with funds.

title: Sewage Nielsen: Wastewater Consumption Index
one_liner: Weekly per-capita consumption of alcohol, nicotine, cannabis and caffeine, measured from metabolites in city wastewater and sold to alt-data funds and regulators as a Nielsen for vices.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Funds take 6+ months to evaluate alt-data; per-sample lab cost and unproven alpha.
judges.note: Original and large, but long sales cycles, plant agreements and lab costs preclude fast first customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak proven link from wastewater metabolites to equity returns; few alt-data buyers.
judges.note: Original, with a day-one backtest from archived samples. Niche signal, uncertain that funds pay $60-250k.

judges.fatal_flaw: Archived samples may have degraded; weak proven link between sewage signal and sales.
judges.note: Un-gameable consumption panel with a COVID-archive backtest. Idea is original, but the alpha and plant access are unproven.

title: Night Shift Tox Bulletin for Opioid Settlement Counties
one_liner: A no-patient-data network where rural ER nurses text in what they are seeing, turned into weekly local drug-supply alerts sold to counties spending opioid settlement money.
cluster_name: Behavioral health and addiction care capacity

judges.fatal_flaw: Cold-start nurse network, hospital-policy risk, and a small settlement-funded buyer base.
judges.note: Highly original human-sensor insight and timely; more public-health nonprofit than venture-scale company.

judges.fatal_flaw: County council sales cycles and unproven signal quality from volunteer nurses
judges.note: Original sensor insight and budgeted settlement funds; small tickets and slow procurement limit first-six-month count.

judges.fatal_flaw: Nurse-sourced anecdotes are unreliable, and small county ACVs come with slow sales.
judges.note: Novel human-sensor channel; medetomidine is a real shift and settlement money exists. Small prize and unproven signal quality.

title: Orphan Fleet Depot for Bankrupt-Maker Electric Buses
one_liner: Sustainment-as-a-service for school districts and transit agencies stuck with electric buses whose manufacturer went bankrupt, using the military's orphan-platform playbook (salvaged parts pool, configuration control, depot repair, availability guarantees).
cluster_name: Customers stranded when a product's maker disappears

judges.fatal_flaw: High-voltage battery repair liability, technician hiring and parts capital before revenue
judges.note: Real stranded-asset pain and fixed contracts, but small fleet count and capital-heavy depot; start as mobile service.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny addressable fleet and capital-heavy depot; districts slow and cash-strapped.
judges.note: Military sustainment playbook for orphaned buses is clever and timely, but market is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable fleet and capital needed for parts and depot.
judges.note: Military DMSMS playbook for orphaned EV buses is a smart transplant. Real pain, but the prize is small.

title: Narrow Networks and Reference Pricing for Pet Insurers
one_liner: Pet insurers reimburse whatever clinics invoice while losing about 10 points a year to price/mix inflation; build the pet-insurance 'PPO' from affordable-care clinics whose invoices run about 44% lower.
cluster_name: Pet owners and insurers squeezed by rising vet bills

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurer sales cycles are long and clinics may not discount; Trupanion-style direct-pay competes.
judges.note: Pet-insurance PPO analogy is non-obvious and real, but two-sided and slow to first revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Chicken-and-egg: insurers need clinic volume, clinics need steering; slow insurer sales.
judges.note: Smart payer-side steering insight, but few buyers, long insurer sales cycles, and no clinic volume to bargain with.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers move slowly; steering owners to in-network clinics may not shift behavior.
judges.note: Payer-side wedge in pet insurance, importing the human-health PPO lesson. A real lever nobody has pulled, with a clear savings gap.

title: Inverter-Telemetry Credit Bureau for African Solar
one_liner: Turn the cloud data that hybrid inverters and batteries already stream into a consented energy cash-flow score, so lenders, insurers and installers can finance an asset boom that official statistics cannot see.
cluster_name: Informal finance and payment frictions in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Vendor-cloud data access and consent may block scale; slow African lender sales cycles.
judges.note: Non-obvious: inverter is collateral and sensor. Huge unbanked asset boom, real 2026 shift, vendor-neutral data moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Inverter clouds control data access; lenders few; Nithio-style scorers already compete
judges.note: Telemetry as alt-credit data is smart and vendor-neutral, but access and lender-volume risk are real.

judges.fatal_flaw: Multi-country lender adoption and consent-based data access take far longer than six months.
judges.note: Novel dataset and vendor-neutral position, but distant customers, partnerships and long lender sales cycles.

title: Outside-Processing Milk Run for Job Shops
one_liner: Scheduled pickup routes and batching software for the heat-treat, plating and anodize bottleneck behind reshored machining.
cluster_name: US machine shops and reshoring manufacturers

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin route-density economics; shops can ship by carrier and vendors may bypass the milk run.
judges.note: Real bottleneck insight (queue time, not touch time). One-van pilot is scrappy and cheap, but defensibility is weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Many process vendors already run their own pickup routes; route density economics are thin.
judges.note: Real lead-time bottleneck and a one-van pilot is cheap, but low-margin logistics with heavy working-capital and density needs.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-margin regional van logistics needs route density before it works.
judges.note: Finishing is the true bottleneck and batching is a smart fix; first pilot is cheap, but hard to scale.

title: Hospice for Dying Congregations
one_liner: A managed 'final season' service for congregations that are closing, covering the closing liturgy, an oral-history archive, member placement and a community-first sale of the building.
cluster_name: Shrinking institutions with idle buildings

judges.fatal_flaw: Denominations buy slowly and closures are small-ticket, so revenue per client stays low
judges.note: Sell the funeral, earn the property fee: genuinely non-obvious wedge into stranded church real estate.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small total market and slow denominational buyers; not software-scalable.
judges.note: Emotional insight is real and unusual, but roughly a services niche with limited ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable market and denominational sales cycles; needs clergy-credible founder.
judges.note: Acute, specific pain with fee-paying buyers and a real insight, but the niche is small and trust-gated.

title: Model-of-Origin Forensics for AI Music Catalogs
one_liner: Attribute a track to the generator and version that made it, so catalog owners and litigators can separate legacy unlicensed-model output from the rest.
cluster_name: Defensible authenticity evidence for disputed digital media

judges.fatal_flaw: Legal exposure unproven; generators keep shifting, so classifiers drift and the market stays niche
judges.note: Model-of-origin is a sharper question than AI-or-not, but it looks more like a feature or a forensic consultancy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Legal exposure from legacy AI tracks is unproven; classifiers race each model update.
judges.note: Sharp wedge above 'AI or not' detectors and high price points, but demand speculative and buyer pool small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Legal exposure is unproven, and generators evolve faster than the classifier.
judges.note: Attribution to model and version prices like legal risk, not consumer AI-or-not detection; hinges on unproven liability.

title: Permit-as-Firmware Groundwater Pump Governor
one_liner: A smart pump controller that hard-enforces a farmer's groundwater allocation and lets an agent trade unused acre-feet with neighbors before the pump ever exceeds its limit.
cluster_name: Water scarcity: irrigation allocation and new supply

judges.fatal_flaw: Growers may refuse hard pump stops that risk orchard loss; installs sell slowly.
judges.note: Law turned into a physical budget, SGMA enforcement begins 2027, real dollar penalties, pump installers as a channel; GSA data is a moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hardware retrofit with slow GSA cycles; growers won't accept hard pump stops
judges.note: Real $500/AF penalty pain, but hardware, trading legality and crop-loss risk delay the first ten paying wells.

judges.fatal_flaw: Growers will resist hard pump stops, and the hardware sales cycle is slow.
judges.note: Legal budget turned into a physical budget is a sharp framing; SGMA timing fits; retrofit hardware slows first revenue.

title: Waiver-Funded Home Modification Back Office and Factoring
one_liner: Handle the prior-authorization paperwork and advance payment for small contractors who do ramps and bathroom retrofits funded by Medicaid waivers and VA grants.
cluster_name: Cash-flow gaps from slow-paying institutions

judges.fatal_flaw: Small tickets, state-by-state rules, and factoring needs credit-line capital.
judges.note: Contractor cash flow, not demand, gates funded mods; boring, credible, but modest and capital-hungry.

judges.fatal_flaw: Factoring needs outside capital, and waiver rules and payer risk vary by state.
judges.note: Proven back-office-plus-advance model; real 60-120 day cash gap; scalable only with a credit line.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-hungry factoring in fragmented state waiver programs with a small contractor pool.
judges.note: Sees contractor cash flow as the true bottleneck, but small TAM and heavy state-by-state grind.

title: Heat-Number Vault for Water-Project Compliance
one_liner: A registry that matches mill test reports to heat numbers for every pipe, valve and hydrant, producing audit-ready domestic-origin binders for SRF water projects and tariff-tier evidence for importers.
cluster_name: Brands substantiating origin, recycled-content and green claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Small engineering firms pay little; the pain is narrow and tedious to scale.
judges.note: Boring but real dual-use origin trail; feasible by hand, though the prize is modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Narrow niche with modest ARPU; compliance-document tools and consultants can absorb it.
judges.note: Real documentation pain and dual-use data for water and tariffs; small but sellable wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small engineering firms may keep doing binders by hand at low cost.
judges.note: Mandated origin paperwork gates loan disbursement, so the budget exists. Concierge at $1.5k per project sells now.

title: Orphaned Job and Membership Rescue Desk
one_liner: When a PE roll-up of contractors collapses, package its unfinished jobs, prepaid maintenance memberships and warranties and hand them to healthy local contractors, while lenders and trustees get paid for the recovery.
cluster_name: Private-equity roll-up aftermath

judges.fatal_flaw: Trustee authority over customer data and slow two-sided restructuring sales cycles
judges.note: Valuable asset is unfulfilled service obligations, not the brand. Private-credit lenders lack operators, and WARN notices are a free lead feed.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs estate authority over customer data; lumpy, slow trustee and lender sales.
judges.note: Clever asset insight and free WARN leads, but legally gated, lumpy revenue and two-sided coordination.

judges.fatal_flaw: Estate authority over customer data and lumpy, unpredictable bankruptcy deal flow.
judges.note: Original: valuable asset is unfulfilled service obligations; lenders lack ops, but episodic and legally gated.

title: Universal Robot Cone: Vendor-Neutral Keep-Out Zones
one_liner: One tap, or one cheap beacon dropped on the floor, creates a temporary no-go zone that every robot brand in the building obeys, with a log to prove it.
cluster_name: Deploying robots in the real world

judges.fatal_flaw: API-pushed keep-out zones are not safety-rated; OEMs will not cooperate or accept liability
judges.note: Neutral stop line is a sharp idea, but safety-critical and dependent on rival vendors' cooperation. Slow standards path.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs rival OEM cooperation; few sites run multi-vendor fleets yet.
judges.note: Neutral safety stop-line and liability log is an original, potentially large layer; early market and slow first customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Robot vendors' closed APIs and uncertified stop signals create safety-liability and integration blockers.
judges.note: Sharp neutral-safety insight but few multi-vendor sites; vendor cooperation and certification gate any real product.

title: Claims Desk for Government-Paid Childcare
one_liner: A medical-billing-style revenue-cycle service that turns small providers' attendance sheets into clean subsidy and universal-program claims and advances the cash within 48 hours.
cluster_name: Cash-flow gaps from slow-paying institutions

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny per-provider revenue, state-by-state rule fragmentation, incumbents like Brightwheel can bundle.
judges.note: Payer-shift RCM plus factoring for childcare is credible and doable by hand, but ARPU and fragmentation hurt.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny per-provider revenue, state-by-state rules, factoring needs outside capital
judges.note: RCM-for-childcare analogy is plausible but weakly evidenced why-now; low ARPU and lender dependence.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-state rules and small provider revenue limit ACV; advances need outside capital.
judges.note: Acute cash-flow pain, hand-run service starts with a spreadsheet, reachable via provider groups. Revenue from first claims.

title: Forensic Chat-Log Analysis for AI-Harm Lawsuits
one_liner: A court-defensible method and service that turns exported chatbot transcripts into escalation timelines, sycophancy evidence and missed-crisis reports for plaintiffs, defense counsel and regulators.
cluster_name: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a handful of cases exist; credentialed experts and academics already compete
judges.note: Timely niche with no standard method, but tiny caseload and expert-witness credibility barrier.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few cases at first; plaintiffs may prefer academic experts over a new vendor.
judges.note: Litigation wave is live; a side-agnostic validated coding method is defensible; first customers via free pilots.

judges.fatal_flaw: Expert-witness services do not scale; case volume small and lumpy.
judges.note: Timely litigation wave, side-agnostic methodology could become a standard, but essentially a forensic consultancy.

title: Layoff Early-Warning for Credit Unions
one_liner: Turns public WARN notices and layoff signals into member-level outreach lists, so lenders can offer hardship plans about 60 days before payments are missed.
cluster_name: Employers restructuring for AI: layoffs, severance and displaced workers

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit-union sales and core/ACH data integration take longer than six months
judges.note: Clever public-signal-to-book join with clear ROI, but nice-to-have and slow, compliance-heavy buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders can already see payroll ACH stopping sooner; WARN data lags and covers few layoffs.
judges.note: Plausible and sellable to credit unions, but a thin data feature with a small TAM.

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit unions are slow buyers; member-data use raises fair-lending and privacy questions.
judges.note: Public WARN data joined to payroll ACH descriptors is a cheap, sharp wedge; ROI in avoided charge-offs.

title: Sunset Software Co: Pledge-Funded Tool Revival
one_liner: When a B2B tool announces its shutdown, customers pre-commit to paid 'extended life' contracts, and a small operator takes over only if a threshold is met.
cluster_name: Customers stranded when a product's maker disappears

judges.fatal_flaw: Sporadic deal flow, tiny tools, and founder or acquirer IP limits.
judges.note: Clever pre-committed pledge de-risks the acquisition, with zero CAC and day-one revenue. Small prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny revenue per tool; customers and founders can fork or migrate instead.
judges.note: Pledge-threshold revival is inventive and low-risk, but it is a deal-by-deal portfolio business with limited scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Each dying tool is tiny revenue, and pledged customers churn once a replacement appears.
judges.note: Pledge-threshold model for tool continuity is clever and evidenced by real shutdowns. Lifestyle-scale portfolio with weak defensibility.

title: IEEPA Refund Ledger for CPAs and Controllers
one_liner: An accounting workbench that turns IEEPA refund data into correct inventory, cost-of-goods, tax and audit entries.
cluster_name: Recovering IEEPA tariff refunds and surcharges

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time refund event; CPAs already handle with spreadsheets.
judges.note: Accounting-event framing is right, but a temporary, crowded niche; duty sub-ledger expansion is speculative.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time refund event; Big Four guidance and Excel templates commoditize it fast.
judges.note: Year-end close deadline, CPA channel, $1.5K engagements sellable quickly; accounting angle nobody else covers.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time event; Big-4, CPA software and ERP vendors will commoditize the workflow fast.
judges.note: Refund as accounting event is a sharp, timely wedge with easy CPA-channel first sales, but the window is short and defensibility low.

title: Yield Twins and Robotic Cells for Regional Beef Packers
one_liner: Start with 3D vision yield scoring on the fabrication line and grow into robotic trimming cells for independent packers.
cluster_name: Skilled-trades labor gap

judges.fatal_flaw: Robotic trimming is very hard; incumbents like Marel and packer in-house systems already exist.
judges.note: Big prize with real labor and margin squeeze; software-first wedge pays before robots, but the pitch is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Conservative packers, a few hundred plants, and long trust-building before paying for camera pilots.
judges.note: Yield software pays before any robot exists, and margins are thin. The addressable customer count is small and Marel incumbents exist.

judges.fatal_flaw: Incumbent meat-processing vendors own vision and budgets at small packers are thin.
judges.note: Software-pays-first before the robot is sensible, but packers are a slow, small market and robotics is the distraction.

title: Alternative-Use Memos for Office Special Servicers
one_liner: A fixed-fee, five-day, non-conflicted resolution memo (convert, hold, sell, owner-user sale) for distressed office loans, written for the asset status report.
cluster_name: Repricing softening property markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Servicers trust established brokers and appraisers; slow credibility for unknown vendor.
judges.note: Real distress and high per-asset price, tiny buyer universe; sample memos prospect cheaply but sales are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Special servicers and directing holders may distrust outside memos; small annual deal count.
judges.note: Right buyer identified (directing certificateholder bears the loss); conflict-free alternative-use memo is a fixed-fee, quick-to-sell product.

judges.fatal_flaw: Servicers rely on appraisals and broker opinions under fiduciary norms; small, consulting-like market.
judges.note: Buyer insight (directing certificateholder) is smart and pilot is easy, but ceiling is low and repeat volume limited.

title: Insurer-Backed Self-Certified Permits for ADUs
one_liner: Japan-style private building confirmation: AI code review plus a licensed private reviewer plus an insurer-backed compliance warranty, so an ADU or small addition gets a certified package in about 48 hours where state law allows private providers.
cluster_name: Small builders' crew coordination, permits and speed

judges.fatal_flaw: MGA capacity and jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction rules could stall the insured-warranty piece.
judges.note: Huge, painful market; insurer-carried risk is a real non-consensus twist on crowded AI permitting; Florida private-provider law gives a wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: No insurer will underwrite unproven AI plan review within six months.
judges.note: Insurer-backed self-certification is a bold idea. Permit-tech is crowded and the liability chain is fragile.

judges.fatal_flaw: Depends on insurer and jurisdiction acceptance; Symbium-type incumbents already exist.
judges.note: Real permit pain and a Florida private-provider path, but insurer backing is slow and the ADU market is small.

title: 30-Day Capacity-Window Plan After Early Alzheimer's Diagnosis
one_liner: A productized sprint that uses the legally competent window after an early blood-test diagnosis to lock down legal, financial, safety and care plans.
cluster_name: Dementia and Alzheimer's care at home and in memory care

judges.fatal_flaw: Clinic referral channel is slow; attorney partnerships and referral-fee rules complicate distribution.
judges.note: Genuine capacity-window insight and fixed fee, but services-heavy and dependent on slow referral partners.

judges.fatal_flaw: Fragmented referral channel; nurse-plus-attorney service hard to scale beyond a boutique.
judges.note: Legal-capacity clock is real insight tied to blood-test diagnosis; services-heavy, consumer-paid, modest scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Elder-law firms already sell POA packages; referral channel constrained
