judges.note: Capacity-window clock is a real insight from blood tests; feasible service, but the wedge is narrow and copyable.

title: Bereavement Aftercare for Independent Funeral Homes
one_liner: A white-label 13-month aftercare program that funeral homes buy to keep the newly widowed connected after the casseroles stop.
cluster_name: Hospice, dying and the first weeks of bereavement

judges.fatal_flaw: Ceiling is modest; funeral homes are notoriously slow, price-sensitive buyers.
judges.note: Buyer owns the list and pays at the right moment; easy to start, but limited prize and copyable.

judges.fatal_flaw: Independent homes may not fund $300 per family; facilitator labor caps margin.
judges.note: Right buyer (the funeral director owns the list), but a services-heavy program with unproven ROI and modest market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Existing aftercare vendors and labor-heavy delivery squeeze margin at $300 per family.
judges.note: Funeral directors are a reachable buyer via associations, but the service is human-intensive and competes with incumbents.

title: Origin Assay: Forensic Testing of Metal Melt Origin
one_liner: A lab test that says where steel or aluminum was actually melted, so US-melt claims stop resting on paperwork alone.
cluster_name: Brands substantiating origin, recycled-content and green claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Classifier may not discriminate origin; building the mill reference library is costly.
judges.note: Real duty arbitrage, but science risk and up-front sample library defeat a six-month revenue timeline.

judges.fatal_flaw: Scrap mixing may blur fingerprints; classifier may never reach audit-defensible accuracy.
judges.note: Tariff tiers make melt origin money and proof the arbitrage. Big prize, but the science is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Chemistry may not discriminate melt origin reliably enough for legal-grade claims.
judges.note: Tariff arbitrage makes proof valuable; Oritain-style precedent and reference-library moat. High technical risk, big payoff.

title: Distributor Credit Radar for Failing Restaurants
one_liner: A weekly early-warning score on each restaurant account, built from public signals and distributors' own order and payment data, so food distributors can tighten terms before the customer goes dark.
cluster_name: Restaurants' idle hours, used oil and credit risk

judges.fatal_flaw: Distributors may not share AR data; credit-reporting incumbents already serve foodservice.
judges.note: Clear credit-manager buyer, ROI is one avoided write-off; own-order-decline signal is real insight.

judges.fatal_flaw: Distributors resist sharing AR data, and trade-credit bureaus already exist.
judges.note: Practical and sellable, and the consortium data pool is a real moat. But the insight that restaurants fail before they stop paying is mild.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small buyer base, low ACV, and distributors reluctant to pool payment data.
judges.note: Back-test wedge is credible and consortium data is a moat, but a modest prize and trade-credit insurers already exist.

title: Micropollutant Bill Calculator for Generic Drug Makers
one_liner: A dataset and model that estimates each pharma and cosmetics company's share of Europe's new micropollutant treatment bill, sold first to generic manufacturers who cannot pass the cost on.
cluster_name: Recycling quality, distressed capacity and battery/EPR compliance

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a few dozen buyers; industry bodies will fund their own allocation studies.
judges.note: Non-obvious regulatory allocation fight, but tiny buyer set, slow timeline and consultant-style revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer set, consulting-like revenue, and the scheme is not live until 2028
judges.note: Highly non-obvious: owning the allocation key dataset in a 10x-cost fight. Real UWWTD shift. Small prize, consulting-scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a few dozen buyers, slow reg-affairs cycles, and credibility depends on contested inputs.
judges.note: Real lobbying budgets and a neutral-dataset insight, but a consultancy-sized market and long sales to pharma.

title: The Weekly Mail Box for Mom
one_liner: A prepaid return envelope where a parent drops all her mail. It gets scanned, triaged, shredded, and turned into a 'what needs doing' digest for her adult child.
cluster_name: Adult children managing aging parents from afar

judges.fatal_flaw: Parents must physically mail originals; trust, liability and churn when the parent dies.
judges.note: Charming ritual-based wedge and usable manual start. Consumer CAC and high-touch operations cap scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consumer CAC and human QA labor squeeze the claimed 70% margin.
judges.note: Insightful envelope ritual, $49/month, manual launch possible, wholesale channel via money managers; trust and CAC are hurdles.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consumer CAC, privacy of opened mail and weak defensibility against mail scanners.
judges.note: Envelope-ritual insight is genuinely human and low-tech; can be run manually and charged from day one.

title: Workout GC for Stalled Spec Homes
one_liner: A finish-the-house crew and re-sequencing service sold to construction lenders, not builders, for homes stuck at 40-90% complete.
cluster_name: Small builders' crew coordination, permits and speed

judges.fatal_flaw: Taking over half-built homes brings liens, licensing, warranty liability and thin services margins.
judges.note: Selling to the lender, not the builder, is the right reframe; flat-fee triage gives a cheap first sale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-heavy GC liability, cycle-dependent, low software margin.
judges.note: Good insight to sell to lenders, but it is a low-margin construction services business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Taking on construction liability, payroll and insurance; banks buy slowly and use existing consultants.
judges.note: Lender-as-buyer insight is sharp, but operating GC work is heavy and the first paid contract in 30 days is unrealistic.

title: Good-Better-Best Estimate Engine for Vet Clinics
one_liner: AI scribes are turning into a free feature, so the money moves to the moment a client sees the estimate: automate tiered spectrum-of-care plans that turn declines into partial acceptance.
cluster_name: Pet owners and insurers squeezed by rising vet bills

judges.fatal_flaw: PIMS vendors like IDEXX can add tiered estimates natively; small per-clinic ACV.
judges.note: Revenue-at-estimate insight and decline-reason data are real, but it is a feature riding on incumbent PIMS platforms.

judges.fatal_flaw: PIMS vendors and IDEXX can bundle estimating; browser-overlay integration is brittle.
judges.note: Decision-moment revenue over scribe is sound, but it is vertical AI for vets with fast-following incumbents.

judges.fatal_flaw: PIMS integration friction and IDEXX/Covetrus bundling could squeeze a standalone overlay.
judges.note: Revenue-at-decision-moment budget line, clear SaaS pricing, success-fee alignment; decline-reason data is a real wedge.

title: Forever Guardian: Lifetime Care After Parents Are Gone
one_liner: A prepaid, life-insurance-funded successor-care plan in which a named team becomes the lifelong advocate, money manager and care coordinator for an adult with a disability after the parents are gone.
cluster_name: Solo agers without family to act as proxy, executor or guardian

judges.fatal_flaw: Lifetime care liability and state guardianship licensing make underwriting and scaling hard.
judges.note: Huge emotional market; pre-death home visit doubles as moat and funnel; insurance funding is sticky, if operationally heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lifetime care liability priced upfront needs reserves, guardianship licensing and long trust-building
judges.note: Urgent parental fear, attorney channel, Shadow Year sells early; long-tail liability is the danger.

judges.fatal_flaw: Multi-decade care liabilities are underpriced at $100-200 per month; licensing and actuarial risk.
judges.note: Real, urgent need and a good relationship-first funnel, but the promise is capital-intensive and slow to prove.

title: Celebration-of-Life Concierge Using Restaurants' Dead Hours
one_liner: A flat-fee, turnkey memorial-gathering service for families who buy a cheap direct cremation and then have to improvise a goodbye, hosted in restaurants, breweries and hotel rooms during their empty weekday hours.
cluster_name: Families choosing direct cremation with no ritual

judges.fatal_flaw: Grief-driven one-off purchases, so partner referral volume must carry acquisition.
judges.note: The ceremony unbundled from direct cremation and nobody owns it. Concierge start works, though low tech defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-margin event services; fragmented venues and providers, weak defensibility.
judges.note: Real unbundling gap after direct cremation, but a concierge-marketplace with thin moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Labor-intensive concierge; hard to reach families at decision moment
judges.note: Unowned category, partner-referral channel, decent per-event margin; scale-limited services business, but profitable early.

title: Pay-Per-Attendance Social Prescriptions for Loneliness
one_liner: A settlement layer where health systems and employers pay small local groups (Men's Sheds, choirs, walking clubs) a fixed fee for every verified attendance by a doctor-referred lonely patient.
cluster_name: Loneliness and purpose: belonging programs for isolated adults and elders

judges.fatal_flaw: Payers won't fund without proven ED savings; paid attendance invites gaming
judges.note: Paying hosts per attendance reframes loneliness, but no US reimbursement path and slow payer sales.

judges.fatal_flaw: Health-system and employer sales cycles far exceed 6 months, and ROI proof takes years.
judges.note: Paying hosts per attendance is clever, but the buyer is slow and the outcome data is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Health payers slow to buy without proven ROI; long sales cycles and attendance-outcome proof.
judges.note: SilverSneakers-style pay-per-visit for third places; turns retention into revenue. Big MA upside, non-consensus, cheap pilot.

title: Pre-Procedure GLP-1 Readiness for Endoscopy and Ortho
one_liner: A 7-day workflow plus day-of gastric ultrasound that stops GLP-1 patients from being cancelled or aspirating at surgery centers.
cluster_name: GLP-1 patients' transitions: procedures, medication changes, quitting and aftercare

judges.fatal_flaw: Anesthesia liability and clinician resistance slow adoption of a new POCUS protocol.
judges.note: Real cancellation cost and timely guideline shift, but clinical workflow change sells slowly and needs credentialed staff.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow ASC sales; nurse POCUS liability; anesthesia groups write own protocols.
judges.note: Real post-ASA-reversal operational gap sold on avoided cancellations, but standard-of-care will likely commoditize into guidelines.

judges.fatal_flaw: A feature for surgery centers; clinical liability and slow anesthesia-group sales.
judges.note: Real and timely workflow gap around GLP-1 patients at surgery. Per-case pricing is clear, but it reads more like a feature than a company.

title: Fry-Oil Co-op Escaping Evergreen Renderer Contracts
one_liner: Aggregate independent restaurants' used cooking oil, sell it to biofuel buyers at market with sensor-verified traceability, and hand the owner the check the big renderer keeps.
cluster_name: Restaurants' idle hours, used oil and credit risk

judges.fatal_flaw: Renderer contracts, small per-restaurant oil value and route density limit margins.
judges.note: Contract calendar as the growth engine is clever, and 45Z traceability helps. Per-customer economics are thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin per-restaurant economics; low urgency because owners think removal is free.
judges.note: Contract-calendar wedge is smart and founder owns test sites, but tiny tickets and sensor complexity.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin spread, route density needs collectors, and Restaurant Technologies and Darling already lock in the market.
judges.note: Renewal-calendar-as-CRM is a sharp wedge and traceability adds value, but the commodity logistics business has weak economics.

title: Royalty-Paying Archive of Master Tradespeople's Hands
one_liner: Pay retiring master electricians, pipefitters and welders to record expert egocentric video with think-aloud narration, license it to robotics companies, and share royalties with the workers.
cluster_name: Real-world skill and object data for robot and industrial-AI builders

judges.fatal_flaw: Robotics buyers resist royalty tails and few buyers concentrate demand.
judges.note: Retiring masters plus narrated data is a sharper wedge than generic crowds, but sits in the crowded expert-data pattern.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few concentrated buyers, and expert-hour cost may exceed license price.
judges.note: Original supply wedge, and prepaid pilots cut risk. Ten paying customers is unlikely, since only a handful of robotics buyers exist.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few concentrated buyers; on-site capture logistics and per-hour price are unproven.
judges.note: Expert tacit-skill egocentric data with royalties is distinctive, though egocentric-data vendors are proliferating and buyers are few.

title: Notary Network as the Proof-of-Human Layer for Hiring
one_liner: Use the millions of already-commissioned notaries as in-person witnesses who certify that a remote job candidate is a real, physically present person and not a deepfake or proxy.
cluster_name: Verifying real human skill, identity and authorship in hiring and education

judges.fatal_flaw: $99 and scheduling friction per candidate; hiring funnels will not accept it.
judges.note: Clever presence-attestation insight, but poor economics and bad candidate experience.

judges.fatal_flaw: Candidates resist in-person notary meetings; use limited to final-stage, high-risk hires.
judges.note: Contrarian presence attestation with existing network. Fraud pain is real; cheap to launch, 15-20 startups reachable through CISO groups.

judges.fatal_flaw: Candidate friction and cost, and notaries may not be able to attest presence alone.
judges.note: Contrarian answer to deepfake hiring: presence beats software detection. Existing bonded notary network, fast pilots. Market limited to high-risk roles.

title: Second Reader for Consumer Scan Anxiety
one_liner: An independent internist plus CBT-for-health-anxiety clinician who reads your Function, Superpower or full-body-scan results and tells you what not to chase.
cluster_name: Follow-up gaps and anxiety after consumer scans and mega-panels

judges.fatal_flaw: Clinician liability and weak consumer willingness to pay for 'ignore this' reads.
judges.note: Contrarian side of the longevity boom; plausible B2B2C later, but consumer entry is fragile.

judges.fatal_flaw: Second-opinion medicine needs state licensure and malpractice cover; easily copied by clinicians.
judges.note: Timely worried-well wedge; anxiety CBT hidden inside a second opinion; independent from testing firms' retest incentives.

judges.fatal_flaw: Physician time makes $99-199 reads unprofitable; multistate licensing and liability
judges.note: Novel anti-testing angle and reachable communities, but consumer CAC and clinician cost break unit economics.

title: PFAS Farm Passport for Food Buyers and Lenders
one_liner: A screening-plus-sampling service that tells dairy co-ops, produce processors and ag lenders which supplier farms carry PFAS risk from sludge spreading or contaminated irrigation water, and certifies the clean ones.
cluster_name: PFAS exposure, testing and disposal

judges.fatal_flaw: Co-ops may prefer not knowing which supplier farms are contaminated.
judges.note: Correctly reads that the EPA rollback shifts risk onto private buyers. Desktop screening from public data is cheap, and the wedge is unusual.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers avoid testing that creates liability when no farm-level PFAS limit exists.
judges.note: Private-standard thesis is smart and desktop screening is cheap, but slow co-op buyers and unclear action thresholds.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sampling costs and buyer willingness unproven while EPA loosens; farms resist being screened.
judges.note: Private buyer-fear beats public rule is good insight; niche, lab-dependent, uncertain demand.

title: The 4 A.M. Ride Guild
one_liner: A dispatch network of night-owl local drivers, paid per ride by hospitals and jails, that gets rural patients and released inmates home at hours when Uber and Medicaid rides do not exist.
cluster_name: Rural and underserved patients who cannot reach care

judges.fatal_flaw: Rural night ride volume too low to fund 24/7 dispatch; insurance and driver liability.
judges.note: Sharp nurse-level insight that supply is the constraint, but tiny volumes and hospital budgets limit the prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin night ride volume per county and liability make unit economics fragile
judges.note: Supply, not demand, is the constraint; rural hospital funding real; can be run with Twilio and retainers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rural night ride volume too thin to cover driver guarantees and insurance.
judges.note: Real discharge gap and hospital foundations pay retainers; manual Twilio pilot cheap, but per-county economics thin.

title: True Pop: De-duplicated Card Scarcity Data
one_liner: A data product that uses image matching to remove crack-and-resubmit double counts from graded-card population reports, showing lenders and dealers how many physical copies actually exist.
cluster_name: Trading cards and collectibles market infrastructure

judges.fatal_flaw: Grading companies can block scraping or publish their own dedupe; small paying market.
judges.note: Sharp, non-obvious data insight tied to collateral lending; ceiling probably low without expanding to verification.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slab-photo matching accuracy and PSA data-terms risk; few buyers
judges.note: Contrarian: the scarcity ground truth is double-counted where dollars concentrate; lender underwriting hook, but data access is fragile.

judges.fatal_flaw: PSA could dedupe itself or block scraping; buyer base is small.
judges.note: Sharp insight on double-counted pops and cheap hand-verified start, but few lenders will pay.

title: Market Surveillance for Entertainment Prediction Markets
one_liner: Sportradar-style integrity monitoring for the boom in prediction-market contracts on awards, charts, box office and game releases, where insiders and bot farms can swing outcomes.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a handful of buyers, who may build in-house or buy from Sportradar.
judges.note: Timely integrity gap in entertainment contracts; legal-defense budget is real, but buyer pool is tiny and concentrated.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a handful of buyers, who may build in-house or hire Sportradar-type firms
judges.note: Sharp insight on entertainment insiders and a legal-defense budget, but a tiny customer count makes ten customers impossible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a handful of buyers, and Sportradar or Nasdaq surveillance may extend into it.
judges.note: Timely picks-and-shovels for the hottest 2026 market. Concentrated buyers and an entertainment-only niche limit the prize.

title: Pre-Engineered Single-Stair Plan Sets
one_liner: License stamped, fire-marshal-ready plan sets for 4-6 story single-stair buildings so small developers can use the new law without a $250K custom design.
cluster_name: Small builders' crew coordination, permits and speed

judges.fatal_flaw: Plan sets need costly engineering up front; fire-marshal approval is local and slow.
judges.note: Sharp insight that legalization needs templates. Housing is large and timing is good, but it is services-heavy and state-by-state.

judges.fatal_flaw: Site-specific structural, geotech and local amendments limit plan-set reuse.
judges.note: Legalization does not build housing; templates and fire-marshal comfort do. Timely, but reuse economics are optimistic.

judges.fatal_flaw: Stamped engineering per state, architect liability, slow small-developer demand.
judges.note: Good insight that templates unlock legalization, but producing engineered sets needs capital and licensed partners upfront.

title: Lot-Level Verification for Generic Semaglutide Importers
one_liner: A shared-API lineage database plus independent identity and impurity testing for distributors and pharmacy chains buying the flood of post-patent generic semaglutide.
cluster_name: Access, affordability and supply integrity for GLP-1 and compounded drugs

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-lot lab economics are thin and buyers may trust regulators or certificates of analysis.
judges.note: Shared-API correlated risk across 40 brands is a sharp, evidenced insight; free recall radar is cheap lead-gen.

judges.fatal_flaw: Transient event; regulators and big buyers' own QA commoditize lot testing.
judges.note: Sharp shared-API insight and strong timing, but testing is commodity and the window is limited.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers already have GMP supplier-qualification duties and access to commodity labs.
judges.note: Timely recall event and API-lineage insight, but certification credibility and lab commoditization limit paid demand.

title: The 3 A.M. Pharmacist Desk for Konbini
one_liner: A neutral, multilingual, 24-hour remote pharmacist service that issues the emailed certificate the new law will require before konbini without pharmacists can sell OTC drugs.
cluster_name: Rural and underserved patients who cannot reach care

judges.fatal_flaw: Chains will build or lock in; law effective 2027 so no core revenue yet.
judges.note: Regulatory window with insider founder; plausible 3am supply-side wedge; revenue delayed.

judges.fatal_flaw: Law takes effect spring 2027; no legal sales or revenue within six months
judges.note: Insider founder and clear timing window, but pharmacy licensing and regulation gate any revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Revenue gated on spring-2027 rule; chains like Lawson can absorb it
judges.note: Sharp insight that licensed night-shift multilingual labor is the bottleneck; founder-market fit; but first revenue is late.

title: Asset-Light Black Mass Desk Under BIS Rule
one_liner: A trading and compliance desk that becomes the default outlet for US black mass sellers, using the rule's toll-processing exception instead of building plants.
cluster_name: Critical minerals and rare-earth supply chain recovery and provenance

judges.fatal_flaw: Only dozens of sellers; needs insider relationships and lot financing; rule may shift.
judges.note: Regulatory-forced flow, asset-light, good per-lot economics; small customer pool and trust barriers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few sellers and thin domestic buyers; regulatory dependence and legal complexity.
judges.note: Contrarian read of Ascend/Li-Cycle failures; the BIS rule creates a fresh, dated wedge; asset-light and non-obvious.

judges.fatal_flaw: Depends on a temporary rule and a thin black-mass market that could shrink or change.
judges.note: Smart read of Ascend and Li-Cycle failures, but a narrow brokerage niche tied to regulation.

title: Tariff Refund Recovery for Downstream Buyers
one_liner: Importers of record are collecting over $100B in tariff refunds, but the small businesses that paid tariff surcharges on their invoices are owed a share and nobody is collecting it for them.
cluster_name: Recovering IEEPA tariff refunds and surcharges

judges.fatal_flaw: Downstream buyers' legal claim to importers' refunds is weak; vendors will resist
judges.note: Hot, contingency-priced, easy demos; recovery rates are doubtful and the window is closing fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: Claims legally weak without contract clauses; one-time window; crowded tariff-refund field.
judges.note: Near-duplicate of I0133 with less depth. Credit-memo settlement is clever, but it is a windfall play.

judges.fatal_flaw: Downstream buyers' legal claim to importers' refunds is weak; vendors can simply refuse.
judges.note: Inversion: nobody watches who funded the refund. Timely, contingency-based, but the legal basis is shaky and the space is crowding.

title: Callback Verification Network for Invoice-Paying Agents
one_liner: A consortium ledger of verified vendor bank details plus automated out-of-band callbacks that gives accounts-payable agents a signed safe-to-pay attestation before they send money to changed payment instructions.
cluster_name: Small firms and property managers defending against fraud and impersonation

judges.fatal_flaw: AP platforms, Trustpair and Early Warning can bundle bank-detail verification; cold-start ledger.
judges.note: Consortium data network with real defensibility and a large fraud pool. Agentic AP adds urgency, but incumbents are close.

judges.fatal_flaw: Vendor-verification incumbents exist; the shared ledger has a brutal cold start.
judges.note: Real agent-era fraud gap and out-of-band callback is clever, but competitors and network cold start weigh.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consortium ledger cold start, and Trustpair-style vendor verification already exists.
judges.note: Real BEC pain and a bookkeeper channel, but the agent-security framing is crowded and the ledger needs scale first.

title: Rural Jail Pharmacy-in-a-Box for Independents
one_liner: Turn the local independent's blister packing, delivery and controlled-substance discipline into a per-inmate contract for the county jail that the sheriff is afraid of.
cluster_name: Rural sheriffs, jails and small police agencies

judges.fatal_flaw: Correctional pharmacy licensure, DEA rules, and small per-county contracts make it slow to scale
judges.note: A real liability pain and good local-relationship insight, but a tiny fragmented market and a regulated, service-heavy model.

judges.fatal_flaw: Correctional pharmacy licensure and slow county procurement delay first revenue.
judges.note: Real liability pain and local pharmacist channel, but regulatory burden and multi-year county sales cycles.

judges.fatal_flaw: Correctional pharmacy licensure and state rules could block independents.
judges.note: Reframes jail meds as a sheriff liability problem. Buyer is the risk pool, delivery is local, and it sits below bid thresholds.

title: Turn Foreman Paper Sign-In Sheets Into Court-Ready Records
one_liner: Foremen text a photo of the daily paper sign-in sheet, and the system timestamps it, flags overtime, break and travel-time errors, and builds an audit-ready record. The crew changes nothing.
cluster_name: Workforce compliance for remote, tipped and platform workers

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers do not feel compliance risk; time-tracking apps can add photo capture
judges.note: Smart no-behavior-change wedge sold through insurers and CPAs. Its own evidence shows buyers don't feel the pain.

judges.fatal_flaw: Owners feel no compliance pain until sued; agent-dependent channel is slow.
judges.note: Clever no-behavior-change wedge and cheap to build; own evidence shows buyers don't perceive urgency.

judges.fatal_flaw: Owners don't feel wage-hour risk, so willingness to pay stays low.
judges.note: Sell defensibility atop existing paper habit via insurers and CPAs; strong evidence, cheap to test, but easily copied.

title: Contingency-Fee Audit of OTA Markups and Payouts
one_liner: Mystery-shop every downstream reseller and reconcile every OTA payout, then take a share of the money and direct bookings recovered.
cluster_name: Overtouristed destinations, tour operators and independent hotels

judges.fatal_flaw: OTAs seldom pay recovery claims to small hotels, and rate-parity tools already crowd the market.
judges.note: Contingency audit is an easy pitch to independents, but recovery is hard to enforce and reaching thousands of hotels is costly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hotels fear OTA retaliation in ranking; rate-parity monitoring vendors already exist.
judges.note: Proven contingency-audit model with a real leakage gap for independents; mid-size prize and imitable.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hotels fear OTA retaliation; mystery-shopping costs erode contingency margins.
judges.note: Freight-audit analogy is sound and contingency pricing eases sales, but insight is fairly familiar and incumbents adjacent.

title: Patent-Grade Variant Maps for Biologics
one_liner: Pooled-screening service that generates the sequence-function data biologics patents now need after Amgen v. Sanofi, plus a mirror-image design-around report for companies facing sequence claims.
cluster_name: Wet-lab reagents and screens for AI-designed therapeutics

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs wet-lab capacity and slow IP-counsel sales; unproven that courts accept the data
judges.note: Clever post-Amgen angle, but capital-heavy and a long sale to conservative buyers. No revenue within six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Post-filing data cannot add new matter; lawyers may not credit pooled screens.
judges.note: Original link between Amgen v. Sanofi enablement and cheap DNA, with buyers on both offense and defense. Needs a wet lab.

judges.fatal_flaw: Courts may not accept sampled variant data as enabling full genus scope
judges.note: Truly contrarian: post-Amgen enablement becomes wet-lab throughput. Buyers on both sides; needs lab partner.

title: Third-Party Maintenance for Orphaned Robots
one_liner: Like third-party server maintenance for IT, a spares-and-support contract for robots whose makers failed, were acquired or stopped supporting them.
cluster_name: Customers stranded when a product's maker disappears

judges.fatal_flaw: Cannot support robots without proprietary firmware; buying inventory needs capital.
judges.note: Sensible analogy to server maintenance, but the orphan pool is small and technically hard to service.

judges.fatal_flaw: No firmware or source access; orphan pool still small and heterogeneous.
judges.note: Third-party maintenance analogy for post-boom robot shakeout is contrarian but early and capital-heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Too early; orphan fleet small, heterogeneous, and spares business is capital-heavy.
judges.note: Park Place-style third-party maintenance for robots is a real large analog; timing and capital are the issue.

title: Post-Divorce Beneficiary Cleanup for Family Lawyers
one_liner: Sell divorce attorneys a flat-fee sweep that finds and fixes stale beneficiary designations, since the will is the least important estate document.
cluster_name: Making family estate plans fair and contest-proof

judges.fatal_flaw: Getting current designations from custodians requires client credentials; $300 tickets can't fund paralegal work.
judges.note: Sharp divorce-moment wedge, but it is really a feature with a low ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Custodians make designations hard to retrieve, and lawyers must adopt a new vendor.
judges.note: Beneficiary forms beat wills, and divorce is the moment lawyers care. Unglamorous, real, easy manual start. Weak why-now.

judges.fatal_flaw: Custodians respond slowly, and clients can fix designations themselves for free.
judges.note: Easy to pilot with solo family-law firms at $295-495, real malpractice fear, but thin prize and manual fulfilment.

title: Airline-Grade Depot Maintenance for Drone Fleets
one_liner: A swap-based depot and records service that applies airline maintenance discipline to police drone-as-first-responder, ag-spray and utility inspection fleets.
cluster_name: Aircraft and drone operators: maintenance, parts, permits and navigation

judges.fatal_flaw: OEMs already service fleets, and the exchange pool is capital-heavy against $450-900 per month fees.
judges.note: Independent multi-vendor depot is a plausible wedge as Chinese-drone restrictions age fleets, but the economics are unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Exchange-pool inventory capital; manufacturers control parts and service; slow agency procurement.
judges.note: Real fleet-discipline gap, but the subscription needs spare airframes up front and competes with OEM service plans.

judges.fatal_flaw: Drone OEMs and dock vendors will bundle swap service; spare-pool capital needed.
judges.note: Fast-growing DFR fleets and Chinese-parts squeeze; airline-style records plus rotable pool is differentiated but capital-hungry.

title: Overnight First-Call Co-op for Independent Funeral Homes
one_liner: A shared night-and-weekend answering, dispatch and chain-of-custody service so small funeral homes never lose a call at 2 a.m.
cluster_name: Independent funeral homes facing key-person, overnight and consolidation pressure

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable market, local density required, night-staffing liability.
judges.note: Genuine pain and easy pilot, but a regional services business capped at modest size.

judges.fatal_flaw: Existing removal and answering services already cover first calls; thin per-call margin.
judges.note: Fast to start and real overnight pain, but a local labor business with low defensibility and modest prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Funeral-home answering and removal services already exist, and local density is needed.
judges.note: Unglamorous and feasible: run the phone desk yourself and charge per call. Insight is modest and the moat thin.

title: Menu Trial Lab: Restaurants as Food-Brand Test Sites
one_liner: A network of two-to-five-unit restaurants that run randomized menu experiments for food brands and commodity boards, and get paid for it.
cluster_name: Restaurants' idle hours, used oil and credit risk

judges.fatal_flaw: Few brand buyers with small budgets; slow to scale operator network.
judges.note: Matched-pair testing in twin restaurants is inventive, but the prize is small and sales are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-store matched-pair samples are underpowered; brands won't pay $10-25k for noisy results.
judges.note: Operator-founder edge and A/B-in-twin-kitchens insight are original, but demand and statistical rigor are shaky.

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-site matched pairs are statistically weak, so brands may distrust the scorecard.
judges.note: Operator-founder can run trial one immediately; brand and checkoff trial budgets exist; high gross margin per trial.

title: GLP-1 Off-Ramp Program for Cash-Pay Prescribers
one_liner: A structured 12-week landing program for people stopping GLP-1 drugs, sold to the prescribers who lose revenue the day a patient quits.
cluster_name: GLP-1 patients' transitions: procedures, medication changes, quitting and aftercare

judges.fatal_flaw: Prescribers profit from staying on-drug; Noom, Ro, and Hims will bundle off-ramps.
judges.note: Unowned discontinuation moment is real, but buyer logic is muddy and incumbents are close.

judges.fatal_flaw: Prescribers prefer maintenance dosing; Noom and Ro bundle retention; human coaching margin thin.
judges.note: Prescriber-as-buyer is smart and reachable via med spas; value of losing-patient retention unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Clinics profit from continued prescribing, so paying for an off-ramp is a hard sell
judges.note: Owns the unowned stop-moment as a clinic retention tool. Cheap oral GLP-1s make cycling on and off common. Testable fast.

title: Fire-Line Readiness Passport for Contract Wildfire Crews
one_liner: A qualifications, equipment-inspection and shift-ticket system for private wildland fire engine and crew owners, built so they are never rejected at check-in or paid late.
cluster_name: Cash-flow gaps from slow-paying institutions

judges.fatal_flaw: Only about 1,000 firms; the market is too small to venture-scale.
judges.note: Genuine niche pain with high willingness to pay, but the author concedes the market is tiny.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny TAM of about 1,000 firms, seasonal, and agencies could change their systems.
judges.note: Paperwork-as-collateral insight, very unusual customer, hand-run audits sell fast, and a payments layer follows.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small market (~1,000 firms) and agency-specific rules cap the ceiling.
judges.note: Named niche, urgent rejection and late-pay pain, high willingness to pay, association reachable, paid audits fund the MVP.

title: Inheriting the Lease: Rent-Stabilized Succession Service
one_liner: A service that helps families of rent-regulated elders build and keep the co-residency evidence that lets them inherit a below-market lease, and files the succession claim within days of a death.
cluster_name: Small commercial tenants and renters facing landlord leverage

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny geography-limited market with legal-services risk and one-shot demand per family.
judges.note: Genuinely overlooked asset class, but small TAM and lifestyle-business economics.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hard to reach families before a death; legal-practice limits
judges.note: Truly non-obvious: the biggest inheritance is a lease, lost to missing paperwork. Attorney-channel wedge is cheap to test.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers feel no urgency until death; unauthorized-practice-of-law risk and low ticket.
judges.note: Sharp overlooked-asset insight and attorney channel, but the low-price, preparedness purchase is hard to sell.

title: Part-Time Retired Journeymen as Apprentice Supervisors
one_liner: Supervision-as-a-service: retired licensed tradespeople work 2-3 days a week as the supervising journeyman that lets small shops deploy the apprentices and helpers they already have.
cluster_name: Skilled-trades labor gap

judges.fatal_flaw: State rules often require on-site supervision, and liability and insurance deter shops and retirees
judges.note: Supervision minutes, not labor, as the scarce good is a sharp insight. It is still a staffing marketplace, with regulatory variance.

judges.fatal_flaw: State rules may require the supervising journeyman to be the shop's own employee
judges.note: Real scarcity of supervision minutes, hourly billing gives immediate revenue, but licensing, liability and thin margin need per-state verification.

judges.fatal_flaw: Licensing rules often require supervisor be a company employee on site; liability.
judges.note: Supervision-minutes insight is sharp; staffing-marketplace economics and state-by-state rules hurt.

title: Conformity Cases for Learning-Enabled Robots
one_liner: A compliance workbench and pre-assessment service that builds the CE-marking safety case for machines whose behaviour comes from ML models (warehouse robots, cobots, humanoids) ahead of the new EU Machinery Regulation.
cluster_name: Deploying robots in the real world

judges.fatal_flaw: Few paying customers today; humanoid EU deployment and notified-body acceptance may take years.
judges.note: Hard regulatory date and no playbook for ML safety cases. Precedent-setting acceptance would be durable, but the market is thin now.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs deep functional-safety expertise; small buyer pool with entrenched consultancies and notified bodies.
judges.note: Real Jan 2027 deadline and high tickets, but depends on an expert co-founder and few startups.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few funded ML-robot startups buy; regulatory dates may slip; scarce safety-case talent is needed.
judges.note: Real Machinery Regulation deadline, but it is regulation-driven compliance for humanoids, a crowded narrative, with slow notified-body dynamics.

title: Dead-Lead Exchange for Solar Installers
one_liner: A reason-coded exchange where solar installers sell their disqualified leads (bad roof, shade, small panel) to roofers, arborists and electricians, with a bounty when the homeowner comes back to buy solar.
cluster_name: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: TCPA consent and installer failures; supply depends on shrinking solar installers
judges.note: Closed-loop arbitrage on a proven lead-cost pain. Spreadsheet-runnable, quick trades revenue, both sides motivated.

judges.fatal_flaw: Declining solar market and TCPA consent friction; lead volume per installer is small.
judges.note: Clever reason-coded lead recycling, but a lead-gen marketplace in a shrinking industry with a weak why-now.

judges.fatal_flaw: Shrinking solar lead supply after 25D expiry and TCPA consent liability.
judges.note: Clever cross-trade lead recycling with real willingness to pay and spreadsheet-feasible start, though lead-gen is commoditized.

title: Satellite Settlement Radar for Condo Buildings
one_liner: Use free satellite radar archives to give condo boards a 10-year movement history of their building, and turn it into litigation-grade evidence when a neighboring construction project caused the settlement.
cluster_name: Novel environmental and infrastructure data from satellites and crowd-sensing

judges.fatal_flaw: InSAR resolution limits; boards and engineers may avoid documenting settlement liability.
judges.note: Cheap to produce, but buyer urgency unclear and engineers unlikely to rely on screening reports.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sentinel-1 resolution too coarse for building-level, litigation-grade settlement evidence
judges.note: Free archive gives instant history, but accuracy limits and existing InSAR vendors weaken credibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: InSAR resolution limits and engineers' reluctance cap the report market; small unless claims work scales.
judges.note: Free radar archives give instant decade of history; claim funnel is the real money. Niche, but sharply non-obvious.

title: Through-the-Package Drug Verification Library
one_liner: A subscription spectral fingerprint library and scan-on-receipt workflow that lets pharmacies and wholesalers verify what is actually in a sealed vial or blister pack, using off-the-shelf handheld Raman/NIR devices.
cluster_name: Access, affordability and supply integrity for GLP-1 and compounded drugs

judges.fatal_flaw: Raman/NIR struggles with dilute peptides in sealed aqueous vials; false results.
judges.note: Real gap after DSCSA, but technical feasibility and buyer willingness to pay per scan are doubtful.

judges.fatal_flaw: Handheld Raman/NIR may not detect dilute or lyophilized peptide dosing errors through glass.
judges.note: Verifies contents, not paperwork; the spectral library is a compounding data moat. Technical validity risk is high.

judges.fatal_flaw: Through-package Raman may miss dilution in vials, and buyers may not pay per scan
judges.note: A spectral library compounds with each scan, but the science is hard and demand from small dispensers is unproven.

title: Pay-on-Close Homebuyer Readiness for Builders
one_liner: A builder-funded coaching and underwriting-repair program for the roughly half of showroom visitors who cannot yet qualify, paid per closing instead of through rate buydowns.
cluster_name: Repricing softening property markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Success-fee attribution disputes and RESPA referral-fee constraints; builders' captive lenders may do this in-house.
judges.note: Builder incentives buy payment relief, not qualification; pay-per-closing model is clever and pilot-ready.

judges.fatal_flaw: Long builder sales cycle, delayed pay-on-close cash, RESPA referral-fee risk
judges.note: Big prize and sharp insight, but success-fee cash arrives months late and builder buying is slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: RESPA limits on success fees and long lag from coaching to closing.
judges.note: Incentives buy payment relief, not qualification. Real builder pain, but builders' lenders already coach, and attribution is messy.

title: Crop Scouts of the Sea for Seafood Buyers
one_liner: A paid panel of working skippers and tender operators that texts in daily run, quality and delivery-limit data, sold to seafood buyers and lenders days to weeks before the market sees it.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer universe and seasonal fishery; recruiting skippers and antitrust caution.
judges.note: Neat alt-data wedge with cheap backtest, but small market and hard to generalize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny seasonal buyer universe; real proof arrives only after the June-July run.
judges.note: Original alt-data wedge with a good panel moat, but first paying subscribers likely land after the six-month window.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool, seasonal testing until June, and antitrust and MNPI exposure.
judges.note: Fleet-speed information as alt-data is a real insight, but the niche market caps the prize and slows validation.

title: Beaver Warranty for County Culverts and Roads
one_liner: A 5-year no-clog guarantee that keeps beavers out of culverts using flow devices and sensors, and later sells the wetlands they build to water and wildfire agencies.
cluster_name: Condition monitoring for asset owners and their service contractors

judges.fatal_flaw: Small niche, simple copyable devices, slow public procurement.
judges.note: Charming warranty framing with solid cost data, but sub-venture scale and low defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: County budgets cap deal size; local wildlife-control firms already install flow devices.
judges.note: Warranty reframing of recurring emergency labor is clever and evidence-backed; sub-$50k purchases sell fast, market modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow county procurement, seasonal installs, and warranty liability if beavers defeat the devices.
judges.note: Genuine cost data and warranty framing; sub-$50k deals dodge bidding; niche market and slow public-sector cycle.

title: Independent Pharmacy GLP-1 Aftercare Studios
one_liner: A turnkey cash-pay aftercare membership that gives independent pharmacies their first PBM-free service line.
cluster_name: Independent pharmacies squeezed by PBMs, refund floats and deserts

judges.fatal_flaw: Patients unlikely to pay $49 monthly beyond cash-pay drug cost; pharmacies fragmented.
judges.note: Sharp non-PBM revenue angle for independents, but weak willingness to pay and hard distribution.

judges.fatal_flaw: Overstretched pharmacists may not run protocols, and patients may not pay for aftercare.
judges.note: Contrarian read: cash-pay GLP-1 gives independents a PBM-free service line. Association channel makes 5-pharmacy pilot feasible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Patients unlikely to pay $49 a month for aftercare; pharmacists lack bandwidth.
judges.note: Sensible pharmacy wedge, but weak consumer willingness to pay and slow channel via wholesaler groups.

title: GitHub Outage Hot-Standby Forge
one_liner: A managed Forgejo standby that continuously mirrors repos, PRs, issues and Actions workflows, runs monthly failover drills, and lets a team ship a hotfix in minutes when GitHub is down, so nobody has to migrate off GitHub.
cluster_name: AI builders' dependency risk: model retirement, cost blowouts and platform death

judges.fatal_flaw: Teams won't trust a standby forge; GitHub may fix reliability; Actions parity is hard.
judges.note: Real 2026 pain and clever insurance framing, but a sync product that GitHub or GitLab can undercut.

judges.fatal_flaw: Outages annoy but rarely trigger spend; GitHub or GitLab mirroring is good enough.
judges.note: Reachable devs and a clever drill-badge angle, but low ARPU, heavy sync engineering, and vitamin-like insurance.

judges.fatal_flaw: Syncing PRs and Actions faithfully is very hard, and GitHub may fix reliability.
judges.note: Insurance-not-migration framing is smart, but tied to a transient outage narrative and existing backup tools.

title: Medicare-First Longevity Kit for Independent Practices
one_liner: Longevity medicine built on what Medicare already pays for, sold as a workflow kit to independent primary-care practices.
cluster_name: Preventive and longevity care outside conventional insurance

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded CCM/APCM billing vendors, and independent practices are slow to adopt new workflows.
judges.note: Medicare-first longevity is a good reframe of a cash-pay fad, but it's really billing-capture software with known competitors.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded with value-based-care enablers, and tiny independent-practice customer base.
judges.note: Medicare angle on longevity is a smart reframing, but it is a billing workflow in a crowded field.

judges.fatal_flaw: Aledade-style ACO enablers already serve independents; claims-data access for the audit is doubtful.
judges.note: Revenue-share on billing capture gives clear ROI; Medicare-first twist beats cash longevity; reachable via IPAs.

title: ZIP-Level Appetite Radar for Distressed Markets
one_liner: A live map of which carriers are actually binding homes in which distressed ZIPs, sold to agents and to carriers owing coverage quotas.
cluster_name: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: Appetite changes weekly; carrier per-policy bounties may need licensing; wholesalers already answer.
judges.note: Agents in distressed CA ZIPs pay for 'who will write this'; spreadsheet MVP; time-limited but acute.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-bind carrier bounties may require licensing; agent-data network has a cold start.
judges.note: Carriers owing CA quotas as price-insensitive distribution buyers is a fair insight; appetite tools already exist.

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers won't publish appetite, and quote probing may violate terms; California-only for now.
judges.note: Quota-obligated carriers as buyers is a fresh angle, but appetite data is ephemeral and agents have existing tools.

title: 48-Hour Takedown Desk for Small Platforms
one_liner: A hosted notice-and-removal service that lets small user-content platforms meet the TAKE IT DOWN Act's 48-hour clock while filtering out weaponized false claims.
cluster_name: Youth online safety and age-assurance compliance for small platforms

judges.fatal_flaw: Small platforms may not pay $199/month; 24/7 human review squeezes margins.
judges.note: Live federal 48-hour clock is urgent; false-claim abuse layer is the insight; trust-and-safety incumbents exist.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small platforms pay little, and big trust-and-safety vendors can undercut
judges.note: Live federal 48-hour clock with FTC letters out. The statute's missing false-claim safeguard, a shared claimant graph, is a defensible product.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small platforms rarely pay; trust-and-safety vendors and StopNCII already cover much of it.
judges.note: Claimant-reputation graph is a real add, but statute-driven compliance BPO for small buyers caps the prize.

title: Shared Apprentice Pools for Office Work
one_liner: A group-training organisation (the Australian trades model) for white-collar work. It employs new grads, trains them to supervise AI output, and rotates them across several mid-size hosts that share the cost and get first pick.
cluster_name: Entry-level pipeline broken by AI

judges.fatal_flaw: Staffing-style margins and payroll float; host demand for juniors unproven when AI absorbs junior tasks.
judges.note: Biggest prize here; coordination-failure framing is non-obvious and now-relevant. Execution and margin risk keep it from the top.

judges.fatal_flaw: Staffing-style working capital and thin margins; hosts can hire directly.
judges.note: Framing the junior freeze as a training externality is smart, but it is a staffing firm and accounting still wants juniors.

judges.fatal_flaw: Payroll working capital plus co-employment complexity; it is essentially a staffing agency.
judges.note: Coordination-failure framing is smart, but hosts may not pay for juniors AI is replacing; capital-heavy.

title: Tip Passport: Mortgage-Ready Records for Tipped Workers
one_liner: An app that logs every cash and card tip in a lender-grade ledger so young bartenders, stylists, servers and valets can claim the new tip deduction and finally qualify for a mortgage or lease.
cluster_name: Gig, tipped and cash workers unable to prove income

judges.fatal_flaw: Self-logged cash tips aren't verifiable to lenders, and workers fear audits over past underreporting.
judges.note: Nice incentive-flip insight and a large worker base, but consumer distribution is hard and the ledger's value is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Self-logged tip ledgers carry little weight with lenders; consumer CAC is high.
judges.note: Timely tax hook and reachable niche, but the lender-acceptance claim is unproven and consumer pricing is low.

judges.fatal_flaw: Self-logged cash tips lack lender credibility, and workers still fear audits.
judges.note: Incentive flip from hiding to documenting income is insightful, but a self-reported ledger is unverifiable and consumer churn is high.

title: Blue UAS Bill-of-Materials Origin Auditor
one_liner: Part-by-part origin verification so 60,000-drone orders do not fail on hidden Chinese-origin motors, radios and cameras.
cluster_name: New defense and drone suppliers: compliance and financing hurdles

judges.fatal_flaw: Sub-tier origin data is opaque, and makers can keep self-certifying until forced.
judges.note: Genuine compliance budget for drone makers. Needs a customs analyst and RF lab, and the audit's authority is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few customers; government Blue UAS process and trade-data incumbents crowd provenance auditing.
judges.note: Real compliance gating item, but crowded Drone Dominance thesis and services-heavy teardown work.

judges.fatal_flaw: Exiger, Altana and Sayari-type incumbents, and few buyers.
judges.note: Drone Dominance makes origin provenance gating. Trade-data plus teardown catches repackaged parts, a real if narrow wedge.

title: Data Estate Broker for Main Street Closures
one_liner: An appraisal-and-brokerage service that finds, de-identifies and sells the operational exhaust (quotes, work orders, dispatch logs, inspection records) of retiring or closing non-tech firms to AI buyers.
cluster_name: Rights-cleared human data and vetted expert workers for AI labs

judges.fatal_flaw: Rights, privacy and data-quality doubts may stall the first closed sale.
judges.note: Non-consensus new asset class with a proven price (Spirit); supply is huge, but first deals are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: One Spirit sale is not a market; de-identification and privacy backlash; sparse buyers.
judges.note: Boring-industry data estates are an interesting gap, but small firms' data is thin and first sale is hard.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sellers rarely own clean data rights; buyer willingness to pay for messy SMB data unproven.
judges.note: Clever arbitrage from one Spirit sale, but one data point, rights and privacy risk, lumpy success-fee income.

title: Payroll and Proof-of-Trust for Household Staff
one_liner: A WhatsApp payroll, advance and verified-record product for Nigeria's drivers, housekeepers, nannies and gatemen, paid for by their employers.
cluster_name: Gig, tipped and cash workers unable to prove income

judges.fatal_flaw: Very low ARPU, naira volatility, CBN licensing, and employers slipping back to cash.
judges.note: Employer-paid household payroll creates a credit dataset no bureau holds; wedge is real, replicable across markets.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny ARPU per worker and CBN wallet/lending licensing dependence.
judges.note: Employer-paid peace of mind creates a credit dataset no bureau holds. Unusual customer, but thin early revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: About $2 per worker per month ARPU, naira volatility, and wallet and lending regulation.
judges.note: Real employer-as-lender pain, but tiny ARPU and payout compliance make Nigerian unit economics fragile.

title: Verified-Outreach Ledger for Government and Utilities
one_liner: A system where police, courts, tax offices and utilities log every outbound contact so residents can confirm in 20 seconds that they really called.
cluster_name: Seniors targeted by impersonation scams and the institutions that bear the losses

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny ACV government sales; residents rarely verify; branded caller ID competes.
judges.note: Trust-deflation insight is real. Residents must adopt a new habit, and agency budgets are small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Residents won't verify and staff won't log every contact; adoption chicken-and-egg.
judges.note: Timely pain and cooperative-contract channel, but low ACV and two-sided behavior change required.

judges.fatal_flaw: Residents won't verify; scammers spoof the verification line; slow low-ACV government sales
judges.note: Trust-deflation insight is genuinely non-obvious; make legitimate caller provable; adoption behavior unproven.

title: UL for Talking Toys: Behavioral Safety Lab
one_liner: An independent lab that red-teams AI toys and kid-facing companion gadgets with child personas, then sells scorecards and a 'passed' seal to brands and retailers.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Narrow, seasonal AI-toy market; a seal only matters if retailers mandate it.
judges.note: Regulator-fear creates a new lab category; retailers buy assurance now. Expandable to all kid-facing AI.

judges.fatal_flaw: No mandate to buy a seal; toy brands avoid tests and holiday window closing.
judges.note: Novel lab category, but buyers are few, concentrated, and decide before a startup has credibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers; UL, Intertek and advocacy groups can absorb the category.
judges.note: Timely behavioral testing lab for AI toys; public report is a good wedge but the customer pool is tiny.

title: Indonesia Halal Rescue for Food Exporters
one_liner: A fast-track service that gets mid-size food, supplement and cosmetics exporters registered and documented under Indonesia's mandatory halal regime, then keeps them compliant.
cluster_name: Exporters meeting foreign sustainability and representation rules

judges.fatal_flaw: Deadline spike is temporary and needs real halal-regime expertise and credibility.
judges.note: Hard legal cliff, compliance budget, high ticket, reachable exporter lists; cash within weeks, monitoring later.

judges.fatal_flaw: 3-6 month certification cannot be rescued in three weeks; demand is a one-off.
judges.note: Sharp deadline, but consultancy work for a cliff that has essentially passed.

judges.fatal_flaw: Deadline is three weeks away, certification takes months, and it's a one-off consulting spike
judges.note: Fast first sales on a real customs gate. Crowded consultants and a cliff-driven business with no durable moat.

title: Do-Not-Transact Registry: GAMSTOP for Scams
one_liner: An opt-in registry, controlled by consumers and their families, that crypto ATMs, gift-card sellers and wire desks must check before completing a high-risk transaction.
cluster_name: Seniors targeted by impersonation scams and the institutions that bear the losses

judges.fatal_flaw: Operators check only if mandated; voluntary enrollment and cold-start are hard.
judges.note: Precommitment registry sold as B2B legal cover is a sharp reframe. Adoption needs legislation, but the Do-Not-Call analogy could be huge.

judges.fatal_flaw: Kiosk operators profit from scam volume; without a mandate they won't integrate or pay.
judges.note: GAMSTOP-style pre-commitment is a smart reframe that makes protection a B2B compliance lookup. Enrollment and operator incentives are weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Operators gain nothing until mass enrollment exists; no legal mandate to check registry.
judges.note: Clever GAMSTOP-style reframing, but chicken-and-egg enrollment and unclear legal safe harbor stall the first payers.

title: Harvest Inns: Motel Wings as Farm Crew Housing
one_liner: A hospitality-grade operator that master-leases wings of underused rural motels and sublets compliant beds, meals and transport to growers who cannot house H-2A crews.
cluster_name: Housing for workers priced out of tight markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Master-lease liability and H-2A inspection risk before any revenue; seasonal cash cycle.
judges.note: Big real pain and hospitality-operator insight, but capital, compliance liability and political risk hurt bootstrapping.

judges.fatal_flaw: Master-lease working capital and immigration-enforcement politics squeeze a thin-margin hospitality operator.
judges.note: Housing is the binding H-2A constraint; idle motels exist; a Civeo-style ag lodging operator is non-obvious and pre-sellable.

judges.fatal_flaw: Seasonal master-leases tie up capital and add liability if growers pay late.
judges.note: Man-camp analog for H-2A crews using idle motels. Immigration crackdown shifts demand, and the prize is sizeable.

title: Pre-Surveyed Superload Corridors for Data Center Freight
one_liner: A subscription library of continuously re-verified main supply routes for 100-400 ton transformer and switchgear moves, so heavy-haul carriers stop paying for a bespoke route survey on the same corridors every time.
cluster_name: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers may keep buying per-move surveys; routes go stale and permits still gate.
judges.note: Non-obvious niche with few, reachable buyers, a cheap rig and a clear data-freshness moat. Timed to the data-center transformer crunch.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few carriers buy; route data goes stale and per-move permits already survey.
judges.note: Timely freight pain but capital-intensive surveying for a small, project-based buyer pool.

judges.fatal_flaw: Engineer-stamped routes carry liability; route data decays and permit offices resurvey anyway.
judges.note: Pre-classified supply routes for transformer moves is a fresh angle. Crew and rig capex, plus carriers may not buy.

title: Clinic-Sponsored Tuition for Loan-Capped PT Students
one_liner: Sports-medicine PT and athletic-training employers fund tuition for students shut out of federal loans, in return for a structured work commitment.
cluster_name: Colleges and training programs under new federal loan caps and earnings tests

judges.fatal_flaw: Section 127 covers only $5k per year; clinics won't front six-figure tuition.
judges.note: Loan-cap pain is real, but the funding math does not work and payoff is years away.

judges.fatal_flaw: Stay-or-pay clause limits and a possible court reversal of loan caps.
judges.note: Employer as the only PT-risk underwriter is a sharp reframe of the loan-cap shock; a paid placement fee is quick to test.

judges.fatal_flaw: Stay-or-pay clause limits and a small PT-only market cap the business.
judges.note: Employer as the underwriter after loan caps is non-consensus, and the timing is exact. Generalizes to nursing and OT.

title: Flat-Fee Estate Close-Out Pods for Middle-Class Heirs
one_liner: A retired probate attorney supervises 2-3 junior associates and an AI workflow to close $200K-$2M estates for a flat fee, filling the gap between a $400/hr attorney and nothing while giving locked-out grads a paid apprenticeship.
cluster_name: Executors and small probate firms drowning in estate paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Flat fee near $3.9k with slow probate cycles cannot cover attorney plus associates
judges.note: Real, budgeted pain with a funeral-home channel, but pod payroll versus revenue per estate does not clear.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unauthorized-practice and ethics rules, and slow court-driven estates, constrain flat-fee margins.
judges.note: Real middle-class gap and an apprenticeship angle. Feels like an AI-enabled services roll-up with heavy regulatory friction.

judges.fatal_flaw: UPL and fee-splitting rules plus existing flat-fee probate competitors cap scaling.
judges.note: Big underserved middle-class estate market; AI-plus-supervised-junior model credible but services-margin and regulatory-bound.

title: Vacancy-Permit Kit for Half-Empty Offices
one_liner: A sensor and inspection package that keeps half-empty office buildings insurable and safe during the 12-36 months of limbo before resolution.
cluster_name: Condition monitoring for asset owners and their service contractors

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers must accept the protocol in writing; special-servicer sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: Specific, budgeted insurance-exclusion pain and pilotable at $5K, but hardware installs and per-sf revenue are thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers may not accept the protocol; revenue per building is small.
judges.note: The 31% vacancy-clause insight is real and non-obvious, but a sensor kit for distressed owners is a small, cost-averse market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers may not accept sensors as vacancy substitute; slow servicer buying.
judges.note: Real insurance-denial gap in distressed offices, but narrow, hardware-installed, small ARPU per building.

title: Professional Health-Care Agents for Solo Agers
one_liner: A subscription 'designated agent' nurse-advocate with health-care proxy authority who is reachable at 2 am, sold to solo agers and to hospitals stuck with unbefriended patients.
cluster_name: Solo agers without family to act as proxy, executor or guardian

judges.fatal_flaw: 24/7 agent liability and malpractice exposure at 60-80 clients per advocate.
judges.note: Solo-ager gap is real and payable, but unit economics ignore 2 am liability and existing care managers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Professional proxy authority carries heavy liability and conflict-of-interest scrutiny; labor-bound scaling.
judges.note: Real, growing gap with an underserved cohort. Attorneys are a feasible channel, but it stays a services business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Personal legal liability of acting as proxy for 60-80 strangers; hard to insure.
judges.note: Real gap with a proven willingness to pay (care managers). Estate-attorney channel works; hospital unbefriended-patient fees add revenue.

title: Servicer-Funded Nonrenewal Rescue Agent for Homeowners
one_liner: When a homeowner's policy is nonrenewed, an agent contests the machine-made underwriting flag, documents mitigation and reshops 30 carriers plus the FAIR plan, paid by the mortgage servicer that would otherwise face a coverage lapse.
cluster_name: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: Servicers profit from force-placed coverage; weak incentive and slow enterprise sales.
judges.note: Real pain but payer thesis shaky; licensed agency plus servicer pilots are slow to close.

judges.fatal_flaw: Servicers may not pay; placement is commodity brokerage and carrier portals resist agents.
judges.note: Huge insurance-crisis problem with an unusual lender-paid distribution angle, but the payer's incentive is doubtful.

judges.fatal_flaw: Servicers profit from force-placed coverage and are slow to pay per rescue.
judges.note: Servicer-as-payer is a clever flip. Insurance brokerage is licensing-heavy and buyer's urgency is unproven.

title: H-2A Housing-as-a-Service for Growers
one_liner: Lease pre-certified modular seasonal housing by the bed so growers can actually use H-2A visas.
cluster_name: Housing for workers priced out of tight markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-intensive; zoning and inspection variance slow deployment; pricing left as placeholder.
judges.note: Beds are the binding H-2A constraint; asset-backed, recurring seasonal revenue; deposits can pre-sell before building.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-heavy modular fleet with zoning and DOL inspection hurdles before revenue
judges.note: Real binding constraint for growers, but asset build precedes cash and pricing is blank.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-heavy modular units face slow inspection and zoning; revenue model left unspecified.
judges.note: Beds, not visas, bind H-2A; financeable, recurring asset. Sound thesis but thin plan and slow build.

title: Elder-Intelligible Voice for Healthcare AI Calls
one_liner: An audio layer that reshapes AI-agent voices so listeners 75+ with age-related hearing loss actually understand phone calls, sold per minute to healthcare voice-agent companies.
cluster_name: Language, hearing and communication barriers in services and workplaces

judges.fatal_flaw: Voice-AI platforms can absorb this as a feature; per-minute revenue is small.
judges.note: Genuine psychoacoustics insight, measurable and testable fast, but a feature-sized layer sold into a crowded voice stack.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-minute revenue is tiny and voice-AI vendors can add EQ themselves.
judges.note: Genuine psychoacoustic insight, but few small buyers and thin economics make it a feature.

judges.fatal_flaw: Voice-AI platforms can add clear-speech tuning natively; per-minute revenue tiny.
judges.note: Psychoacoustics plus telephony bandwidth, not warmth, is the real barrier for seniors; measurable and cheap to test.

title: CMMC Enclave for CNC Shops
one_liner: A prebuilt, shop-floor-aware CUI enclave and evidence pack that gets 20-person machine shops through CMMC Level 2 without rebuilding their IT.
cluster_name: New defense and drone suppliers: compliance and financing hurdles

judges.fatal_flaw: PreVeil, Summit 7 and MSP enclaves already sell CMMC-in-a-box to shops.
judges.note: Real deadline and useful OT scoping wedge, but this is the predictable compliance-in-a-box play in a crowded market.

judges.fatal_flaw: MSPs and enclave vendors already crowd CMMC; appliance support erodes margins.
judges.note: Forced-spend deadline, OT-aware scoping is a real wedge, fast revenue; more MSP-like than venture-scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Crowded CMMC enclave vendors, and assessor acceptance of a home-built appliance is unproven.
judges.note: Hard Nov 2026 deadline, budgeted compliance, MEP and prime channel. The OT-scoped boundary is a real wedge.

title: Sewershed Chemical Fingerprinting to Trace PFAS Sources
one_liner: A network of automated samplers plus non-target mass-spectrometry that bisects a city's sewer tree to find which industrial sources are putting PFAS into the plant.
cluster_name: PFAS exposure, testing and disposal

judges.fatal_flaw: Lab-heavy consulting economics and slow municipal procurement cap scale and first-customer speed
judges.note: Sewer-tree bisection is clever; buyer is utility legal/finance seeking cost recovery from polluters. PFAS liability is large.

judges.fatal_flaw: Government procurement is slow; sampler capex and six-figure first sale
judges.note: Compelling tree-bisection method, but utility sales cycles and upfront field costs exceed a scrappy six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Public-utility sales cycles are slow, and cost recovery from polluters is legally hard.
judges.note: Sewer-tree bisection like contact tracing, sold to utility legal and finance; big PFAS prize; needs a lab partner.

title: Owner-Statement Auditor for Landlords With Property Managers
one_liner: Forward your property manager's monthly owner statements and get back the line items that don't add up: repairs with no invoice, charges on the wrong property, reserve draws that hide shortfalls, and true days vacant.
cluster_name: Landlords in soft markets: vouchers, evictions, vacancies and retention

judges.fatal_flaw: Low ARPU and churn once owners finish the backfill audit
judges.note: Demand evidenced in forums, reachable community, near-zero CAC, cheap manual MVP, white-label channel through bookkeepers.

judges.fatal_flaw: $9 per door with low owner engagement; churn once the audit finds nothing.
judges.note: Real forum pain and a neutral auditor position, but low ARPU, and PM portals offer line detail.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small landlords pay little and churn; PM-native reporting can undercut.
judges.note: Neutral auditor insight is evidence-backed with instant first revenue, but a low-ARPU, small market.

title: Outsourced Elder-Exploitation Desk for Credit Unions
one_liner: A managed service where trained specialists take flagged older-member transactions, call the member and trusted contact, file reports and document compliance.
cluster_name: Seniors targeted by impersonation scams and the institutions that bear the losses

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit-union sales cycles are slow and labor-heavy service caps scale.
judges.note: Named buyer with duty of care, avoided-loss pricing, services-first so no build risk; CUSO channel.

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit unions buy slowly and will not risk liability for hold decisions.
judges.note: Human case handling for the institution with a duty of care is sensible but fairly foreseeable.

judges.fatal_flaw: Elder-fraud outsourcing is the obvious idea; institutions can hire or buy from fraud vendors.
judges.note: Clear buyer and ROI pricing, but predictable elder-fraud pitch with no distinctive wedge beyond human case handling.

title: Rescue Monitoring for Orphaned Home Solar
one_liner: An installer-agnostic gateway plus subscription that watches home solar systems whose installer went bankrupt, produces warranty-ready evidence, and dispatches a vetted local electrician.
cluster_name: Residential solar leftovers: orphaned systems, leases and liens

judges.fatal_flaw: Homeowners won't pay subscriptions when inverter clouds exist; hardware fragmentation.
judges.note: Real orphan wave but small consumer payment willingness. The servicer angle is the only serious buyer.

judges.fatal_flaw: Many inverter families, hardware support, and low consumer willingness to pay monthly.
judges.note: Real orphan fleet and lender payer, but hardware plus dispatch network is heavy for scrappy team.

judges.fatal_flaw: Orphan wave is finite; hardware CAC and servicer takeovers cap the market.
judges.note: Real, urgent, underserved fleet; lenders as second payer is smart, but it is a shrinking niche.

title: Texas Data-Center Water Filing and Attestation
one_liner: A fixed-fee compliance service that meters, calculates, files and PE-attests data-center water reports for the operators who ignored Texas's mandatory water survey.
cluster_name: Water scarcity: irrigation allocation and new supply

judges.fatal_flaw: Enforcement and PE-attestation requirement are speculative; $500 fine lets miners ignore it
judges.note: Deadline-driven and fixed-fee, but regulatory premise unproven and needs metering ops plus PE partner.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time regulatory wave with only ~280 customers; rules may soften or lapse.
judges.note: Urgent deadline, easy first sales, but small market and event-driven revenue that fades.

judges.fatal_flaw: Enforcement is uncertain, and small operators may ignore a $500-fine regime.
judges.note: Sharp timing and a long-tail compliance wedge. Demand hinges on rules not yet written. Needs a PE partner.

title: Exchange for Unused Grid Interconnection Headroom
one_liner: A market where owners of unused interconnection capacity and stalled queue positions sell time-sliced access to batteries and data centers that cannot wait for the queue.
cluster_name: Getting power for large loads and storage

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin, bespoke, ISO-rule-constrained transfers may never produce marketplace liquidity
judges.note: Huge prize, acute why-now; insight that paid-for studies are the asset. Success fees are large even at 20 MW.

judges.fatal_flaw: FERC transfer rules and long deal cycles make a first success fee unlikely in 6 months.
judges.note: Big prize and sharp insight on paid-for studies, but regulation, illiquid two-sided market, and brokers-only deals.

judges.fatal_flaw: Transfer rules limit deals; thin, broker-driven liquidity keeps volume tiny.
judges.note: Completed studies as the asset is smart, and the prize is large. Regulatory transfer friction and few transactions slow it.

title: Manufactured-Home Replacement With Salvage Financing
one_liner: A turnkey 'old home out, new home in' program for manufactured-home communities: hazmat survey, salvage and teardown of pre-1976 units, pad prep, then set-and-hookup crews for new factory-built homes, with scrap and reuse value helping finance the job.
cluster_name: Households upgrading homes: electrification, roofs and solar loans

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-margin field crews, local permit variation and asbestos liability make scaling hard.
judges.note: Real end-of-life housing stock, exit-of-old-unit bottleneck insight, reachable park-owner buyers; labor-heavy services.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-margin, crew-heavy operations with hazmat licensing; salvage value is too small to move economics.
judges.note: Real demand from park owners and a clear fixed-price offer, but it is a capital-hungry services business that scales poorly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Field-crew, hazmat and capital intensity; local operations don't scale
judges.note: Unglamorous and non-obvious: the bottleneck is removing the old unit. Salvage offsets cost and revenue is real. Low software leverage.

title: Notarized Sky: Satellite Image Authenticity Desk
one_liner: A verification desk that tells insurers, traders and newsrooms whether a 'satellite photo' is real, by corroborating it against independent archives and issuing a signed chain-of-custody attestation.
cluster_name: Defensible authenticity evidence for disputed digital media

judges.fatal_flaw: Demand is episodic and lumpy, and buyers can use existing OSINT firms or imagery vendors.
judges.note: Corroboration-as-attestation is a sharp insight and a tiny team can do it, but the buyer set is small and slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer set and bespoke desk work that does not scale.
judges.note: Corroboration over detection is the right framing and Hormuz demand is real, but it stays a boutique.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool tied to conflict cycles; OSINT incumbents already do this.
judges.note: Corroboration, not detection, is the right reframe. Marine war-risk underwriters pay, but the market is narrow.

title: DIC Finder for Veteran Families at Funerals
one_liner: A tool that reads a veteran's death certificate, hospice diagnosis and DD-214 to spot survivor benefits the widow does not know exist, sold to funeral homes and hospices rather than to families.
cluster_name: Hospice, dying and the first weeks of bereavement

judges.fatal_flaw: VA fee and accreditation rules restrict monetizing leads; funeral homes may not pay SaaS.
judges.note: Funeral director as the only professional in the room is a sharp wedge on real unclaimed DIC money. Legal structure is fragile.

judges.fatal_flaw: Nice-to-have for funeral homes; VA accreditation and fee rules create legal exposure.
judges.note: Clever trigger-event channel and reachable buyers at $149/month, but weak urgency and retention, needs VSO partner.

judges.fatal_flaw: VA accreditation and fee rules limit the model, and funeral homes pay low SaaS ARPU.
judges.note: Clever distribution through funeral homes and hospice at the trigger event. The sale is easy but the prize is modest and regulation-sensitive.

title: Insurer-Proof Watch Service for Inherited Houses
one_liner: A subscription that keeps a parent's empty house insured during probate by producing the dated inspection log insurers require, plus leak sensors and mail and utility handling.
cluster_name: Houses caught in death, divorce or care transitions

judges.fatal_flaw: Local gig-labor service with low ticket, so it is hard to scale beyond probate referrals.
judges.note: The inspection log as the insurer-required product is a good insight, but it is essentially a vacant-property check service.

judges.fatal_flaw: Existing vacant-property inspection services; modest lifetime value per customer.
judges.note: Inspection log as the insured-vacancy product is a real wedge with a clear probate-attorney channel, but fairly obvious.

judges.fatal_flaw: Weekly $35 visits leave thin gross margin; local density hard to reach.
judges.note: Urgent, specific buyer reachable through probate attorneys, and the log-as-product insight is good. Unit economics are marginal.

title: Sworn Testator Depositions for the Deepfake Era
one_liner: Estate attorneys refer aging or blended-family clients to a 45-minute sworn Q&A on intent and capacity, taken by a reporter who certifies it and stored in an escrow vault that opens on death. Because a human certified it, it stays credible when video can be faked.
cluster_name: Making family estate plans fair and contest-proof
