judges.fatal_flaw: Admissibility is uncertain by state; attorneys unlikely to route meaningful volume.
judges.note: Neat deepfake-era angle on human-certified intent, but niche volume and unproven legal value cap it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Transcripts don't prove capacity; deepfake will contests remain rare, so attorneys won't refer.
judges.note: Human-certified record vs deepfakes is clever, but the threat is speculative and existing capacity evidence suffices.

judges.fatal_flaw: Admissibility uncertain; attorneys are conservative referrers, so sessions may stall.
judges.note: Original, high ticket per session, attorney-billed cost; a few pilots feasible, but market is modest.

title: Decoy Employees: Canary Tokens for People
one_liner: AI-run fake accounts-payable and help-desk staffers listed where attackers scrape, with voice agents that answer, harvest attacker infrastructure and alert the real team the moment anyone probes.
cluster_name: Small firms and property managers defending against fraud and impersonation

judges.fatal_flaw: Unclear budget owner; legal and HR risk; likely a feature of deception platforms
judges.note: Creative canary-employee idea, but attackers recon through LinkedIn and data brokers, so hit rate is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Alerts on attacker probing aren't actionable enough to justify $1.5-3K monthly spend.
judges.note: Novel canary framing, but CISOs are cautious about impersonation personas and legal exposure; weak budget line.

judges.fatal_flaw: Decoy hit rate may be too low to justify subscription; legal and HR friction.
judges.note: Canary employees invert attacker automation into telemetry; genuinely novel deception angle but unproven signal volume and buyer urgency.

title: Cloud-Bricking Escrow for Hardware Brands
one_liner: A neutral escrow-and-standby service that holds a hardware brand's cloud backend and local-mode firmware, and takes over the moment the cloud vendor fails.
cluster_name: Customers stranded when a product's maker disappears

judges.fatal_flaw: Brands rarely pay for insurance against vendor death until after it happens.
judges.note: Original, regulation-timed idea with no obvious incumbent, but small market and a weak buyer urgency curve.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brands will not pay for tail-risk insurance before a failure, and escrow triggers are hard to litigate.
judges.note: Real bricking stories, but the buyer feels no urgency and CRA does not mandate this.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brands don't buy insurance-like escrow until they've been burned
judges.note: Live-fleet escrow fits the CRA and recent bricking cases. Buyer is the brand, not the consumer. Sales are hard until pain hits.

title: Hospital-Guaranteed Loans for Excluded Health Programs
one_liner: Employer-cosigned, service-obligation tuition loans for nursing, OT, PT and counseling students that the new federal caps abandoned.
cluster_name: Colleges and training programs under new federal loan caps and earnings tests

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs balance-sheet capital, and hospital procurement is slow. Rule changes could reopen the federal loan caps.
judges.note: Big prize from a fresh policy shock, and employer-as-underwriter is a real insight. Bank-partner model lets a small team start.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs lending capital, bank partner and hospital guarantees; slow hospital sales cycles.
judges.note: Sharp why-now and underwriting insight, but it is a lending business needing capital before first revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Stay-or-pay limits, lending capital and licensing; private lenders will fill gap
judges.note: Employer as underwriter is a sharp reversal of the loan-cap narrative; real July 2026 shift.

title: Evac Cash: Payout When Ordered to Evacuate
one_liner: A few dollars a month buys a $500-$2,500 wire within hours of an official mandatory evacuation order for your address, covering hurricane, wildfire and burn-scar flood orders.
cluster_name: Fast parametric cash for weather and disaster shocks

judges.fatal_flaw: Adverse selection and state insurance licensing make parametric cover slow and costly to launch.
judges.note: Legal-act trigger nearly eliminates basis risk; employers and governments co-pay. Regulatory drag is the main risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurance licensing, adverse selection before storms, and thin premium per customer.
judges.note: Legal-act trigger removes basis risk and has two payers, but parametric microinsurance is slow and needs an MGA.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs MGA, fronting carrier and state approvals before any revenue; adverse selection.
judges.note: Legal-act trigger is clever, but insurance licensing and consumer CAC on $3-15/month premiums are punishing.

title: Credit Ratings and Insurance for Virtual Power Plants
one_liner: A neutral firmness rating plus a parametric shortfall policy, so hyperscalers and utilities can buy VPP megawatts they can actually count.
cluster_name: Utilities avoiding costly network upgrades with distributed flexibility

judges.fatal_flaw: Ratings need buyers who pay; the insurance wrap needs reinsurer capital and enough dispatch data.
judges.note: A neutral firmness standard for VPP megawatts is a toll-collector position. Non-consensus and timely, but slow to get paying customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Ratings lack credibility without a buyer mandate; insurance wrap needs balance sheet.
judges.note: Trust, not enrollment, is the real VPP bottleneck. Rating agency toll is big if it works. Hard to land early.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs reinsurer capacity and a credible rating track record before any paying customer appears.
judges.note: Big idea but insurance wrap, licensing, and enterprise sales make first revenue in six months unlikely.

title: Prospecting for Brackish Aquifers Like Gold
one_liner: A water-exploration company that maps, options and permits high-yield brackish and fresh aquifers before developers need them, then sells or leases 'water-ready' sites and supply.
cluster_name: Water scarcity: irrigation allocation and new supply

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-intensive drilling and option-buying; Texas groundwater politics; reports alone are just consulting.
judges.note: Water rights as new mineral rights for data centers; huge asset-owner upside, consulting entry, few startup rivals.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-heavy drilling and hydrogeology credibility; buyers unlikely to pay for unproven maps.
judges.note: Water as gating item for data centers is real; 'water is the new mineral rights' is a known meme and slow to monetize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Drilling and option positions are capital-heavy, and public-data reports lack a credible geologist.
judges.note: Big prize and real water scarcity, but credentialing and capital needs outrun a scrappy team.

title: Real-Brine Library and DLE Benchmark Lab
one_liner: A neutral bank of characterised real brines, matrix-matched reference materials and public bake-offs of direct lithium extraction vendors, so nobody has to run a $3M private pilot to compare technologies.
cluster_name: Critical minerals and rare-earth supply chain recovery and provenance

judges.fatal_flaw: Lab capex, brine sourcing and depressed lithium market; entrenched proficiency-testing providers
judges.note: Insightful benchmark gap, but slow, capital-heavy and dependent on vendor funding.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few, cash-strapped lithium customers make the market very small.
judges.note: Deep-insider neutral benchmark with a real moat and quick interlab revenue, but the TAM is tiny.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small niche buyer pool; vendors may not pay for benchmarks that could expose them.
judges.note: Genuinely non-obvious: DLE is a data-credibility problem; leftover pilot brines are the asset; interlab rounds pay fast.

title: Verified-Offer Shield Against H-2A Recruitment Scams
one_liner: A WhatsApp-native registry where growers publish verifiable H-2A job offers and authorized recruiters, so workers can check any offer in seconds and growers get proof they never sanctioned a fee-charging middleman.
cluster_name: Workforce compliance for remote, tipped and platform workers

judges.fatal_flaw: Growers may not pay to protect workers; small early market, politically fraught.
judges.note: Right buyer insight, but compliance pain is indirect and $15-40 per worker is unproven demand.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small revenue pool; growers may not pay for worker-side verification.
judges.note: Buyer-is-liable-grower insight is good; WhatsApp-native fits workers, but prize is modest.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small prize; growers may not pay per worker and scammers simply migrate channels.
judges.note: Grower-as-payer for worker-side fraud protection is a smart inversion; WhatsApp-native and quick to pilot with an association.

title: Pickleball Courts Inside Empty Fellowship Halls
one_liner: A turnkey operator that converts congregations' idle gyms and fellowship halls into revenue-sharing indoor pickleball venues, with lines, nets, insurance and booking handled.
cluster_name: Shrinking institutions with idle buildings

judges.fatal_flaw: Congregations can host pickleball themselves; thin margins and low defensibility.
judges.note: Feasible and clever reuse of idle halls, but pickleball is a trend everyone knows and the moat is minimal.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pickleball growth may plateau; thin per-site margins and slow congregation decision-making.
judges.note: Clever asset-light reframe of court shortage as liability problem; easy first customers, though scale is operationally heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Local ops grind; churches insure-averse or already run own pickleball
judges.note: Cash in month one with a $1.5k kit and a clear insight, but hard to scale beyond a local operator.

title: Delay Insurance for Data Center Energization
one_liner: Parametric insurance and pricing data that pay developers and lenders when the utility misses its committed energization date.
cluster_name: Cover and data for emerging or neglected risks

judges.fatal_flaw: Reinsurers may reject utility-delay risk; moral hazard and vague committed dates.
judges.note: Huge exposure, unhedged risk, parametric trigger. Index data can sell before insurance capital arrives.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs MGA licensing and reinsurance backing before any premium revenue.
judges.note: Big prize and neat parametric insight, but regulatory and capital hurdles block early revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Reinsurer capacity, MGA licensing and moral-hazard concerns won't clear in six months.
judges.note: Parametric trigger on the utility's own committed date is a sharp reframe of the AI buildout's largest schedule risk.

title: Emeritus: Paying 80-Year-Old Tradespeople for Tacit Knowledge
one_liner: Recruit retired machinists, lineworkers, boiler operators and railroad and telephone technicians in their 70s-90s, pay them hourly to teach on camera, and sell the corpus to AI labs, robotics companies and industrial firms.
cluster_name: Real-world skill and object data for robot and industrial-AI builders

judges.fatal_flaw: AI labs' willingness to pay $500-2,000/hr for retiree video is unproven
judges.note: Distinctive supply insight, but concentrated speculative buyers and elder-consent complexity.

judges.fatal_flaw: Robotics buyers want hand-motion data, and spoken tacit knowledge may not transfer.
judges.note: Retirees as expert-data supply is an unusual wedge, but this thesis is now crowded and demand is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Labs may not buy retiree interview video; consent and capacity issues with elderly contributors.
judges.note: Unusual supply of clean-rights tacit expertise sold to hungry robotics and LLM buyers. High variance, big upside, demand unproven.

title: Rent Renewal Desk for Small Tenants
one_liner: Contingency-fee lease-renewal negotiation for tenants under 5,000 square feet, armed with the comps and lease abstraction that landlords get from CoStar-class data and small tenants never see.
cluster_name: Small commercial tenants and renters facing landlord leverage

judges.fatal_flaw: Contingency on small savings cannot cover negotiation labor; reliable comps data is scarce.
judges.note: Real asymmetry and referral channels, but per-deal economics are thin and customers are fragmented.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small-tenant savings are too small; negotiating requires brokerage licensing and comp data.
judges.note: Real asymmetry, and LLM lease abstraction is cheap. But the pooled-comps moat is slow and contingency economics are thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: High CAC and tiny per-deal fees; comps data thin at first.
judges.note: Real information asymmetry and pooled-lease moat, but small tickets and slow, lumpy contingency revenue.

title: Short-Time Compensation as a Service
one_liner: Software and admin that lets employers shrink hours instead of headcount using state work-sharing programs, where unemployment insurance replaces part of the lost wages, as an alternative to AI-driven layoffs.
cluster_name: Employers restructuring for AI: layoffs, severance and displaced workers

judges.fatal_flaw: Employers and states resist work-sharing; low uptake exists for a reason.
judges.note: Unused subsidy is a non-obvious hook, but state fragmentation and employer reluctance cap demand.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employers historically ignore work-sharing; the decision-maker rarely wants the admin burden.
judges.note: Contrarian: existing unused subsidy as anti-layoff hedge. Decades of low take-up suggest demand is weaker than it looks.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employers default to layoffs; qualifying events are rare and state approvals are slow.
judges.note: Unused subsidy is a nice insight, but volume per customer is small and urgency is weak.

title: Widow's First 90 Days, Sold Through Funeral Homes
one_liner: The pharmacy sees a death first, because refills stop. Package a pharmacist-led medicine cleanup and 90-day check-in program for the surviving spouse, and sell it to funeral homes as their aftercare offering.
cluster_name: Hospice, dying and the first weeks of bereavement

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs a pharmacist-founder and a controlled-substance handling process; small tickets across three parties.
judges.note: Sharp insight (pharmacy sees death first), but a multi-party channel with regulatory handling and low per-family revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small per-family fees; funeral homes are slow adopters and margins are thin
judges.note: Pharmacy sees death first and holds collector authority funeral homes lack. Non-obvious channel pairing, though the prize is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Funeral homes may not pay; the pharmacy operational burden is high; defensibility is low.
judges.note: Clever pharmacist-plus-funeral-director channel and DEA collector angle; easy pilot but a modest ceiling.

title: Widowhood Risk Program Sold to Medicare Payers
one_liner: Use hospice's early knowledge that a caregiver spouse is about to become a widow to enroll them in a 180-day protective program, paid for by Medicare Advantage plans and ACOs.
cluster_name: Hospice, dying and the first weeks of bereavement

judges.fatal_flaw: Payers may not fund it; ROI unproven and health-plan sales cycles are long.
judges.note: Non-obvious insight: hospice sees the widowhood risk months before claims do. Modest prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Medicare Advantage plans buy slowly, so no paying customers within six months.
judges.note: Sharp insight that widow is the unpaid second patient; hospice channel is real but payer proof takes over a year.

judges.fatal_flaw: Spouse often sits in a different plan; MA payback proof and sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: Widowhood effect is real and underpriced, with hospice as early-warning intake. Large prize, but no paying plan within six months.

title: Retreat Options for Eroding Oceanfront Homes
one_liner: An annual retainer that reserves a house-mover and demolition slot and triggers automatically when satellite-measured setback hits a preset distance.
cluster_name: Flood and fire survivors: mapping, buyouts, claims and rebuilding

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a few hundred exposed homes; a retainer may be treated as insurance.
judges.note: Acute pain and a novel capacity option, but a tiny market. Ten founding homes at $1,200 is plausible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable owner base; insurance-like liability and contractor capacity hard to secure.
judges.note: Contractor-capacity option triggered by trusted measurement is novel, but market is thousands of homes and heavily local.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny owner base; may be regulated as insurance; contractor capacity promise is unenforceable
judges.note: Option-on-contractor-capacity is a neat insight with a news hook, but the market is only hundreds of homes.

title: AI Chat-History Exposure Assessments for Breach Counsel
one_liner: When infostealers grab employees' AI sessions, tell breach counsel what the attacker could actually have read and whether notification is triggered.
cluster_name: Recorded and AI-created data exposure for small firms

judges.fatal_flaw: Incidents are rare and IR firms can build this in-house.
judges.note: Timely niche in breach forensics, but more a feature of IR tooling than a company.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sporadic incident volume and legal risk handling stolen infostealer data.
judges.note: Genuine empty niche for breach counsel with $7.5K tickets, but demand is lumpy and channel-dependent.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few incidents; attacker's actual reads are hard to prove without provider logs.
judges.note: Sharp reframing: notification turns on chat content, not stolen cookies. IR-boutique channel is feasible; incident volume is lumpy.

title: Tariff Surcharge Clawback for Downstream Buyers
one_liner: A contingency recovery-audit firm that claws back tariff surcharges buyers paid on duties their suppliers have since had refunded.
cluster_name: Recovering IEEPA tariff refunds and surcharges

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time windfall; buyers' legal claim to supplier refunds is weak and mostly settles as credits.
judges.note: Fast to first revenue and an underserved downstream angle, but a transient contingency project, not a durable company.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers fear supplier relationships; weak contract claims settle as small credits; window closes fast
judges.note: Downstream-buyer angle on IEEPA refunds is non-obvious, but it is a crowded refund-recovery pile and time-boxed.

judges.fatal_flaw: Generic version of the same wedge; weak leverage; crowded with recovery firms.
judges.note: Same tariff-surcharge thesis as I1300 but vaguer; flat-fee scan helps cash, still an obvious idea.

title: Turnkey Six-Bed Care Homes for Nurse-Operators
one_liner: A licensing-and-operations platform that turns ordinary houses into small licensed residential care homes run by nurses and experienced aides.
cluster_name: Home and residential care: labor supply, family caregivers and small-scale models

judges.fatal_flaw: Licensing consultants abound; regulation and resident-liability exposure
judges.note: Large prize, but small-care-home licensing playbook is widely known and senior-housing gap is the consensus bet.

judges.fatal_flaw: State-by-state licensing and resident-safety liability with copyable playbooks.
judges.note: Supply constraint is permission, not concrete; big prize, fast first customers, but thin defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Operators need house, capital and state license; many existing consultants and courses.
judges.note: Reachable buyers and a $2,500 entry product; proven licensed-home models; crowded consulting and operator failure risk.

title: Funeral Home Land-and-Business Split Advisory
one_liner: An advisor that separates aging independent funeral directors' real estate from their operating business. The land goes to housing developers, the shrunken business is leased back or sold to a consolidator, and the advisor earns fees and a small equity slice.
cluster_name: Independent funeral homes facing key-person, overnight and consolidation pressure

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow, deal-by-deal advisory with few transactions, not a scalable software business.
judges.note: Genuinely non-obvious land-versus-operation split, and fees per deal are large. It stays a real-estate advisory shop.

judges.fatal_flaw: Real-estate splits close in 12-18 months; owners are emotionally attached and unresponsive
judges.note: Clever land-versus-business insight, but cash arrives late and needs deal and zoning expertise.

judges.fatal_flaw: Zoning, entitlement and emotional owners make deals slow; few close within months.
judges.note: Splitting land from an obsolete operating business is a genuinely non-obvious real-estate arbitrage tied to cremation and zoning reform.

title: Live-In Caretaker Tenants for Homes in Probate
one_liner: A managed service that places vetted short-term tenants in homes stuck in probate. The rent covers carrying costs, the occupied status keeps the house insured, and the estate gets a caretaker instead of a vacant liability.
cluster_name: Houses caught in death, divorce or care transitions

judges.fatal_flaw: Executors fear liability; tenant rights complicate turnover; occupied-rider insurance unproven.
judges.note: Real vacancy pain and attorney channel, but services-heavy at $250/month with legal exposure.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tenant-protection laws, executor authority and insurer acceptance make each house risky.
judges.note: Creative reframing of probate vacancy as supply; unit economics ($250/mo) and legal risk limit scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Occupants can gain tenant rights that block sale, and executor-authority liability is high.
judges.note: Probate as hidden housing supply is sharp, but property guardian models exist and legal risk is severe.

title: Paid Exit Capture: Layoffs Become Agent Evals
one_liner: Pay departing employees a completion bonus to turn their tacit exception-handling know-how into the eval sets and edge-case playbooks the employer's AI agents need, before that knowledge walks out.
cluster_name: Employers restructuring for AI: layoffs, severance and displaced workers

judges.fatal_flaw: Legal, IP and incentive friction; the severance window is short and HR-sensitive.
judges.note: Timely and clever: paying leavers for eval ground truth; big if it works, but enterprise sales are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Enterprises unlikely to fund during layoffs; angry leavers and legal friction lengthen cycles.
judges.note: Original angle on layoffs as eval source, but large-enterprise buyers rarely close within six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employers hesitate to run this during sensitive layoffs; leaver incentives and legal exposure.
judges.note: Incentive redesign is clever, but buyers are HR-averse and the ground-truth value claim is untested.

title: Licensed Cozy Games for Memory Care
one_liner: A turnkey activity program for senior living made of commercially licensed cozy indie games, in a kiosk kit that logs resident participation for compliance paperwork.
cluster_name: Dementia and Alzheimer's care at home and in memory care

judges.fatal_flaw: Small activity budgets; hardware kits and per-title licensing make unit economics thin.
judges.note: Clever licensing arbitrage and compliance-logging angle; small market, weak moat, easily copied.

judges.fatal_flaw: Understaffed facilities pay little, and dementia usability of games is unproven.
judges.note: Licensing arbitrage plus compliance logging is a fair wedge, but it is small-ticket senior-care tech with modest defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Facility budgets and admin approvals slow sales; developer revenue share squeezes margin and hardware logistics.
judges.note: Licensing arbitrage plus compliance-log workflow, clear buyer (activity director), cheap pilots. Original wedge in an unglamorous, reachable market.

title: Betting Profit-and-Loss Statements for Credit Unions
one_liner: Turn a member's bank ACH data into an 'investment-style' betting P&L (what they recovered per dollar deposited) and optional spending guardrails, licensed per member to credit unions and neobanks.
cluster_name: Households in debt distress

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit unions move slowly; bettors will not self-select into tool.
judges.note: Framing insight is decent, but B2B sales are slow and consumer pull for a P&L is weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit-union sales cycles are slow; bettors won't self-select into guardrails.
judges.note: Clever ROI reframing for bettors and viral consumer wedge; but B2B2C distribution and modest ARPU.

judges.fatal_flaw: Credit unions buy slowly; consumers reject tools that frame them as gamblers.
judges.note: 'Recovery ratio' investor vocabulary is clever, timely with prediction markets; B2B revenue lags six months.

title: Robot Finger That Makes Legacy Instruments Agent-Operable
one_liner: A camera-plus-servo retrofit box that presses buttons, turns knobs and reads displays on validated lab and test equipment from the outside, giving decade-old instruments an API without touching their software.
cluster_name: Autonomous and AI-directed labs: infrastructure, safety and access

judges.fatal_flaw: GxP quality units will still demand qualification; per-instrument hardware dev slows sales.
judges.note: Interesting validation-sidestep insight, but hardware, interface diversity and cautious regulated buyers delay first revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: GxP QA may refuse unvalidated actuators; every instrument needs custom mounting.
judges.note: Revalidation-avoidance insight is real and non-obvious. Hardware customization and slow QA buying slow first revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Per-instrument mechanical fragility, and validated GxP labs approve new devices slowly.
judges.note: Revalidation, not tech, blocks lab automation; an operator-equivalent actuator is a sharp wedge with recurring revenue and a big installed base.

title: Install Clubs: Brazilian Consórcio for Home Contractors
one_liner: A contractor-anchored, interest-free buying pool: 60-200 homeowners pay monthly into escrow and each month a few move up the queue (by draw or bid) to get their roof, heat pump or solar+battery installed.
cluster_name: Households upgrading homes: electrification, roofs and solar loans

judges.fatal_flaw: Contractor fronts installs to early winners, creating an unlicensed credit product.
judges.note: Creative structure, but escrow, state deposit laws and contractor-default risk block early revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: State deposit, lottery and escrow laws, plus contractor-default risk borne by prepaying homeowners.
judges.note: Imports the consórcio as a prepaid-service queue, which is truly original. Legal and trust risk is heavy, and demand is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: State prepaid-deposit and lottery laws; homeowners' money at risk if contractor fails.
judges.note: Original import with real contractor pain, but waiting for install doesn't fit urgent roofs and heat pumps.

title: Pattern-Less Foundry Network via Printed Sand Molds
one_liner: Print sand molds centrally and pour them at idle small foundries to deliver castings in about two weeks with no patterns.
cluster_name: US machine shops and reshoring manufacturers

judges.fatal_flaw: Casting quality, liability and coordinating 10-30 foundries; printed-sand bureaus already exist.
judges.note: Idle furnace hours plus a printed-mold interface is interesting, but capital-heavy with an unproven tariff-driven demand claim.

judges.fatal_flaw: Casting quality liability and foundry coordination; printed-sand bureaus can go direct.
judges.note: Non-obvious pattern-less casting interface with real reshoring pull; capital-heavy, quality risk, slow to first orders.

judges.fatal_flaw: Casting quality and liability; on-demand manufacturing incumbents; thin 25-35% margin
judges.note: Manual brokered first orders are feasible and reshoring helps, but quality, certs and incumbents limit scaling.

title: Supply-Continuity Escrow for Hardware Startups
one_liner: Software-style source-code escrow, but for physical products: startups deposit CAD, BOMs and tooling data, and a pre-qualified micro-factory network is contractually obligated to keep making parts for buyers if the startup dies.
cluster_name: Customers stranded when a product's maker disappears

judges.fatal_flaw: Release rights are hard to enforce; buyers rarely value continuity enough to pay.
judges.note: Interesting escrow analogy, but physical continuity is hard to prove, unenforceable in bankruptcy, and the startup buyer base is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cash-poor startups will not pay; buyers may not accept escrow as real continuity
judges.note: Fresh framing: growth spend funds the continuity network. Proof-of-manufacturability is a real moat. Trust and validation costs are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Contractual micro-factory obligation is hard to enforce and validate; buyers pay only after a deal stalls.
judges.note: Deal-closing letter is an easy sell to founders; $2.5k pilot feasible, but lawyering-heavy.

title: Training-Day School Inside Youth Sports Facilities
one_liner: Turn the empty weekday hours of club-sports facilities into ESA- and scholarship-funded microschools for serious young athletes.
cluster_name: Microschools, homeschoolers and shrinking districts

judges.fatal_flaw: Occupancy codes, school registration and teacher hiring make each site slow and heavy.
judges.note: Idle facilities meet ESA money cleverly, but execution is operationally heavy and policy-dependent.

judges.fatal_flaw: School registration and occupancy code delay launches; ops-heavy per site.
judges.note: ESA money is real budget and idle-hours pain is concrete. Sales need legal setup first; per-site revenue decent but slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Change-of-occupancy code and school-operator burden are heavy; running schools is a different business.
judges.note: Uses idle facility hours with ESA money, but it is a heavy compliance lift and close to Alpha School copycats.

title: Licensed Principal-of-Record for Financial Agents
one_liner: Buy a retiring independent insurance agency, then rent its licenses, carrier appointments and supervision layer to AI-agent builders that need a legally accountable entity behind every quote and bind.
cluster_name: Accountability and guardrails for AI agents acting for others

judges.fatal_flaw: Agent-builder demand for bound insurance is thin today; state rules may require each sub-producer licensed.
judges.note: Licenses plus appointments are the scarce input; renewals fund it. A sponsor-bank-style toll on autonomous sellers, and non-consensus.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs seven-figure acquisition capital, regulatory blessing, and few paying agent startups.
judges.note: Renewal book gives cash flow, but capital and regulation rule out a scrappy start.

judges.fatal_flaw: License-renting looks like fronting to regulators; buying an agency needs capital.
judges.note: Accountable principal for AI sellers is a sharp idea. Renewals fund it, but the capital and regulatory risk are heavy.

title: Neutral Noise-and-Flight Monitors for Drone Hubs
one_liner: Independent noise and flight-log monitoring that gives cities and neighbors a referee for drone-delivery hub permits, and gives operators and retail hosts approvable evidence.
cluster_name: Aircraft and drone operators: maintenance, parts, permits and navigation

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers are a few large operators with long procurement cycles; cities cannot pay.
judges.note: Fresh, real permit friction and a neutral-referee angle, but tiny customer count and hardware-lite, city-dependent sales.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market of a few hundred sites; operators paying for neutrality invites conflict-of-interest doubts.
judges.note: Local permitting as binding constraint is a sharp insight, but revenue ceiling is very low.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a few hundred sites total, so the prize is small at $6k a site.
judges.note: Local permitting, not the FAA, gates drone hubs; neutral referee is non-obvious, timely (Lowe's launch), and cheap to start.

title: Second Look: Illustrators as Fake-Image Examiners
one_liner: A bench of displaced illustrators and retouchers trained as human image examiners who certify or flag photos in insurance claims, rental deposits, and e-commerce refunds, with written, defensible reasons.
cluster_name: Defensible authenticity evidence for disputed digital media

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers bundle detection or build in-house; low per-image price limits scale
judges.note: Human explainability wedge is original and quick to pilot, but slow insurer sales and thin volume.

judges.fatal_flaw: Human review does not scale; capture-time provenance and automated tools undercut it.
judges.note: Defensible human rationale versus probability scores is a good contrarian angle, but is an arms race with limited scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Human review services don't scale; detectors and provenance standards will commoditize
judges.note: Defensible-explanation insight is good and buyers are pained now, but it is a services business.

title: Technique Capture for Cell Therapy Tech Transfer
one_liner: Instrumented video-and-sensor capture of the 'artisanal' manual steps in cell therapy processes, turned into numeric parameters and training packages for CDMO tech transfer.
cluster_name: Real-world skill and object data for robot and industrial-AI builders

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool in a contracting cell-therapy sector; long procurement cycles.
judges.note: Tech-transfer insurance framing avoids automation bets and is original, but the market is narrow and shrinking.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool; customers may keep know-how in-house or rely on CDMO handoffs.
judges.note: Tech-transfer insurance framing is smart and needs no capex, but the market is narrow and the data play speculative.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cash-strapped biotechs and CDMOs own tech transfer; video-to-parameters value unproven.
judges.note: Budgeted tech-transfer pain and capital-light, but bespoke sales to a narrow, downturn-hit buyer.

title: Tip Provenance Ledger for Tipped-Occupation Employers
one_liner: An evidence trail that classifies every dollar as a voluntary tip, service charge, pool or cash tip, to support new tip-deduction reporting.
cluster_name: Workforce compliance for remote, tipped and platform workers

judges.fatal_flaw: Toast, Square and payroll vendors will bundle tip classification; low price per location.
judges.note: Strong deadline-driven why-now and quick pilots, but it is a feature POS vendors will absorb.

judges.fatal_flaw: POS and payroll vendors will bundle tip reporting; restaurants resist paying $29 a month.
judges.note: Real January 2027 deadline, but low ARPU, churny restaurant customers and thin incremental value.

judges.fatal_flaw: Toast, Square and payroll vendors will add provenance fields natively; low price points.
judges.note: Tip-deduction incentive to relabel pay is real and deadline-driven, but SMB compliance software is easily bundled.

title: Import Compliance Desk for Hobby Brands
one_liner: Subscription compliance for small tabletop, designer-toy, card-accessory and collectible brands covering CPSC eFiling, product certificates, EU representative and tariff classification.
cluster_name: Tariff cost, classification and customs for small importers

judges.fatal_flaw: Low ARPU niche; customs brokers and generic compliance vendors can serve it, and the deadline is transient.
judges.note: Easy first sales via a time-boxed CPSC deadline. Niche compliance with weak defensibility and a small ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small, price-sensitive customers may churn after one-off audit.
judges.note: Hard CPSC deadline just live, reachable communities, $299 audit wedge; ten paying customers in months is realistic.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small revenue per brand; freight forwarders, brokers and labs already bundle CPSC filings.
judges.note: Timely eFiling deadline and niche vertical rulings, and a $299 audit is quick to sell, but the prize and moat are small.

title: Get Paid to Care: Family Caregiver Enrollment
one_liner: A navigator that gets family caregivers onto Medicaid and VA payrolls, then becomes the fiscal intermediary that pays them.
cluster_name: Home and residential care: labor supply, family caregivers and small-scale models

judges.fatal_flaw: Approval and hours rest with state assessors; free public navigators may undercut the $349 fee.
judges.note: Consumer pays upfront for money-making outcome; reachable via caregiver groups; strong Medicaid-cut timing; fast first sales.

judges.fatal_flaw: Families won't pay $349 for enrollment help that counties give free.
judges.note: Paid-relative pathway is useful but well known, and state budget cuts erode it. Consumer-paid navigation is a weak business.

judges.fatal_flaw: States contract few fiscal intermediaries; high consumer CAC; paid-relative rules may tighten.
judges.note: Large, real paid-relative pathway insight; the FI phase is the prize but hard to win.

title: Financial-Aid Overflow Desk for New Loan Caps
one_liner: A managed service plus software that classifies programs as professional versus graduate, tracks lifetime caps and prevents mis-awards at small colleges' aid offices.
cluster_name: Colleges and training programs under new federal loan caps and earnings tests

judges.fatal_flaw: One-cycle compliance pain; incumbent aid vendors patch software within a year.
judges.note: Defined reachable buyers and $5K audit entry; consulting-heavy, bridge loans need capital, small prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Vendors catch up or rules change, shrinking the 12-18 month window.
judges.note: Acute, dated pain at underserved small aid offices; fast audit sale, but insight is mostly timing.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time rule window; a services desk for small colleges with tight budgets.
judges.note: Temporary regulatory-confusion opportunity. Small offices can't pay much, and rules may change again.

title: Street-Level Gas Pipe Retirement Optimizer
one_liner: Software plus a turnkey block-by-block electrification crew that tells gas utilities which streets to retire instead of replace.
cluster_name: Households upgrading homes: electrification, roofs and solar loans

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility sales cycles are long, and turnkey electrification crews add heavy operational burden.
judges.note: Reframes pipe-replacement capex as the electrification budget. Large prize and regulator pull; the analytics pilot is sellable.

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility procurement is slow; turnkey crews are capital-heavy; consultants and nonprofits already pilot.
judges.note: Pipe-replacement capex as hidden electrification budget is right and huge, but insiders already know it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Regulated utility sales cycles of 12-24 months and crew delivery needs before revenue.
judges.note: Smart insight on stranded pipe, but a bootstrapper cannot reach ten utilities in six months.

title: Tariff Surcharge Clawback for Downstream Payers
one_liner: Recover itemized tariff surcharges from suppliers who were refunded the tariffs, on contingency, and give surcharge-collecting firms a defensive ledger.
cluster_name: Recovering IEEPA tariff refunds and surcharges

judges.fatal_flaw: Claims of $200-$8k against suppliers yield thin contingency economics and high dispute cost.
judges.note: Same tariff-clawback thesis as I1300 but aimed at tiny firms with smaller, weaker claims and a one-time window.

judges.fatal_flaw: Suppliers have no clear legal duty to pass on refunds; claims uneconomic.
judges.note: Timely SCOTUS-driven angle on downstream payers, but legal basis is shaky and the tariff-refund cluster is crowded.

judges.fatal_flaw: Downstream payers usually lack a contractual claim; demand-letter response rates likely low.
judges.note: Urgent money and easy lead gen, but weak legal basis, tiny claims, thin contingency, and a closing window.

title: Random-Sample CPA Audits of AI Bookkeeping
one_liner: A $79/month independent assurance layer where a licensed CPA reviews a random sample of a micro-business's AI-categorized transactions and signs a monthly accuracy attestation backed by a penalty-reimbursement guarantee.
cluster_name: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Penalty-reimbursement guarantee and attest independence rules create liability that outruns $79/month.
judges.note: Checking is cheaper than doing, and independence is structurally closed to Intuit and Xero. Error-rate data becomes a Consumer Reports asset.

judges.fatal_flaw: Micro-businesses won't pay $79 a month on top of bookkeeping; CPA liability for attestations.
judges.note: Independent-assurance framing is smart, but the buyer's willingness to pay is doubtful and the guarantee is hard to underwrite.

judges.fatal_flaw: Micro-owners won't pay $79/month for verification; CAC and churn break the economics.
judges.note: Independent-auditor logic is sound, but the buyer is vague and price-sensitive. Reselling through bookkeeping firms is the better route.

title: Caring Contacts as a Service for Hospitals
one_liner: Outsourced, human-edited follow-up messages and calls after a suicide-risk emergency visit or crisis call, run on a compliance-grade platform hospitals and 988 centers can buy per patient.
cluster_name: Behavioral health and addiction care capacity

judges.fatal_flaw: Unclear payer and slow hospital procurement; small per-patient budgets
judges.note: Evidence-backed and non-consensus, with an accreditation hook. Market is small and funding is grant-dependent.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hospital and 988 procurement is slow, budgets small, one-staffer alternative is cheap
judges.note: Human note beats AI detection is contrarian and evidence-based; but small ticket and slow public-sector sales.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hospital and 988 procurement cycles exceed six months; clinical liability slows pilots.
judges.note: Evidence-based, budget lines exist, but sales into health systems and crisis centers is slow and pilot-dependent.

title: Vendor Exit Desk for Fleets and Contractors
one_liner: A contingency-fee service that gets small fleets and home-service contractors out of predatory software and telematics contracts, and recovers the money the vendors keep billing.
cluster_name: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: Contracts are enforceable; recoveries are small and unauthorized-practice-of-law risk is real.
judges.note: Self-identifying reviewer leads are clever. But it is a B2B cancel-subscription service, with low recovery odds and little moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Binding contracts limit recoveries; contingency economics and unauthorized-practice risk are shaky.
judges.note: Self-identifying leads and acute dollar pain; quick to first cases, but recovery rates and legal exposure are uncertain.

judges.fatal_flaw: Signed multi-year contracts are enforceable; recoveries are rare, with unauthorized-practice-of-law risk.
judges.note: Self-identifying leads are clever, but a contingency desk for contract disputes has low win rates and doesn't scale.

title: Break-Glass Interim Operators for Deceased Owners' Businesses
one_liner: An on-call bench of laid-off COOs and ops directors who step in within 48 hours when the sole owner of a small business dies, keeping it alive until the heirs can sell or close it.
cluster_name: Owner wind-down, sudden death and tacit-knowledge handoff

judges.fatal_flaw: At-need demand is sporadic; heirs' trust and legal authority hard to win
judges.note: Estate needs a verb not a noun; idle senior operators as supply; attorneys and CPAs are reachable channel.

judges.fatal_flaw: Owner deaths are rare, unpredictable events; pre-need retainers sell like insurance, slowly.
judges.note: Great framing of the estate needing a verb, but referral trust takes time and demand is lumpy.

judges.fatal_flaw: At-need demand is lumpy and hard to sell before death; bench staffing economics.
judges.note: Good 'estate needs a verb' insight. Services bench with sporadic engagements, so it will not become a very large company.

title: Rails Weather: Live Nigerian Payment Reliability Index
one_liner: An independent, always-on measurement of which bank-to-bank transfers are actually working right now, sold as an API and SLA evidence.
cluster_name: Informal finance and payment frictions in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Small Nigerian market; PSPs already hold own reliability data; low price points.
judges.note: Cheap viral status page and neutral-evidence insight, but weak payers and tiny revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny Nigerian ARPU; probe transfers need many bank accounts and may breach terms.
judges.note: Scrappy, neutral time-to-credit data is genuinely novel; ThousandEyes-for-rails could travel across emerging markets.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small revenue per customer, and banks may block probe accounts or flag round-tripping.
judges.note: Downdetector for Nigerian payment rails. Time-to-credit versus reported success is an original metric, and the neutral evidence has real dispute value.

title: Regulatory Slip Desk for Compliance Budget Decisions
one_liner: A probability-weighted deadline desk that tells compliance heads which rules will probably slip, which will not, and which controls are worth building now regardless.
cluster_name: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers want certainty not probabilities; analyst-style subscription hard to scale or defend.
judges.note: Options framing is insightful and public track record is a moat, but it is essentially a research newsletter business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers want certainty and law-firm cover, not probabilistic slip forecasts they cannot defend.
judges.note: Content-led and cheap to launch with pre-sales at $6k, but the forecasting moat is unproven and credibility takes time.

judges.fatal_flaw: Compliance heads are punished for betting on delay, so they will not budget from probabilities.
judges.note: Options-thinking about regulatory slip is fresh. Public track record is a moat, but buyer behavior is doubtful.

title: Wet-Lab Materials Bill-of-Materials Scanner
one_liner: Black Duck for biology: scan a startup's plasmids, cell lines, antibodies and enzymes for license, MTA and patent encumbrances before an investor or acquirer does.
cluster_name: Biotech capital: diligence and salvage

judges.fatal_flaw: Building a reliable encumbrance database is slow, attorney-heavy and liable if wrong.
judges.note: Original 'bill of materials for biology' with two-sided diligence demand. Deal wave helps; narrow buyer pool and database moat are unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers may not see encumbrances as urgent; curated encumbrance database is costly to build.
judges.note: High price per scan and novel BOM framing, but tiny market and diligence rarely hinges on it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Encumbrance database is hard to curate; only a few thousand buyers.
judges.note: Clever diligence angle with two-sided pull; small TAM and thin why-now.

title: Market Rulebook Red Team for New Venues
one_liner: Turn a trading venue's plain-English rulebook into an executable model, then use adversarial agents to find manipulation exploits and propose rule patches before real attackers do.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers with small budgets; in-house teams and existing DeFi simulation firms compete.
judges.note: Rulebook-as-uncompiled-code is interesting and prediction markets are booming. Tiny customer set and DARPA is not demand.

judges.fatal_flaw: Formalizing rulebooks and finding real exploits is R&D-hard, with few buyers.
judges.note: Rulebook as uncompiled code is a clever frame. Prediction-market venues are plausible buyers, but technical risk is high.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers; rule audits are unproven budget line and DARPA hook is inference.
judges.note: Novel and smart, but tiny buyer universe and unproven willingness to pay $25k for rule audits.

title: Fresh-Address Desk for Medicaid Plans
one_liner: Turn Title I front offices into a consent-based channel that keeps families on Medicaid, paid per household retained by health plans and hospitals, with a revenue share to the school.
cluster_name: Benefit-rule changes: Medicaid work rules, SNAP and ACA cliffs

judges.fatal_flaw: Schools and immigrant families resist data-sharing with plans; FERPA and Medicaid marketing rules.
judges.note: School front office as freshest low-income address channel; big Medicaid retention budgets; consent design is the moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Three-party consent, district approval and Medicaid marketing rules stall first revenue
judges.note: Sharp insight about school records, but multi-party privacy-laden sale is unlikely to close 10 payers in six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: FERPA and privacy backlash; principals refuse to become insurer data channel.
judges.note: School secretary holds freshest low-income contact data is a genuine insight. Consent and trust make it fragile.

title: Universal Depot Operator for Stacked EPR Programs
one_liner: One neutral drop-off depot per town that serves batteries, paint, oil containers, textiles and small e-waste for many producer responsibility programs at once.
cluster_name: Recycling quality, distressed capacity and battery/EPR compliance

judges.fatal_flaw: PROs may keep their own haulers; per-site volumes are tiny and margins thin.
judges.note: Sound aggregator insight with regulatory tailwind; ops-heavy, slow to scale, but real budgets exist.

judges.fatal_flaw: PROs have entrenched hauler contracts, per-site volumes are tiny, and ops capital is heavy.
judges.note: Good stacked-EPR insight but ops-heavy and dependent on slow PRO contracts. Colorado volumes are too small to fund a depot.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few PRO buyers; hazmat permitting for mixed streams; long institutional sales cycles.
judges.note: One-trip-many-programs aggregation is logical but buyer count is tiny and incumbents hold host relationships.

title: Parametric Recovery Cover for Tourism Towns
one_liner: Annual parametric policies bought by destination tourism boards that pay out within days when fire, smoke, flood or road closures crater visitor demand, even with no physical damage.
cluster_name: Fast parametric cash for weather and disaster shocks

judges.fatal_flaw: Public-entity sales cycles, basis risk, and scarce capacity for tiny-town risks.
judges.note: Original buyer (tourism board with lodging-tax funding) but small premium pool, long sales cycle, and insurance licensing overhead.

judges.fatal_flaw: Broker licensing, public-entity procurement and basis risk make the first bound policy slow.
judges.note: Tourism boards as parametric buyers, backed by public lodging-tax loss histories. Softening reinsurance is a real why-now.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs a fronting carrier and licensed MGA capacity, and public procurement is slow.
judges.note: Smart buyer insight (tourism boards) but licensing, basis risk and public budget cycles make the first bound policy slow.

title: Wind Tunnel for Agent Markets and Pricing Collusion
one_liner: Simulate your pricing or buying agent against thousands of rival agents to see whether it drifts into tacit collusion, manipulation or first-offer traps before regulators or rivals do.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers, unproven standard, and long sales to antitrust counsel
judges.note: Interesting crash-test framing with big tickets, but credibility takes years and 10 customers in six months is unlikely.

judges.fatal_flaw: Same discoverability problem, and broader framing gives buyers less urgency than the sharper twin.
judges.note: Same idea as I0739 with a weaker, eval-flavored framing and less legal wedge. Still credible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Audit results are discoverable evidence; vendors avoid documenting collusion propensity.
judges.note: Crash-test standard for pricing agents is original and timely, but few buyers and privilege structuring is required.

title: Fee-Free Hire Receipts for Migrant Workers
one_liner: A worker-held credential proving a migrant was recruited without fees and paid as contracted, sold to suppliers and brands that must prove no forced labour, and portable to the worker's next job.
cluster_name: Exporters meeting foreign sustainability and representation rules

judges.fatal_flaw: Brand buyers' urgency is 15+ months out; audit incumbents exist; enforcement may slip
judges.note: Compelling worker-side insight, but vague multi-country customer and long, budget-less sales cycles.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brands buy slowly ahead of 2027 enforcement; NGO and worker-voice vendors already occupy the space.
judges.note: Worker-held fee-free receipts prove a negative that audits cannot; EU deadline is real but the ground is partly crowded.

judges.fatal_flaw: EU enforcement may be diluted; hard field ops verifying zero fees in source corridors.
judges.note: Worker-held evidence is genuinely non-consensus and large; slow brand sales and scrappy-team execution burden.

title: PFAS-Cleared Succession for Plating Shops
one_liner: Fixed-price wastewater and PFAS readiness reports that let retiring plating and anodizing owners sell to buyers and lenders, feeding a buyer marketplace.
cluster_name: US machine shops and reshoring manufacturers

judges.fatal_flaw: A few hundred sales a year; environmental consultants already sell diligence reports.
judges.note: Sharp reshoring-finishing insight but a very small, lumpy niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few shop transactions per year; needs credible PFAS engineering capability to deliver reports.
judges.note: Real deal-blocking pain, brokers as channel, $9-18K reports; small niche but high-ticket and highly defensible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few plating-shop transactions a year, and environmental consultants already sell diligence reports.
judges.note: Finishing, not machining, is the reshoring bottleneck; unpriced water and PFAS liability blocks succession. Real but niche.

title: Human Trust-Anchor Service for Driverless Freight Hubs
one_liner: A neutral crew and signature service at autonomous-truck terminals that replaces the driver's role as freight's witness: pre-trip inspection, condition-of-freight capture, signed digital BOL and inspector liaison, priced per handoff.
cluster_name: Autonomous-vehicle fleets' ground infrastructure and stakeholders

judges.fatal_flaw: AV carriers will vertically integrate hub handoffs; volumes are tiny for years
judges.note: Sharp insight that driverless trucks remove the witness. Too early, with only about 200 trucks.

judges.fatal_flaw: Too few driverless handoffs today; buyers concentrated in a few AV carriers.
judges.note: Insightful witness framing, but volumes are tiny now and it depends on a handful of AV carriers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only about 200 driverless trucks today, and carriers may staff terminals themselves.
judges.note: Sharpest reframe: driverless trucking removes the witness. Real 2026 shift, but volume is early and the buyer pool tiny.

title: Skill Rooms: Proctored Work-Sample Studios for Hiring
one_liner: Walk-in, device-free testing studios where candidates take a 90-minute employer-designed work sample under ID-verified proctoring, with a portable score that many employers honor.
cluster_name: Verifying real human skill, identity and authorship in hiring and education

judges.fatal_flaw: Physical studios, candidate no-shows and employer acceptance make unit economics thin.
judges.note: Real hiring-fraud pain, but per-sitting economics and metro logistics slow a scrappy team.

judges.fatal_flaw: Candidates won't travel to studios, and employers can run on-site tests themselves.
judges.note: Portable proctored score is a real network-effect prize as remote hiring signal collapses. Physical footprint and cold start are hard.

judges.fatal_flaw: Physical studios are capital heavy, and employers rarely honor another firm's portable score.
judges.note: Obvious response to AI cheating; Pearson VUE and in-person interview returns limit the space; two-sided cold start.

title: Bonded US-Only Remote Operators for Robots
one_liner: A staffing company for physical AI: background-checked, bonded, US-resident remote operators working from secure facilities on SLA-backed shifts to assist robotaxis, delivery robots and teleoperated humanoids.
cluster_name: Teleoperated labor and remote pilot workforces

judges.fatal_flaw: Big fleets build teleop in-house; staffing margins and startup customers' budgets are thin.
judges.note: Operator-hours scale with robot fleets; US-only auditable labor is a real political wedge, but weak defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Big fleets keep operators in-house, and small robot startups buy few hours.
judges.note: Labor arbitrage is plausible, but the customer base is tiny and liability and integration burdens are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Large fleets in-source remote assistance; small robot startups are cheap buyers
judges.note: Political fight over where operators sit is real; staffing model has low defensibility.

title: Audit-Proof Family Night in a Box
one_liner: Fixed-price, compliance-packaged family engagement events for Title I schools, paid from the federally required parent-engagement set-aside, with the monitoring binder as the real product.
cluster_name: K-12 districts' legal service duties: IEPs, attendance, nutrition and Title I

judges.fatal_flaw: District procurement and seasonality slow sales; event logistics cap margins and scale.
judges.note: Earmarked money principals fear to spend; binder is the real product; pilots sellable to a principal without a district RFP.

judges.fatal_flaw: District procurement is slow and event-service margins limit scale.
judges.note: Audit-fear-as-product is non-obvious and timely with unspent funds, but small niche and a services business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Event-services business with no software leverage; small earmarked pool, slow district buying.
judges.note: Audit-fear insight is sharp, but a catering-and-binder business will not scale to venture size.

title: Contractor Location and Payout Attestation for Sanctions Safety
one_liner: Continuous proof that remote contractors are where they say and are paid where they claim, giving employers evidence against North Korean IT-worker sanctions exposure.
cluster_name: Verifying real human skill, identity and authorship in hiring and education

judges.fatal_flaw: EOR and payroll platforms already screen payouts; small firms may not feel urgency.
judges.note: Sharp finance-and-legal budget angle and a cheap CSV audit wedge. Small ACV, and a crowded hiring-fraud neighborhood.

judges.fatal_flaw: EOR and payroll platforms will bundle payout screening; device attestation requires contractor consent.
judges.note: Payout-account chokepoint and finance/legal buyer are good insights, but incumbents own the rails and the threat is niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Narrow exposure, and identity and payments-risk vendors can add it as a feature.
judges.note: Payout-account chokepoint and finance/legal buyer are sharp, but it is a feature-sized market.

title: Legal Price Bargaining Co-ops for Salmon Fleets
one_liner: Back-office software and staff that let independent salmon boats negotiate price as one bloc under the 1934 Fishermen's Collective Marketing Act, as the Bering Sea crab fleet already does.
cluster_name: Fisheries and ecosystem-service operators

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable market, and fishermen distrust collective action and fear processor retaliation.
judges.note: Sharpest contrarian insight: a 1934 antitrust exemption is unused because operations are missing, not law. Tiny but defensible wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny TAM, antitrust fear, and fleets historically fail to cohere.
judges.note: Unusual and legally clever insight, but revenue per association is tiny and adoption depends on fishermen's collective will.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyer is an association that does not exist yet, and processors will resist.
judges.note: Original legal insight, but organizing hundreds of fishermen first means a slow sales cycle and a small prize.

title: Private Set Intersection Mule Graph for Credit Unions
one_liner: Let hundreds of small banks and credit unions ask 'has anyone flagged this payee account?' without revealing customers or lists, using cryptographic private set intersection.
cluster_name: Banks and platforms disrupting scam networks and recovering victims' funds

judges.fatal_flaw: Network-effect cold start plus long credit-union security reviews and core integrations.
judges.note: Sound idea for fraud sharing, but slow sales, integration burden and entrenched consortia.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cold-start network among slow-buying credit unions; Verafin and Early Warning own distribution.
judges.note: Cryptography removes the sharing objection, but fraud consortia are crowded and sales cycles are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cold-start network effect and slow core-processor sales; Early Warning and Verafin incumbents.
judges.note: PSI removes the liability and leakage objection to sharing. A regional league can seed it. Bank sales are slow.

title: Make Platforms and Receiving Banks Pay Scam Refunds
one_liner: A contingency-fee desk that packages evidence so banks can recover mandatory scam reimbursements from receiving institutions and, in the EU, from the platforms where the scam ran.
cluster_name: Banks and platforms disrupting scam networks and recovering victims' funds

judges.fatal_flaw: UK 50:50 split is already scheme-automated; EU platform liability is not yet law
judges.note: Claims-market framing is smart, but the core premise is partly wrong and the platform leg is premature.

judges.fatal_flaw: Platform liability not yet in force; UK 50:50 split already automated.
judges.note: Contingency claims market is clever, but recoverable dollars near term look small and unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: UK 50:50 split already settles via scheme; platform liability not yet law.
judges.note: Liability creates a claims market and contingency pricing is clean. The UK split is largely automated, which shrinks the prize.

title: Sell the Route, Not the Business
one_liner: A standardized customer-book sale with a retention earn-out held in escrow and released automatically from payment data.
cluster_name: Trade-shop succession and buyouts

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny deal sizes, lumpy transaction revenue, and legal and licensing friction in customer-list sales.
judges.note: Retention-escrow earn-out is a genuine product and the competitor is the natural buyer, but liquidity is hard and take is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny per-deal fees; customer consent and non-portability of relationships weaken the asset
judges.note: Selling the book with retention escrow is neat, but silver-tsunami small-business exits are widely targeted.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sourcing sellers is hard, deals are small and slow, and escrow may raise money-transmitter issues
judges.note: Real gap below broker size. The competitor-as-buyer insight is good and a hand-brokered first three deals are feasible.

title: Side-Selling Early Warning for Milk and Coffee Coops
one_liner: A churn-prediction and targeted-advance service that tells dairy and coffee cooperatives which farmers are about to side-sell to cash brokers, and triggers the right cash intervention before the volume walks away.
cluster_name: Smallholders and rural households in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Small, cash-poor Kenyan coops; churn model is a feature; not venture-scale.
judges.note: Good insight that side-selling is a cash-timing problem, but the market is narrow and founder-dependent.

judges.fatal_flaw: Coops may lack working capital or clean data to fund advances.
judges.note: Side-selling as cash-timing, not disloyalty; institutional buyer, performance-priced, founder has warm access; small per-coop prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Coop board sales cycles and coops lacking working capital to fund advances.
judges.note: Sharp insight (side-selling is cash-timing) and outcome-based pay, but pay-on-lift plus a 60-day test delays revenue.

title: Right-Size Rx: Deprescribing After GLP-1 Starts
one_liner: Pharmacist outreach that adjusts insulin, sulfonylureas and BP meds in the weeks after a GLP-1 start, sold to payers on avoided harm and drug spend.
cluster_name: GLP-1 patients' transitions: procedures, medication changes, quitting and aftercare

judges.fatal_flaw: Payers buy slowly and existing MTM vendors can bolt on triggered outreach.
judges.note: Real clinical protocol gap next to GLP-1 spend; CFO-line framing is smart, large prize, slow payer cycle.

judges.fatal_flaw: Existing MTM vendors and hard-to-prove savings; long payer pilot cycles
judges.note: Genuine unowned clinical gap in a huge drug wave, but a pharmacist-services model with thin PMPM economics.

judges.fatal_flaw: Payer sales cycles are long and pharmacists need prescriber authority to adjust meds.
judges.note: Genuine clinical gap with CFO-friendly savings, but payer pilots and prescriber protocols won't close in six months.

title: Rescue Orphaned Steno Notes With Stroke-Level AI
one_liner: A translation service that turns retired or deceased reporters' unreadable steno files into certifiable transcripts for stalled appeals, using a neural stroke-to-text model in place of the missing personal dictionary.
cluster_name: Small litigation practices lacking evidence, records and benchmark tools

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market, slow court buyers, and idiosyncratic steno makes model accuracy doubtful.
judges.note: Acute, invisible pain; workable as retired-reporter service at first, but small prize and uncertain tech.

judges.fatal_flaw: Personal briefs make decoding unreliable; tiny addressable market.
judges.note: Highly original hidden problem (orphaned steno notes) with real retirement-wave why-now, but very small prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market: a few appeals per court, slow procurement, and certification friction.
judges.note: Highly original and urgent for stalled appeals, but the prize is small and one-off per file.

title: Peer-Made Aide Training in Creole, Spanish, Tagalog
one_liner: A library of short scenario videos made by experienced home-care aides in their own languages, RN-reviewed and sold to agencies as required in-service training that keeps new aides from quitting.
cluster_name: Home and residential care: labor supply, family caregivers and small-scale models

judges.fatal_flaw: Creator supply and quality control hard; low per-aide price and content-vendor competition.
judges.note: Peer credibility as a retention device is a real insight; modest ARPU and slow agency procurement.

judges.fatal_flaw: Incumbent e-learning vendors; low ARPU and upfront content production
judges.note: Compliance line item is budgeted and peer-made angle is genuine; reachable via agency associations, but modest revenue per agency.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agencies buy cheapest compliance training; $9-14 per aide is a hard sell
judges.note: Peer-in-your-language credibility as a retention device is a real insight, but it is low-ACV content in a crowded training niche.

title: Rain-Day Revenue Insurance for Patio Restaurants
one_liner: Parametric weather cover for restaurants: pick your bad-weather trigger, get paid automatically when it hits, with payouts calibrated to your own POS history.
cluster_name: Fast parametric cash for weather and disaster shocks

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs MGA and carrier licensing; parametric weather incumbents may already cover restaurants
judges.note: POS history as underwriting fixes basis risk, a real insight. Big SMB market. Carrier dependency slows the first live policies.

judges.fatal_flaw: Adverse selection and licensing; owners rarely buy demand-risk cover and no season to sell
judges.note: POS-calibrated triggers to cut basis risk is a good idea, but insurance heavy, unverified competitors, and owners choose their own triggers.

judges.fatal_flaw: No revenue until a licensed MGA and reinsurer are signed; adverse selection on owner-picked triggers.
judges.note: Founder-owned restaurants and POS-fitted triggers are a real insight, but insurance licensing gates any sale.

title: The Second Ceremony After Direct Cremation
one_liner: A scattering-day and celebration-of-life concierge for the majority of families who chose cremation with no service and later realize they need a ritual.
cluster_name: Families choosing direct cremation with no ritual

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time purchase, hard to reach families through cremation providers who resist.
judges.note: Real unbundling of ritual, easy first customers, but obvious to death-care watchers, local, and hard to scale or defend.

judges.fatal_flaw: Local, lumpy, hard-to-scale service with costly customer acquisition in a one-time grief moment.
judges.note: Real gap after direct cremation, fair unit economics, providers and hospice as channels. Five events achievable without technology.

judges.fatal_flaw: Infrequent, local, planner-heavy purchase with costly customer acquisition and low tech leverage.
judges.note: Real unbundled second-funeral vacuum with growing cremation share, but a lifestyle event service, not a scalable platform.

title: Tell Us Once: US Death-Event Switchboard
one_liner: Verify an executor once, then let agents notify and close dozens of institutions for you, building toward a reusable 'authority to act' credential the institutions accept.
cluster_name: Executors and small probate firms drowning in estate paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Institutions demand originals and their own forms, so agents cannot bypass verification and human ops cost eats margin.
judges.note: Real one-time executor pain, funeral-home channel is reachable, but there are existing estate services and the credential vision is grandiose.

judges.fatal_flaw: Institutions won't accept a private credential; Empathy, Lantern and others already compete.
judges.note: Voice and browser agents applied to estate close-out is the obvious agent play; the credential vision is far off.

judges.fatal_flaw: Institutions legally demand their own certified documents; unlikely to accept a shared credential
judges.note: Recurring universal event, funeral-home distribution; but estate-admin startups and voice-agent playbooks are increasingly crowded.

title: Voucher Lease-Up Desk for Soft Markets
one_liner: An ops service that gets units voucher-ready and through housing-authority inspection and paperwork in days, turning Section 8 from a hassle into the cheapest demand source in a soft market.
cluster_name: Landlords in soft markets: vouchers, evictions, vacancies and retention

judges.fatal_flaw: Delays come from housing-authority queues the product cannot control.
judges.note: Per-lease-up pricing and soft-market timing help, but the bottleneck sits with authorities, not landlords.

judges.fatal_flaw: Housing-authority delays, not landlord paperwork, are the true bottleneck; soft market may reverse.
judges.note: Cycle-time framing is neat and pay-per-lease-up is easy to test, but small market and dependent on authority funding.

judges.fatal_flaw: Bottleneck is housing authority backlog, not landlord prep; authority funding stress.
judges.note: Cycle-time framing in soft markets is smart. Value depends on authorities operators can't control.

title: CRA Technical-File Compiler Built Into CI
one_liner: A GitHub/GitLab app that assembles the Cyber Resilience Act technical documentation, Annex I evidence and draft declaration of conformity from every release, so compliance is a build artifact rather than a consulting project.
cluster_name: EU digital product laws for small connected-device makers

judges.fatal_flaw: Full application not until Dec 2027; urgency lags and CRA tooling is crowding
judges.note: Live regulation, dev-tool wedge, paid pilots at EUR 3-5k feasible; urgency moderate, competition rising.

judges.fatal_flaw: Vanta, Drata, SBOM vendors and consultants bundle CRA modules; standards still unsettled.
judges.note: Hard deadline and a dev-first angle help, but it is crowded compliance automation with an unproven willingness to pay.

judges.fatal_flaw: SBOM and GRC vendors bundle CRA; buyers wait for harmonised standards
judges.note: Dev-tool framing is smart but this is compliance-automation with a regulatory hook, already crowded.

title: Real Gross Margin Diligence for AI Startups
one_liner: Quality-of-earnings for agent companies: restate COGS at unsubsidized token prices, retry waste and expiring credits so investors see true unit economics.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Services business; QoE firms and diligence teams will absorb it; small market.
judges.note: Real pain and timing, but consulting-shaped with weak moat and limited prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lumpy deal flow and diligence credibility; QoE incumbents can add token-cost analysis.
judges.note: High tickets, reachable investors, sharp credit-subsidized COGS insight; ten engagements in six months is a stretch.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small services business; Big-4 and QoE boutiques will add token-cost restatement
judges.note: Timely AI M&A wave; gateway logs over the GL is a good point, but low defensibility and a small prize.

title: Flood Cover Sold to the Lender
one_liner: Homeowners won't buy flood insurance, but the bank holding their mortgage should, because the uninsured flood loss lands on the lender's collateral.
cluster_name: Flood and fire survivors: mapping, buyouts, claims and rebuilding

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders can't easily charge borrowers outside mandated zones; regulation and unclear lender ROI.
judges.note: Sensible flip of the buyer to the party bearing the loss; big pool and cheap capacity, but insurance sales cycles are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: MGA licensing and capacity required; community banks slow and cannot mandate coverage.
judges.note: Good distribution-flip insight, but regulated insurance product and slow bank buyers delay revenue beyond six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders cannot force-place non-mandatory flood cover; MGA licensing is heavy and slow.
judges.note: Sell to the party bearing unmandated loss is a sharp reframe, but regulation and sales cycle block six-month revenue.

title: Hazmat Sidecar for Small Old-House Repairs
one_liner: A flat-price, same-week asbestos and lead test-and-remove service that solo-to-five-tech plumbing, HVAC, electrical and flooring shops call when a small job in a pre-1980 house hits suspect material, with the waste manifest handled for them.
cluster_name: Households upgrading homes: electrification, roofs and solar loans

judges.fatal_flaw: Local hazmat service with per-state licensing, liability and poor scalability.
judges.note: Real gap under abatement minimums and an insight about the disposal chain, but it is a local trades business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Upfront certifications, pollution insurance and disposal agreements delay first revenue; local, hard to scale.
judges.note: Real per-job cash pain for trade shops, flat-price service, unit economics work locally; bootstrapper-friendly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Licensing, liability and low job density make a local hazmat service slow to scale.
judges.note: Disposal-chain bottleneck is a real insight, but it is a licensed, labor-heavy local service with weak defensibility.

title: Drone Hub Siting and Permit Intelligence
one_liner: Parcel-level zoning, noise and neighbor-risk scoring, plus done-for-you permit filing, for retailers and drone operators expanding launch hubs.
cluster_name: Aircraft and drone operators: maintenance, parts, permits and navigation

judges.fatal_flaw: Walmart and Wing handle zoning in-house; few hundred sites caps the market
judges.note: Sky is federal, ground is local: true bottleneck shift. But buyers are sophisticated and the site count is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: A handful of buyers and few hundred sites; law firms and in-house teams substitute.
judges.note: Timely and clear ground-versus-sky insight, but tiny customer count and low site volume cap the prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer set of enterprise operators; land-use counsel already does this work.
judges.note: Good insight that zoning is the new bottleneck, but few buyers and enterprise access makes ten customers hard.

title: Blank-First Microplastics: Clean Kits and Data Forensics
one_liner: Sell certified low-shed sampling kits, blank/spike proficiency samples, and legacy-data re-analysis to microplastics labs whose glove-contaminated numbers are now in doubt.
cluster_name: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny lab market; free shed scoreboard may let labs just switch gloves.
judges.note: Concrete negative-control wedge with reachable buyers and cheap start. Market is small and one-paper dependent.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer universe of labs; regulatory demand may not fund a real business.
judges.note: Clever negative-control insight but niche. Small labs and one-off forensic jobs limit the prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny lab market; glove makers can self-certify low-shed products.
judges.note: In a measurement crisis, sell negative controls; Michigan glove paper plus California testing program; scrappy-feasible.

title: Rent Seasonal Nitrate Treatment, Don't Build Plants
one_liner: Trailer-mounted nitrate-removal skids rented to small farm-belt utilities only for the 60-120 days a year when river or shallow-well nitrate spikes.
cluster_name: Small water utilities: staffing, revenue leakage, lead lines and nitrate

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow municipal procurement; incumbents already rent mobile ion-exchange units; brine disposal.
judges.note: Sell-the-peak rental reframes capex as opex; real need, but capital-heavy and incumbents exist.

judges.fatal_flaw: Skids are capital-heavy, utility procurement is slow, and Xylem and Veolia already rent mobile treatment.
judges.note: Real compliance pain with SRF money and a good peak-rental insight. A scrappy team faces long public sales and brine logistics.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-heavy; incumbents already rent mobile ion-exchange; brine disposal; slow utility procurement.
judges.note: Sell-the-peak framing is logical but not new. Hardware and logistics too heavy for scrappy team.

title: Turf-Ban Pivot Desk for Lawn and Irrigation Crews
one_liner: A done-for-you back office that turns lawn-maintenance crews into rebate-financed turf-removal and drip-conversion contractors, and uses their weekly routes as a cheap verification network for water utilities.
cluster_name: Water scarcity: irrigation allocation and new supply

judges.fatal_flaw: 10% of small rebates is thin; bridge financing adds lending risk.
judges.note: Reachable crews and real disruption, but bundle is sprawling and per-job revenue is low.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small lawn firms are hard to reach, and rebate processing is easy to copy.
judges.note: Weekly crew routes as a verification network is clever. Turf bans are real. The core business is still rebate paperwork.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rebate programs are capped and shrinking, and the product sprawls across rebates, finance, marketing and verification.
judges.note: Crew routes as verification network is a nice insight, but core is rebate paperwork with sprawling scope.

title: Care-Home Trigger Desk: Evacuate, Shelter, Cool
one_liner: Automatic, pre-contracted action triggers that move older residents before fire, flood or heat-driven power loss becomes lethal.
