one_liner: Biotechs pay for dogs' cancer care in exchange for clean, immune-competent efficacy data, solving pet-owner affordability and drug-developer validation at once.
cluster_name: Pet owners and insurers squeezed by rising vet bills

judges.fatal_flaw: Biotech sales cycles and INAD regulation preclude revenue within six months.
judges.note: Interesting two-sided logic but heavy clinical infrastructure and 30% margins strain a scrappy team.

judges.fatal_flaw: Regulatory, clinic-network and sponsor sales cycles too slow; thin 30% margin.
judges.note: Two-sided fix for owner affordability and drug validation is inventive and timed to the FDA NAM shift, but heavy to execute.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sponsors rarely pay for dog data; comparative oncology is slow, niche and regulated.
judges.note: Creative two-sided funding swap, but sponsor demand is unproven and unit economics are thin.

title: Orphan Appliance Parts, Crowdsourced From Repair Techs
one_liner: Quirky (dead 2015) crowdsourced gadgets from hobbyist inventors; the 2026 version prints the discontinued $6 plastic part that keeps a $900 appliance out of the landfill, and pays the repair tech who specced it a royalty.
cluster_name: Customers stranded when a product's maker disappears

judges.fatal_flaw: Small tickets, safety liability, and RepairClinic-scale incumbents; print quality and fit unreliable.
judges.note: Right crowd flip versus Quirky, but low-value parts marketplace with fragmented long tail.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low per-part volume, product liability, and printing and shipping costs squeeze margins.
judges.note: Good insight that techs are the right crowd, not hobbyists; easy start on eBay, but a thin business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny ticket sizes across a huge long tail of SKUs; existing Etsy print sellers.
judges.note: Under-$10k start, immediate sales, tech-royalty loop is neat; ceiling is low and liability risk is nonzero.

title: Chain-of-Custody Certificates for Spent PFAS Media
one_liner: A broker and tracking service that consolidates spent GAC and ion-exchange media from small utilities, routes it to verified destruction, and issues auditable certificates that document where the waste went.
cluster_name: PFAS exposure, testing and disposal

judges.fatal_flaw: Incumbent waste haulers and reactivators can offer certificates; destruction capacity and timing are early.
judges.note: Documentation-and-liability-as-product is insightful; change-outs mostly 2028+, so early revenue is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hazardous-waste hauling liability and licensing; Calgon and Veolia bundle take-back; demand pre-2028 thin.
judges.note: Real long-tail liability fear, but early timing and incumbents with reactivation capacity.

judges.fatal_flaw: Reactivation vendors and waste majors already offer take-back; brokerage has thin defensibility.
judges.note: Buyers want absolution more than cheapest disposal is sharp, but timing is early and incumbents hold the physical assets.

title: Loss-Curve Intelligence for Autonomous Trucking Insurance
one_liner: A benchmark and risk-scoring workbench that helps insurers, brokers and carriers price driverless-truck coverage using evidence instead of 'unknown'.
cluster_name: Cover and data for emerging or neglected risks

judges.fatal_flaw: Too few driverless miles and operators unwilling to share telemetry for years.
judges.note: Defining the exposure denominator is a smart FICO-style play, but the market is a few dozen underwriters and data is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few driverless trucks means too little loss data and too few buyers for years.
judges.note: Insight on exposure units is good, but the market barely exists, and a $30k pilot in a month is fantasy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Driverless-truck exposure is tiny for years; too little loss data to support pricing benchmarks.
judges.note: FICO-of-autonomy framing is appealing, but market is years early and data buyers are few; AI-insurance space is crowded.

title: Groundskeepers: Custodianship for AI-Built Software
one_liner: Property management for software: a monthly subscription where a named junior-developer 'groundskeeper' keeps small businesses' AI-built apps patched, backed up, monitored, and alive, with a senior signing off.
cluster_name: Recorded and AI-created data exposure for small firms

judges.fatal_flaw: Platforms and agents will bundle maintenance; human-in-loop economics thin at $149-499.
judges.note: Custody-versus-cleanup framing is smart and the long tail is large, but it is the popular 2026 vibe-code idea.

judges.fatal_flaw: SMBs feel no urgency until an incident, and labor-heavy custody is easily copied.
judges.note: Reachable buyers and workable margin per groundskeeper, but low defensibility and an obvious post-vibe-coding idea.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-ARPU SMB churn; Lovable, Replit and hosts will bundle maintenance themselves.
judges.note: Custody-versus-cleanup framing is neat, but it is an AI-services agency riding the vibe-coding wave with no moat.

title: Vet-Prescribed Walks for Post-Surgery and Senior Dogs
one_liner: Certify dog walkers to deliver vet-written controlled-walking protocols after cruciate and spinal surgery, and to send structured mobility reports back to the clinic.
cluster_name: Veterinary practices: capacity, workforce, diagnostics and drugs

judges.fatal_flaw: Local service with capped scale and thin marketplace-style margins.
judges.note: Desperate owners, vet referral trust wedge, quick local start, decent bundle economics. Small prize but profitable.

judges.fatal_flaw: Local low-scale service with injury liability and thin per-visit margins.
judges.note: Rehab-extender trust gap is real and vets can refer, but small prize and no defensibility beyond local relationships.

judges.fatal_flaw: Walker liability and vet distrust; local gig labor caps scale.
judges.note: Post-op protocol is a decent niche, but pet-walking services are crowded and low ceiling.

title: Independent Leakage Audits for Age Verification
one_liner: A red-team lab that measures how easily under-16s slip past each platform's age check (VPN, borrowed ID, face tricks) and sells defensible evidence to platforms, counsel and insurers.
cluster_name: Youth online safety and age-assurance compliance for small platforms

judges.fatal_flaw: Audit findings are discoverable evidence of non-compliance; platforms may avoid commissioning them.
judges.note: Assurance-market insight is good, but government trials exist, testing evasion is legally delicate, and sales are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Platforms won't buy discoverable evidence of failure; testing with borrowed IDs is legally fraught.
judges.note: Assurance-market framing is sound and timely, but existing certifiers and regulators' own testing compete; buyer incentive is awkward.

judges.fatal_flaw: Platforms avoid commissioning discoverable evidence of their own age-check failures.
judges.note: Assurance-market framing is smart, but buyers may not want discoverable leakage evidence; niche and legally delicate.

title: AI-Native Estate Settlement Firm Under Arizona ABS
one_liner: A licensed alternative business structure that runs uncontested probate and small-estate work end-to-end at a flat fee, with attorneys supervising agent-driven workflows.
cluster_name: Executors and small probate firms drowning in estate paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Referral acquisition, attorney-supervision ratios and ABS licensing delay could cap margins and speed.
judges.note: Large underserved probate market and a real regulatory moat. AI-native law is trendy but the ABS and funeral-home wedge is specific.

judges.fatal_flaw: ABS license, malpractice and unauthorized-practice risk delay first revenue.
judges.note: Legal, cheap flat-fee probate is real, but it is the obvious AI-law-firm pitch gated by regulation.

judges.fatal_flaw: ABS licensing, malpractice and Arizona-only scope constrain a scrappy team; AI-native law thesis is crowded.
judges.note: Probate is an underserved niche, but 'AI-native services firm' is now a familiar template.

title: Step-Down Club: Maintenance After the Max Dose
one_liner: A cheap maintenance membership that turns the majority of GLP-1 users who quit or plateau into a planned step-down and a monetizable restart.
cluster_name: GLP-1 patients' transitions: procedures, medication changes, quitting and aftercare

judges.fatal_flaw: Telehealths will bundle step-down in-house; $19/mo consumer churn cannot fund acquisition.
judges.note: Good ex-user insight, but low ARPU, prescriber licensing needs, and a crowded GLP-1 field.

judges.fatal_flaw: Dose step-down needs prescribing, so it becomes a telehealth with high CAC and low ARPU.
judges.note: GLP-1 aftercare is the obvious 2026 pitch in a crowded field; the ex-user insight is decent.

judges.fatal_flaw: Telehealths own ex-users and can build step-down in-house; needs prescriber partner.
judges.note: Discontinuation as modal outcome and restart-as-lead is a good angle, backed by SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN. Crowded space.

title: AI-Off Proficiency Checks for Clinicians
one_liner: E.M. Forster's The Machine Stops and Asimov's The Feeling of Power turned into recurrent, pilot-style checks that measure whether clinicians still perform well when the AI is switched off.
cluster_name: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Clinicians and carriers have no urgency; the deskilling evidence is contested.
judges.note: Unaided-proficiency currency à la aviation is contrarian, but no clear buyer and slow validation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rests on one contested study; specialty boards could own credentialing; slow hospital sales
judges.note: Non-obvious deskilling-currency angle sold as insurance evidence; aviation analogy is strong but demand unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: No one is required to buy; evidence base is one contested observational study.
judges.note: Buyers unclear, no mandate or budget, and clinicians resist being tested to satisfy insurers.

title: Work-Authorization Continuity Benefit for Care Employers
one_liner: An employer-paid benefit that screens every care worker for legal pathways, tracks EAD renewals and reverification, and plans backfill.
cluster_name: Immigrant households and workers: status deadlines and paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Most affected workers lack any legal pathway; screening risks false hope and employer liability
judges.note: Timely reframing as continuity problem, but legally fraught, politically risky, and incumbents own I-9 tracking.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employers fear liability from touching workers' status; thin-margin agencies buy slowly.
judges.note: Acute, large retention pain with clear payer, but sensitive legal ground and slow employer sales cycles.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employers avoid knowing worker status; discrimination and legal-liability risk; low per-worker price.
judges.note: Real workforce pain, but politically fraught, legally risky for employers, and hard to sell as an employer benefit.

title: Second-Life Studio: Shelved Human Drugs for Dogs
one_liner: Mine the wreckage of failed human biotechs for safe, clinical-stage molecules that make viable dog and cat drugs, and broker them to animal-health companies.
cluster_name: Biotech capital: diligence and salvage

judges.fatal_flaw: Multi-year licensing cycles; no plausible first revenue or cash within six months.
judges.note: Clever arbitrage, but brokerage deals are rare and lumpy, need pharma credibility and capital.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow to revenue; animal-health BD teams may not pay for screens; FDA veterinary path.
judges.note: Commercial-threshold-not-biology insight is real and zombie assets are cheap, but defensibility and near-term cash are weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Long deal cycles; animal-health BD teams rarely pay for screening reports up front.
judges.note: Human failure threshold is commercial, not biological; real precedents, but first cash in six months is doubtful.

title: Recovery Units: Hospital Step-Down in Lease-Up Apartments
one_liner: Master-lease vacant units in lease-up apartment buildings near hospitals and rent them by the night as staffed 7-30 day recovery apartments for patients who have no safe home to be discharged to.
cluster_name: Home and residential care: labor supply, family caregivers and small-scale models

judges.fatal_flaw: Licensure and liability for staffed unlicensed recovery apartments; hospitals won't discharge into them.
judges.note: Sharp cross-budget arbitrage between lease-up vacancies and $2,500 avoidable hospital days. Operationally heavy, but a first pilot is feasible.

judges.fatal_flaw: Master-lease capital and clinical liability before hospital contracts close.
judges.note: Interesting arbitrage but needs staffing, leases and slow hospital procurement; licensing and short-stay rules add risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: Staffed short-stay medical units face licensing, liability and slow hospital procurement.
judges.note: Clever link between lease-up concessions and hospital avoidable days, but operationally heavy and regulatory-exposed for a scrappy team.

title: Archival Footage Authenticity Clearance for Documentaries
one_liner: A per-film clearance service that proves each archival still and clip is real, so producers and E&O insurers can sign off.
cluster_name: Defensible authenticity evidence for disputed digital media

judges.fatal_flaw: Documentary market is small and per-film budgets are tiny.
judges.note: Nice wedge as a new column in the clearance line, but a small prize in a crowded authenticity-detection space.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small niche market; clearance houses or detector vendors could bundle the check.
judges.note: Sits in an existing clearance budget, a human-in-loop service is easy to start, and E&O insurers pull demand.

judges.fatal_flaw: Documentary market is tiny and detection is an arms race clearance houses can absorb.
judges.note: Budget-line insight is neat, but niche service with minimal scale and weak defensibility.

title: Whale-Proof Alert Network for Longline Boats
one_liner: A reciprocal, location-fuzzed alert network that lets sablefish and halibut longliners warn each other about orcas and sperm whales without giving up their fishing spots.
cluster_name: Fisheries and ecosystem-service operators

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market of a few hundred boats caps revenue below venture scale
judges.note: Mechanism-design insight is excellent and cheap to pilot, but the prize is very small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only several hundred boats; TAM is well under a few million dollars.
judges.note: Elegant mechanism design, but the addressable market is tiny and seasonal.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a few hundred boats, and skippers may still refuse to share sightings.
judges.note: Urgent, reachable pain via associations and clever mechanism design, but tiny TAM makes it a lifestyle business.

title: Parametric Cover Against Career-Field Collapse
one_liner: Index-based protection that pays out when hiring in a specific occupation falls past a threshold, sold first to bootcamps, income-share funds and private student lenders whose job-guarantee promises are now correlated bets on entry-level demand.
cluster_name: Cover and data for emerging or neglected risks

judges.fatal_flaw: Initial buyers (bootcamps, ISA funds) are tiny and distressed; insurance phase is years away.
judges.note: Non-consensus and intellectually neat, but customers cannot fund it and parametric cover is slow to build.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny, shrinking buyer pool (bootcamps, ISA funds); index basis risk deters carriers.
judges.note: Hedging occupational demand via index is fresh and AI-anchored, but the first customers are dying and phase 3 is far.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny distressed buyer pool; insurance phase needs capital, carriers and regulatory approval.
judges.note: Index subscriptions to bootcamps and ISA funds are a thin market; the real prize sits behind an MGA.

title: Conversion X-Ray: Scan and Warrant Hidden Risks
one_liner: A 10-day scan of vacant office buildings (LiDAR, ground-penetrating radar, riser mapping) with an AI cost-risk budget, evolving into a cost-overrun warranty backed by the data.
cluster_name: Repricing softening property markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Few conversions actually proceed; warranty needs capital and years of data.
judges.note: Predicted-vs-actual dataset is smart, but scanning is commodity and buyers are sparse and slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Engineering firms already do this diligence, and a missed slab cable creates liability.
judges.note: Real $15K services revenue from time-pressed buyers with small capex. The warranty upside is fantasy, but the scan pays alone.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few conversions proceed; warranty needs capital and years of data.
judges.note: Actuarial-dataset story is attractive but far off; scanning services alone are commodity and demand is sporadic.

title: Hardware-Origin Audits for Drones and Robots
one_liner: Teardown-level bill-of-materials and firmware audits that prove what is really inside a 'US-made' drone or robot, sold to small makers, to the public-safety and utility buyers who must prove compliance, and to insurers.
cluster_name: New defense and drone suppliers: compliance and financing hurdles

judges.fatal_flaw: Makers resist audits; Blue UAS and federal lists may preempt an unknown auditor.
judges.note: Belief in compliance as the scarce asset is a sound insight; cheap start, but credibility and buyer pull are unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven auditor trust; small makers cannot afford $8-30K audits
judges.note: Belief-in-compliance insight is good, but tiny buyer pool with weak budgets and credibility hurdles.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers willing to pay for audits; makers resist teardown and disclosure.
judges.note: Belief-in-compliance is the scarce asset, true, but boutique services market riding drone hype.

title: CAM and Insurance Pass-Through Audits for Micro-Tenants
one_liner: Read a small tenant's lease, recompute the landlord's annual reconciliation, and dispute overcharges inside the audit window, on contingency.
cluster_name: Small commercial tenants and renters facing landlord leverage

judges.fatal_flaw: Small per-tenant recoveries and lease-audit firms; contingency yield may not support CAC.
judges.note: Deadline-driven contingency for micro-tenants is real, but modest ticket size and generic LLM lease reading.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small recoveries per lease; landlord pushback and slow contingency cash cycles.
judges.note: Proven enterprise category, unserved micro-tenants, deadline-driven urgency; manual audits start immediately via associations.

judges.fatal_flaw: CAM audit firms already work on contingency; small-tenant recoveries are too small.
judges.note: Deadline-driven contingency is sensible, but it's an LLM-reads-lease wrapper in an existing audit niche.

title: Surety Bonds for Agent Operators
one_liner: A customs bond for bots: agent operators post a surety-backed bond so sites, APIs and merchants can say yes to their agents and get paid if the agents misbehave.
cluster_name: Accountability and guardrails for AI agents acting for others

judges.fatal_flaw: Sureties won't underwrite unquantified agent risk, and no buyer demand exists yet
judges.note: Agent-identity and agent-commerce pattern with hypothetical demand, an unpriced risk, and a distant claims history.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agent vendors won't pay until merchants demand bonds; classic chicken-and-egg.
judges.note: Original swing: bonds instead of identity. Big if agent commerce scales, but demand and partners are unproven within 6 months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-sided chicken-and-egg: sites won't whitelist until bonded agents exist, vendors won't pay first.
judges.note: Bond-not-identity insight is novel and anchored in agent-blocking litigation, but market is premature and needs a surety partner.

title: Refundable Deposits Against AI Submission Floods
one_liner: A gateway that makes AI-generated reports, applications and pitches post a small refundable stake, so maintainers only read submissions someone bet on.
cluster_name: Gatekeepers drowning in AI-generated submissions and bot responses

judges.fatal_flaw: Maintainers have no budget, and deposits deter honest reporters.
judges.note: Sound economic idea for spam, but buyers are broke volunteers and friction may kill valid reports.

judges.fatal_flaw: Deposit friction deters honest reporters; maintainers pay nothing and GitHub or platforms can build it.
judges.note: Real curl and HackerOne shift, but stake-as-spam-filter is the first idea anyone has; tiny budget.

judges.fatal_flaw: Honest reporters resist paying; tiny paying base among maintainers and bounty programs.
judges.note: Price as filter for agent spam is a genuine idea and possible protocol, but adoption friction and small early market.

title: Model-Swap Regression Service for Contractors
one_liner: Automated testing and porting that lets defense contractors re-platform their AI workflows to a different model vendor in weeks without losing quality.
cluster_name: AI builders' dependency risk: model retirement, cost blowouts and platform death

judges.fatal_flaw: One-off event-driven migrations; eval platforms and labs offer the same tooling.
judges.note: Fast revenue from a fresh legal event, but it is an evals and consulting play with a small buyer pool.

judges.fatal_flaw: Window is short and big consultancies will compete for the same migration work.
judges.note: Deadline-driven, budgeted compliance event with $15K fixed-price entry; a services-first wedge, but one-time and defense sales are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Transient one-time migration; classified traces block access and vendors ship their own migration tools.
judges.note: Fresh forced-migration event gives a defense wedge, but it is an eval/porting harness with limited durability.

title: Regrade: Stamped Reclaimed Framing Lumber
one_liner: A mobile lumber re-grading and code-acceptance service that turns torn-out framing lumber from chip-pile waste into stamped, sellable studs and joists for ADUs, garages and additions.
cluster_name: Small builders' crew coordination, permits and speed

judges.fatal_flaw: Grading-agency and building-department acceptance is uncertain, and unit economics are thin.
judges.note: Physical, paperwork-gated reuse; the insight is fine but margins and scale are low.

judges.fatal_flaw: De-nailing labor and code-acceptance friction may erase the 20-35% discount
judges.note: Tariff-driven lumber costs and paper-not-supply barrier is plausible. Operationally heavy, low-margin and slow to prove code acceptance.

judges.fatal_flaw: Grade-stamp acceptance by agencies and building departments is uncertain; low margins.
judges.note: Real material-cost pain and a scrappy service, but regulatory acceptance and truck capex.

title: Scam-Compound Geo-Intelligence for Compliance Teams
one_liner: A monthly geospatial register of scam compounds, built from satellite imagery and RF data, that lets exchanges and banks flag payees and merchants with a physical nexus to them.
cluster_name: Banks and platforms disrupting scam networks and recovering victims' funds

judges.fatal_flaw: Mule payees rarely sit near compounds; geographic nexus is weakly actionable for compliance teams.
judges.note: Novel data angle, but imagery and RF costs are high, and buyers may not act on it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak link between a compound's physical location and payee KYC or IP data.
judges.note: Novel geospatial angle with an enforcement why-now, but a thin buyer base and a shaky product-to-buyer link.

judges.fatal_flaw: Payee and KYC addresses rarely map to compounds, so the nexus signal is weak
judges.note: Physical place is a genuine on-chain blind spot, but expensive RF and imagery data and unclear compliance use case.

title: Cask Audit: Proof of Existence for Whisky Investors
one_liner: An independent inspection, gauging and valuation service that verifies investor-owned whisky casks exist, contain what was sold, and are worth what the seller says.
cluster_name: Lenders and investors unable to verify collateral exists

judges.fatal_flaw: Small niche market; brokers under scrutiny won't pay for audits
judges.note: Concrete verification wedge in glut; buyers motivated by loss, but limited market and warehouse cooperation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny niche market, in glut; UK-specific and low per-cask revenue.
judges.note: Real fraud need and cheap execution, but ceiling far too small for venture scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Warehouse cooperation is uncertain, and per-cask fees are small against travel costs.
judges.note: Fraud-driven demand and low-capex inspections. Insolvency practitioners and IFAs are reachable, but the market is narrow.

title: Federal-Equipment Disposition Desk for Closing Labs
one_liner: A compliance-plus-resale service that clears federal-interest, decontaminates and re-homes grant-funded instruments when labs shrink or close.
cluster_name: Biotech capital: diligence and salvage

judges.fatal_flaw: Small, lumpy, one-time transactions; a temporary supply spike and heavy per-asset manual work
judges.note: Real permission-and-liability gap, but a niche commission service with no compounding advantage.

judges.fatal_flaw: Existing lab-equipment liquidators handle most disposals; federal-interest cases are a thin slice
judges.note: Wind-downs are growing; commission on high-value instruments works; compliance passport is a real wedge to sell manually.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow university buyers and small volumes of assets that clear federal-interest rules.
judges.note: Permission, not price, is a good insight. Narrow, compliance-heavy niche with weak scale and incumbents in used-equipment resale.

title: Cap Ledger for the 350-Home Rule
one_liner: An ownership graph that counts which LLCs a single-family rental owner controls, proves grandfathering and build-to-rent exemption, and becomes the audit trail lenders and buyers demand.
cluster_name: Home closings, condo boards and HOAs tangled in title and records rules

judges.fatal_flaw: Rules undefined; operators already know their own counts; very few buyers.
judges.note: Speculative on unfinalized regulation; sophisticated buyers have data in-house, so urgency is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cap definitions unsettled and only a few hundred operators; pricing per home is tiny.
judges.note: Contrarian read: grandfathered portfolios become scarce assets; provable status is balance-sheet. Depends on legislation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a few hundred buyers and legislation definitions unsettled.
judges.note: Clever ownership-graph insight, but tiny customer set and regulatory speculation.

title: The Unrecorded Room
one_liner: Hourly, certified no-recording rooms (phone lockers, no AI notetakers, analog paper only) for conversations too candid to survive a transcript.
cluster_name: Recorded and AI-created data exposure for small firms

judges.fatal_flaw: Firms already have private conference rooms; the hourly premium is unjustified.
judges.note: Provable absence of a record is a clever inversion anchored in real privilege risk, but demand looks gimmicky.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hourly room business with tiny addressable market; lawyers may find phone lockers sufficient.
judges.note: Clever inversion where absence of a record is premium, but small venue economics cap it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Any phone-free conference room substitutes; buyers won't pay premium for an attestation.
judges.note: Cute status-marker idea, but venue capex, shielding cost and vague willingness to pay.

title: Driver's Ed for Smartphones, Sold to Parent Groups
one_liner: Ten-week, cohort-based 'phone license' programs where a whole grade's parents and kids pledge together, kids earn tiered device access through in-person challenges, and the finish is a coming-of-age ceremony.
cluster_name: Parents and adults managing phones, screens and AI toys

judges.fatal_flaw: Labor-intensive in-person delivery, seasonal demand, and hard to scale beyond school-by-school sales.
judges.note: Parents pay now, PTAs are reachable, unit economics work per cohort, and ten paying kids are easy; the prize is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Service delivered cohort by cohort with no software leverage or defensibility.
judges.note: Nice social insight that the phone decision is collective, but it is an in-person program business, not a scalable company.

judges.fatal_flaw: Human-delivered cohorts do not scale, and free Wait-Until-8th pledges compete.
judges.note: Cohort-as-moat insight is real but already mainstream in phone-free-childhood discourse; heavy delivery, PTA-by-PTA sales.

title: Ulysses Contracts for AI Use in Psychosis Recovery
one_liner: A patient-signed pre-commitment plus an app that adds friction and alerts a trusted contact when a recovering patient's chatbot use starts to spiral.
cluster_name: Emotional-AI companions: dependence, harm and continuity

judges.fatal_flaw: iOS blocks device-level monitoring; tiny clinical buyer base with slow program budgets.
judges.note: Thoughtful pre-commitment insight, but a small addressable market and an unbuildable device layer on iPhone.

judges.fatal_flaw: iOS blocks cross-app monitoring, and early-psychosis programs buy slowly.
judges.note: Ulysses pre-commitment for chatbot-linked psychosis is the most original insight here. Real shift, but the market is small and clinical sales are slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: On-device chatbot-use monitoring is technically shaky; clinical sales cycles are long.
judges.note: Interesting pre-commitment insight, but a niche patient population, clinician buyers and privacy risk.

title: Copyright-Registration Autopilot for AI Settlements
one_liner: Monthly bulk US copyright registration and an evidence vault for creators, so they are eligible when AI settlements and claims open.
cluster_name: Creators proving authorship and stopping unauthorized AI use of their work

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-ARPU creator customers, high CAC; future AI settlements may not repeat.
judges.note: Easy to get ten payers at $99, but recurring value hinges on speculative claims; weak retention.

judges.fatal_flaw: Registration only helps future claims; creators won't pay monthly for a speculative option.
judges.note: Registration as cheap option on class actions is clever, but low ARPU and hype-driven demand.

judges.fatal_flaw: Settlement-driven demand is speculative, and creators pay little for cheap registrations.
judges.note: Timely hook but low ARPU and one-off events; registration windows for past settlements have already closed.

title: Kennel Canary: Outbreak Surveillance for Dog Daycares
one_liner: Monthly environmental PCR swabs that give dog daycares, boarders and shelters an early-warning system and proof of due diligence.
cluster_name: Veterinary practices: capacity, workforce, diagnostics and drugs

judges.fatal_flaw: Positive results create discoverable liability, so facilities avoid testing
judges.note: Surveillance sold as due-diligence log is novel, but incentives are perverse and the willingness to pay monthly is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Daycares have low willingness to pay, and positive swabs risk panic and false alarms.
judges.note: Liability-log framing is sharp and the wedge is unusual, but the market is small and lab logistics are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Air-swab PCR is not validated for outbreak prediction; false positives create panic and cost.
judges.note: Liability-protection framing is smart, but recurring willingness to pay is weak and margin thin.

title: Auracast Hearing Access for Churches and Senior Centers
one_liner: Turnkey Bluetooth Auracast broadcast installs that let people with hearing loss hear services, meetings and group activities directly in their own hearing aids and earbuds.
cluster_name: Language, hearing and communication barriers in services and workplaces

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-ACV installs; Listen, Sennheiser and AV integrators are shipping Auracast; hardware commoditizes.
judges.note: Good timing on Auracast, but churches and senior centers are a thin niche selling installs and not software.

title: Satellite Cannibalization Scores for Rural ISP Lenders

cluster_name: New-space economy: operator gaps and LEO service users' risks

title: Water Due Diligence for Senior Housing Deals

title: Documentation-Review Copilot for Notified Bodies and Labs
one_liner: Software that triages and pre-checks manufacturers' technical files for the third-party assessors that CRA, Machinery, radio-cyber and AI Act rules are about to swamp.
cluster_name: EU digital product laws for small connected-device makers

title: Rolling Bio-Uplift Trials for Frontier Labs
one_liner: A standing cohort of novices and benign-proxy wet-lab tasks that measures whether each new AI model actually helps people do biology, within weeks of release.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Very few buyers; wet-lab cohort trials are slow, costly and hard to repeat quickly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs BSL-1 lab, IRB and novice cohort; few buyers and incumbent nonprofit.
judges.note: Highly original and timely, but tiny concentrated customer base and heavy setup for a scrappy team.

title: Age-Signal Rules Engine for App Developers

title: Remote Athletic Trainer Coverage for Rural Schools
one_liner: A subscription sideline triage line, protocol library and documentation service that stretches one licensed athletic trainer across many schools.
cluster_name: Out-of-school time, phone-free play and youth sports safety

judges.fatal_flaw: Remote triage carries liability and may conflict with state athletic-trainer practice acts.

judges.fatal_flaw: Schools lack AT budget; remote triage may not satisfy state AT coverage rules.
judges.note: Risk-pool subsidy angle is clever, but school budgets are why ATs are absent and season is half over.

title: Supplier-Owned Origin Passport for Tier-2 Shops
one_liner: A portable, supplier-owned origin and metal-content passport that answers every customer's questionnaire once.

judges.note: Supplier-owned credential flips the network effect and tariff timing helps, but it is a two-sided cold start against Altana-style players.

title: Men's Repair Crews Funded by Aging-in-Place Budgets

judges.fatal_flaw: Volunteer liability and unproven Medicare Advantage payment for repair jobs.
judges.note: Clever men's-loneliness and repair-labor mashup, but operationally heavy, hard to scale, and payer is uncertain.

title: Mod-Neutral Escrow for Reddit Swap Subs
one_liner: A roughly 2% escrow-and-reputation rail for r/hardwareswap-style trade communities that auto-writes verified trade counts, so buyers stop gambling on PayPal Goods & Services and mods stop refereeing scams.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin margin after escrow partner cut; cold-start liquidity and fraud losses.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny GMV and dependence on Reddit mods; escrow incumbents can copy.

one_liner: At layoff time, employers offer departing remote workers the option to keep their own laptop, remotely wiped and reimaged with a certificate of erasure. The service recovers, refurbishes and resells the devices people don't keep.

title: Year-Three Warranty Claims Agent and Failure Index
one_liner: An agent that files manufacturer, retailer and credit-card extended-warranty claims when your stuff dies, paid on success, whose claims data becomes a durability index that Amazon's star ratings cannot provide.

title: Fitness-Adjusted Longevity Reports for Retirement Advisors
one_liner: A report that turns a client's own wearable and clinic metrics (VO2max, resting heart rate, grip strength, gait speed, sleep) into a life-expectancy range for Social Security claiming, annuity timing and withdrawal-rate decisions, sold to fee-only advisors.
cluster_name: Preventive and longevity care outside conventional insurance

judges.fatal_flaw: Advisor compliance teams won't rely on unregulated mortality estimates; weak willingness to pay.
judges.note: Unusual buyer and cheap to build, but pain isn't urgent or budgeted; advisors may try free only.

judges.fatal_flaw: Advisors won't pay for a crude fitness-based mortality estimate; liability and thin defensibility.
judges.note: Longevity-plus-wearables pitch with a feature-sized product for a skeptical fee-only advisor buyer.

judges.fatal_flaw: Advisors fear liability and the estimate rarely changes the claiming decision.
judges.note: Unusual advisor buyer, but crude hazard-ratio adjustments and existing longevity calculators limit differentiation and pricing.

title: AI Kill-Switch Drills That Unlock Affirmative Cover
one_liner: A third-party 'shutdown drill' and evidence certificate proving a company can halt its AI systems fast, so carriers will write affirmative AI cover and insureds can qualify for it.
cluster_name: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Carriers may accept self-attestation and give no premium credit, so no one pays.
judges.note: Riding a week-old Beazley launch; the cyber-scan playbook for AI cover could be large, but the drill is thin.

judges.fatal_flaw: No insurer requires drills yet; existing AI-assurance attestation players already occupy the slot.
judges.note: Timely Beazley hook, but AI controls attestation is crowded and demand is hypothetical.

judges.fatal_flaw: No carrier requires drills yet; buyers won't pay before premium discounts exist.
judges.note: Timely Beazley hook but speculative demand, generic AI-compliance service, easily copied by consultancies.

title: Audit Desk for Indie Labels' AI-Remix Royalties
one_liner: Independent monitoring, consent management and statement auditing for the royalties that AI covers and remixes will start generating.
cluster_name: Creators proving authorship and stopping unauthorized AI use of their work

judges.fatal_flaw: AI-remix royalty stream is tiny for years and has no attribution data
judges.note: Royalty audit is a proven profession and indies lack leverage. The revenue base does not exist yet.

judges.fatal_flaw: AI-derivative royalty streams are tiny and undefined today; labels get platform data via Merlin.
judges.note: Royalty auditing for AI remixes is a sensible analogy, but the revenue to audit barely exists yet.

judges.fatal_flaw: AI-derivative royalty streams are near zero today, so there is nothing yet to audit or recover.
judges.note: Royalty auditing is a proven trade, but there is no current budgeted pain and Merlin will negotiate centrally.

title: Muthoot-Style Gold Loans for America's Junk Drawers
one_liner: A mail-in, XRF-assayed loan against gold and jewelry at roughly 24-36% APR, versus 200%-plus at a typical US pawn shop, run through licensed pawn partners for people who need $300-$5,000 and have idle gold worth far more with gold trading around $4,100-$4,500 an ounce.
cluster_name: Households in debt distress

judges.fatal_flaw: Loans of $300-5,000 at 2% monthly cannot cover ad CAC, XRF, insured shipping and state licensing.
judges.note: Timely with gold prices and collateral cuts losses, but the unit economics and per-state pawn rate caps break it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small-loan unit economics fail after assay, insured shipping both ways and state licensing.
judges.note: Interesting arbitrage story with gold at highs, but the storefront-cost thesis ignores logistics and fraud costs.

judges.fatal_flaw: State pawn licensing, mail-in fraud and heavy capital; prior mail-in asset lenders failed.
judges.note: Gold at highs is a real shift, but the pawn-APR-is-only-rent thesis is shaky and capital-heavy.

title: Birth Plan B for Maternity Deserts
one_liner: Carve the last three weeks of childbirth logistics out of the hospital: pre-booked lodging, ride dispatch, nurse triage and an emergency-delivery kit for mothers whose local labor ward closed.
cluster_name: Rural and underserved patients who cannot reach care

judges.fatal_flaw: Payers won't contract before Oct 30 deadline; ops and liability are heavy
judges.note: Logistics wrapper around closed labor wards is smart with real payer; timing and operational complexity hurt.

judges.fatal_flaw: Medicaid plans contract slowly; liability for roadside births; consumers can't afford $349-699.
judges.note: Real need with payer logic, but October obligation deadline is unrealistic and consumer channel is weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Payer procurement is slow; target mothers cannot self-pay $349-699.
judges.note: Sympathetic problem with RHTP tailwind, but Medicaid-plan contracting outlasts the six-month window.

title: Hard-Stop Fuse and Warranty for AI Cloud Bills
one_liner: A free scanner finds unrestricted legacy Google/Firebase and Bedrock exposure, installs a real hard kill-switch, and later sells a capped bill-shock warranty only to accounts that have the fuse installed.
cluster_name: AI builders' dependency risk: model retirement, cost blowouts and platform death

judges.fatal_flaw: $29/month buyers pay only after being burned; warranty needs insurance licensing and capital.
judges.note: Acute but episodic pain, viral free scanner; low ARPU and clouds may ship hard caps themselves.

judges.fatal_flaw: Clouds may ship native hard caps; $29 monthly ARPU is tiny and insurance is regulated.
judges.note: Real bill-shock pain with a scanner-to-warranty ladder. Fast to build, but low ARPU and the platforms can erase the wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: Clouds will ship native hard caps; $29/month ARPU is too small.
judges.note: Real pain, but a feature clouds can close; warranty layer is speculative.

title: Immunogenicity Screens for De Novo Proteins
one_liner: A fast, low-cost HLA-diverse T-cell screen and de-immunize-and-retest loop built for AI-designed proteins that have no natural template to humanize.
cluster_name: Wet-lab reagents and screens for AI-designed therapeutics

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny customer pool, lab operations and established immunogenicity CROs
judges.note: Well-funded niche with real economics insight, but wet-lab capex and CRO competition slow a scrappy start.

judges.fatal_flaw: Wet-lab capital needs, CRO incumbents, and weak assay predictiveness limit early buyers.
judges.note: Donor-cost economics are a real insight in a genuine AI-protein shift, but capital-heavy with few buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Wet-lab CRO service with noisy T-cell assays, entrenched incumbents and few paying customers.
judges.note: Real gap for de novo proteins and a data flywheel, but capital-heavy lab work and slow first revenue.

title: Consolidation Shock Radar for Independent Clinics
one_liner: Every roll-up creates a wave of unhappy clients and departing staff near the acquired clinic; sell independents, would-be founders and lenders a radar that finds those neighborhoods first.
cluster_name: Private-equity roll-up aftermath

judges.fatal_flaw: Independent clinics won't pay monthly for alerts; few trigger events per radius
judges.note: Cheap to test and a clever signal, but weak urgency, tiny ARPU and unproven lead value.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low ARPU independents; unclear that acquisition signals convert into client wins.
judges.note: Roll-up displacement as a time-series signal is fresh, but the vet niche is small and ROI is uncertain.

judges.fatal_flaw: Neighbors already know about acquisitions; signal has soft ROI and a tiny buyer pool.
judges.note: Roll-up displacement as time-series is a fresh framing, but a thin market with weak willingness to pay.

title: Preflight Lab for Steam Frame Verified
one_liner: A shared hardware lab that runs your build on real Steam Frame, Steam Machine and Deck units, finds why it would fail Valve's compatibility review, and fixes it.
cluster_name: Independent game studios and creator businesses

judges.fatal_flaw: Platform-dependent tiny market; Valve can automate checks; hardware capex for a short window.
judges.note: Timely but a picks-and-shovels service for one platform's badge program; small and easily disintermediated.

judges.fatal_flaw: Valve may publish tooling; the opportunity window and revenue pool are small.
judges.note: Timely platform-launch services with easy first customers, but it is a shrinking window and a niche market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable spend; Valve could ship free tools or reshape review.
judges.note: Tiny capex, fresh platform window, repeatable fixes amortized across catalogs. A small but bootstrappable niche with fast first customers.

title: Cool-Hours Slot Exchange for Tour Operators
one_liner: Forecast-driven heat re-scheduling for tour operators, plus a marketplace that sells 7am and 8pm venue slots, turning the coolest hours of the day into a priced, allocated resource.
cluster_name: Overtouristed destinations, tour operators and independent hotels

judges.fatal_flaw: Seasonal, low-budget operators plus two-sided marketplace liquidity; venues may not extend hours.
judges.note: Heat turns overtourism into a time-allocation problem; original framing, but marketplace and seasonality make revenue slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-sided marketplace with seasonal demand and low-tech operators; no proof until 2027 season
judges.note: Interesting time-as-scarcity idea, but cold-start marketplace with European operators and seasonal buying cycle.

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-sided marketplace of tiny operators and venues; seasonal, weak willingness to pay.
judges.note: Cool hours as a scarce resource is a nice reframe, but three products and marketplace cold start.

title: Approved-Protocol Envelope Guard for AI-Directed Labs
one_liner: Middleware that turns an institution's biosafety approval into machine-readable limits and stops any agent-proposed experiment that falls outside them before a robot runs it, leaving an insurer-grade black-box record.
cluster_name: Autonomous and AI-directed labs: infrastructure, safety and access

judges.fatal_flaw: Few AI-directed labs exist today; near-term buyers are tiny and cloud labs may build it in-house.
judges.note: Contrarian and possibly right long term. Unusual buyer (biosafety officer) and insurer trace-data angle, but very early.

judges.fatal_flaw: Very few labs run agent-directed protocols today, so buyers are scarce.
judges.note: Biosafety officer as buyer and insurer-trace angle are original, but the market is premature.

judges.fatal_flaw: Almost no labs let agents change protocols, so no current buyer or budget.
judges.note: Agent-guardrails pitch for a tiny, hypothetical market; biosafety officers lack purchasing power.

title: Blinded Self-Trials for Your Supplement Stack
one_liner: Mail-order double-blind crossover kits that tell you which of your own supplements move your own labs and wearable data, and which you can stop paying for.
cluster_name: Preventive and longevity care outside conventional insurance

judges.fatal_flaw: Noisy wearable outcomes give mostly inconclusive results; supplement repacking and placebo matching hurt margins.
judges.note: Subtraction as a product is a fresh angle. Consumer CAC is high and statistical power is weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: N-of-1 supplement crossovers are noisy and inconclusive; repackaging raises regulatory issues
judges.note: Subtraction is a fresh insight and biohackers are reachable, but statistical power is weak and per-trial cost is high.

judges.fatal_flaw: Single-person crossover trials are underpowered, so most results come back inconclusive.
judges.note: Subtraction pitch is contrarian, but it sits in the crowded longevity and wearables lane and the statistics undercut it.

title: GPS Spoofing Alarm Using LEO Signals
one_liner: A passive receiver that listens to Starlink, OneWeb and Iridium-style signals and flags when GPS disagrees.
cluster_name: Aircraft and drone operators: maintenance, parts, permits and navigation

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven signal-of-opportunity R&D and hardware; no clear buyer for months.
judges.note: 'Disagree, don't navigate' is a good insight, but it is a research-grade hardware bet with slow marine and insurer sales.

judges.fatal_flaw: Proprietary LEO signals, slow maritime sales, and cheaper existing spoofing detectors.
judges.note: Integrity-not-navigation is a smart framing, but it is hardware-heavy and the 6-month customer path is weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Deep-tech hardware on undocumented LEO signals, with no paying customers within six months.
judges.note: Integrity alarm beats navigation is a sharp insight amid rising jamming. Feasibility, plus rivals like Xona and Iridium PNT, sink it for scrappy teams.

title: Screw-Pile Foundations That Skip the Concrete Crew
one_liner: Engineered helical-pile foundations with torque-logged QA and prefab floor cassettes, installed in a day, for spec homes, ADUs and factory-built homes where foundation crews are booked out for weeks.
cluster_name: Small builders' crew coordination, permits and speed

judges.fatal_flaw: Helical piles are known and not clearly cost-parity on expansive Texas clay soils.
judges.note: Designing out the scarce crew is real. Helical piles already exist as an installer trade, so novelty is torque logs plus cassettes.

judges.fatal_flaw: Helical piles usually cost more than slabs; codes and lender acceptance vary.
judges.note: Trade-bypass insight, but helical piles are old and the parity-cost claim is doubtful.

judges.fatal_flaw: Helical-pile contractors already exist; priced at parity and rig capital is heavy.
judges.note: Real crew-bottleneck pain, but the wedge is a known technique and needs equipment plus engineering approvals.

title: W-2 Employer-of-Record for AI-Training Experts
one_liner: A task-metered payroll, benefits and contract layer that lets data vendors and labs engage expert contractors as short-term employees without the misclassification and breach exposure of 1099 mass onboarding.
cluster_name: Rights-cleared human data and vetted expert workers for AI labs

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin EOR margins; Deel-type EORs and the vendors themselves can copy.
judges.note: Plumbing for challenger data vendors is sensible but narrow; lawsuit-driven why-now is fragile.

judges.fatal_flaw: 8-12% payroll margin is thin; Deel and Remote exist and marketplaces prefer 1099.
judges.note: Plumbing for challengers in a crowded expert-data market; customer concentration and low-margin EOR.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers profit from 1099 status; payroll float squeezes margin; Deel-type EORs commoditize.
judges.note: Concrete compliance pain, but payroll working capital and misclassification suit unfunded; buyers resist paying.

title: Gig Social-Security Compliance Engine for Mid-Size Platforms
one_liner: A four-week compliance package for India's long tail of aggregator platforms that cannot build labour-code tooling in-house.
cluster_name: Workforce compliance for remote, tipped and platform workers

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak or delayed Indian enforcement; tiny per-worker fees and long-tail buyers resist paying.
judges.note: Mid-size platform wedge is sensible, but regulatory pull is uncertain and revenue per customer is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Labour-code rules still unsettled; incumbents (payroll, compliance vendors) and platforms' in-house teams can cover it.
judges.note: Long-tail platforms with founder-liability budget is sensible; per-worker pricing decent; regulatory ambiguity limits durability.

judges.fatal_flaw: Contribution rules still in flux and enforcement weak, so urgency uncertain.
judges.note: Underserved mid-size platforms with founder exposure, but Indian SMB SaaS selling and unsettled rules slow closes.

title: Vacant-House Concierge for Parents Moving Into Care
one_liner: One monthly plan that insures, inspects, maintains and eventually sells the house left empty when a parent moves to memory care or dies.
cluster_name: Houses caught in death, divorce or care transitions

judges.fatal_flaw: Weekly inspections make gross margin thin and operations geography-bound
judges.note: Real pain and attorney channel, but ops-heavy plan with insurance dependency squeezes margins.

judges.fatal_flaw: Ops-heavy local field service with insurance dependency and low-frequency, hard-to-reach customers.
judges.note: Anchoring at the care move is smart timing, but it is a labor-intensive service with weak scalability.

judges.fatal_flaw: Local field logistics do not scale, and referral volume from attorneys is low-frequency.
judges.note: Anchoring on the care move rather than death is a mild insight, but it is essentially absentee property management with insurance.

title: AI-Washing Forensics for Investors and Buyers
one_liner: A five-day outside-in diligence product that tests whether an AI startup's product is real autonomy, its revenue is real, and its users are human.
cluster_name: Buyers unable to verify vendor, algorithm or AI-safety claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Micro-VCs won't pay $15-40k; founders won't open data rooms; tech-diligence firms exist.
judges.note: Outside-in testing of AI claims is sensible but reactive to Builder.ai, with a buyer-budget mismatch.

judges.fatal_flaw: VCs are cheap and fast; services-heavy work with few buyers.
judges.note: Timely (Builder.ai), outside-in testing is doable. Feels like a diligence consultancy with a small buyer pool.

judges.fatal_flaw: Outside-in tests cannot verify revenue; investors may refuse to pay for it
judges.note: Investors are urgent and have budget, but the product overlaps with existing diligence firms.

title: Solar Monitoring Data as Appliance Stethoscope
one_liner: Use the consumption data already sitting in installers' monitoring portals to spot dying air conditioners, resistance heat, hidden EVs and always-on pool pumps, then sell verified leads to HVAC and electrical contractors with a share back to the installer.
cluster_name: Households upgrading homes: electrification, roofs and solar loans

judges.fatal_flaw: Lead volume per installer is tiny; OEM API access and homeowner opt-in rates are low.
judges.note: HVAC pays for intent leads and hand-validation is cheap, but installer channel yields few leads.

judges.fatal_flaw: OEM API access and homeowner consent can be revoked; Bidgely and Sense already disaggregate load
judges.note: Clever data reuse, but lead-gen on a small installed base with weak defensibility and platform dependence.

judges.fatal_flaw: OEM API terms and consent limit commercial use; lead-gen conversion unproven.
judges.note: Consumption data as appliance stethoscope is clever, but load-disaggregation lead-gen exists and depends on OEM goodwill.

title: Vet Tech Apprenticeship Intermediary
one_liner: Registered-apprenticeship sponsorship as a service, letting clinics grow their own technicians through a paid pathway with wage support and retention contracts.
cluster_name: Veterinary practices: capacity, workforce, diagnostics and drugs

judges.fatal_flaw: State apprenticeship rules vary; thin margins and slow workforce-funding cycles.
judges.note: Sensible retention wedge, but a small intermediary business dependent on grants.

judges.fatal_flaw: State licensure rules and apprenticeship registration delay first paying clinics.
judges.note: Clinics feel acute tech shortage and turnover; recurring per-apprentice fees; sponsor registration is slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: State licensing rules and consolidators' in-house programs limit demand; grants are slow.
judges.note: Employer release-time framing is decent. Revenue depends on grants and registration lag, with modest prize.

title: Fill-Level Sensors for Remote Vault Toilets
one_liner: Satellite-capable fill-level and usage sensors for the vault toilets on public land and in campgrounds, so pump trucks go where and when they are actually needed.
cluster_name: Condition monitoring for asset owners and their service contractors

judges.fatal_flaw: Government and concessionaire procurement is slow, and savings per toilet are unproven.
judges.note: Feasible hardware pilot and reasonable payback, but seasonal, low-ARPU and already served by portable-toilet sensor vendors.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny niche with thin per-unit revenue and hardware survival issues in vaults.
judges.note: Concrete pain and fast pilots, but it is an IoT feature for a small customer set.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable market, slow agency procurement, sensors fouling in corrosive vaults.
judges.note: NB-NTN makes remote toilet monitoring feasible; unusual niche, but the prize is small and hardware is fiddly.

title: Shared Emergency Desk for Autonomous Fleets
one_liner: A neutral 24/7 first-responder interface (hotline, dispatch API, geofence directives) that small AV, robot-truck and delivery-robot operators rent instead of building.
cluster_name: Autonomous-vehicle fleets' ground infrastructure and stakeholders

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool; large operators build their own desks; liability exposure.
judges.note: Regulatory pull and neutral-interface logic are real, but the prize is small and BPO-like.

judges.fatal_flaw: Only a few dozen small AV operators; big fleets build their own desks.
judges.note: Regulatory pull is real (NHTSA letter), but this is a tiny buyer pool and a commodity BPO with liability.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers, 24/7 staffing and liability, and large operators build their own desks
judges.note: Regulatory push is real but the customer pool is tiny. Requires a costly always-on operation.

title: Frozen Models: Long-Term Support for AI Deployments
one_liner: A 'Red Hat for AI models': host specific model versions with a written 5-7 year availability guarantee, reproducibility pack and migration diff-testing, for companies that cannot let their AI change under them.
cluster_name: AI builders' dependency risk: model retirement, cost blowouts and platform death

judges.fatal_flaw: A startup cannot credibly guarantee 5-7 years; clouds already pin versions and host open weights
judges.note: Stability-as-product insight is real but vendor-viability paradox and hyperscaler pinning undercut it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Labs and clouds can extend deprecation windows and pin versions, commoditizing the offer.
judges.note: Model-stability-as-product is a sensible insight, but it's LLM infra with a 'Red Hat for X' analogy and frontier-quality gap.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers can self-host pinned open weights, and cloud vendors already offer version guarantees.
judges.note: Good regulated-buyer insight, but bank sales cycles are long and the value is mostly a contract wrapper.

title: Knowledge Trusts That Pay Heirs From AI Licensing
one_liner: A fiduciary licensing shop that records a retiring or terminally ill master practitioner's judgment, holds the rights in an estate-friendly trust, sells non-exclusive licenses to AI buyers, and pays royalties to the expert and later the heirs.
cluster_name: Rights-cleared human data and vetted expert workers for AI labs

judges.fatal_flaw: Labs are unlikely to pay meaningful royalties for individual experts' corpora; a complex two-sided legal structure.
judges.note: Novel estate-licensing twist on the expert-data marketplace pattern, but the demand and pricing are unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: AI labs unlikely to pay meaningful royalties for single-expert corpora
judges.note: Estate-as-licensor angle is original; the cash wedge is really knowledge-capture consulting, and licensing demand is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Licensing revenue from AI buyers is unproven; the trust structure is legally complex.
judges.note: Creative estate angle, but the real wedge is a consulting sprint and long, uncertain licensing payoff.

title: Contest-Proof Signing: Capacity Sessions for Wills
one_liner: A recorded, clinician-run capacity and intent session at will signing, so a later contest by disappointed heirs has strong evidence against it.
cluster_name: Making family estate plans fair and contest-proof

judges.fatal_flaw: Recorded sessions can be discoverable and backfire; clinicians reluctant to opine.
judges.note: Cheap to pilot with attorneys, but pain is latent and lawyers already use physician letters.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lawyers fear recordings can backfire as evidence of confusion; clinician liability.
judges.note: Creating capacity evidence at signing is logical, but the why-now is thin and the practice already exists.

judges.fatal_flaw: Attorneys fear recordings create discoverable evidence; clinician liability limits adoption.
judges.note: Evidence manufactured at signing is a neat idea, but small lawyer-gated services niche.

title: Human-Backed Login for Senior-Serving Software
one_liner: A drop-in login layer for apps whose users are 65+ that replaces passwords with a two-tap flow, a spoken one-time code by phone call (landline included), family delegates and a live concierge who can walk anyone in.
cluster_name: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Vendors can wire voice OTP themselves; tiny per-user revenue and thin market.
judges.note: Contrarian against passkeys, with human-backed login grounded in real complaints. Quick to test but a small prize and easy to copy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Vendors must integrate an SDK; $299 minimum plus concierge staffing yields thin economics.
judges.note: Real evidenced pain and human-plus-voice-code insight, but small vendors, integration friction, low ARPU.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market; vendors can wire Twilio voice OTP themselves; a feature not a company.
judges.note: Sharp user insight from the HN thread, but niche buyers and a $299/month minimum cap the prize.

title: GLP-1 Size-Curve Index for Apparel Planners
one_liner: A monthly 'size-shift index' that tells merchandise planners, airlines and furniture makers how GLP-1 adoption is moving their customers' bodies.
cluster_name: Businesses adapting to GLP-1 users' changed consumption

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs proprietary partner data; a research product, not a scalable company.
judges.note: Timely GLP-1 hook, but obvious, thin moat, easily replicated by Circana and similar.

judges.fatal_flaw: No proprietary leading data, and retailers' own sell-through already reveals size shifts.
judges.note: Interesting trend, but the data is weak and it is a pitch to skeptical planners.

judges.fatal_flaw: No ZIP-level GLP-1 data exists; the index rests on weak proxies.
judges.note: Timely leading-indicator angle, but GLP-1 downstream plays are widely discussed and the data moat is missing.

title: Deorphanization Factory for AI-Nominated Enzymes
one_liner: A pooled-substrate, NGS-readout assay line that assigns function to hundreds of AI-nominated unknown enzymes per week for hundreds of dollars each.
cluster_name: Wet-lab reagents and screens for AI-designed therapeutics

judges.fatal_flaw: Wet-lab capex and a tiny buyer pool with in-house or CRO alternatives.
judges.note: Real bottleneck, but capital-intensive lab build before revenue and few customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs wet-lab capex and few buyers; existing protein-testing services already compete.
judges.note: Timely tie to agent discovery, but 'characterization is the bottleneck' is consensus and hard for a scrappy team.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs wet-lab capital; Adaptyv, Ginkgo and others already sell characterization to few buyers.
judges.note: Timely picks-and-shovels for AI-discovered enzymes; standardized passport is interesting but buyers are few.

title: Tele-Drive Home for Retirement Golf Carts
one_liner: A designated-driver and remote-driving service for owner-owned golf carts in age-restricted communities, starting with humans and automating later.
cluster_name: Adult children managing aging parents from afar

judges.fatal_flaw: Liability for impaired drivers and carts; tiny niche
judges.note: Quirky, unusual customer; human ride-home service starts now; teleop phase is speculative and TAM is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Liability, HOA and insurer resistance; niche market; teleop phase unrealistic.
judges.note: Quirky and non-obvious with a human-run start, but capped market and heavy liability.

judges.fatal_flaw: $15 rides needing two drivers lose money; teleop phase faces hardware and legal walls.
judges.note: Vivid niche and immediate human service, but unit economics are weak and later phases are speculative.

title: Landed-Cost Lock for Crowdfunding Creators
one_liner: A per-campaign engine that decides what each pledge tier really costs to land in each country (HTS class, duties, freight, platform and pledge-manager fees) and configures the tariff surcharge and shipping table before a creator commits.
cluster_name: Crowdfunded hardware makers and indie product brands

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool of cash-strapped creators who need the tool once per campaign.
judges.note: Decision layer above Kickstarter's collection tool is real but obvious, and the niche caps the prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny niche of crowdfunding creators; tariff regime keeps shifting after the IEEPA ruling
judges.note: Feasible quick sales but a narrow consulting-plus-spreadsheet product; feature-scale prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small crowdfunding creator market, and platforms or pledge managers could bundle the feature.
judges.note: Highly feasible: public campaigns give a cold-email teardown wedge and $750 audits. Prize is small.

title: Second-Life Desal Membranes for Farms and Towns
one_liner: Buy retired reverse-osmosis elements from big desal plants, test and recondition them, and sell them with a performance guarantee to farms, greenhouses and small systems.
cluster_name: Water scarcity: irrigation allocation and new supply

judges.fatal_flaw: Variable used-membrane quality makes performance guarantees costly, and an informal used-element market exists.
judges.note: Tangible low-tech business with a clear buyer. Needs $50-100k inventory and test rig, and guarantee risk squeezes margins.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cheap new Chinese RO elements erode the price gap; used-element quality risk.
judges.note: Untouched aftermarket is a real angle, but small prize and performance guarantee liability.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small market; variable membrane performance and warranty liability
judges.note: Original aftermarket angle, but tiny prize and quality uncertainty limit it to a niche business.

title: Wildfire Evacuation Autopilot for Campsites and Hotels
one_liner: Satellite fire-spread alerts plus pre-contracted buses, routes and multilingual guest messaging turn every tourist lodging in fire country into an evacuation node.
cluster_name: Heat, fire and evacuation protection for vulnerable people

judges.fatal_flaw: Very low ACV from fragmented campsites, and government alert systems are free.
judges.note: Genuine duty-of-care gap, but small per-site revenue and slow, seasonal, fragmented sales.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low ACV of about EUR 390 and liability if an alert fails
judges.note: Genuine duty-of-care pain with a federation channel. Cross-border sales in several languages cap the upside.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low ticket (EUR 390/site), seasonal, fragmented regional buyers
judges.note: Real forced duty for campsites, but the insight is thin and alerts are easy to copy.

title: Playable-Until Guarantees for Online Games
one_liner: Sell publishers a pre-funded shutdown trust plus an escrowed server kit, so a dated playability guarantee becomes a selling point for $70-80 online games instead of a legal risk.
cluster_name: Customers stranded when a product's maker disappears

judges.fatal_flaw: No mandate exists, so publishers face cost without a forced reason to pay.
judges.note: Appealing to gamers, but publishers see liability, and EU declined a rule; buyer is unmotivated.

judges.fatal_flaw: Publishers won't fund shutdown trusts; the customer base is tiny.
judges.note: Clever liability-capping logic and topical, but publishers pay nothing today and the market is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Publishers see no revenue lift from a badge and won't fund trusts.
judges.note: Original: a bounded, dated, funded promise caps liability; Stop Killing Games gives an audience, but the prize is small.

title: Own-Your-Office Buyer Groups for Practices
one_liner: Assemble dentists, clinics, law and accounting firms into buyer clubs that buy discounted vacant office buildings and split them into owner-occupied condos financed with SBA loans.
cluster_name: Repricing softening property markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Multi-million acquisition capital and 12+ months before any sponsor fee.
judges.note: Sharp owner-user arbitrage insight, but capital, condo law and closing timelines break the six-month test.

judges.fatal_flaw: Assembling a dozen practices to close on a distressed building takes far longer than six months
judges.note: Owner-user willingness to pay exceeds investors' bids, but it is capital-heavy real estate syndication with condo and SBA friction.

judges.fatal_flaw: Bulk closings need capital and time; multi-party condo financing rarely closes in six months.
judges.note: Owner-user value can exceed the investor bid at distressed office bases. Fragmented demand aggregation is unaddressed, but capital-heavy.

title: Motor-Rewind Shops Become Drone-Motor Cells
one_liner: Qualify a network of existing U.S. electric-motor repair shops to wind and test compliant drone motors with non-Chinese magnets for Drone Dominance suppliers.
cluster_name: New defense and drone suppliers: compliance and financing hurdles

judges.fatal_flaw: Motor quality and consistency at 4-5x import cost; drone makers vertically integrate.
judges.note: Unusual hidden-capacity wedge in a hot sector, but distributed manufacturing quality and qualification are hard.

judges.fatal_flaw: Repair shops rewind large motors, not tiny needle-wound drone motors; magnet supply immature.
judges.note: Hidden-capacity insight is nice, but skill mismatch, qualification and defense procurement slow first revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Non-Chinese magnet supply, not winding skill, is the real bottleneck; drone stators differ.
judges.note: Hidden repair-shop capacity is a fresh angle on drone supply, but magnets bind and prize per tranche is small.

title: Disaster-Pause Rider for Small-Business Loans
one_liner: A parametric portfolio rider that lets CDFIs and credit unions automatically pause small-business and farm loan payments after a disaster, with the lender made whole by a pre-funded payout.
cluster_name: Fast parametric cash for weather and disaster shocks

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs a licensed carrier, reinsurer and slow-moving CDFI buyers before revenue.
judges.note: Clever contractual-pause distribution, but insurance capacity and regulatory setup gate the first dollar.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs insurance carrier paper and regulator acceptance; long community-lender sales cycles.
judges.note: Clever lender-liquidity framing with loan-embedded distribution, but parametric is crowded and six-month traction is unrealistic.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs MGA licensing and reinsurer capacity; community lenders buy slowly.
judges.note: Embedding the pause as a loan clause solves distribution. Lender liquidity insight is good, but licensing slows the first sale.

title: Condo Vote Toolkit for Tourist-Flat Bans
one_liner: A compliant e-vote, notice and evidence kit that lets condo communities decide the fate of tourist flats building by building, sold to the property administrators who run those votes.
cluster_name: Overtouristed destinations, tour operators and independent hotels

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny per-vote revenue; jurisdiction-specific legal templates limit scale.
judges.note: Real deadline pain but EUR149 tickets, fragmented paper-based buyers, easy to replicate.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small, jurisdiction-bound, one-time votes; the legal premise is admittedly unverified.
judges.note: Good administrator channel and clear pain per vote, but volume is capped and legal templates need local counsel.

judges.fatal_flaw: Spanish community-management software incumbents exist; language and local-counsel burden for a scrappy team.
judges.note: Overtourism fight moved to the building assembly; unusual customer (administradores), but the claim 'no vendor sells there' is doubtful.

title: SOX Evidence Packs for Agent-Run Controls
one_liner: Control libraries, walkthrough scripts and test evidence that let auditors accept AI agents inside financial close, AP and reconciliations.
cluster_name: Proving AI controls and human review to insurers, auditors and clients

judges.fatal_flaw: Auditors, not vendors, define acceptable evidence; Big-4 will build their own
judges.note: Standards-vacuum hook is plausible but it is AI-compliance picks-and-shovels of the crowded consensus type.

judges.fatal_flaw: Big-4 firms and the PCAOB will set the format, not a startup.
judges.note: Real standards vacuum and quick consulting revenue, but it is compliance-in-a-box for agents and a narrow niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few finance teams have agents in ICFO scope yet; it reduces to consulting.
judges.note: Agent-compliance pitch is crowded, but $20-60k assessments could sell to nervous controllers.

title: Sundowning Night Companion Speaking in Family's Voice
one_liner: A bedside device that detects night waking and reorients a person with dementia in a voice they consented to, escalating to a caregiver or remote night aide.
cluster_name: Dementia and Alzheimer's care at home and in memory care

judges.fatal_flaw: Clinical and ethical validation plus hardware make sales slow; voice-clone backlash risk.
judges.note: The consented voice will is a real insight and night care is expensive, but it is a hardware and clinical slog.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hardware plus clinical validation; ethically contested voice cloning
judges.note: Real night-shift pain, but device, dementia ethics and consumer channel make early sales slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven clinically; cloned voice may distress patients; liability
judges.note: 'Voice will' reframes consent cleverly, but efficacy is unvalidated and senior-companion tech is crowded and regulatory-fraught.

title: After-School Shop Clubs Run by Retired Tradespeople
one_liner: Screen-free after-school care for ages 10-15 inside idle trade-school and union shops, staffed by retired journeymen who teach kids to build real things.
cluster_name: Out-of-school time, phone-free play and youth sports safety

judges.fatal_flaw: Child-safety liability, licensing and insurance around power tools could block launch.
judges.note: Three idle assets funding each other is neat and locally sellable, but liability-heavy and hard to scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Child licensing, insurance and mentor liability make each shop a heavy local operation.
judges.note: Three idle assets pay each other, but low-margin child care that does not scale.

judges.fatal_flaw: Child-care licensing and liability; scaling shop-by-shop is slow and local.
judges.note: Clever three-way subsidy and a viable 12-kid pilot, but a local service business with limited prize.

title: Customs Broker-as-Software for LatAm Micro-Importers
one_liner: Tariff walls turn Temu-era resellers into importers, so sell them classification, duty prepayment and pre-filed declarations.
cluster_name: Tariff cost, classification and customs for small importers

judges.fatal_flaw: Mexican customs filing requires a licensed agente aduanal; rules and tariffs are volatile.
judges.note: Concrete buyer, urgent new tariff wall, strong per-parcel economics; needs a licensed broker partner and duty-float capital.

judges.fatal_flaw: Customs brokerage is licensed per country, and parcel margins are thin.
judges.note: Me-too customs classification software with a thin insight; incumbents and local brokers hold the licenses.

judges.fatal_flaw: Licensed-broker requirements and volatile LatAm duty rules can block a software-only offering.
judges.note: Compliance-tax insight is sound and consolidators are reachable, but regulatory dependence and Zonos-type competitors.

title: Worker-Ownership Succession for Home Care Agencies
one_liner: A specialist shop that helps retiring home-care agency owners sell to their caregivers via an ESOP or worker co-op, plus a shared back office for the converted agencies.
cluster_name: Trade-shop succession and buyouts

judges.fatal_flaw: Deals are slow and thinly financed; owners want cash, not ESOP paper.
judges.note: Ownership as a retention tool is sensible but well-trodden by employee-ownership nonprofits. Long sales cycle.

judges.fatal_flaw: Long ESOP and co-op conversion cycles; specialist consultants already exist; change-of-ownership rules
judges.note: Sensible succession angle, but sales cycle is long and $12k assessments must be sold to wary owners.

judges.fatal_flaw: ESOP conversions take 9-12 months and small agencies cannot fund advisory fees.
judges.note: Sensible retention logic, but slow, consultative, low-frequency deals make it a boutique advisory rather than a scalable company.

title: Certified Refurb Phone Pipeline for Africa
one_liner: The memory crunch kills the cheap new phone, so the next wave of African users arrives on graded, warrantied used handsets.
cluster_name: Smallholders and rural households in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin per-handset margin, credit and customs risk; informal importers already dominate used phones.
judges.note: Memory crunch why-now is real and trust in used devices is the gap, but capital-heavy trading.

judges.fatal_flaw: About $10 per handset margin with credit risk and grey-market competition.
judges.note: Memory-price crunch is a real why-now and trust in used devices is plausible, but unit economics are thin and refurb is established.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin per-handset margin, working-capital and FX drag, and established refurbishers.
judges.note: Real market shift, but inventory-heavy, credit-extending distribution across borders is hard to bootstrap.

title: Broker Non-Payment Bond-Claim Collective for Small Carriers
one_liner: A service that files carriers' unpaid-load claims against the broker's surety bond and FMCSA record, pools every claimant against the same broker, and publishes a real days-to-pay broker score built from actual payment outcomes.
cluster_name: Freight brokers, carriers and shippers: fraud, liability and disputes

judges.fatal_flaw: Claims are tiny and bond pays pro rata; carrier users have little cash.
judges.note: Pooling claims for payment-behavior data is clever, but existing broker credit scores and low willingness to pay hurt.

judges.fatal_flaw: Claims are tiny and the bond pool is pro rata, so the contingency fee barely covers effort.
judges.note: Data on broker pay-speed is smart, but $600 claims at 20% will not fund manual claim filing; unauthorized-practice risk too.

judges.fatal_flaw: $600 loads with 20% contingency cannot fund attorney-reviewed claim filing.
judges.note: Payment-behavior data from claims is a good idea, but per-claim economics are tiny and broker credit scores exist.

title: Buy the Orphaned License of Dead Models
one_liner: Acquire or secure exclusive commercial-licensing rights to hugely downloaded open models and tools whose company died, then sell clean, warranted commercial licenses plus a public orphan-license registry.
cluster_name: Customers stranded when a product's maker disappears

judges.fatal_flaw: Rights chain is unverifiable and permissive TTS alternatives make buyers switch rather than pay.
judges.note: Clever scarcity framing but hinges on one dead startup's IP; demand is mostly hobbyists and swappable.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rights chain likely murky or unassignable, and permissive TTS models make it obsolete.
