judges.note: Clever arbitrage, but essentially a one-model opportunity with legal risk and a small prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: XTTS is aging and being replaced; users already free-ride, so few will pay for a license
judges.note: Clever dead-startup IP arbitrage with proven download demand, but the market is small and legally murky.

title: Aid-in-Dying Program-in-a-Box for Hospices
one_liner: Sell newly-legal states' hospices and health systems the policies, forms, trained consulting-clinician panel and logistics they need to participate in medical aid in dying.
cluster_name: Hospice, dying and the first weeks of bereavement

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable market with regulatory and referral-fee legal risk; controversial for hospices.
judges.note: Timely with Illinois and New York, real clinician bottleneck, but the ceiling is low and liability high.

judges.fatal_flaw: Willing clinician roster, licensing and referral-fee law; free advocacy-group support competes.
judges.note: Timely Illinois and New York laws, but hospice buyers are cautious and delivery depends on scarce willing physicians.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few non-religious hospices will buy; referral-fee and telehealth legal risk
judges.note: Real new-state bottleneck in clinical capacity, but modest buyer pool and sensitive sales.

title: Supplier-side questionnaire firewall citing the VSME cap
one_liner: A forward-to tool that answers big customers' ESG, NIS2 and EUDR questionnaires from one evidence vault and flags which questions the law says a small supplier can decline.
cluster_name: Exporters meeting foreign sustainability and representation rules

judges.fatal_flaw: Omnibus cap shrinks questionnaire demand; low ARPU through slow accountant channel.
judges.note: Right-to-refuse wedge via accountants is unusual, but ESG tailwind faded and revenue per client is tiny.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low SME ARPU, crowded questionnaire automation, and regulation is being scaled back.
judges.note: Accountant channel and right-to-decline angle are smart, but it is compliance-SaaS on shrinking ESG demand.

judges.fatal_flaw: SMEs will not pay monthly to decline questionnaires; ESG demand is shrinking
judges.note: Accountant channel and right-to-decline wedge are clever, but sits in fading ESG compliance with low urgency.

title: Silver Crews: Retiree Work Co-ops for US Towns
one_liner: A membership co-op for retirees 62+ that contracts with towns, school districts and HOAs for short, insured, daytime jobs (crossing guards, school and library aides, grounds work, event staffing) and acts as employer of record.
cluster_name: Loneliness and purpose: belonging programs for isolated adults and elders

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin markup after workers' comp and payroll; municipal procurement is slow.
judges.note: The Japanese Silver Center model is a real import, but SCSEP and staffing firms overlap. Low margin, slow public buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin staffing margins and workers'-comp costs rule out venture-scale returns.
judges.note: Real wrapper insight from Japan's model and easy first contracts, but staffing co-ops are low margin and low defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Staffing markup of 15-25% leaves thin margin; municipal procurement and classification rules slow sales.
judges.note: Scrappy via existing PEO and HOAs, but this is a low-margin staffing business.

title: Half-Pro Remodeling: Homeowner Does the Easy 60%
one_liner: Fixed-price booking of only the licensed, permit-required slice of a project while homeowners or handymen do demo, prep and finish, with photo-verified handoffs.
cluster_name: Households upgrading homes: electrification, roofs and solar loans

judges.fatal_flaw: Platform leakage on small tickets, and pros carry liability for DIY prep they didn't do.
judges.note: Angi-style marketplace variant; the licensed-hour framing is clever but a take-rate marketplace on $300-1,500 jobs rarely works.

judges.fatal_flaw: Licensed pros won't warrant or inspect homeowner prep; two-sided marketplace liquidity is hard
judges.note: Licensed-hour demand unit is a real insight, backed by blended-work data. Liability and cold-start marketplace risk remain.

judges.fatal_flaw: Pros won't reprice risk on DIY prep; two-sided liquidity and disintermediation.
judges.note: Uber-for-repairs marketplace with liability from homeowner prep; supply-side pros are hard to hold.

title: Dog Walk Plus: Wellness Checks for Isolated Seniors
one_liner: Turn the daily dog walk at an older client's home into a consented, structured wellness check with escalation, sold to their adult children.
cluster_name: Adult children managing aging parents from afar

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny local service with home-entry liability and no scalable moat.
judges.note: Trusted-entrant wedge is genuinely clever and the first 10 families come from existing clients. The ceiling is low.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small scale and unbounded liability if a check misses a medical emergency.
judges.note: Dog walker as the accepted visitor is a clever wedge, and first customers come fast. Local, low-priced service.

judges.fatal_flaw: Gig-walker liability and consent risk; tiny per-family revenue.
judges.note: Dog-as-Trojan-horse framing is clever, but a protocol on top of a low-margin local service.

title: Mini Cat Bonds for Co-ops and Counties
one_liner: Cat bond capital is at record highs but deals under $50M are uneconomic. Make a $5-25M cat bond a 90-day, low-cost, template product for the sponsors the market ignores.
cluster_name: Cover and data for emerging or neglected risks

judges.fatal_flaw: Structuring fees are thin versus legal cost; sponsors and regulators move slowly.
judges.note: Non-consensus, structural gap with abundant capital; too hard for a scrappy team to close deals in six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Securities structuring and investor placement take many months before first fee
judges.note: Real market gap but legal complexity, slow public sponsors and $150k cost target make a first deal unlikely in six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Structuring needs regulated credentials and capital; the first deal takes over six months.
judges.note: Cost per deal as the constraint is right but known to insiders. Long public-sector sales cycle.

title: Dog Walkers as Repeat-Pass Sidewalk Inspectors
one_liner: Pay dog walkers a few dollars a day to mount a phone on their chest and sell the resulting block-by-block sidewalk condition layer to cities, utilities, and delivery-robot operators.
cluster_name: Novel environmental and infrastructure data from satellites and crowd-sensing

judges.fatal_flaw: Two-sided cold start plus slow city procurement and privacy pushback.
judges.note: Memorable supply insight, but crowdsourced data quality, walker liquidity and municipal sales are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow municipal procurement, uneven dog-walker video quality and privacy backlash.
judges.note: Original supply insight: repeat passes enable change detection. ADA mandates create budget, but the city buyer is slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cities are weak, slow buyers; chest-mounted cameras on dog walkers are a privacy nonstarter.
judges.note: Repeat passes as scarce asset is a nice insight, but weak willingness to pay and awkward supply behavior.

title: Permit Concierge for Rare-Plant and Reptile Sellers
one_liner: A checkout-integrated paperwork and permit service that lets hobby breeders of orchids, aroids, cacti, tarantulas and reptiles legally fill foreign orders instead of pushing buyers to the gray market.
cluster_name: Exporters meeting foreign sustainability and representation rules

judges.fatal_flaw: Hobby-seller niche with per-shipment margins, low volumes and high permit-error liability.
judges.note: Real cliff for honest sellers and a provenance-book insight, but the prize is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny sellers may not absorb $150 per shipment; niche market is small.
judges.note: Genuine unserved compliance pain, zero competition, manual start; propagation-record moat, but small prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Permit service cost exceeds value of typical hobby shipment; tiny niche
judges.note: Provenance book is a clever idea, but unit economics do not work for $50-200 plant sales.

title: Deposit Gate That Kills Korean Bulk-Order Scams
one_liner: A KakaoTalk-native verify-and-deposit link that small Korean restaurants, bakeries and caterers send to any big or suspicious order, since scammers never pay a deposit and real customers do.
cluster_name: Small firms and property managers defending against fraud and impersonation

judges.fatal_flaw: Korea-only, low ARPU, and free police advice already says ask for a deposit.
judges.note: Sharp, precise scam insight and easy pilot, but small prize and needs a Korean-native team.

judges.fatal_flaw: One narrow Korean scam pattern; Kakao, Naver or police could absorb it.
judges.note: Sharp, well-evidenced wedge and easy pilots, but small TAM and closer to a feature than a company.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rare event and roughly $7/month ARPU; owners rarely pay for rare-event protection.
judges.note: Sharp precise rule and deposit filter, but small-shop ARPU is tiny and Kakao or POS vendors could copy it.

title: Standby Mass-Fatality Cooler Network for Counties
one_liner: A retainer-based network of vetted funeral homes with cooler space, vans and chain-of-custody training that counties and hospital coalitions can activate when the morgue overflows.
cluster_name: Hospice, dying and the first weeks of bereavement

judges.fatal_flaw: Government procurement is slow, and mass-fatality events are too rare to fund retainers.
judges.note: Paying idle funeral-home capacity to stay ready is unusual and plausible. Federal retreat gives a hook. Small, grant-dependent prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny, grant-dependent government market with slow procurement and rare activation events.
judges.note: Sensible underused-capacity insight, but a small, slow, non-venture-scale business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Counties buy preparedness only after a disaster; grant-funded, slow procurement.
judges.note: Clever idle-capacity insight, but no daily pain and government sales cycles stretch past 6 months.

title: Outage Pucks: Street-Level Blackout Cover
one_liner: A $25 plug-in sensor that proves your power is out and triggers a cash payout after 12 dark hours, turning neighborhoods of pucks into their own insurance oracle and a data feed utilities will pay for.
cluster_name: Fast parametric cash for weather and disaster shocks

judges.fatal_flaw: Puck can be unplugged for payouts; hardware plus insurance is two hard businesses.
judges.note: Crowd-verified outage oracle is inventive, yet moral hazard and weak consumer demand hurt.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurance licensing, reserves and adverse selection; rare outages make CAC exceed premiums.
judges.note: Clever crowd-verified oracle, but hardware plus insurance capital and consumer CAC are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Smart meters already reveal outages; insurance licensing and puck-unplugging fraud.
judges.note: Crowd-verified parametric cover is inventive, but hardware plus insurance plus consumer CAC makes it heavy.

title: Disordered-Eating Tripwire for GLP-1 Prescribers
one_liner: A cheap, documented eating-disorder screen and escalation network embedded in GLP-1 telehealth intake.
cluster_name: GLP-1 patients' transitions: procedures, medication changes, quitting and aftercare

judges.fatal_flaw: Feature-sized, low price per screen, buyers are the shakiest telehealth players.
judges.note: Liability-driven and timely, but a thin screening feature with weak willingness to pay.

judges.fatal_flaw: Screener is trivial to copy; telehealths won't pay without a mandate or lawsuit.
judges.note: Liability concentrates in white-label medical groups, a sharp read. Concentrated buyers and low per-patient price cap the prize.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers, tiny $3-6 per patient, and a simple questionnaire that is easy to copy.
judges.note: Timely liability logic, but small ticket, narrow buyer set, and no clear pain until suits arrive.

title: Rebuild-Cost Audit Sold Through Agents' E&O Fear
one_liner: A 15-minute independent rebuild-cost check at renewal that documents limits, sold to the agents and E&O carriers who hold the underinsurance tail.
cluster_name: Homeowners and communities losing property insurance in high-risk areas

judges.fatal_flaw: Verisk and Cotality own replacement-cost valuation; E&O carriers unlikely to pay.
judges.note: E&O-fear buyer is interesting but unproven, and incumbents dominate valuation data.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agents rarely pay per policy; Verisk and Cotality valuation tools already embedded
judges.note: Post-fire underinsurance is real, but E&O buyer is indirect and the premium-credit path is a long shot.

judges.fatal_flaw: Verisk and Cotality own valuation data; agents resist documenting underinsurance.
judges.note: E&O carrier as buyer is a good twist, but valuation tools are entrenched and the LA data are widely known.

title: AI-Guided Feline Heart Screening by Technicians
one_liner: Handheld ultrasound with AI probe guidance lets technicians capture heart clips on cats, with remote cardiologist over-read making HCM screening a routine add-on instead of a referral.
cluster_name: Veterinary practices: capacity, workforce, diagnostics and drugs

judges.fatal_flaw: Cardiologist read cost leaves thin margin; novice handheld echo quality and adoption uncertain.
judges.note: Clear clinic add-on with cheap trial, but low scan volume per clinic and thin unit economics.

judges.fatal_flaw: Blood-test screening (proBNP) and scarce technician scope limit demand; incumbents adding vet AI.
judges.note: AI acquisition guidance plus pooled over-reads is a good framing, but the pet-health niche is small and contested.

judges.fatal_flaw: Owners rarely pay for asymptomatic cat screening; probe and clinic sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: AI-guided acquisition is a sensible insight, but low willingness to pay and crowded vet imaging AI limit the prize.

title: Retiree Remote-Assist Bench for Robot Fleets
one_liner: A certified, US-based, part-time pool of retirees (ex-truckers, dispatchers, yard hands) who resolve robot and AV exceptions, billed by the assisted hour to fleet operators.
cluster_name: Teleoperated labor and remote pilot workforces

judges.fatal_flaw: AV fleets will not outsource safety-critical remote assist to part-time third-party retirees
judges.note: Timely offshore-assist controversy, cute retiree supply angle, but trust, latency and in-house preference undermine it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Fleets can use offshore agents far cheaper than $45-65 an hour.
judges.note: Creative supply framing for teleoperation, but the economics and latency and liability make it weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few concentrated buyers who insource remote ops and prefer cheapest offshore labor.
judges.note: Unusual supply-side insight, but only a handful of buyers with heavy safety and integration demands.

title: Exit Ramps for Dying AI Platforms
one_liner: A converter plus fixed-price migration service that turns Flowise flows, OpenAI Agent Builder graphs and Assistants API integrations into portable, regression-tested code.
cluster_name: AI builders' dependency risk: model retirement, cost blowouts and platform death

judges.fatal_flaw: One-time migration wave with small buyers; coding agents commoditize converters; deadline nearly passed.
judges.note: Real deadline but transient, tiny-ticket services work, not a lasting company.

judges.fatal_flaw: One-off deadline market; coding agents let agencies self-migrate cheaply.
judges.note: Fast cash from stranded agencies before Nov 30, but small, ephemeral prize with no defensibility after deadline.

judges.fatal_flaw: Assistants API already shut down, and free migration guides plus n8n undercut paid conversions.
judges.note: Real deadlines, but demand is a one-time, fading services spike. Parity-report differentiator is nice but the market is thin.

title: Robot Gymnasium Inside a Dead Mall
one_liner: Lease dying mall wings for pennies, stage them as real-world sets, and rent them by the day to robotics startups that need diverse places to collect training data.
cluster_name: Real-world skill and object data for robot and industrial-AI builders

judges.fatal_flaw: Data-collection methods shift to human video, homes and sim; almost no defensibility.
judges.note: Cheap real-estate arbitrage for robotics startups, but a commodity service riding a shifting data paradigm.

judges.fatal_flaw: Customers concentrated and may build their own collection sites; lease and set capital upfront.
judges.note: Cheap dead-mall leases are clever and deposits are testable, but the buyer pool is small and well-funded rivals emerge.

judges.fatal_flaw: Startups may collect data in-house or at home; paid demand for rented sets unproven.
judges.note: Dead-mall set arbitrage is inventive and cheap to pilot, but robot-data demand and ops complexity are uncertain.

title: Metering Unmetered Wells From Orbit
one_liner: Estimate monthly pumping for every unmetered irrigation well by fusing radar subsidence, satellite crop water use and electricity data, and sell it to groundwater regulators.
cluster_name: Water scarcity: irrigation allocation and new supply

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow, small government budgets; free OpenET and consultancies already compete.
judges.note: Sensible calibrated-estimate insight, but agency contracts are small and satellite-data-for-X is crowded.

judges.fatal_flaw: Government procurement plus technically hard InSAR accuracy; incumbent ET vendors already sell agencies.
judges.note: Real regulatory need and budgets exist, but R&D-heavy, slow public sales, and estimate defensibility is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: InSAR cannot attribute pumping per parcel; OpenET incumbents; slow government buyers.
judges.note: NISAR timing and calibrate-to-sample logic are sound, but science overreaches and regulators buy slowly.

title: Contrast Capture: Recovering Iodine From Post-Scan Urine
one_liner: Capture iodinated and gadolinium contrast agents from patients' urine at CT and MRI centers, funded by the drug makers who now owe EU wastewater EPR fees, and recover the iodine and gadolinium.
cluster_name: Recycling quality, distressed capacity and battery/EPR compliance

judges.fatal_flaw: Patient compliance and unproven regulator acceptance of capture as EPR credit; long pilot funding cycle.
judges.note: Highly original pharma-EPR payer angle, but tiny per-scan material value and a long path to revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: No paying EPR payer exists yet; needs hospital capture infrastructure and years.
judges.note: Clever payer insight, but patient-compliance logistics and pilot funding put revenue well beyond six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: EPR schemes are years from paying; patient urine-capture compliance is unproven.
judges.note: Non-obvious payer (pharma via EU wastewater EPR) and large avoided cost. Revenue within six months is unrealistic.

title: Renewal-Match Agent for Concession-Market Renters
one_liner: An agent that tracks true net-effective rents nearby, negotiates a renewal match with the landlord's leasing bot, and moves you if they refuse, paid only on savings.
cluster_name: Small commercial tenants and renters facing landlord leverage

judges.fatal_flaw: Savings per renter are tiny; consumer acquisition cost exceeds a 25% cut.
judges.note: Consumer bill-negotiation pattern; landlords already counter, and locator fees turn it into an existing business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Landlord revenue-management pricing, locator licensing, and consumer trust and acquisition cost.
judges.note: Loyalty-tax framing is fine, but consumer agent-negotiates-your-bill is a well-trodden pattern.

judges.fatal_flaw: Landlords rarely negotiate renewals by bot; consumer acquisition cost swamps the savings share.
judges.note: Locator-fee economics are real, but agent-negotiates-for-you is the obvious framing and consumer CAC hurts.

title: Quibi for Home-Care Aides: Serialized Compliance Training
one_liner: Quibi's 90-second premium episodes failed as a consumer subscription; as a serialized vertical drama that home-care aides watch to fulfill their mandatory annual training hours, the same format has a captive, budgeted buyer.
cluster_name: Home and residential care: labor supply, family caregivers and small-scale models

judges.fatal_flaw: Quibi analogy over-sells; training buyers want compliance content, not drama
judges.note: Same buyer as peer-made training but weaker credibility; drama engagement thesis unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: State-approved training-hour rules and incumbent CE libraries (Relias) may block price and acceptance.
judges.note: Original format-to-buyer flip; cheap to pilot, mandated budget, extendable to other frontline compliance training.

judges.fatal_flaw: Compliance buyers pick cheapest checkbox training, and established training vendors exist.
judges.note: Fun Quibi reframing, but drama does not unlock budgets. Agencies buy hours cheaply, and ARPU is tiny.

title: Business Identity Watch: LifeLock for LLCs
one_liner: Continuous monitoring of the state filings, liens and listings that define a small business, with a fast response kit when someone hijacks them.
cluster_name: Small firms and property managers defending against fraud and impersonation

judges.fatal_flaw: SMB owners rarely pay for monitoring; state filing data is fragmented and slow.
judges.note: Legitimate gap: entities are unwatched. But it is a low-ARPU SMB subscription reliant on bank distribution.

judges.fatal_flaw: SMB owners will not pay monthly for monitoring until they are victimized.
judges.note: LifeLock analogy with weak urgency, slow bank and CPA distribution, and low ARPU against high CAC.

judges.fatal_flaw: Owners won't pay monthly for monitoring; many states already offer free filing alerts.
judges.note: State filing as root of trust is a decent observation; a 'LifeLock for X' analog with weak willingness to pay.

title: Battery-Islanded Feeders Instead of Undergrounding
one_liner: Sell utilities islandable rural feeders powered by enrolled home batteries as a cheaper alternative to undergrounding and repeated wildfire power shutoffs.
cluster_name: Utilities avoiding costly network upgrades with distributed flexibility

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow utility procurement plus protection and safety engineering for customer-owned batteries islanding a feeder.
judges.note: Huge wildfire-capex budget, real cost gap versus undergrounding, non-obvious use of batteries already installed; hard but big.

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility sales cycles run 12-24 months and depend on utility capex
judges.note: Big prize but needs utility pilots, grid-forming hardware and regulatory approvals before any revenue; not a scrappy-team business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility protection and safety liability, plus customer-owned batteries, make islanding pilots very slow.
judges.note: Compares against $3M-per-mile undergrounding, which is sharp. Long utility sales cycle and heavy engineering, adjacent to the crowded home-VPP pattern.

title: Compliance-as-Code for EWA and BNPL
one_liner: State-by-state earned wage access and BNPL rules are being written fast. Turn them into an API that checks fees, tips and disclosures before each product release.
cluster_name: Consumer lenders' compliance and loss pressures

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers, and fintech law firms and incumbents can copy the tracker.
judges.note: Compliance-as-code for a narrow, fast-moving rule set is timely but small and easy for law firms to replicate.

judges.fatal_flaw: Very few EWA/BNPL customers; law firms and regtech incumbents can copy it.
judges.note: Timely enforcement hook, but a narrow customer base and a rules tracker that is easy to replicate.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer universe; law firms already deliver this as consulting.
judges.note: Live enforcement makes budget urgent and ACV is high, but only dozens of buyers exist. Free tracker helps lead generation.

title: Ticketmaster Exit Kits for Independent Venues
one_liner: A contract-audit and migration service that tells venue owners exactly when and at what cost they can leave exclusive ticketing deals, then moves them safely.
cluster_name: Small venues, performers and event vendors

judges.fatal_flaw: Small audit market; venues bound by contracts, and alternative ticketers already court them.
judges.note: News-driven hook with real fear-of-broken-on-sale insight, but low revenue per venue and easy for consultants.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small venue TAM; contract advances lock venues in; consulting revenue does not scale.
judges.note: Timely antitrust opening, but a services-and-consulting play with limited market and existing ticketing alternatives.

judges.fatal_flaw: Rival ticketing vendors will do contract review and migration free to win the venue.
judges.note: Timely antitrust verdict and real fear of a botched on-sale, but small buyer pool and paid audits get undercut.

title: Chargeback Guarantee for Agent-Placed Orders
one_liner: A merchant-side gateway that checks the shopper's signed mandate against the cart, keeps a tamper-proof decision record, and reimburses chargebacks on approved agent orders.
cluster_name: Payments, escrow, disputes and human fulfilment for agent transactions

judges.fatal_flaw: Signifyd, Riskified and Forter already guarantee chargebacks and will cover agent orders.
judges.note: Mandate-versus-cart is a smart signal, but merchants have little agent volume yet and loss reserve capital is heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agent order volume is tiny; card networks and Signifyd-type players may absorb the rulebook.
judges.note: Guarantee model is proven and the mandate-versus-cart signal is clever, but timing and capital are risks.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs reserve capital to guarantee chargebacks while agent order volume is still tiny.
judges.note: Agent-commerce plumbing is crowded and underwriting blind, with little data to price the guarantee.

title: Per-Class Portable Benefits for Fitness Instructors
one_liner: A payout layer that skims a small per-class contribution from studios and class apps into each 1099 instructor's own injury income protection, health-premium credit and retirement account, structured to give studios legal cover under portable-benefits laws.
cluster_name: Gig, tipped and cash workers unable to prove income

judges.fatal_flaw: Margin-thin studios won't add per-class contributions without a legal mandate.
judges.note: Class events are a natural unit for portable benefits. Needs insurer and legal work, and studio payers lack a compelling reason.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs insurer partner and portable-benefit legal structure; studios have little reason to pay.
judges.note: Class events are a neat contribution unit, but studios' incentive is weak and regulation heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Studios have no reason to pay per class; insurance and benefits regulation is complex.
judges.note: Clever per-class unit, but the buyer's willingness to pay is weak and the segment is small.

title: Independent Audits for Per-Outcome Agent Invoices
one_liner: The DoubleVerify of AI agents: sample and verify the resolutions, meetings and approvals you were billed for, then claim credits for the fakes.
cluster_name: AI builders' dependency risk: model retirement, cost blowouts and platform death

judges.fatal_flaw: Contracts may lack audit rights; recoverable credits are small; observability vendors can add it.
judges.note: DoubleVerify-for-agents analogy has merit as outcome pricing spreads. Early, and buyers must open data access.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small early buyer pool; vendors control outcome data and credit disputes are contract-bound.
judges.note: Interesting DoubleVerify analogy and contingency model, but outcome-priced buyers are few and access to their data is hard.

judges.fatal_flaw: Recoverable credits are smaller than the audit fee; vendors will expose their own outcome logs.
judges.note: Sophisticated 'DoubleVerify for agents' analogy pitch on agent-infra/evals; value proposition thin versus subscription price.

title: Real-Time Dental Benefits Texting Before December 31
one_liner: A dental-office tool that texts patients their actual remaining insurance dollars and a wallet card, filling the Q4 schedule that insurers' broken apps leave empty.
cluster_name: Provider revenue leaks and payer denials

judges.fatal_flaw: Dental 271 remaining-benefit data is unreliable; Weave, RevenueWell and PMS vendors already text benefit reminders.
judges.note: Fastest path to first cash with a deadline-driven Q4 pilot, but low ARPU and feature-not-company risk.

judges.fatal_flaw: Existing dental marketing tools already text benefit reminders; differentiation is thin.
judges.note: Fast to pilot but a me-too dental SaaS feature with no deep insight or moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Bolt-on feature in crowded dental engagement tools; seasonal demand.
judges.note: Fast to first customers via Open Dental, but a feature-sized wedge with weak defensibility.

title: Part-Time Seats: Districts Sell Classes to Homeschoolers
one_liner: Software and a playbook that lets shrinking districts enroll homeschoolers and microschoolers a la carte and capture per-pupil funding they are now losing.
cluster_name: Microschools, homeschoolers and shrinking districts

judges.fatal_flaw: Part-time FTE funding is small and district sales cycles are slow.
judges.note: Empty-seat insight is clever, but prize per district is small and state-statute dependent.

judges.fatal_flaw: Public district procurement cycles and restrictive state statutes prevent quick paying customers.
judges.note: Budget-stress pain is real, but district sales are slow and shared-time law varies by state.

judges.fatal_flaw: District procurement is slow, funding per part-time seat is small, and state law varies.
judges.note: Empty seats as an asset is a fair insight, but buyer is slow and the revenue case is thin.

title: Costly-Commitment Kits for Fitness Congregations
one_liner: A retention product for boutique gyms and run clubs that borrows religion's real community mechanism, costly commitment, to turn members into a congregation.
cluster_name: Independent gyms, studios and racquet venues

judges.fatal_flaw: Rituals are copyable, effect on retention unproven, low ACV.
judges.note: Quirky sociology insight but gimmick-level product; consultancy not a company.

judges.fatal_flaw: Unproven that rituals lift retention; owners may find it cultish and skip
judges.note: Original sociology insight and reachable owners, but weak evidence and soft, easily-cut spend.

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak proof of ROI; owners may find ritual kits gimmicky and pay little.
judges.note: Costly-signaling sociology is a real contrarian insight against friction removal. Product is odd and willingness to pay is doubtful.

title: Contingency Royalty Audits for Game Developers
one_liner: A $99 automated statement check that finds provable underpayments in publisher royalty reports, then hands winnable cases to forensic accountants on contingency.
cluster_name: Independent game studios and creator businesses

judges.fatal_flaw: Broke small-studio customers and slow contingency cash; tiny market
judges.note: Cheap free-tool lead gen and clear cost insight, but small prize and lumpy contingency revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small recoveries, developers fear publisher retaliation, and audit rights are hard to exercise.
judges.note: Cheap pre-audit is clever, but game developers are a tiny, poor market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small addressable market; recoveries are small and publishers can stall.
judges.note: Cheap pre-audit to unlock contingency is neat, but the niche is small and dispute-heavy.

title: Population-Diverse iPSC Villages for Drug Safety
one_liner: Pool 50-100 genetically diverse donor iPSC lines in one dish and read out each donor's drug response by genotype, giving pharma a 'clinical trial in a dish' for roughly the cost of one experiment.
cluster_name: Wet-lab reagents and screens for AI-designed therapeutics

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs wet lab, iPSC licensing and scRNA-seq capital before first sale
judges.note: Scientifically interesting but capital-heavy, slow pharma sales, and competitors exist.

judges.fatal_flaw: Wet-lab capital, long pharma sales cycles, and CROs can copy the assay.
judges.note: Real science with FDA tailwind; pooling collapses cost of diversity; moat is consented donor panel.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs wet-lab capital and long pharma validation cycles; incumbents (Evotec, Greenstone) already present
judges.note: Pooling collapses diversity cost is clever science, but infeasible for scrappy team to reach paying customers fast.

title: Task-Shifting Engine for Tech-Led Vet Visits
one_liner: Standing-order templates, scheduling and a state-by-state supervision rules database that let clinics move routine care from vets to technicians and, soon, VPAs, without breaking practice acts.
cluster_name: Veterinary practices: capacity, workforce, diagnostics and drugs

judges.fatal_flaw: PIMS vendors and corporate vet groups own workflow; rules database is a niche feature.
judges.note: Plausible scope-of-practice analogy, but small niche and easily absorbed by incumbents.

judges.fatal_flaw: Independent vet clinics have small software budgets; urgency is moderate and rules change slowly.
judges.note: Real workforce shortage and a rules-database moat, but a research-heavy product sold to low-budget clinics.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small rules-database market; corporate vet groups build protocols in-house.
judges.note: Scope-of-practice analogy is sound, and a free checker is a cheap wedge. The prize is niche and the VPA tier is early.

title: Visitor-Levy Back Office for Councils
one_liner: White-label registration, returns, audit and enforcement software plus a service desk that lets local councils run a new tourist levy without building it.
cluster_name: Overtouristed destinations, tour operators and independent hotels

judges.fatal_flaw: Council procurement cycles make ten customers in six months unrealistic; incumbent tax vendors.
judges.note: Statutory budget exists and timing is live, but government sales are slow; expect two or three pilots.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow council procurement and incumbent tax and lodging platforms; long time to first revenue.
judges.note: Real statutory demand and funded budget line, but slow-selling govtech with established suppliers and low originality.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small council TAM; Avalara and Granicus already sell lodging-tax compliance.
judges.note: Budget line exists before the system, but government sales are slow and the market is small.

title: Staffed Junk Playgrounds as Apartment Amenity
one_liner: Adventure playgrounds with loose parts, dirt, tools and trained playworkers, installed on unused lots at family-heavy apartment communities and sold to landlords as a renewal lever.
cluster_name: Out-of-school time, phone-free play and youth sports safety

judges.fatal_flaw: Landlord and insurer liability aversion; retention lift is hard to prove.
judges.note: Original, contrarian buyer (landlord). But fire pits and hammers on apartment lots collide with risk-averse insurers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Liability, staffing and site-by-site operations make scaling hard; retention ROI unproven.
judges.note: Non-obvious landlord-as-buyer angle, but a labor-heavy trend bet with weak defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Property insurers will resist fire pits and tools, and staffing eats the $3-5k monthly fee.
judges.note: Creative but thin or negative margins, uninsurable liability, and slow landlord procurement.

title: Recurring-Route Repricing Desk for Service Owners
one_liner: Read-only connect a lawn, pool, cleaning or pest route to its books, find the customers who are losing money, and hand the owner ready-to-send price-increase letters.
cluster_name: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: Jobber and Housecall Pro can add job costing; tiny $99-199/month ACV.
judges.note: Small-business, boring-trades pattern. Real pain, but low ACV and incumbents own the data.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny ARPU and churn; manual audits at $149 have thin margin.
judges.note: Price increases pay for themselves; first paid audits in weeks via Reddit and Jobber community; cash-positive fast.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-ARPU owners will not pay; Jobber can add per-customer margin reports natively.
judges.note: Feasible and evidenced pain, but it is small-business trades tooling with a thin wedge.

title: Toll Fermentation in Dead Alt-Protein Plants
one_liner: Buy or lease bankrupt alt-protein bioreactor capacity for pennies and run it as a toll fermenter for whey-alternative brands.
cluster_name: Protein and fermentation capacity squeeze

judges.fatal_flaw: Buying and operating bioreactor plants needs tens of millions and specialist operators.
judges.note: Genuinely contrarian distressed-asset thesis, but capital and ops needs are far beyond a scrappy team's six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-heavy; Series A/B brands can't credibly sign take-or-pay reservations to finance purchase.
judges.note: Distressed fermenter capacity meets whey supply panic. Sharp timing arbitrage, but asset-heavy and financing-gated.

judges.fatal_flaw: Requires millions to buy or lease plants; food-grade and process-transfer barriers.
judges.note: Timely capacity bargain but heavy capex, strain-specific processes, and no revenue before anchor contracts.

title: Supply-House-Branded Back Office for Tiny Shops
one_liner: White-label quote, invoice, parts-pricing and trade-credit software delivered to solo-to-5-tech shops through their local independent supply house counter.
cluster_name: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: Distributors are not software buyers and tiny shops won't adopt; ServiceTitan-type competitors.
judges.note: Counter-distribution wedge is smart, but it is trade-SaaS with weak adoption and a slow distributor sales cycle.

judges.fatal_flaw: Distributors may not pay or build well; a crowded trades-software space with incumbents.
judges.note: Distribution-through-supply-house is a real angle, but it is essentially vertical SaaS for trades with payments.

judges.fatal_flaw: Distributors buy slowly, tiny shops churn, and software is easily commoditized.
judges.note: Supply-house counter as distribution wedge is smart, but it is still vertical trade SaaS with payments.

title: Age-Tier Compliance for Roblox-Style Creator Studios
one_liner: Pre-flight scanner and consulting that checks user-generated game experiences against Roblox Kids (<9), Select (9-15) and 16+ tier rules before discovery demotion costs revenue.
cluster_name: Youth online safety and age-assurance compliance for small platforms

judges.fatal_flaw: Roblox can ship its own classifier; small studio market and shifting rules.
judges.note: Cheapest to start: personalized mini-audits to mis-tiered studios with revenue at stake; ten $1.5k sales is realistic.

judges.fatal_flaw: Roblox can ship its own tier checker; the studio niche is small.
judges.note: Timely platform-policy consultancy niche, but dependent on one platform and tiny in size.

judges.fatal_flaw: Roblox can ship native tier tooling; tiny and platform-dependent customer base.
judges.note: Timely, but a consultancy riding one platform's policy churn; ceiling is low.

title: Employer-Backed Block Leases for Hourly Workers
one_liner: A broker that packages 20-100 unit block leases in concession-heavy buildings, backed by an employer's credit guarantee and payroll deduction, to cut rent for hourly workers without raising wages.
cluster_name: Housing for workers priced out of tight markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Employers unwilling to guarantee tenant credit; two-sided sales and legal complexity
judges.note: Landlord buys occupancy certainty is a real angle; concession glut timely; execution heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employers won't extend credit guarantees; concession cycle is temporary; tiny commissions.
judges.note: Landlord-buys-certainty framing is clever, but the two-party sale is slow and the fee per deal is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Employers rarely give credit guarantees; three-party lease structuring is complex.
judges.note: Owner concession savings are real, but needs an employer balance sheet and coordination across three parties.

title: Closed-Loop Solvents for the Generic GLP-1 Wave
one_liner: Solvent-recovery-as-a-service for peptide CDMOs and new generic semaglutide makers, because the pill era and the April 2026 patent expiries multiply peptide API output and its solvent waste.
cluster_name: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Indian API makers already run in-house solvent recovery; GMP reuse limits and skid capex slow sales.
judges.note: Non-consensus, physical, timely: the GLP-1 wave is a solvent story. Audit-then-toll wedge is credible.

judges.fatal_flaw: GMP revalidation for recovered solvent plus heavy skid capex and India operations.
judges.note: Physical capex, pharma regulatory friction, and overseas plants make first paying customers slow and costly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capex-heavy, GMP reuse limits; existing solvent recyclers already serve pharma.
judges.note: Solvent mass as GLP-1's hidden footprint is fresh, but Indian plants already recover solvents and scrappy entry is hard.

title: Pharmacy Friendly Calls, Paid by Adherence Stars
one_liner: Independent pharmacies run weekly human-led friendship calls to isolated refill customers, funded by the Medicare adherence performance that loneliness quietly erodes.
cluster_name: Loneliness and purpose: belonging programs for isolated adults and elders

judges.fatal_flaw: Independent pharmacies cannot pay unless adherence payments actually reach them.
judges.note: Human-led against the AI-companion consensus is fresh, but the star-ratings payment chain is indirect and the adherence lift is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Independents cannot fund it and plans will not pay for unattributable adherence lift.
judges.note: Senior-loneliness pattern with a clever channel, but payer chain is unproven and callers are labor-intensive.

judges.fatal_flaw: $12-18 per patient per month exceeds refill margin gained; payers don't pay until proven.
judges.note: Clever channel and human-led angle, but pharmacy ROI doesn't pencil before plan contracts materialize.

title: TAKE IT DOWN Desk for Small Platforms
one_liner: Outsourced 48-hour notice-and-removal operations (intake, requester verification, adjudication, audit logs) for forums, hosts and indie social apps.
cluster_name: Youth online safety and age-assurance compliance for small platforms

judges.fatal_flaw: Small platforms won't pay; request volumes tiny and sensitive-imagery review carries liability.
judges.note: Real May 2026 enforcement hook and adjudication-not-filtering insight, but buyers are cheap and ops are gnarly.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small platforms have little budget; handling sensitive imagery creates liability and reviewer burnout.
judges.note: Real FTC clock but buyers usually just remove content on request. Staffed-desk margins and legal risk are heavy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyers with weak willingness to pay; moderator harm and liability exposure.
judges.note: Statute-hook compliance BPO; near-duplicate of the other takedown desk without the abuse-graph differentiation.

title: Chosen-Kin Circles for Solo Agers
one_liner: Mutual health-care-proxy circles of 3-4 unrelated solo agers with legal packets and a professional backstop, sold as estate planning but delivering belonging.
cluster_name: Solo agers without family to act as proxy, executor or guardian

judges.fatal_flaw: Ongoing legal liability and retention for a belonging product sold as legal paperwork.
judges.note: Attorney-referred wedge is smart, but the pain is not urgent and unrelated members' reciprocal duties are fragile.

judges.fatal_flaw: Matched strangers unlikely to accept proxy duty; liability when a crisis hits.
judges.note: Sells the legal wrapper and belonging arrives as by-product; a big demographic, but the matching is hard to make trustworthy.

judges.fatal_flaw: Matching strangers into legally binding proxy circles is hard to sell, staff and insure.
judges.note: Selling documents to deliver belonging is clever, but liability, low frequency and tiny per-customer economics.

title: Shopfloor Pulse: Voice-Agent Census of Job Shops
one_liner: Voice agents phone thousands of US machine shops monthly, publishing a real-time index of lead times, backlog and price pass-through.
cluster_name: Investors, lenders and venues wanting real-economy ground truth

judges.fatal_flaw: Alt-data buyers need history; low call response and TCPA risk undermine the index.
judges.note: Voice-survey census is a cute cost-collapse insight, but the buyers are picky and the data quality shaky.

judges.fatal_flaw: Alt-data buyers need long backtestable history before paying; TCPA risk.
judges.note: Novel data source, but a paid pilot within 6 months is a stretch.

judges.fatal_flaw: Shops may not answer or share lead times; TCPA exposure and sample bias undermine index credibility.
judges.note: Cheap census of unsurveyed firms is clever, but few alt-data buyers and data quality is doubtful.

title: Scrap-to-Tab: Supply-House Credit for Trade Scrap
one_liner: A weekly scrap-and-refrigerant buy-back inside independent HVAC, plumbing and electrical supply houses that pays contractors in credit against their supply-house tab.
cluster_name: Critical minerals and rare-earth supply chain recovery and provenance

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-margin scrap logistics with refrigerant handling rules and slow supply-house adoption.
judges.note: Supply counter as a checkpoint is smart, but it is a physical low-margin operation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin scrap spreads, refrigerant handling rules and supply-house counter logistics kill unit economics.
judges.note: Sharp insight that the supply counter is a checkpoint. Operationally heavy, with low value per contractor per week.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin scrap spreads; contractors already sell to yards; refrigerant licensing burden.
judges.note: Tab credit at supply counter is neat but small. Why-now claims about rare earths are a stretch.

title: Tech-to-Owner Buyout Kit for Trade Shops
one_liner: Package and finance the sale of sub-$5M trade shops to their own senior technicians or managers, then keep them on a shared back office so the acquired shop does not stall.
cluster_name: Trade-shop succession and buyouts

judges.fatal_flaw: Employee buyers lack capital; per-deal fee brokerage barely scales.
judges.note: Silver-tsunami trades thesis is widely held. Employee-buyout twist is sensible but a deal-factory business, not software.

judges.fatal_flaw: Deal cycles of 6-12 months mean the first success fees land after the horizon
judges.note: Real succession gap, but crowded with brokers and SBA lenders. Slow to first cash, and roll-up adjacent.

judges.fatal_flaw: Deal cycles exceed six months; tech buyers lack down payments and qualifications.
judges.note: Anti-roll-up employee buyout is sensible but well-trodden succession territory with slow success fees.

title: Closure-as-a-Service for Colleges and Grad Programs
one_liner: Orchestrating orderly teach-outs, transcript custody and student transfers for shutting colleges and graduate programs that the new loan caps and demographics are about to gut.
cluster_name: Colleges and training programs under new federal loan caps and earnings tests

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers are insolvent institutions; small lumpy market with long sales cycles.
judges.note: Trustee-style closure service is a clever reframe, but few hundred events, weak budgets, and slow regulators.

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers are cash-strapped institutions that will not prepare for closure until it is too late.
judges.note: Closure as recurring standardized service is a fair reframe, but the money and buying timing are wrong.

judges.fatal_flaw: At-risk colleges are in denial and cash-poor; sales cycles are long and closing clients can't pay.
judges.note: Recurring closure workload is real but buyers won't purchase readiness early. Existing consultancies overlap.

title: Junior Studio OS for Teen Game Developers
one_liner: Payroll, enforceable contracts, a custodial legal shell and payout splitting for teenage Roblox and Fortnite creator teams that already run large studios without knowing they are businesses.
cluster_name: Independent game studios and creator businesses

judges.fatal_flaw: Small, cash-poor market; minors' contract validity varies by state, creating legal liability.
judges.note: Fresh customer and a $299 done-for-you offer via Discord is testable now, but the prize is narrow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny TAM; minors' contracts stay voidable and Roblox could add splits natively.
judges.note: Legal-personhood insight is fun, but few teen studios can pay and revenue potential is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few teen studios earn enough, and minors' legal setup invites liability.
judges.note: Unusual customer and true legal-personhood insight, but very small market and unauthorized-practice risk.

title: Mitigation Grant Packets for Small Towns
one_liner: A packet factory and compliance tracker that gets small governments through FEMA and state mitigation grants without clawbacks.
cluster_name: City and county governments: thin staff, grants and vendor oversight

judges.fatal_flaw: BRIC window closed and funding unstable; crowded with small grant consultants
judges.note: Proven fixed-fee service, easy to sell by cold email, small towns underserved; program timing hurts urgency.

judges.fatal_flaw: Grant-writing consulting with unstable federal programs and low lifetime value per town.
judges.note: Real need, but it is a paperwork services shop with a generic insight and thin recurring revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Grant-consultant market exists and federal funding whipsaws; municipal buyers are slow.
judges.note: Generic government-paperwork services play with unstable program timing. Little non-obvious insight.

title: On-Demand Human Witnesses for Scrap and Recycled Claims
one_liner: A network of trained, insured, credentialed ex-auditors and QA people who can be dispatched within 24 hours to physically inspect scrap lots and witness recycled-content claims, producing tamper-evident signed reports.
cluster_name: Recycling quality, distressed capacity and battery/EPR compliance

judges.fatal_flaw: Buyers won't trust unknown gig inspectors over established inspection firms; liability.
judges.note: Human presence as scarce asset is a fashionable theme; thin-margin scrap trade and quality control are hard.

judges.note: Human-presence-in-the-AI-era theme is neat, but it is a thin-margin inspector marketplace with supply-side trust burdens.

judges.fatal_flaw: Gig inspectors create liability and trust problems; scrap buyers have thin margins.
judges.note: Speed-and-price wedge against incumbent inspectors, but two-sided supply, insurance and low willingness to pay.

title: Gig Income Shock Cover From Pooled Data
one_liner: Insure the algorithm: pay drivers when they are deactivated or when regional platform earnings collapse, using pooled earnings data to defeat moral hazard.
cluster_name: Gig, tipped and cash workers unable to prove income

judges.fatal_flaw: Adverse selection and gameable deactivations; drivers won't pay $10-20 monthly premiums.
judges.note: Interesting pooled-index insight, but insurance licensing, low ARPU and thin willingness to pay limit it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurance licensing, adverse selection and sparse pooled earnings data.

judges.fatal_flaw: Bespoke phage lab operations across countries cannot hit unit economics or fast first revenue.

title: Parametric Lease-Up Delay Insurance

judges.note: Large prize and neat parametric logic, but correlated risk and capital needs rule out scrappy first revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs reinsurer capacity; basis risk and adverse selection make first policy slow.
judges.note: Clever parametric hedge on lease-up carry, sizeable premium pool, but MGA build and correlated macro risk delay traction.

title: Celebration-of-Life Halls in Closed Churches

title: Tenant Childcare Consortium Powered by 45F Credits

judges.note: Clever 45F intermediary structure but requires real estate, licensed operation and tax certainty; slowest to revenue.

title: Router-and-Breaker Screen Control Sold by Trades
one_liner: HVAC, electrical and plumbing shops install tamper-proof, infrastructure-level screen and AI-companion controls as a maintenance-plan add-on for families with kids 8-15.

title: Compute-Heated Housing: GPUs as the Boiler Room
one_liner: Put a liquid-cooled AI rack in an apartment tower's mechanical room and use its waste heat as the building's hot-water plant, cutting utility costs while hosting power-starved compute.

judges.fatal_flaw: Building power, fire-code and resilience limits make small GPU racks uneconomic.
judges.note: Clever heat-load match, but distributed compute in apartment buildings has failed repeatedly. Slow, physical, and capital-hungry.

title: Independent Service Roll-Up for Lab Robots

judges.note: Uptime insight and wind-down parts supply are neat, but a services roll-up is not a seed-fundable software company.

judges.note: Time-series moat starting day one is real, but demand rests on EU enforcement actually biting.

judges.note: Time-series moat is real, but it is AI-compliance tooling with speculative demand.

title: CJIS 6.0 Identity Kit for Small Agencies
one_liner: A managed multifactor and identity-verification stack that works in patrol cars, radio dead zones and shared workstations, ready for the Oct 1, 2027 CJIS deadline.
cluster_name: Rural sheriffs, jails and small police agencies

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow government procurement and incumbent MFA vendors (Duo, Yubico) can meet the deadline.
judges.note: Fixed deadline and an MSP channel help, but it is small-ticket compliance with a long sales cycle.

judges.fatal_flaw: CJIS-compliant MFA incumbents exist; small-agency procurement slow and deadline 13 months away.
judges.note: Fixed deadline and MSP channel help, but not yet urgent and pilots are free.

judges.fatal_flaw: Slow government procurement; Duo, Microsoft and Yubico resellers already serve CJIS MFA.
judges.note: Fixed deadline and MSP channel are sensible. Offline mode is the only differentiator, and the idea is not surprising.

title: Immigration Deadline Sentinel for Work-Permit Households
one_liner: The wealthy keep immigration counsel on retainer to calendar, file early and bridge gaps; for $20/mo, give H-4, OPT, asylum-applicant and DACA households an encrypted deadline vault and family-readiness plan.
cluster_name: Immigrant households and workers: status deadlines and paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Low-ARPU consumers, unauthorized-practice risk, and sensitive-data trust barrier.
judges.note: Real deadline pain but consumer $20/mo and existing immigration apps; employer channel is unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low willingness to pay, trust and privacy barriers, unauthorized-practice risk; Boundless and others compete.
judges.note: Timely rule change and sensible employer channel, but consumer $20/mo among fearful households is a weak base.

judges.fatal_flaw: Trust and unauthorized-practice-of-law risk, with employer platforms already serving this segment.
judges.note: Real EAD rule change, but a $20 consumer app for a fearful population is hard to sell.

title: Cell-Type-Restricted Promoters for Safer AAV
one_liner: AI-designed, primary-cell-validated regulatory sequences that switch AAV or LNP transgenes on only in target tissues and off in the liver.
cluster_name: Wet-lab reagents and screens for AI-designed therapeutics

judges.fatal_flaw: Gene therapy funding slump and slow licensing; requires a scientific team with wet lab.
judges.note: Good insight that the cassette is the second lever toxicity depends on. Modular IP, but small, slow market.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs lab capital and PhD team; biotech sales cycles too long for six months.
judges.note: Real safety problem and modular IP, but $50k wet-lab spend and slow cash-strapped biotech buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs a wet lab and long validation; muscle-specific promoters already exist; no revenue in 6 months.
judges.note: Sarepta shift is real but the insight is not new, and a scrappy team cannot execute.

title: Identical Object Kits for Robot Data Farms
one_liner: Manufacture and ship standardized kits of hundreds of everyday-object variants, panels of handles, hinges and knobs, and task fixtures, so that every home and lab collecting robot training data uses the same physical objects.
cluster_name: Real-world skill and object data for robot and industrial-AI builders

judges.fatal_flaw: Few concentrated buyers who can standardize objects themselves; hardware fulfillment overhead
judges.note: Physical-layer standard is an unusual angle riding the robot-data boom; market small and demand unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few buyers; data vendors and labs will standardize their own objects.
judges.note: Standardized-physical-layer idea is interesting but sells hardware kits to a small, well-funded customer set.

judges.fatal_flaw: Robot learning wants object diversity, and the few buyers can build kits in-house.
judges.note: Standardized physical layer is original, but it contradicts the generalization-through-variety consensus. Benchmark ambition is unproven.

title: Mahjong Leagues for Senior Living Communities
one_liner: A turnkey mahjong program (kits, instructors, scoring app, inter-community leagues) sold to senior-living activity directors.
cluster_name: Loneliness and purpose: belonging programs for isolated adults and elders

judges.fatal_flaw: Seniors already play free; activity directors unlikely to pay $300-600 monthly.
judges.note: Reframes a Gen Z trend toward older buyers, but is easy to copy and has a low ceiling.

judges.fatal_flaw: Trend-driven fad with low ARPU; kits and instructors are a services grind.
judges.note: Riding a media wave into a low-budget activities line; little defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Not an urgent pain; fad-driven with low ACV and instructor cost drag.
judges.note: Cheap to pilot and activity-budget buyers exist, but small prize, trend-riding, weak defensibility.

title: Recycled-Content Claim Defense Files
one_liner: Litigation-grade, SKU-level substantiation files for recycled-content claims, built on purchase-to-claim reconciliation rather than more certificates.
cluster_name: Brands substantiating origin, recycled-content and green claims

judges.fatal_flaw: Weak legal mandate after veto; brands may not pay for bespoke consulting.
judges.note: Reconciliation insight is sound, but demand softened by the veto and the work is consulting.

judges.fatal_flaw: Brands may drop recycled claims rather than pay to defend them.
judges.note: Good 'reconciliation not certificates' insight, but it is consulting-shaped with a thin market after the veto.

judges.fatal_flaw: No active enforcement or mandate, so claim substantiation is a deferrable vitamin purchase.
judges.note: Reconciliation insight is sound, but legal buyers lack urgency after the veto; slow enterprise cycle.

title: Parametric Outage Cover for Satellite Internet Users
one_liner: A $60 probe network and parametric policy that pays cash when a satellite-dependent operation loses connectivity.
cluster_name: New-space economy: operator gaps and LEO service users' risks

judges.fatal_flaw: Requires insurer and reinsurer partners; probe alone will not sell
judges.note: Good measurement insight but needs regulated underwriting; buyers would not pay for probes alone.

judges.fatal_flaw: Outages are short and rare, so premiums are tiny relative to MGA and reinsurer setup cost.
judges.note: Independent measurement unlocks pricing; probe subscription gives a wedge, but the insurable loss is small.

judges.fatal_flaw: Outages are rare and short, so the premium pool is tiny; buyers can multi-link.
judges.note: Measurement-before-insurance logic is right, but the risk is small and the probe alone is a thin product.

title: Affordable Capital-Stack Solver for Conversion Developers
one_liner: A structuring engine and expert memo that tells first-time affordable developers which subsidy stack is fundable for a given office conversion, with a calendar of deadlines.
cluster_name: Repricing softening property markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Lumpy consultancy-like demand; subsidy rules vary by city, hard to automate
judges.note: Real knowledge gap for first-time affordable developers, but tiny buyer base and consultant substitute.

judges.fatal_flaw: Few office-conversion deals; a human-expert memo business, not software.
judges.note: Useful for first-time developers, but tiny deal flow and consultant-style delivery limit size and defensibility.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny, vague customer pool; consultants already serve it and deals close slowly.
judges.note: Real expertise arbitrage and high-stakes deals, but few buyers and one-off memos limit scale.

title: PFAS Test-Result Exchange for Small Brands
one_liner: A members' data pool where small brands share lab results indexed by supplier, material lot and SKU, so nobody pays $500+ to test the same fabric or coating twice.
cluster_name: PFAS exposure, testing and disposal

judges.fatal_flaw: Brands will not share failing test data; results are lot-specific and hard to reuse.
judges.note: Shared testing is sensible, but cold-start data pooling and discoverability fears block members.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cold-start data pool; brands reluctant to share adverse results; labs could copy.
judges.note: Credit-bureau-for-materials framing is sensible; small members, contribution incentives unclear, regulation fluid.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lot-to-lot variation weakens pooled data; co-op cold start; regulatory dates unverified.
judges.note: Shared testing pool is sensible, but cold-start data cooperative with weak transferability of results across lots.

title: Extranet Takeover Defense for Independent Hotels
one_liner: Managed monitoring and fraud response for hotels' OTA extranet logins and guest-messaging channels, the credential theft that turns into guest payment scams.
cluster_name: Small firms and property managers defending against fraud and impersonation

judges.fatal_flaw: Small hotels only buy security after being hit; OTA 2FA may shrink the threat.
judges.note: Acute, widely reported scam pain and a cheap monitoring stack. Association and channel-manager distribution is plausible but ARPU is low.

judges.fatal_flaw: Small hotels rarely buy security services; low price points make distribution uneconomic.
judges.note: Generic SMB phishing and credential monitoring dressed for hotels; the attack is real but the offering is me-too.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hotels won't pay EUR 49+ per month; OTAs could patch the vulnerability themselves.
judges.note: Real fraud pattern, but low ARPU, hard distribution and dependence on OTA platform behavior.

title: A Teaching Hospital Inside a Dead Hospital
one_liner: Lease a wing of a closed hospital and run it as a full-scale simulation hospital that nursing schools rent by the student-day.
cluster_name: Shrinking institutions with idle buildings

judges.fatal_flaw: Capex-heavy lease, state board approval, and students must travel to remote dead hospitals.
judges.note: Vivid reuse of dead hospitals, but real-estate risk and approvals make six-month revenue unlikely.

judges.fatal_flaw: Leasing a dead hospital wing is capital-heavy with slow school and state-board approvals.
judges.note: Real nursing seat shortage and clever building reuse. Lumpy, capex-heavy and dependent on state sign-off.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-heavy lease and equipment plus state-board approval before revenue; slow school sales.
judges.note: Vivid idea, but building, faculty, mannequins and grant-dependent buyers make it a capital project.

title: Heatwave Demand Signals for Cool-Climate Hotels
one_liner: A revenue-management add-on that turns heatwave forecasts in origin cities into rate floors, minimum stays and direct-booking campaigns for hotels in cool refuge regions, days before the booking surge arrives.
cluster_name: Overtouristed destinations, tour operators and independent hotels

judges.fatal_flaw: Independent hotels pay little and revenue-management vendors can add heat signals.
judges.note: Cute timing arbitrage, but it is a feature that low-ARPU independent hotels will churn from.

judges.fatal_flaw: Uplift is hard to prove and small hotels pay little for revenue tools.
judges.note: Sharp leading-indicator insight, tourism boards can fund; independent hotels have low ARPU and rate tools exist.

judges.fatal_flaw: Low ticket for small hotels; weather-aware pricing tools already exist.
judges.note: Origin-city heat as leading indicator is smart, but coolcation is a known trend and ARPU is tiny.

title: Two A.M. Any-Tradition Rites and Interpreter Line
one_liner: A 24/7 dispatch of vetted ritual specialists and death-trained interpreters for families outside the majority faith, sold to hospices and palliative units.
cluster_name: Hospice, dying and the first weeks of bereavement

judges.fatal_flaw: Families usually have their own clergy, so hospices will not pay retainers for rare dispatches.
judges.note: Humane, non-obvious niche, but demand is sparse and per-dispatch economics are weak.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market and thin hospice budgets; 24/7 rare-tradition dispatch is operationally brutal.
judges.note: Genuine insight on time-critical ritual competence, but very small prize and hard supply logistics.

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin per-hospice budget and hard-to-operate 24/7 multi-tradition roster with quality control risk.
judges.note: Genuine unmet need and defensible trust moat; low dispatch volume caps revenue per customer.

title: Passive Wellness Alerts From Water Meter Patterns
one_liner: A subscription that texts an adult child, or their parent's home-care agency, when an older person living alone has no expected water activity: no wearable, no camera, just the meter that is already on the house.
cluster_name: Adult children managing aging parents from afar

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility data access is slow; consumer CAC and hardware installs undermine economics.
judges.note: Clever signal, but passive eldercare monitoring is a crowded pattern with abandonment and channel problems.

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility data access and meter hardware installs; seniors' families churn passive monitors.
judges.note: Water as sign-of-life is cute, but it is senior monitoring with hard channel economics.

judges.fatal_flaw: Utility data access and meter hardware installs are slow; senior monitoring gets abandoned.
judges.note: Clever proof-of-life signal, big TAM, but crowded eldercare category and heavy distribution hurdles.

title: Settlement Claim Autopilot for Ticket Buyers
one_liner: A privacy-first app that reconstructs a fan's ticket purchase history and files claims in ticketing settlements and refund orders, paid per validated claim by administrators and plaintiff firms.
cluster_name: Unclaimed money: settlements, refunds, penalties and unpaid invoices

judges.fatal_flaw: Consumer acquisition cost exceeds the $3-15 per-claim payout; administrators run their own outreach.
judges.note: Good buyer insight, but tiny per-claim economics and existing claim-filing apps.

judges.note: Timely settlements and receipt parsing, but the buyer thesis is shaky and it is a thin consumer app.

judges.fatal_flaw: Defendants and administrators gain from low claim rates; small payouts, existing claim-filing services.
judges.note: Rides ticketing liability wave, but the per-claim bounty buyer is unlikely to exist. Consumer path yields about $30 recoveries.

title: Human Concierge for Phone-Free Adults
one_liner: A $29 per month phone number staffed by humans who handle the app-only chores of modern life (QR menus, parking, rides, boarding passes, 2FA migration) so people can keep their dumbphone.
cluster_name: Parents and adults managing phones, screens and AI toys

judges.fatal_flaw: Human-labor service at $29 per month doesn't scale beyond a tiny niche.

judges.fatal_flaw: Human errands at $29 per month lose money; tiny, churning dumbphone niche.
judges.note: Cute reframing of dumbphone friction, but labor-heavy unit economics and small market.

title: PO-Backed Working Capital for Drone Sub-Tier
one_liner: A specialty lender that advances cash against Gauntlet-winner purchase orders to the motor, battery and casting shops that must ship first.
cluster_name: New defense and drone suppliers: compliance and financing hurdles

judges.fatal_flaw: Depends on lender capital and on order flow from a small set of primes
judges.note: Prime-routed payment reduces credit risk, but it is a capital-heavy lender riding drone-order hype.

title: SOC 2 for Rent-Pricing Algorithms

title: Laid-Off Auto Technicians to Water Operators

judges.fatal_flaw: Licensing experience hours and slow workforce funds limit cohort economics.

title: Turn Half-Empty School Wings Into Child Care

title: Dr. Simi USA: Pharmacy-Plus-Consult for the Uninsured
one_liner: Small-format, generic-first pharmacies with a nurse-practitioner consult room beside the counter, posted cash prices and no insurance needed, following Mexico's Farmacias Similares model and landing in US pharmacy deserts.
cluster_name: Independent pharmacies squeezed by PBMs, refund floats and deserts

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin generic margins, NP scope rules and malpractice; big-retail clinics have failed.

title: Offline Brain for Talking Toys
one_liner: A sub-$20 on-device speech-and-language module that lets toys hold child-safe conversations with no cloud, no audio leaving the toy and parent-readable summaries on the parent's phone.
cluster_name: Parents and adults managing phones, screens and AI toys

judges.fatal_flaw: Toy design cycles miss holiday 2026, and chip vendors or Chinese ODMs bundle equivalent modules

title: Do-Not-Clone Voice Registry With Inference-Time Checks
one_liner: A privacy-preserving registry that voice-cloning vendors query before creating a clone, so voice actors and narrators can block or price unauthorized cloning at the moment of input.
cluster_name: Creators proving authorship and stopping unauthorized AI use of their work

judges.fatal_flaw: Voluntary registry; open-source cloners and bad actors never call it.
judges.note: Input-time check is a good reframe, but do-not-train registries have a poor adoption history.

title: Fuel Surcharge Autopilot for Route-Based Services
one_liner: An add-on for field-service software that adds a transparent, index-linked, capped and self-expiring fuel line to invoices, and explains it to customers.
cluster_name: Small trade and service firms underpricing and leaking margin

judges.fatal_flaw: A feature that Jobber or Housecall Pro can ship natively; fuel shock is transient.

title: Referee Body-Cams and Abuse Evidence Layer
one_liner: A clip-on camera and incident-report service that gives youth and high school officials proof and gives leagues grounds to ban abusive spectators.
cluster_name: Out-of-school time, phone-free play and youth sports safety

judges.fatal_flaw: Recording-consent laws and minors' privacy, plus association budgets that barely exist.

title: Buyer-Side RFP Claim Verifier for Cities
one_liner: Automated reference-checking and claim-testing for the flood of AI-polished bids that city procurement offices cannot separate.
cluster_name: Gatekeepers drowning in AI-generated submissions and bot responses

title: Physically Verified Protocol Skills for Lab Agents

title: Executor-of-Last-Resort for Solo Agers

judges.fatal_flaw: Fiduciary licensing and payoff decades out; subscription revenue is small for trust risk.

title: Closing-Risk Radar for New-Construction Loan Officers

title: Trade-Crew Capacity Forward Book for Builders

judges.fatal_flaw: Subs will not report capacity honestly or consistently; builders can't act on it.

title: Sleep-Apnea-to-GLP-1 Pathway for DME Suppliers
one_liner: A co-management service that lets sleep labs and CPAP suppliers prescribe, retest and retain patients as they lose weight.

judges.fatal_flaw: DMEs cannot prescribe; needs clinicians and prior-auth work; regulatory complexity.
judges.note: DME as gatekeeper for OSA-GLP-1 is a fair angle, but the operational and clinical burden is heavy for a small team.

title: Independent Safety Registry for Pet Medicines
one_liner: A neutral post-market surveillance system for veterinary drugs and biologics, built on pet-insurance claims plus owner-reported outcomes.
cluster_name: Veterinary practices: capacity, workforce, diagnostics and drugs

judges.fatal_flaw: Insurers won't share claims data early; no data means no product.
judges.note: Good credibility gap, but data-trust cold start and first revenue likely beyond six months.

judges.note: Sentinel-style registry is a fresh angle, but the market is small and data access is hard.

title: Verified Cool-Night Rooms for Heat-Stressed Europe
one_liner: Cheap in-room sensors prove a hotel room stays below about 26C at night, sold as a certificate, a refund guarantee and a machine-readable rating for booking agents.

judges.fatal_flaw: No platform consumes the rating; hotels won't pay to publish evidence their rooms run hot.
judges.note: Measurable-comfort-as-ranking-signal depends on agent-booking adoption that doesn't exist yet.

title: App-Diet Service for the Phone-Upgrade Freeze
one_liner: As phones get unaffordable, today's handset becomes a five-year handset, so old-device performance decides who keeps users.
cluster_name: Smallholders and rural households in emerging markets

judges.note: Second-order effect of the handset freeze is a decent insight but it becomes a small consulting audit.

judges.note: Neat second-order insight, but a scrappy team selling $15-40k audits to distant banks is slow.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consulting not product; banks and wallets can build lite apps in-house.
judges.note: Nice second-order insight but a services audit business with no scalable product or moat.

title: Hotel-Signed Days-in-Country Proofs for Remote Teams
one_liner: Hotels and co-living spaces issue signed, privacy-minimal 'nights in this country' attestations, so employers can prove where remote staff worked without tracking their phones.
cluster_name: Workforce compliance for remote, tipped and platform workers

judges.fatal_flaw: Hotels won't issue attestations at scale; employers can use existing travel records.

judges.note: Original consent-based presence records, but a feature for payroll tools with weak supply-side pull.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hotels won't issue attestations; mobility vendors already own employer relationships.
judges.note: Clever consent-based evidence angle, but two-sided adoption problem and modest employer pain.

title: Resident Proof for Two-Tier Tourist Pricing
one_liner: A privacy-preserving QR proof of residence lets towns, museums and transit charge visitors more and locals less without building databases or discriminating by nationality.
cluster_name: Overtouristed destinations, tour operators and independent hotels

judges.fatal_flaw: Municipal procurement is slow, EU discrimination law is contested, and EUR 10-30K deals are small.
judges.note: Identity is a real bottleneck, but towns are slow, contested legally, and depend on EU wallets that are not ready.

judges.fatal_flaw: EU nationality-discrimination law risk plus slow municipal sales and tiny per-town contracts.
judges.note: Identity as the bottleneck is neat and timed to EU wallets, but the small-town SaaS prize and legal exposure are poor.

judges.fatal_flaw: Municipal sales are slow and small; EU wallets may make resident proof free.
judges.note: Identity, not pricing, is the bottleneck for resident-visitor pricing. Original, but small per-town ARR and legal exposure.

title: Exchange for Shelved Academic Projects and Null Data
one_liner: Buy the 'graveyard' of academic labs, meaning abandoned projects, validated knockout lines, half-built assays and failed-experiment data, and resell them as dossiers with an interview slot to seed biotechs and AI-bio data teams. Supply is anchored by a paid lab-closure clearance service.
cluster_name: Biotech capital: diligence and salvage

judges.fatal_flaw: Illiquid marketplace of unvalidated reagents; buyers distrust provenance; tiny prices.
judges.note: Exit-knowledge capture is a novel idea, but marketplace liquidity, IP and MTA friction, and low asset value undermine it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Dossier demand is unproven and university IP and MTA friction stalls sales.
judges.note: Exit-knowledge capture from departing postdocs is genuinely non-obvious; concierge wedge is real but the buyer market is speculative.

judges.fatal_flaw: University IP and MTA approvals stall sales, and the marketplace faces a two-sided cold start.
judges.note: Clever exit-knowledge insight, but buyers are unproven and closure fees compete with dumpsters.

title: Screwworm-Era Rescue Transport Compliance Desk
one_liner: With screwworm confirmed in Texas, dogs leaving Texas and New Mexico need a fresh vet inspection certificate and destination permits; run the compliance desk that keeps shelter transports moving.
cluster_name: Pets at risk: owner crises, shelters and transport paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Regulatory shock is temporary and the market is tiny.

judges.note: Urgent and immediately sellable per-animal service, but small prize, low-budget shelters and labor-heavy delivery.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cash-poor nonprofit customers and a temporary outbreak rule regime cap revenue.
judges.note: Very timely screwworm rule shift, but small per-animal margins and grant-dependent buyers limit the business.

title: Drone Incident Desk for Cities and Venues
one_liner: Detection-to-handoff service that turns a drone sighting into a documented, legally routed federal referral for local agencies that cannot legally jam anything.
cluster_name: Rural sheriffs, jails and small police agencies

judges.fatal_flaw: Federal agencies will not cooperate; Axon/Dedrone bundling; tiny municipal budgets.

judges.note: Buying liability cover, not detection, is a good insight. Government sales and vague authority slow it.

title: Scam Fire Drills: A Security Detail for Grandparents

judges.fatal_flaw: Consumers won't pay $20/month; bank sales are slow; a 24/7 human hotline is costly.
judges.note: Rehearsal-not-awareness is a fresh angle and banks bear losses, but scam-protection is crowded and unit economics are hard.

judges.fatal_flaw: Consumer CAC and 24/7 hotline costs; bank sales cycles are long.
judges.note: Rehearsal insight is decent, but senior-scam protection is crowded and unit economics are heavy.

title: Slop-Risk Diligence for Creator-Business Buyers
one_liner: A fixed-price quality-of-earnings report that prices the platform-policy cliff hiding inside a YouTube channel, newsletter or podcast network for sale.
cluster_name: Independent game studios and creator businesses
