judges.note: Utility-when-distribution-stops-paying is reasoned, but news-reactive, public-sector sales, easily replicated reminders.

judges.fatal_flaw: Public-sector insurers buy slowly; the IRDAI draft may change; insurers already send renewal reminders.
judges.note: Utility framing is plausible, but at Rs 30-80 per renewal the volume needed and procurement delays are heavy.

title: Disaster-Day Instant Cash Parametric Cover
one_liner: Pay a fixed sum to a household's phone within hours of an official evacuation order or multi-day power shutoff, funded by cheap capital that is hunting for granular parametric risk.
cluster_name: Fast parametric cash for weather and disaster shocks

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs an MGA, carrier capacity and insurance regulatory approval before revenue.

title: Proof-of-Ingestion Traps for Creators' Content
one_liner: Plant unique, statistically detectable traps in creators' work, then probe AI models to produce evidence that the content was ingested.
cluster_name: Creators proving authorship and stopping unauthorized AI use of their work

title: Old Job Kits for Dementia Sundown Hours

title: Funding Waterfall at the Vet Estimate

judges.fatal_flaw: Multi-sided lending with credit risk; clinics slow to adopt; charity funds small.

title: Independent Robot Bake-Off and Acceptance Lab

judges.fatal_flaw: Vendors control access and reject unflattering tests; capital-heavy physical lab.
judges.note: Independent verification is real need, but pay-to-play credibility and thin buyer base.

title: Notice Desk with Contingency Penalty Abatement

title: Live Herd Maps for Hiking Apps
one_liner: Collar-derived herd positions pushed to hiking and mountain-bike apps so hikers reroute around cattle, funded by the destination that profits from the landscape.
cluster_name: Overtouristed destinations, tour operators and independent hotels

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny market, slow destination-body sales and dependence on collar adoption.

title: Indigenous-Language Voice Compliance for Farm Crews

title: Blind Validation Enclaves for Clinical AI
one_liner: Confidential-computing sandboxes where a hospital's private patient data and a vendor's private model meet, and only a signed performance report leaves.

judges.fatal_flaw: Long hospital sales cycles; BeeKeeperAI-style enclaves already exist.

title: Together Suites: Adjacent Units for Grandparent Care
one_liner: Lease linked or adjacent apartment pairs to a young family and a grandparent, with a fire-rated interior door where code allows, a relocation concierge, and help getting the grandparent paid through child care subsidy relative-care rules.

title: Fandom Events in Empty Cinema Auditoriums

judges.fatal_flaw: Rights holders control everything; thin box-office splits and existing cinema event distributors.

title: Green-Claims Clearance for EU-Bound Brands

title: Pre-Confirmation Screwworm Risk Feed for Cattle Markets

title: Weaver Ant Crews for Cashew and Mango Orchards

title: Demumu With a Body: Paid Welfare-Check Responders
one_liner: Parent-paid check-in safety for Chinese-, Indian- and Korean-speaking students and migrants living alone abroad, where a missed check-in triggers a paid local door-knock instead of an email to someone 10,000 km away.

judges.fatal_flaw: Students resist parental surveillance; sparse responder density makes dispatch economics and liability bad
judges.note: Sharp buyer insight (tuition-paying parents), but it chases a viral fad and dispatch is hard.

title: Night Season: After-Dark Programming for Heat-Struck Venues
one_liner: A turnkey production company that converts heat-crushed summer attendance at zoos, gardens and ballparks into ticketed after-dark shows, with heat-triggered scheduling, on revenue share.

title: Paid Caregiver Demonstration-Data Cooperative

title: Bring-Into-Use Satellites for Spectrum Filing Holders

title: Convert Legacy RPA Bots Using Their Own Logs
one_liner: Use years of bot execution logs as free ground-truth tests to convert brittle RPA bots into monitored agents at a fixed price per bot.

title: Front Door for AI Callers at Local Businesses

title: Trust Oracle for Rental Listings and Agents

one_liner: Turn informal savings groups into a credit bureau and stablecoin treasury that asset financiers can lend against.
cluster_name: Informal finance and payment frictions in emerging markets

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders do not yet pay for group scores, and it is not feasible in six months
judges.note: Stablecoin and informal-finance pattern with thin ARPU; building a bureau needs months of data before any revenue.

judges.fatal_flaw: Vague customer; savings groups will not pay and financier demand is unproven
judges.note: Stablecoin plus emerging-market fintech with three customer types and regulatory drag; hard to prove lender value.

judges.fatal_flaw: Many failed savings-group apps; logging burden and weak lender demand.
judges.note: Digitizing chamas plus stablecoin treasury is a recycled fintech-for-emerging-markets pitch with no new mechanism.

title: Paid Holds: Options Market for Booking Agents
one_liner: A merchant plugin that sells time-limited holds on appointments, tables and inventory to shopping and booking agents, so agent traffic becomes fee revenue for the merchant instead of something to block.
cluster_name: Merchants and bureaucracies that AI agents cannot reach or navigate

judges.fatal_flaw: No agent demand for paid holds; merchants must install a plugin first.
judges.note: Agent-to-agent commerce recycled, with a cold-start marketplace problem and tiny fees.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agent-driven booking volume is negligible, and merchants will not install a plugin for it.
judges.note: Agent-commerce primitive with customers that barely exist; a fee on phantom demand will not close paying merchants.

judges.fatal_flaw: No meaningful agent booking volume yet; merchants can simply require deposits.
judges.note: Clever options framing, but the buyer is a hypothetical agent economy; agent-commerce plumbing is crowded.

title: Tele-Operated Night Aides for Small Care Homes
one_liner: Metered remote-aide hours operating an off-the-shelf mobile manipulator robot in 6-16 bed residential care homes, so labor crosses borders when workers cannot.
cluster_name: Teleoperated labor and remote pilot workforces

judges.fatal_flaw: Robots can't reliably do overnight care tasks, and licensing requires on-site awake staff.
judges.note: Humanoid/home robot plus senior care hype; regulatory, safety and capability barriers make first customers unlikely in six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Staffing rules require on-site humans; robot lease plus remote labor won't hit 40% margin.
judges.note: Robot hardware, regulator sign-off, and dementia-care risk make first paying homes unlikely in six months.

judges.fatal_flaw: Staffing rules count on-site humans, and a $25K robot can't do meaningful overnight care
judges.note: Contrarian labor-arbitrage angle, but robots plus senior care is crowded hype with high safety, liability and feasibility risk.

title: Agent-Bookable Gateway for Local Trades
one_liner: A per-business endpoint that lets consumers' AI agents get a photo-based quote, hold a slot and pay a deposit at a local trade without a phone call.
cluster_name: Merchants and bureaucracies that AI agents cannot reach or navigate

judges.fatal_flaw: Agent-originated local bookings barely exist; there is no demand to monetize yet.
judges.note: Agent-commerce endpoint for boring trades stacks two consensus themes; supply built before any demand.

judges.fatal_flaw: No real consumer-agent demand yet; platforms will define standards and disintermediate.
judges.note: Agent-commerce pattern for SMBs; speculative demand, crowded protocols, and low ARPU.

judges.fatal_flaw: No consumer agent booking volume exists yet, so owners won't pay for hypothetical demand.
judges.note: Solution in search of demand. Local trades pay for leads and calls today, not agent endpoints.

title: Sub-Tier Surge Twin for the Industrial Base
one_liner: A digital twin of foundries, forges and motor makers that shows which supplier breaks first in a 180-day fight.
cluster_name: US machine shops and reshoring manufacturers

judges.fatal_flaw: Govini, Exiger and others own supply-chain visibility; twin outputs rely on thin data.
judges.note: Defense-plus-digital-twin is consensus; vague product with entrenched competitors.

judges.fatal_flaw: Sub-tier capacity data is opaque; a twin needs data it cannot get.
judges.note: Defense-tech digital twin with vague data; PE-first-buyer angle is only mildly non-obvious.

judges.fatal_flaw: Vague model without proprietary data; defense and PE buyers slow to pay.
judges.note: Digital-twin defense pitch with fuzzy wedge; hard to prove accuracy or land first paid pilot.

title: Cross-Border Income Passport for Freelancers
one_liner: Give stablecoin-paid remote workers a verifiable, portable income record that landlords, lenders and visa agents accept.
cluster_name: Gig, tipped and cash workers unable to prove income

judges.fatal_flaw: Landlords and lenders won't accept a new attestation without a bureau-scale network.
judges.note: Stablecoin freelancer plumbing with a familiar pitch; acceptance is the unsolved bottleneck.

judges.fatal_flaw: No lender or landlord trusts a startup's attestation, creating a verifier chicken-and-egg.
judges.note: Stablecoin remittance-adjacent, vague customers, $15 tickets and unproven acceptance.

judges.fatal_flaw: Lenders and landlords won't accept self-run attestations; stablecoin space crowded.
judges.note: Stablecoin freelancer-income pitch is a listed cliché with no trust anchor or unusual wedge.

title: Babel Tables for Multilingual Community Programs
one_liner: A tabletop translation hub that lets a senior-center lunch, ESL class or church group hold one conversation across four languages in real time.
cluster_name: Language, hearing and communication barriers in services and workplaces

judges.fatal_flaw: Phones and earbuds already do live multi-language translation, making a dedicated puck redundant
judges.note: Table-as-unit framing is clever, but hardware for slow-procuring senior centers faces free consumer translation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Senior-center budgets are tiny and free earbud translation from Google, Apple and Samsung undercuts hardware.
judges.note: Table-as-unit is a nice reframe, but hardware sold to low-budget buyers is a poor business.

judges.fatal_flaw: Senior centers lack budget; free phone translation apps already deliver most of the value.
judges.note: Hardware plus translation for cash-poor buyers. Commodity tech, government-funded sales, and weak willingness to pay.

title: Paid Shelter-Dog Field Trips, Fees Per Adoption
one_liner: Professional walkers take the longest-stay shelter dogs on 3-hour public field trips with photos and behavior reports, and shelters pay a small trip fee plus a success fee for each adoption.
cluster_name: Pets at risk: owner crises, shelters and transport paperwork

judges.fatal_flaw: Shelters lack budgets; success fee is hard to attribute; low ticket size.
judges.note: Sympathetic but shelters cannot pay; grant-dependent and hard to scale beyond a local service.

judges.fatal_flaw: Shelters lack budget and volunteers already do field trips free.
judges.note: Pet-service gig play with a small ticket and existing free alternatives. Weak why-now.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cash-strapped shelters cannot fund outcome fees; tiny, grant-dependent market.
judges.note: Nice insight on kennel-stress evaluation, but pet-services niche with weak payers.

title: Turn Podcast Fans Into Local Chapters
one_liner: A chapter-in-a-box that lets mid-size creators convert engaged, lonely audiences into weekly local meetups, with insurance, host training and venues handled.
cluster_name: Loneliness and purpose: belonging programs for isolated adults and elders

judges.fatal_flaw: Fans unlikely to pay $12 monthly; volunteer-host liability and low ARPU.
judges.note: Niche community plus loneliness is a well-worn pattern; creator revenue share is hard to sustain.

judges.fatal_flaw: $120 a month per chapter revenue cannot cover insurance, host and venue costs.
judges.note: Niche community play with consumer economics too small and heavy liability; creator dependence.

judges.fatal_flaw: Fans will not pay $12 a month; volunteer host churn and liability erode margins.
judges.note: Niche community and creator pattern; the parasocial on-ramp line is clever but the business is fragile.

title: Drone-Ready Rx Lockers as Adherence Infrastructure
one_liner: A lockable, temperature-buffered, authenticated receiving station at a senior's home that accepts drone or courier drops and quietly reports whether the medication was retrieved.
cluster_name: Adult children managing aging parents from afar

judges.fatal_flaw: Depends on drone networks reaching seniors' homes; hardware box with unproven payer.
judges.note: Senior-tech hardware bet on speculative drone-delivery adoption with unclear payer.

judges.fatal_flaw: Drone delivery to senior homes isn't scaled; hardware and plan procurement cycles are slow.
judges.note: Aging-in-place hardware sold to payers; clever proof-of-life angle but demand depends on non-existent drone volume.

judges.fatal_flaw: Home drone Rx delivery is not at scale; hardware plus payer sales is slow.
judges.note: Speculative hardware waiting on drone-network scale; senior-tech pattern with an interesting proof-of-life angle.

title: Escrow Notary for Agents Hiring Humans
one_liner: A neutral adjudication layer that agents pay per task to verify that a hired human really did the physical job before escrow releases, built to withstand AI-forged proof.
cluster_name: Payments, escrow, disputes and human fulfilment for agent transactions

judges.fatal_flaw: Agent-hires-human demand is tiny and hype-driven; marketplaces may never need a notary.
judges.note: Agent-to-agent commerce plumbing on a speculative marketplace with thin real volume.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agent-hires-human demand barely exists; marketplaces already show thin supply.
judges.note: Agent-commerce and agent-marketplace pattern; interesting verification thesis but market is nascent.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agent-hires-human volume is negligible, so there are almost no buyers
judges.note: Agent marketplace and primitives cliché with a customer base that barely exists. Nobody has budget for it.

title: A Suable LLC With Reserves for Every Agent
one_liner: Mass-produced, series-LLC legal wrappers that give each paid agent a registered agent for service of process, a capital reserve, and tax handling, so counterparties have someone to sue.
cluster_name: Accountability and guardrails for AI agents acting for others

judges.fatal_flaw: Indie agent developers won't pay $49/month; no enterprise buyer requires it.
judges.note: Agent-identity primitive with a speculative buyer and legal-wrapper hype. Veil-piercing limits the value of the reserve.

judges.fatal_flaw: No buyer demand for per-agent LLCs; veil-piercing and formation costs undermine reserve premise.
judges.note: Agent-identity primitive dressed as legal wrapper; solution looking for a problem.

judges.fatal_flaw: Veil-piercing means little real shield; buyers won't require entity plus reserve.
judges.note: Agent identity and wallet primitive pitch; speculative demand and self-admitted legal caveat undermine the product.

title: Vet-Verified Escrow for Puppy Purchases
one_liner: Buyer funds sit in escrow and release to the seller only after a licensed vet exam confirms the animal is healthy and the microchip matches.
cluster_name: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Scam victims skip escrow; breeders resist; low purchase frequency and cold-start problem.
judges.note: Pet marketplace variant with infrequent transactions and two-sided cold start. Buyers who need protection are the least likely to use it.

judges.fatal_flaw: Scam sellers won't use escrow; honest breeders don't need it
judges.note: Real scam pain but a low-frequency two-sided marketplace with thin take rate and hard buyer acquisition.

judges.fatal_flaw: Cold-start marketplace; sellers won't wait for exam, and returning a failed puppy is unworkable
judges.note: Escrow release mechanics conflict with physical handoff; pet marketplace pattern; weak unit economics.

title: Roll-Up of Compounding-Stranded Weight-Loss Clinics
one_liner: Buy distressed med spas and weight-loss clinics that lost their compounded GLP-1 margin, and convert them into aftercare-plus-aesthetics businesses.
cluster_name: Access, affordability and supply integrity for GLP-1 and compounded drugs

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs acquisition capital and medical-practice ownership structure; patients churn once compounding ends.
judges.note: Distressed roll-up needs real capital and clinical operations; a scrappy team can't easily execute.

judges.fatal_flaw: Capital-intensive roll-up of distressed assets, unfundable at seed and legally exposed.
judges.note: Roll-up plus GLP-1 clinic pattern; stranded patient lists may churn and it is not a scalable tech company.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs acquisition capital and patients walk away; a roll-up is not scrappy-team feasible.
judges.note: PE roll-up of a shrinking GLP-1 clinic niche is the predictable distressed-asset thesis; no unusual insight.

title: Satiety Peptides for Small-Portion Foods
one_liner: Screen food-grade peptides that trigger the body's own GLP-1 release and put them in high-protein snacks.
cluster_name: Businesses adapting to GLP-1 users' changed consumption

judges.fatal_flaw: In vitro GLP-1 assays rarely predict real satiety; long ingredient sales cycles.
judges.note: GLP-1-snack trend chasing with unproven efficacy, slow ingredient adoption and claim limits.

judges.fatal_flaw: In-vitro GLP-1 secretion rarely translates to human satiety; long ingredient sales cycles.
judges.note: GLP-1 plus protein snack is the reflexive food idea; weak science, slow ingredient sales, no real wedge.

judges.fatal_flaw: In-vitro GLP-1 assays don't prove satiety; CPGs demand clinical data; no revenue soon.
judges.note: GLP-1-hype ingredient play with long R&D and sales cycles; no path to paying customers in six months.

title: Waze for Agents: Live Bureaucracy Route Data
one_liner: A pay-per-lookup feed of the current, tested state of consumer and government web procedures (form changes, outages, hidden requirements, real step timings), sold to browser agents just before they attempt an errand.
cluster_name: Merchants and bureaucracies that AI agents cannot reach or navigate

judges.fatal_flaw: Customers are agent startups with tiny volumes; agents will learn drift themselves.
judges.note: Agent-infrastructure pitch selling $0.01 lookups to other startups; no budgeted buyer or durable moat.

judges.fatal_flaw: Paying customers are early agent startups; brittle canaries across thousands of government flows.
judges.note: Browser-agent and x402 hype pattern; labs will build route knowledge themselves and buyers are unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Customers are a few agent startups paying pennies; labs and browsers will absorb route data.
judges.note: Browser-agent and agent-primitive pitch is crowded; freshness data insight is real but the buyer pool is thin.

title: Teleoperated Pack-and-Pick Robots Piloted from Latin America
one_liner: Robot arms run by foundation models, with remote pilots in Guatemala or Colombia fixing the edge cases, sold per box.
cluster_name: Teleoperated labor and remote pilot workforces

judges.fatal_flaw: VLA arms unreliable on delicate berries; incumbent agri-robotics and teleop firms; capital-heavy.
judges.note: Physical-AI plus teleoperation is a crowded 2026 pattern; the thin plan doesn't show why this team wins.

judges.fatal_flaw: Robot reliability and capex; half-human speed rarely beats cheap labor economics.
judges.note: Physical-AI teleop pitch with heavy hardware capital; LatAm pilots are a wedge but the economics are unproven.

judges.fatal_flaw: Hardware capital, unreliable manipulation, and unproven per-case economics before any revenue.
judges.note: Physical-AI teleoperation; robots at half human speed rarely beat crews, and capex delays first sales.

title: Guardrail Gateway for Hotel AI Agents
one_liner: A proxy between hotel AI agents (voice, chat, booking) and PMS, POS and door-lock APIs that enforces per-action permissions, spend limits and human approval for irreversible actions.
cluster_name: Accountability and guardrails for AI agents acting for others

judges.fatal_flaw: Hotel is a tiny vertical and PMS vendors will ship scoped agent permissions natively.
judges.note: A vertical agent-guardrail wrapper on a crowded pattern, with a small market and low per-property pricing.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny buyer pool; PMS and AI vendors will build permissions in-house.
judges.note: Agent guardrails is a crowded category; hotels aren't buying it yet and vendor customers are few.

judges.fatal_flaw: Agent-guardrail category is crowded and PMS vendors will build native permissions.
judges.note: Agent security and guardrails dressed in a hotel niche; a tiny buyer and an obvious picks-and-shovels play.

title: Overtourism Feed for AI Travel Agents
one_liner: A destination-signed, machine-readable feed of live capacity, closures and dispersal incentives that AI trip agents query, so places can steer planning before tourists arrive.
cluster_name: Overtouristed destinations, tour operators and independent hotels

judges.fatal_flaw: No AI agents consume the feed yet, and DMOs buy slowly.
judges.note: MCP-feed-for-AI-travel pitch with no demand side and slow public buyers.

judges.fatal_flaw: AI agents are not obliged to obey feeds; DMOs pay slowly and small.
judges.note: Agent-infrastructure hype attached to slow-paying tourism boards; a robots.txt-style claim without leverage.

judges.fatal_flaw: No AI trip agent has incentive to consume it; DMOs are slow buyers.
judges.note: MCP-feed-for-agents buzzword pitch stacked on AI travel planner; unproven demand and weak buyer economics.

title: Peak-Season Exchange for Idle Warehouse Robot Hours
one_liner: A marketplace and price index that moves idle AMRs and robots-as-a-service capacity between 3PLs and retailers to cover seasonal peaks, priced per robot-hour.
cluster_name: Deploying robots in the real world

judges.fatal_flaw: No liquidity: RaaS vendors will not sublease and idle-fleet supply is tiny.
judges.note: Marketplace with almost no supply, a tiny addressable market, and unproven demand for hourly robot rental.

judges.fatal_flaw: Idle robot supply barely exists; integration per site kills a marketplace.
judges.note: Marketplace on a hype asset class with no supply. Trailer-market analogy is premature by years.

judges.fatal_flaw: No liquidity: too few deployed robots, and integration and insurance kill marketplace economics.
judges.note: Premature marketplace for a fleet that barely exists; Airbnb-for-idle-assets pattern with no supply.

title: Surety-Bonded License Plates for AI Agents
one_liner: A registrar that binds each autonomous agent to a legally accountable, insured principal through a surety bond and a revocable credential merchants and platforms can check.
cluster_name: Accountability and guardrails for AI agents acting for others

judges.fatal_flaw: No loss history to underwrite; card networks will carry agent liability themselves.
judges.note: Agent identity and liability layer that networks will absorb; premature and crowded.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs surety carrier underwriting and licensing with no proven merchant demand for bonded agents.
judges.note: Agent-liability layer with no buyers yet, dependent on carrier and MGA capacity. Crowded, speculative and regulated.

judges.fatal_flaw: No loss data to underwrite; merchants do not yet demand bonded agents.
judges.note: Suretyship is a smart analogy, but it is another agent trust or identity layer with no demand or actuarial base.

title: Meeting Subtext Captions for Neurodivergent Workers
one_liner: An on-screen coach for Zoom and Teams that flags conversational subtext (a question aimed at you, a topic shift, rising frustration) and supports post-meeting debriefs, sold through autism and ADHD coaches.
cluster_name: Language, hearing and communication barriers in services and workplaces

judges.fatal_flaw: Affect and subtext inference is unreliable and stigmatizing; tiny per-seat revenue via coaches.
judges.note: AI coach/notetaker hybrid with weak payers, accuracy risk, and $50-per-client economics.

judges.fatal_flaw: Inferring tone in real time is unreliable and privacy-fraught; meeting-tool bundling.
judges.note: Notetaker/coach variant with small coach channel and ethical and accuracy risks.

judges.fatal_flaw: Real-time affect inference is unreliable and stigmatizing; payers are small coaches.
judges.note: AI coach for a wellness niche; obvious idea, dubious accuracy and thin monetization.

title: Credit Union Tokenized Deposit Network
one_liner: Give thousands of small credit unions a shared 24/7 tokenized-deposit settlement network so they can answer the 'war for deposits' together instead of losing it one by one.
cluster_name: Cross-border money movement and stablecoin rails

judges.fatal_flaw: FedNow already gives 24/7 settlement; slow credit unions; consortium execution risk.
judges.note: Stablecoin-era consortium pitch with weak why-now. Existing rails cover the stated pain.

judges.fatal_flaw: FedNow and RTP already give credit unions 24/7 settlement; cooperative governance is slow.
judges.note: Stablecoin-flavored fintech cliche with a slow-moving buyer and an already-solved settlement problem.

judges.fatal_flaw: Needs licensed trust-bank partner and slow credit-union consensus before any transaction revenue.
judges.note: Consortium network-effect play with heavy regulatory dependence; classic stablecoin cliche, no path to ten customers.

title: Rent Ledger for Adult Kids Living at Home
one_liner: A simple lease, payment and credit-reporting layer that lets parents charge their adult children rent, build the kids' credit history, and quietly bank the money as a down-payment fund.
cluster_name: Singular / uncategorized

judges.fatal_flaw: Parents will not pay $12/month; lenders may not credit parent-landlord rent
judges.note: Consumer fintech with weak urgency and unvalidated credit assumptions.

judges.fatal_flaw: Bureaus and lenders may ignore parent-landlord rent; parents won't pay $12 monthly.
judges.note: Consumer fintech with unvalidated core assumptions and low ARPU; more a feature than a company.

judges.fatal_flaw: Bureaus and lenders unlikely to credit parent-landlord rent; parents unlikely to charge it.
judges.note: Generic consumer-fintech app on an unvalidated assumption; the family-rent insight is cute, not defensible.

title: Lend Against Battery Earnings for Vet Bills
one_liner: A wallet that routes VPP and demand-response payouts into a dedicated pet-care fund, then advances emergency vet money against the battery's telemetry-verified future earnings.
cluster_name: Pet owners and insurers squeezed by rising vet bills

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny VPP payouts cannot collateralize vet bills; consumer-lending regulation.
judges.note: Mashes pet finance with home VPP; contrived, small cash flows, and lending compliance burden.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny overlap of battery owners with pets; lending licensing and credit risk swamp it.
judges.note: Contrived pairing of VPP payouts and vet-bill BNPL; feature-level audience and heavy regulation.

judges.fatal_flaw: Tiny overlap of battery owners, pet owners and lending; regulatory and credit risk.
judges.note: Stacks VPP, pet insurance and lending; no urgent buyer, heavy licensing, distribution nearly impossible.

title: Pay-on-Green: Escrow Released by Executable Tests
one_liner: Escrow for agent-to-agent work where the negotiated object is a hashed acceptance test, and money moves only when the test passes.
cluster_name: Payments, escrow, disputes and human fulfilment for agent transactions

judges.fatal_flaw: Agent-to-agent commerce volume barely exists, so there is nothing to escrow.
judges.note: Agent marketplace and escrow meta-pitch with speculative buyers. Cannot find ten real paying customers.

judges.fatal_flaw: No real agent-to-agent demand or liquidity; marketplace escrow with no buyers yet.
judges.note: Test-as-contract escrow is intellectually neat but it is agent-marketplace hype, early, and dependent on a market that doesn't exist.

judges.fatal_flaw: No real volume of agent-to-agent purchases yet; two-sided cold start.
judges.note: Agent commerce escrow with crowded protocols and no demonstrated buyers within six months.

title: Remote-Piloted Care Robots: Labor by Teleoperation
one_liner: Mobile manipulators supervised by remote pilots handle non-clinical night-shift chores in memory care, importing labor by bandwidth instead of visa.
cluster_name: Teleoperated labor and remote pilot workforces

judges.fatal_flaw: Stretch-class robots can't safely or usefully work around dementia residents at night.
judges.note: Humanoid/teleop hype in senior care; capability and safety gaps, and the economics rest on robot reliability.

judges.fatal_flaw: Safety and liability in memory care and unproven teleop robots make early revenue unlikely.
judges.note: Robot hardware, capital-heavy and crowded pattern; assisted-living buyers will not accept unproven robots near residents.

judges.fatal_flaw: Robots can't safely do memory-care chores; unit economics and liability fail.
judges.note: Home/care robot cliché with teleop twist. Capability, safety and cost gaps make pilots implausible.

title: Worker-Owned Agentic Back-Office Cooperatives
one_liner: A franchise-in-a-box that helps laid-off finance and admin staff form co-ops running agent-leveraged bookkeeping, payroll and billing services for local small businesses, keeping the surplus themselves.
cluster_name: Employers restructuring for AI: layoffs, severance and displaced workers

judges.fatal_flaw: Thin margins, co-op governance friction and E&O liability; Bench showed the unit-economics trap.
judges.note: Ideological AI-bookkeeping play with no venture-scale economics; the ownership insight doesn't create a moat or growth.

judges.fatal_flaw: Co-op formation, financing and bookkeeping liability stack; ownership-lever thesis is unproven.
judges.note: Bundles AI bookkeeping, roll-up and co-op trends; complex, slow to first revenue and hard to defend.

judges.fatal_flaw: Forming co-ops with laid-off staff, plus E&O insurance, is slow and operationally complex.
judges.note: AI bookkeeping with ideology layered on; co-op formation drags time to revenue, quality varies, and Bench-style economics loom.
